cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.COMPANY: The company the record is about, like the one a consumer complained about or the one that won a research award. Blank in most rows of the FHFA tables.
cols.DATE_RECEIVED: The date the agency received the complaint, report, or application.
cols.TAGS: Keywords attached to the record, usually joined with commas. Some rows hold an empty list [].
cols.IS_CLOSED: Whether the complaint or investigation is closed: True or False.
cols.SOURCE_ID: A short name for the source feed the row came from, like fed_cfpb_complaints. In the ITIS other-sources table it is a plain number instead, which needs a lookup.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.COMPLAINT_ID: CFPB's complaint number. Each row has its own value.
cols.DATE_SENT_TO_COMPANY: Date CFPB forwarded the complaint to the company.
cols.DAYS_RECEIVED_TO_COMPANY: Days between CFPB getting the complaint and sending it to the company. Almost always 0.
cols.RECEIVED_MONTH: Month the complaint came in, stored as the first day of that month.
cols.RECEIVED_YEAR: Year the complaint came in, stored as January 1 of that year.
cols.PRODUCT: The kind of financial product, like credit reporting, debt collection or mortgage.
cols.SUB_PRODUCT: A narrower product, like Credit reporting or Checking account. I do not know is a common answer.
cols.ISSUE: What went wrong, like Incorrect information on your report.
cols.SUB_ISSUE: A narrower problem, like Information belongs to someone else. Blank on some rows.
cols.SUBMITTED_VIA: How the complaint was filed: Web, Referral, Phone, Postal mail, Fax or Email.
cols.COMPANY_RESPONSE: How the company closed out the complaint, like Closed with explanation or Closed with monetary relief.
cols.COMPANY_PUBLIC_RESPONSE: The company's optional public statement, picked from set phrases. Blank for about 4 in 10.
cols.IS_TIMELY: Whether the company answered on time.
cols.HAS_NARRATIVE: Whether the consumer's own story was published with the complaint.
cols.COMPLAINT_NARRATIVE: The consumer's story in their own words, with personal details blacked out as XXXX. Blank on about 8 in 10 complaints.

CONSUMER_PROTECTION__FED_CFPB_COMPLAINTS.summary: Consumer complaints about banks, lenders, debt collectors and credit bureaus filed with the federal Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.
CONSUMER_PROTECTION__FED_CFPB_COMPLAINTS.row: One complaint: one consumer's problem with one company, and how the company answered.

cols.CASE_NUMBER: The agency's ID number for one case, in a format that depends on the agency, like 05-2014-5064 or I-200-19058-315794. In the OSHA injury tables it is a small running number like 1, 2 or 3 that repeats across work sites, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.DATA_YEAR: The year the data covers, like 2024. One table runs into future years like 2032.
cols.AGE: The person's age in years, or an age group like 15-24 years in the CDC table. Stored as text in some tables.
cols.SEX_CODE: The person's sex as a number code, mostly 1 or 2, that needs each source's lookup. The injury table also has a few 0s and junk decimals like 5.4699.
cols.RACE_CODE: The person's race as a number code, like 1 to 5. Each source has its own list, so it needs that source's lookup.
cols.HISPANIC_CODE: Whether the person is Hispanic, as a number code like 1 or 2. BJS uses 98 for unknown; NEISS uses 0 and is mostly blank.
cols.NARRATIVE: A free-text account of what happened, as the reporter wrote it, often in capitals with abbreviations. Mostly blank in several tables, and the rail equipment table fills many rows with junk like NoneNoneNone.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.TREATMENT_DATE: Date the patient was treated in the ER.
cols.BODY_PART_CODE: Body part hurt, a number code that needs a lookup.
cols.DIAGNOSIS_CODE: Kind of injury, a number code that needs a lookup.
cols.DISPOSITION_CODE: What happened to the patient after the ER visit, a number code that needs a lookup.
cols.LOCATION_CODE: Where the injury happened, a number code that needs a lookup.
cols.FIRE_INVOLVEMENT: Fire involvement code, 0 to 4; 0 on almost all rows. Codes need a lookup.
cols.PRODUCT_CODE_1: Main product involved, a number code that needs a lookup.
cols.PRODUCT_CODE_2: Second product involved; 0 means none, on most rows.
cols.PRODUCT_CODE_3: Third product involved; 0 means none, on almost all rows.
cols.ALCOHOL_INVOLVED: 1 if alcohol was involved, 0 if not. Mostly blank.
cols.DRUG_INVOLVED: 1 if drugs were involved, 0 if not. Mostly blank.
cols.STRATUM: Hospital group in the sample: C, L, M, S or V; codes need a lookup.
cols.STATISTICAL_WEIGHT: Weight that turns a sample case into a national estimate; add these up instead of counting rows.

CONSUMER_SAFETY__FED_CPSC_NEISS.summary: Injuries tied to consumer products, as seen in a sample of US hospital emergency rooms and gathered by the Consumer Product Safety Commission, 9.8 million cases.
CONSUMER_SAFETY__FED_CPSC_NEISS.row: One injury: one emergency room visit, tied to up to three products.

cols.MFR_NAME: The vehicle or parts maker's name, like Ford Motor Company or Kia America, Inc.
cols.MAKE: The vehicle or equipment brand, like FORD or HONDA.
cols.MODEL_YEAR: The vehicle's model year, like 2015. 9999 shows up often as a placeholder.
cols.COMPONENT: The part of the vehicle involved, like STEERING or SERVICE BRAKES. Some tables add detail after colons.
cols.FAIL_DATE: The date something failed: the car part in NHTSA complaints, or the bank in the FDIC failed-bank list. 1901-01-01 shows up in the complaints as a fake date.
cols.DATE_RECEIVED: The date the agency received the complaint, report, or application.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CMPLID: The record number for this complaint line. Each row has its own value.
cols.ODINO: NHTSA's number for the complaint as filed. Use it to group rows that belong to one complaint.
cols.MODEL: The vehicle model, like F-150 or ACCORD.
cols.CRASH: Whether the problem involved a crash, Y or N.
cols.FIRE: Whether the problem involved a fire, Y or N.
cols.INJURED: How many people were hurt. Most rows are 0.
cols.MILES: Odometer miles when the problem happened. Blank for about half, and 0 also shows up.
cols.OCCURRENCES: How many times the problem happened. Mostly blank.
cols.CMPL_TYPE: How the complaint came in, as a code like IVOQ or EVOQ that needs a lookup.
cols.VIN: The first 11 characters of the vehicle ID number. Junk text like PLEASE PROV shows up as a placeholder.
cols.PROD_TYPE: Kind of product, code V, T, C or E that needs a lookup. V is almost every row.
cols.COMPLAINT_DESCRIPTION: The complaint in the person's own words.
cols.MEDICAL_ATTN: Whether anyone needed medical care, Y or N.
cols.VEHICLE_TOWED: Whether the vehicle had to be towed, Y or N. Blank on rows whose product type is not V.
cols.INVOLVED_CRASH: True when the complaint involved a crash; the CRASH column as true or false.
cols.INVOLVED_FIRE: True when the complaint involved a fire; the FIRE column as true or false.
cols.IS_FATAL: True when the complaint reports at least one death.
cols.CAUSED_HARM: True when the complaint reports anyone hurt or killed.

CONSUMER_SAFETY__FED_NHTSA_COMPLAINTS.summary: Complaints filed with the federal auto-safety agency, NHTSA, about vehicle and equipment safety problems, from crashes and fires to failing parts.
CONSUMER_SAFETY__FED_NHTSA_COMPLAINTS.row: One complaint line: one vehicle part or system named in one person's complaint. A complaint that names several parts takes several rows; ODINO ties them together.

CONSUMER_SAFETY__FED_NHTSA_INVESTIGATION.summary: NHTSA's vehicle safety defect investigations, with each make, model and year covered, the problem looked at and whether a recall followed.
CONSUMER_SAFETY__FED_NHTSA_INVESTIGATION.row: One vehicle in one investigation: one make, model and year covered by one defect probe. One big probe can cover thousands of rows.

cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.POPULATION_2020: How many people lived in the county or census tract in the 2020 Census.
cols.POP_CENTER_LAT: The latitude of the spot where the area's people are centered, its population center, in decimal degrees.
cols.POP_CENTER_LON: The longitude of the area's population center, in decimal degrees. Negative in the U.S.
cols.VINTAGE: Which year's Census map the geography comes from, like 2020. Stored as text.

DIM_COUNTY.summary: The master list of all 3,222 US counties and county equivalents, with FIPS code, state, 2020 population and a population-center point for mapping.
DIM_COUNTY.row: One county: one US county or county equivalent.

cols.DATE_DAY: One calendar day; each row is one date. The calendar table starts at 1700, the date table at 1950.
cols.MONTH_NAME: The month spelled out, like January. One calendar table uses short forms like Jan.
cols.DAY_OF_WEEK_ISO: The day of the week as a number, 1 Monday through 7 Sunday.
cols.DAY_NAME: The day of the week in words. The date table spells it out like Monday; the calendar table uses three letters like Mon.
cols.IS_WEEKEND: Whether the day is a Saturday or Sunday: True or False.
cols.DAY_OF_MONTH: The day of the month, 1 to 31.
cols.WEEK_OF_YEAR_ISO: The week number, 1 to 53, by the international ISO rule.
cols.YEAR_MONTH: The year and month as text, like 2035-12. Good for grouping by month.
cols.US_FISCAL_YEAR: The federal fiscal year, which starts October 1.

DIM_DATE.summary: A plain calendar: one row for every day across about 86 years, split into year, quarter, month, weekday and fiscal year. It holds no events.
DIM_DATE.row: One calendar day: its year, quarter, month, week, weekday and fiscal year.

cols.STATE_FIPS: The state's number code, like 48 or 06, which needs a lookup. Several tables drop the leading zero so 6 means 06, some rows hold other codes like C1, TX, 00 or N/A, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.STATE_USPS: The state's two-letter postal code, like MA. Includes territories like PR and VI.

cols.IS_TERRITORY: True for the five territories, false for the states and DC.

DIM_TRACT.summary: Every US census tract, 85,391 of them, with its county, state, 2020 population and population center point.

cols.CCN: The facility's 6-character Medicare certification number, stored as text; some hold letters, like 38T061. It is almost always blank in the three Open Payments tables.

cols.MATCH_TIER: How strong the match is, 1 to 4. The match rule column says what each tier means; 1 is name plus ZIP.
cols.MATCH_RULE: How the two were paired: name+zip5, name+state, dba+zip5, or street+zip5 for hospitals.
cols.CCN_NAME: The hospital's name as Medicare lists it.
cols.CCN_ZIP5: The hospital's five-digit ZIP code as Medicare lists it.
cols.EIN_NAME: The organization's name as the IRS lists it.
cols.EIN_ZIP5: The organization's five-digit ZIP code as the IRS lists it. Often the headquarters, not the hospital.
cols.EIN_NTEE: The IRS charity category code, like E220 or E22. Codes starting with E are health groups. The rest need a lookup.

cols.FOUNDATION_CODE: What kind of charity it is, like private foundation or public charity, as a two-digit IRS code such as 15 or 16. Needs a lookup.

cols.INCOME_AMT: The nonprofit's total income in dollars, from its latest filing. Zero often means not reported, and one table stores it as text.
cols.REVENUE_AMT: The nonprofit's total yearly revenue in dollars, from its latest filing. Zero often means not reported, and one table stores it as text.

cols.OFFENDER_SEX_CODE: The offender's sex as a code; 98 looks like a don't-know placeholder. The codes need a lookup.
cols.OFFENDER_RACE_CODE: The offender's race as a code. Most rows are -1, a placeholder. The codes need a lookup.
cols.VICTIMIZATION_WEIGHT: How many real victimizations this one survey record stands for. Add these up to estimate national counts.
cols.SERIES_FLAG: Marks whether the crime was one of a series of similar crimes, 1 or 2. The codes need a lookup.
cols.ADJUSTED_WEIGHT: The victimization weight after adjusting for series crimes. Use this one to estimate national counts.

CRIMINAL_JUSTICE__FED_BJS_DATA.summary: Crime victim records from the Bureau of Justice Statistics' national victimization survey, from 1993 on: who the victim was and what happened, almost all as number codes.
CRIMINAL_JUSTICE__FED_BJS_DATA.row: One victimization: one crime reported by one survey respondent, with a weight to scale it up to the whole country.

cols.STATE_FIPS: The state's number code, like 48 or 06, which needs a lookup. Several tables drop the leading zero so 6 means 06, some rows hold other codes like C1, TX, 00 or N/A, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.QUARTER: The quarter the numbers cover, like Q1. The HUD table holds a quarter-end date like 31DEC2025, and the BLS table is empty.
cols.AREA_FIPS: The area code: a 5-digit county code, or a code starting with C for a metro area.
cols.OWNERSHIP_CODE: A number for who owns the employers, 5 on most rows. The codes need a lookup.
cols.INDUSTRY_CODE: The industry, as a NAICS code or a BLS summary code like 10. Names need a lookup.
cols.AGGREGATION_LEVEL_CODE: A code for how detailed the row is, by area type and industry level. The codes need a lookup, and adding rows across levels double counts.
cols.SIZE_CODE: Employer size group; 0 on every row, so it tells you nothing here.
cols.DISCLOSURE_CODE: N on over half the rows; those rows show 0 for jobs and wages, which means hidden, not zero. Blank otherwise.
cols.ANNUAL_AVG_ESTABLISHMENTS: Average number of workplaces during the year.
cols.ANNUAL_AVG_EMPLOYMENT: Average number of jobs during the year. 0 on over half the rows, mostly where figures are hidden.
cols.TOTAL_ANNUAL_WAGES: Total wages paid during the year, in dollars. 0 on over half the rows, mostly where figures are hidden.
cols.ANNUAL_AVG_WEEKLY_WAGE: Average weekly wage, in dollars. 0 where figures are hidden.
cols.AVG_ANNUAL_PAY: Average yearly pay per job, in dollars. 0 where figures are hidden.
cols.YOY_EMPLOYMENT_PCT_CHANGE: Percent change in jobs from the year before. 0 on most rows, often standing in for missing.
cols.YOY_WAGES_PCT_CHANGE: Percent change in wages from the year before. 0 on most rows, often standing in for missing.

ECONOMICS__FED_BLS_QCEW.summary: Jobs, employers and wages by county and industry from the Bureau of Labor Statistics' quarterly census of employment and wages, as yearly averages.
ECONOMICS__FED_BLS_QCEW.row: One area, one industry and one kind of owner, in one year.

cols.ACK_ID: The Labor Department's receipt number for one Form 5500 pension plan filing, starting with the date and time filed. Joins the main form to its schedules.
cols.EIN: The organization's 9-digit federal tax ID number, stored as text. Some rows hold 000000000 as a filler or only 8 digits because a leading zero was lost, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.PLAN_NAME: The name of the employee pension or benefit plan, like a company's 401K plan.
cols.TOTAL_ASSETS_EOY_AMT: Meant to be the dollar value of everything the organization or plan owned at year's end, but empty in both tables.
cols.DATE_RECEIVED: The date the agency received the complaint, report, or application.
cols.ADMIN_NAME: The name of the person or company that runs the pension plan or the water system. Mostly blank in the pension table.
cols.FORM_YEAR: Meant for the form year. Empty in this table.
cols.PLAN_YEAR_BEGIN_DATE: Meant for the plan year's start date; use FORM_PLAN_YEAR_BEGIN_DATE. Empty in this table.
cols.PLAN_YEAR_END_DATE: Meant for the plan year's end date; use FORM_TAX_PRD. Empty in this table.
cols.PLAN_NUM: Meant for the plan number; use SPONS_DFE_PN. Empty in this table.
cols.SPONSOR_DFE_NAME: The employer or group that sponsors the benefit plan, by name.
cols.SPONSOR_DFE_EIN: Meant for the sponsor's federal tax ID; use SPONS_DFE_EIN. Empty in this table.
cols.SPONS_DFE_MAIL_US_STATE: The sponsor's mailing state, as two letters.
cols.TYPE_PLAN_ENTITY_CD: What kind of filer this is, as a number code from 1 to 4; 2 covers almost every row. The codes need a lookup.
cols.TOT_PARTCP_BOY_CNT: How many people were in the plan at the start of the year.
cols.TOT_ACTIVE_PARTCP_CNT: How many people still working for the employer were in the plan.
cols.NET_ASSETS_EOY_AMT: Meant for the plan's net assets at year end. Empty in this table.
cols.TOTAL_ASSETS_BOY_AMT: Meant for the plan's total assets at the start of the year. Empty in this table.
cols.BENEFIT_PYMTS_TOTAL_AMT: Meant for total benefits paid out. Empty in this table.
cols.ADMIN_EXPENSES_TOTAL_AMT: Meant for total administrative expenses. Empty in this table.
cols.FILING_STATUS: Says FILING_RECEIVED on every row. Tells you nothing.
cols.PREPARER_EIN: Meant for the tax ID of whoever prepared the filing. Empty in this table.
cols.BUSINESS_CODE: The sponsor's industry, as a six-digit code like 621111. The codes need a lookup.
cols.FORM_PLAN_YEAR_BEGIN_DATE: The day the plan year started. Most filings start 2025-01-01.
cols.FORM_TAX_PRD: The day the plan year ended. Most filings end 2025-12-31.
cols.TYPE_DFE_PLAN_ENTITY_CD: For pooled investment funds that file, a letter code for the fund type, like C or M. Filled on under 2% of rows; the codes need a lookup.
cols.INITIAL_FILING_IND: 1 if this is the plan's first filing, 0 if not.
cols.AMENDED_IND: 1 if this filing corrects an earlier one, 0 if not.
cols.FINAL_FILING_IND: 1 if this is the plan's last filing, 0 if not.
cols.SHORT_PLAN_YR_IND: 1 if the plan year was shorter than 12 months, 0 if not.
cols.COLLECTIVE_BARGAIN_IND: 1 if the plan comes from a union contract, 0 if not.
cols.F5558_APPLICATION_FILED_IND: 1 if the filer asked for more time on Form 5558, 0 if not.
cols.EXT_AUTOMATIC_IND: 1 if the filer used an automatic deadline extension, 0 if not.
cols.DFVC_PROGRAM_IND: 1 if the filing came in late through the Labor Department's late-filer relief program, 0 if not.
cols.EXT_SPECIAL_IND: 1 if the filer claimed a special deadline extension, such as for a disaster, 0 if not.
cols.EXT_SPECIAL_TEXT: Why a special extension was claimed, in the filer's words, like COVID RELIEF or HURRICANE IDA. Filled on 16 rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_PN: The plan's three-digit number under its sponsor, like 001 or 501.
cols.PLAN_EFF_DATE: The day the plan first took effect.
cols.SPONS_DFE_DBA_NAME: The trade name the sponsor goes by, if any. Mostly blank.
cols.SPONS_DFE_CARE_OF_NAME: A care-of name on the sponsor's mailing address. Mostly blank.
cols.SPONS_DFE_MAIL_US_ADDRESS2: Second line of the sponsor's mailing address, like a suite. Mostly blank.
cols.SPONS_DFE_MAIL_FOREIGN_ADDR1: Mailing street for sponsors outside the US. Filled on 122 rows, mostly one address in Bengaluru, India.
cols.SPONS_DFE_MAIL_FOREIGN_ADDR2: Second mailing line for sponsors outside the US. Filled on 115 rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_MAIL_FOREIGN_CITY: Mailing city for sponsors outside the US, spelled both Bengaluru and Bangalore. Filled on 122 rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_MAIL_FORGN_PROV_ST: Mailing province or state for sponsors outside the US, like KARNATAKA. Filled on 118 rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_MAIL_FOREIGN_CNTRY: Mailing country for sponsors outside the US, as two letters like IN. Filled on 122 rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_MAIL_FORGN_POSTAL_CD: Foreign postal code for the sponsor's mail. Filled on 119 rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_LOC_US_ADDRESS1: The sponsor's physical street address, when it differs from the mailing one. Filled on under 10% of rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_LOC_US_ADDRESS2: Second line of the sponsor's physical address. Filled on about 1% of rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_LOC_US_CITY: The sponsor's physical city, when it differs from the mailing one. Filled on under 10% of rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_LOC_US_STATE: The sponsor's physical state, as two letters, when it differs from the mailing one. Filled on under 10% of rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_LOC_US_ZIP: The sponsor's physical ZIP code, five or nine digits. Filled on under 10% of rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_LOC_FOREIGN_ADDRESS1: The sponsor's physical street outside the US. Filled on 5 rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_LOC_FOREIGN_ADDRESS2: Second line of the sponsor's physical address outside the US. Filled on 5 rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_LOC_FOREIGN_CITY: The sponsor's physical city outside the US. Filled on 5 rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_LOC_FORGN_PROV_ST: The sponsor's physical province outside the US. Filled on 5 rows, all KARNATAKA.
cols.SPONS_DFE_LOC_FOREIGN_CNTRY: The sponsor's physical country outside the US, as two letters. Filled on 5 rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_LOC_FORGN_POSTAL_CD: The sponsor's foreign physical postal code. Filled on 5 rows.
cols.SPONS_DFE_EIN: The sponsor's nine-digit federal tax ID. Use this one; SPONSOR_DFE_EIN is empty.
cols.SPONS_DFE_PHONE_NUM: The sponsor's ten-digit phone number, stored as a number.
cols.ADMIN_CARE_OF_NAME: A care-of name for the plan administrator. Filled on 150 rows.
cols.ADMIN_US_ADDRESS1: The plan administrator's street address, when it is not the sponsor. Filled on about 3% of rows.
cols.ADMIN_US_ADDRESS2: Second line of the administrator's address. Filled on about 1% of rows.
cols.ADMIN_US_CITY: The plan administrator's city. Filled on about 3% of rows.
cols.ADMIN_US_STATE: The plan administrator's state, as two letters. Filled on about 3% of rows.
cols.ADMIN_US_ZIP: The plan administrator's ZIP code, five or nine digits. Filled on about 3% of rows.
cols.ADMIN_FOREIGN_ADDRESS1: The administrator's street outside the US. Filled on 1 row.
cols.ADMIN_FOREIGN_ADDRESS2: Second line of the administrator's address outside the US. Filled on 1 row.
cols.ADMIN_FOREIGN_CITY: The administrator's city outside the US. Filled on 1 row.
cols.ADMIN_FOREIGN_PROV_STATE: The administrator's province outside the US. Filled on 1 row.
cols.ADMIN_FOREIGN_CNTRY: The administrator's country outside the US. Filled on 1 row.
cols.ADMIN_FOREIGN_POSTAL_CD: The administrator's foreign postal code. Filled on 1 row.
cols.ADMIN_EIN: The plan administrator's nine-digit federal tax ID, when it is not the sponsor. Filled on about 3% of rows.
cols.ADMIN_PHONE_NUM: The plan administrator's phone number, stored as a number. Filled on about 3% of rows.
cols.LAST_RPT_SPONS_NAME: The sponsor's name on the plan's last filing, if it has changed. Filled on under 3% of rows.
cols.LAST_RPT_SPONS_EIN: The sponsor's tax ID on the plan's last filing, if it has changed. Filled on under 3% of rows.
cols.LAST_RPT_PLAN_NUM: The plan number on the plan's last filing, if it has changed. Filled on under 3% of rows.
cols.ADMIN_SIGNED_DATE: When the plan administrator signed electronically, with time and time zone, stored as text.
cols.ADMIN_SIGNED_NAME: The person who signed for the plan administrator.
cols.SPONS_SIGNED_DATE: When someone signed electronically for the sponsor, stored as text. Filled on about 9% of rows.
cols.SPONS_SIGNED_NAME: The person who signed for the sponsor. Filled on about 9% of rows.
cols.DFE_SIGNED_DATE: When someone signed for a pooled investment fund, stored as text. Filled on 488 rows.
cols.DFE_SIGNED_NAME: The person who signed for a pooled investment fund. Filled on 488 rows.
cols.RTD_SEP_PARTCP_RCVG_CNT: How many retired or departed people are getting benefits now.
cols.RTD_SEP_PARTCP_FUT_CNT: How many departed people will get benefits later.
cols.SUBTL_ACT_RTD_SEP_CNT: Subtotal of working, retired and departed people in the plan.
cols.BENEF_RCVG_BNFT_CNT: How many survivors of dead participants are getting benefits. Mostly blank.
cols.TOT_ACT_RTD_SEP_BENEF_CNT: Total people in the plan at year end, counting workers, retirees, departed people and survivors.
cols.PARTCP_ACCOUNT_BAL_CNT: How many people had money in their own plan account at year end. Filled on about half of rows.
cols.SEP_PARTCP_PARTL_VSTD_CNT: How many people left during the year before they fully owned their benefits. Mostly blank.
cols.CONTRIB_EMPLRS_CNT: How many employers paid into the plan. Mostly blank, and nearly always 0 where filled.
cols.TYPE_PENSION_BNFT_CODE: The pension plan's features, as two-character codes run together, like 2E2G2R3D. The codes need a lookup.
cols.TYPE_WELFARE_BNFT_CODE: The health and welfare benefits offered, as two-character codes run together, like 4A4B4D. Mostly blank; the codes need a lookup.
cols.FUNDING_INSURANCE_IND: 1 if the plan's money is held with an insurance company, 0 if not.
cols.FUNDING_SEC412_IND: 1 if the plan is funded with section 412 insurance contracts, 0 if not.
cols.FUNDING_TRUST_IND: 1 if the plan's money is held in a trust, 0 if not.
cols.FUNDING_GEN_ASSET_IND: 1 if the plan is paid from the employer's general funds, 0 if not.
cols.BENEFIT_INSURANCE_IND: 1 if benefits are paid through an insurance company, 0 if not.
cols.BENEFIT_SEC412_IND: 1 if benefits are paid through section 412 insurance contracts, 0 if not.
cols.BENEFIT_TRUST_IND: 1 if benefits are paid from a trust, 0 if not.
cols.BENEFIT_GEN_ASSET_IND: 1 if benefits are paid from the employer's general funds, 0 if not.
cols.SCH_R_ATTACHED_IND: 1 if Schedule R is attached to the filing, 0 if not.
cols.SCH_MB_ATTACHED_IND: 1 if Schedule MB is attached to the filing, 0 if not.
cols.SCH_SB_ATTACHED_IND: 1 if Schedule SB is attached to the filing, 0 if not.
cols.SCH_H_ATTACHED_IND: 1 if Schedule H is attached to the filing, 0 if not.
cols.SCH_I_ATTACHED_IND: 1 if Schedule I is attached to the filing, 0 if not.
cols.SCH_A_ATTACHED_IND: 1 if Schedule A is attached to the filing, 0 if not.
cols.NUM_SCH_A_ATTACHED_CNT: Meant for how many Schedule A forms are attached. Empty in this table.
cols.SCH_C_ATTACHED_IND: 1 if Schedule C is attached to the filing, 0 if not.
cols.SCH_D_ATTACHED_IND: 1 if Schedule D is attached to the filing, 0 if not.
cols.SCH_G_ATTACHED_IND: 1 if Schedule G is attached to the filing, 0 if not.
cols.VALID_ADMIN_SIGNATURE: Whether the administrator's e-signature checked out. Every filled row says it was valid.
cols.VALID_DFE_SIGNATURE: Whether a pooled fund's e-signature checked out. Filled on 488 rows; one was not valid.
cols.VALID_SPONSOR_SIGNATURE: Whether the sponsor's e-signature checked out. Filled on about 9% of rows; 5 were not valid.
cols.ADMIN_PHONE_NUM_FOREIGN: The administrator's phone number outside the US. Filled on 22 rows, all one Indian number.
cols.SPONS_DFE_PHONE_NUM_FOREIGN: The sponsor's phone number outside the US, stored as a number. Filled on 183 rows.
cols.ADMIN_NAME_SAME_SPON_IND: 1 when the plan administrator is the sponsor itself. Every filled row says 1.
cols.ADMIN_ADDRESS_SAME_SPON_IND: Meant for a flag for whether the administrator's address matches the sponsor's. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_NAME: Meant for the name of whoever prepared the filing. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_FIRM_NAME: Meant for the preparer's firm. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_US_ADDRESS1: Meant for the preparer's street address. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_US_ADDRESS2: Meant for the second line of the preparer's address. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_US_CITY: Meant for the preparer's city. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_US_STATE: Meant for the preparer's state. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_US_ZIP: Meant for the preparer's ZIP code. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_FOREIGN_ADDRESS1: Meant for the preparer's street outside the US. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_FOREIGN_ADDRESS2: Meant for the second line of the preparer's foreign address. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_FOREIGN_CITY: Meant for the preparer's city outside the US. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_FOREIGN_PROV_STATE: Meant for the preparer's province outside the US. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_FOREIGN_CNTRY: Meant for the preparer's country outside the US. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_FOREIGN_POSTAL_CD: Meant for the preparer's foreign postal code. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_PHONE_NUM: Meant for the preparer's phone number. Empty in this table.
cols.PREPARER_PHONE_NUM_FOREIGN: Meant for the preparer's phone number outside the US. Empty in this table.
cols.TOT_ACT_PARTCP_BOY_CNT: How many working employees were in the plan at the start of the year.
cols.SUBJ_M1_FILING_REQ_IND: Whether the plan must also file Form M-1, as 1 or 2; 2 on almost every filled row. The codes need a lookup.
cols.COMPLIANCE_M1_FILING_REQ_IND: Whether the plan kept up with its Form M-1 filing, as 1 or 2. Filled on about 5% of rows; the codes need a lookup.
cols.M1_RECEIPT_CONFIRMATION_CODE: The receipt number for the plan's Form M-1. Filled on 136 rows, some holding 0 as a placeholder.
cols.ADMIN_MANUAL_SIGNED_DATE: When the administrator signed by hand-entered signature, with time and zone, stored as text. Filled on about 30% of rows.
cols.ADMIN_MANUAL_SIGNED_NAME: The person who hand-signed for the administrator. Filled on about 30% of rows.
cols.LAST_RPT_PLAN_NAME: The plan's name on its last filing, if it has changed. Filled on under 3% of rows.
cols.SPONS_MANUAL_SIGNED_DATE: When someone hand-signed for the sponsor, stored as text. Filled on about 3% of rows.
cols.SPONS_MANUAL_SIGNED_NAME: The person who hand-signed for the sponsor. Filled on about 3% of rows.
cols.DFE_MANUAL_SIGNED_DATE: When someone hand-signed for a pooled fund, stored as text. Filled on 40 rows.
cols.DFE_MANUAL_SIGNED_NAME: The person who hand-signed for a pooled fund. Filled on 43 rows.
cols.ADOPTED_PLAN_PERM_SEC_ACT: 1 if the plan adopted a SECURE Act change, 0 if not; 1 on only 17 rows.
cols.PARTCP_ACCOUNT_BAL_CNT_BOY: How many people had money in their own plan account at the start of the year. Mostly blank.
cols.SCH_DCG_ATTACHED_IND: 1 if Schedule DCG is attached, 0 if not.
cols.NUM_SCH_DCG_ATTACHED_CNT: How many Schedule DCG forms are attached. Filled on 340 rows, mostly 0.
cols.SCH_MEP_ATTACHED_IND: 1 if Schedule MEP is attached, 0 if not.

ECONOMICS__FED_DOL_FORM5500.summary: Annual Form 5500 reports that employers filed with the Labor Department for their pension and health benefit plans, mostly for plan year 2025.
ECONOMICS__FED_DOL_FORM5500.row: One filing: one benefit plan's yearly report from one employer or sponsor.

cols.SITE_ADDRESS: The street address of the site, like the workplace OSHA inspected or the health center's clinic.
cols.SITE_STATE: The state where the site is, as two letters.
cols.SIC_CODE: The four-digit industry code, like 2834 for drug makers. Kept as text so leading zeros like 0783 survive.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The industry code, usually six digits like 722110, which needs a lookup to read. Some tables hold shorter codes like 5416, the OSHA inspections table fills most rows with 000000, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.MAIL_STREET: The mailing street address, in capitals, often a P.O. box.
cols.MAIL_CITY: The city of the mailing address.
cols.MAIL_STATE: The state of the mailing address, as two letters.
cols.MAIL_ZIP: The mailing zip code, 5 digits as text so leading zeros stay. 00000 shows up as a fake value.
cols.OPEN_DATE: The date the case was opened: a NHTSA safety investigation or an OSHA workplace inspection.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.ACTIVITY_NR: OSHA's number for the inspection. Each row has its own. Use it to join to citation and violation tables.
cols.REPORTING_ID: The code of the OSHA office that did the inspection. The codes need a lookup.
cols.STATE_FLAG: A flag for inspections done by a state-run safety program. Empty in this table.
cols.ESTAB_NAME: The name of the business inspected. The same business can appear under slightly different spellings.
cols.SITE_ZIP: The ZIP code of the work site inspected.
cols.OWNER_TYPE: A one-letter code for who owns the business, A through D. The codes need a lookup.
cols.OWNER_CODE: A four-digit code for the owner. Mostly the placeholder 0000; the other codes need a lookup.
cols.ADV_NOTICE: Y if the employer was told about the inspection ahead of time.
cols.SAFETY_HLTH: S for a safety inspection, H for a health inspection.
cols.INSP_TYPE: A one-letter code for why OSHA came. The codes need a lookup.
cols.INSP_SCOPE: A one-letter code for how much of the workplace was inspected, A through D. The codes need a lookup.
cols.WHY_NO_INSP: A one-letter code for why no inspection happened after all. The codes need a lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.UNION_STATUS: A one-letter code for whether workers had a union, like Y, N, A or B. The codes need a lookup.
cols.SAFETY_MANUF: X if this was a safety inspection in manufacturing. Mostly blank.
cols.SAFETY_CONST: X if this was a safety inspection in construction. Mostly blank.
cols.SAFETY_MARIT: X if this was a safety inspection in shipyards or on the waterfront. Mostly blank.
cols.HEALTH_MANUF: X if this was a health inspection in manufacturing. Mostly blank.
cols.HEALTH_CONST: X if this was a health inspection in construction. Mostly blank.
cols.HEALTH_MARIT: X if this was a health inspection in shipyards or on the waterfront. Mostly blank.
cols.MIGRANT: X if the inspection involved migrant farm workers. Mostly blank.
cols.HOST_EST_KEY: A key for the host business when workers were at another company's site. Placeholders like HOST_EST_KEY_VALUE and 000000000 are common.
cols.NR_IN_ESTAB: How many workers were at the workplace.
cols.CASE_MOD_DATE: When the case record was last changed. Blank on about half of rows.
cols.CLOSE_CONF_DATE: The day of the closing meeting with the employer at the end of the inspection.
cols.CLOSE_CASE_DATE: The day OSHA closed the case.
cols.LOAD_DT: The day OSHA loaded this record into its public data.

ECONOMICS__FED_DOL_OSHA_INSPECTIONS.summary: Decades of workplace safety and health inspections by OSHA, the federal job safety agency, with the business inspected, why, and when the case closed.
ECONOMICS__FED_DOL_OSHA_INSPECTIONS.row: One inspection: one OSHA visit to one workplace.

cols.REPORT_ID: The ID of one report or filing. One table holds N/A instead.
cols.AUDITEE_UEI: The audited group's federal UEI number. GSA_MIGRATION fills more than half the rows instead of a real number.
cols.AUDITEE_EIN: The audited group's tax ID number.
cols.AUDITEE_NAME: The name of the group that got federal money and was audited.
cols.AUDITEE_STATE: The audited group's state, as two letters.
cols.AUDITOR_EIN: The audit firm's tax ID number.
cols.AUDITOR_FIRM_NAME: The audit firm, like CLIFTONLARSONALLEN LLP. The same firm can be spelled in different cases.
cols.AUDITOR_STATE: The audit firm's state, as two letters.
cols.AUDITOR_ZIP: The audit firm's ZIP code, as five or nine digits.
cols.ENTITY_TYPE: What kind of group was audited: non-profit, local, higher-ed, state, tribal or unknown.
cols.AUDIT_TYPE: single-audit for almost all, else program-specific. A few say GSA_MIGRATION.
cols.GAAP_RESULTS: The auditor's opinion on the books, like unmodified_opinion or adverse_opinion. Some rows list several, with and without spaces.
cols.IS_GOING_CONCERN_INCLUDED: Yes if the auditor doubted the group could keep going. A few say GSA_MIGRATION.
cols.IS_INTERNAL_CONTROL_MATERIAL_WEAKNESS_DI: Yes if the auditor found a serious weakness in money controls. A few say GSA_MIGRATION.
cols.IS_MATERIAL_NONCOMPLIANCE_DISCLOSED: Yes if the auditor found the group seriously broke the rules. A few say GSA_MIGRATION.
cols.TOTAL_AMOUNT_EXPENDED: Total federal dollars the group spent that year.
cols.IS_LOW_RISK_AUDITEE: Yes if the group counts as low risk. A few say GSA_MIGRATION.
cols.OVERSIGHT_AGENCY: The federal agency overseeing the audit, as a two-digit code like 84 or 14. Needs a lookup.
cols.COGNIZANT_AGENCY: The lead federal agency for big spenders, as a two-digit code. Needs a lookup and is blank on almost every row.
cols.FY_START_DATE: The first day of the group's fiscal year.
cols.FY_END_DATE: The last day of the group's fiscal year.
cols.FAC_ACCEPTED_DATE: The date the Federal Audit Clearinghouse accepted the report.
cols.DATA_SOURCE: Which system the record came from: CENSUS for the older one or GSAFAC for the newer one.

ECONOMICS__FED_FAC_SINGLE_AUDIT.summary: Yearly audits of cities, nonprofits, schools and tribes that spent federal money, from the Federal Audit Clearinghouse.
ECONOMICS__FED_FAC_SINGLE_AUDIT.row: One audit report: one group, one fiscal year, the audit firm, and what the auditor found.

cols.FDIC_CERT: The FDIC's certificate number for a bank, like 30965. Use it to join bank tables. Blank for some failed banks.
cols.FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 06037. One table holds two-digit state codes instead, and nine tables leave it empty.
cols.BANK_NAME: The bank's name, like FAIRFIELD STATE BANK. Capitals in one table, mixed case in the other.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_ABBR: The state, as two letters like TX. Territories like PR and GU show up, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.

cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Fillers like 00000, UNKNO or a lone dash show up, some codes lost a leading zero like 8721, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.SUBSECTION: The IRS 501c subsection as two digits, like 03 for a regular 501c3 charity. Empty in the court table.
cols.AFFILIATION: Whether the nonprofit stands alone or is part of a group, like a central office or a chapter, as a one-digit IRS code. Needs a lookup.
cols.RULING: The year and month the IRS granted the tax exemption, as six digits like 201611 for November 2016. Stored as text.
cols.DEDUCTIBILITY: Whether gifts to the nonprofit are tax-deductible, as an IRS code like 0, 1, 2 or 4. Needs a lookup.
cols.TAX_PERIOD: The month the nonprofit's tax year ended, written year then month, like 202412 for December 2024.
cols.ASSET_CD: The nonprofit's total assets as a size band, a one-digit IRS code from 0 to 9. Higher means bigger. Needs a lookup for the dollar ranges.
cols.INCOME_CD: The nonprofit's yearly income as a size band, a one-digit IRS code from 0 to 9. Higher means bigger. Needs a lookup for the dollar ranges.
cols.FILING_REQ_CD: Which yearly tax form the nonprofit must file, as a two-digit IRS code like 01 or 06. Needs a lookup.
cols.PF_FILING_REQ_CD: Whether the nonprofit must file the private foundation tax form: 1 yes, 0 no.
cols.ACCT_PD: The month the nonprofit's financial year ends, as two digits like 12 for December.
cols.ASSET_AMT: The nonprofit's total assets in dollars, from its latest filing. Zero often means not reported, and one table stores it as text.
cols.INCOME_AMT: The nonprofit's total income in dollars, from its latest filing. Zero often means not reported, and one table stores it as text.
cols.REVENUE_AMT: The nonprofit's total yearly revenue in dollars, from its latest filing. Zero often means not reported, and one table stores it as text.
cols.NTEE_CD: The nonprofit's category by mission, a letter plus digits like X20 or P33. The letter is the broad field. Needs a lookup; often blank.
cols.SORT_NAME: A second name line the IRS keeps for the nonprofit, often a chapter or local number. Blank for most rows.
cols.C_GROUP: Group exemption number, four digits; 0000 on most rows. The codes need a lookup.
cols.CLASSIFICATION: The IRS classification code, like 1000 or 2000. The codes need a lookup.
cols.FOUNDATION: Foundation status code, two digits like 15 or 16. The codes need a lookup.
cols.ACTIVITY: Activity codes, nine digits; 000000000 on most rows, a blank placeholder. The codes need a lookup.
cols.C_ORGANIZATION: Type of organization, as one digit like 1 or 5. The codes need a lookup.
cols.STATUS: Exempt status code; 01 on almost every row. The codes need a lookup.

ECONOMICS__FED_IRS_SOI_CHARITIES.summary: A 2,450-row extract of the IRS master list of tax-exempt organizations, with each group's address, finances and status codes.

cols.DATA_YEAR: The year the data covers, like 2024. One table runs into future years like 2032.
cols.PUBLICATION_DATE: The date the item was published. Three tables leave it empty.
cols.PROGRAM_TYPE: Which HUD loan program the apartment deal ran under, like Basic FHA or Risk Sharing. Empty in the PBGC table.
cols.TABLE_NAME: The name of the source table or report page the row came from, like S-52 or tri.tri_facility. Empty in the two DHS immigration tables.
cols.METRIC_NAME: The label for the number in METRIC_VALUE, pulled out of a spreadsheet. Messy: states, years, percent bands, even column headers like Name.
cols.METRIC_VALUE: The number that goes with METRIC_NAME. Mixes counts, dollars and fractions, so check the label before adding them up; almost always blank in the prison statistics table.
cols.UNIT: The unit the number is measured in, like %, GW, TWh or deaths per 100,000. One table writes percent as PC, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.SOURCE_FILE: The file or link the row was loaded from, like FARA_All_Registrants.csv or a quarter like 2024q2.
cols.NOTES_FLAG: A flag for footnotes on the figure. Empty in this table.

ECONOMICS__FED_PBGC_DATA.summary: Statistics from the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation, the federal pension insurer, stored one number per row.
ECONOMICS__FED_PBGC_DATA.row: One figure: one number, with its year, source table and measure name. The program and unit columns are empty, so the unit is not stated.

cols.PLAN_NAME: The name of the employee pension or benefit plan, like a company's 401K plan.
cols.EIN: The organization's 9-digit federal tax ID number, stored as text. Some rows hold 000000000 as a filler or only 8 digits because a leading zero was lost, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.ADMIN_CITY: The city of the plan's administrator.
cols.ADMIN_STATE: The state of the plan's administrator, as two letters.
cols.PLAN_SPONSOR_NAME: The company or employer that set up the plan.
cols.CONTACT_PHONE_NUMBER: A contact phone number for the plan, as ten digits. Some numbers are shared by plan administration firms.
cols.PLAN_EFFECTIVE_DATE: The day the plan started. Many start on January 1.
cols.PLAN_ID: PBGC's ID for the plan. Nearly every plan has its own.
cols.PN: The plan number within the sponsoring company, three digits like 001 or 002. Pair it with the company's tax ID to name one plan.
cols.PARTICIPANT_COUNT: How many people are in the plan. Small plans with 2 to 9 people are the most common values, about 4 in 10 rows.

ECONOMICS__FED_PBGC_TRUSTEED_PENSION_PLA.summary: About 21,600 pension plans from the federal pension insurer PBGC's trusteed-plans file, with the company behind each plan, a contact number and how many people are in it.
ECONOMICS__FED_PBGC_TRUSTEED_PENSION_PLA.row: One pension plan: one company's plan, its start date, its administrator's city and its number of participants.

cols.BORROWER_NAME: The name of the business that got the SBA loan.
cols.BORROWER_CITY: The borrower's city, in capitals in the SBA loans table and mixed case in PPP, so New York and NEW YORK both show up.
cols.BORROWER_STATE: The borrower's state, as two letters.
cols.BORROWER_ZIP: The borrower's zip code as text. Sometimes 5 digits, sometimes 9 with a dash like 60007-6035; some SBA loan rows show only 4 digits like 6614, likely a lost leading zero.
cols.PROJECT_COUNTY: The county where the loan money is used, in capitals like MARICOPA.
cols.PROJECT_STATE: The state where the loan's project or business is, as two letters.
cols.CONGRESSIONAL_DISTRICT: The congressional district, written differently per table: a bare number like 05, a state plus number like NJ-11 or AZ3, or a full phrase like Oklahoma, Congressional District 1.
cols.LENDER_NAME: The name of the bank or company that made the loan. Almost always blank in the SBA loans table.
cols.APPROVAL_DATE: The date the loan or the drug was approved.
cols.TERM_MONTHS: How many months the borrower has to pay the loan back, like 120 for ten years.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The industry code, usually six digits like 722110, which needs a lookup to read. Some tables hold shorter codes like 5416, the OSHA inspections table fills most rows with 000000, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.NAICS_DESCRIPTION: The industry in words, like Full-Service Restaurants, matching the NAICS code. One table leaves it empty.
cols.BUSINESS_AGE: How old the business was when it got the loan, in words like Existing, 5 or more years. Unanswered shows up often; the two tables use different bands.
cols.LOAN_STATUS: Where the loan stands now. SBA loans use short codes like P I F paid in full, CHGOFF charged off, CURR current; PPP spells it out, like Paid in Full, and also shows Exemption 4.
cols.SUBPROGRAM: The specific loan product, like Guaranty or the FA$TRK Small Loan Express.
cols.CDC_NAME: The nonprofit development company that made a 504 loan. Blank on 7A loans.
cols.CDC_STATE: The state of that development company, as two letters. Blank on 7A loans.
cols.LENDER_STATE: The state of the bank or lender, as two letters. Mostly blank.
cols.THIRD_PARTY_DOLLARS: Money a bank put into a 504 deal alongside the SBA loan, in dollars. Mostly blank.
cols.GROSS_APPROVAL_AMOUNT: The loan amount approved, in dollars. Use this column to add up lending.
cols.APPROVAL_FISCAL_YEAR: The federal budget year the loan was approved, like 2007.
cols.FIRST_DISBURSEMENT_DATE: When the loan money first went out. Month-end dates in the mid-1990s cluster heavily.
cols.BUSINESS_TYPE: How the borrower is set up: CORPORATION, INDIVIDUAL or PARTNERSHIP.
cols.PAID_IN_FULL_DATE: When the loan was paid off. Two 2005 dates show up far more than any others and may be a bulk fill, not real payoff days.
cols.CHARGEOFF_DATE: When the lender wrote the loan off as lost. Blank for most loans.
cols.GROSS_CHARGEOFF_AMOUNT: How much of the loan was written off as lost, in dollars. 0 for most loans.
cols.JOBS_SUPPORTED: How many jobs the borrower said the loan would support. 0 is common.
cols.IS_DEFAULTED: True when the loan defaulted. Only true or blank, so blank does not prove the loan was fine.
cols.LOSS_RATE: The share of the loan that was lost, from 0 to 1. Blank for most loans.

ECONOMICS__FED_SBA_LOANS.summary: Small business loans backed by the Small Business Administration through its 7A and 504 programs, with amounts, jobs supported, and whether the loan was paid off or charged off.
ECONOMICS__FED_SBA_LOANS.row: One SBA-backed loan: one business, one approval.

cols.BORROWER_STATE: The borrower's state, as two letters.
cols.BORROWER_ZIP: The borrower's zip code as text. Sometimes 5 digits, sometimes 9 with a dash like 60007-6035; some SBA loan rows show only 4 digits like 6614, likely a lost leading zero.
cols.LOAN_STATUS: Where the loan stands now. SBA loans use short codes like P I F paid in full, CHGOFF charged off, CURR current; PPP spells it out, like Paid in Full, and also shows Exemption 4.
cols.TERM_MONTHS: How many months the borrower has to pay the loan back, like 120 for ten years.
cols.BUSINESS_AGE: How old the business was when it got the loan, in words like Existing, 5 or more years. Unanswered shows up often; the two tables use different bands.

cols.UTILITIES_PROCEED: Dollars of the PPP loan the borrower said would go to utilities. Often blank; a value of 1 shows up as a placeholder. Text in the big-loans table.
cols.MORTGAGE_INTEREST_PROCEED: Dollars of the PPP loan the borrower said would go to mortgage interest. Mostly blank; text in the big-loans table.

cols.LOAN_STATUS_DATE: Date the loan's current status was set.
cols.INITIAL_APPROVAL_AMOUNT: Dollar amount first approved for the loan.
cols.CURRENT_APPROVAL_AMOUNT: Dollar amount approved now, after any changes.
cols.UNDISBURSED_AMOUNT: Dollars approved but not yet paid out; 0 on every row but one.
cols.SERVICING_LENDER_NAME: The bank handling the loan, like JPMorgan Chase Bank.

cols.LMI_INDICATOR: Y or N: whether the business is in a low-to-moderate income area.
cols.JOBS_REPORTED: How many jobs the business said the loan would support.
cols.TOTAL_PROCEEDS_USED: Total dollars the business reported spending from the loan.
cols.IS_RESOLVED: A true-false flag that is false on every row, so it tells you nothing.

ECONOMICS__FED_SBA_PPP.summary: Paycheck Protection Program loans from the Small Business Administration, 2020 to 2021. Holds 968,524 loans, far fewer than the full program, so treat it as a subset.

cols.RACE: The person's race as the source recorded it: spelled out like White or Asian, or as short codes like W, B or mena that need a lookup. Many rows say Unknown or Unanswered.
cols.ETHNICITY: Whether the person is Hispanic or Latino, in words. Unknown or not-stated values are common.
cols.UTILITIES_PROCEED: Dollars of the PPP loan the borrower said would go to utilities. Often blank; a value of 1 shows up as a placeholder. Text in the big-loans table.
cols.PAYROLL_PROCEED: Dollars of the PPP loan the borrower said would go to payroll. Stored as text in the big-loans table.
cols.MORTGAGE_INTEREST_PROCEED: Dollars of the PPP loan the borrower said would go to mortgage interest. Mostly blank; text in the big-loans table.
cols.RENT_PROCEED: Dollars of the PPP loan the borrower said would go to rent. Mostly blank; text in the big-loans table.
cols.GENDER: The person's sex, written differently by table: Male or Female, M or F, m or f, or Male Owned for businesses. Some rows say Unknown or Unanswered, the clinical trials table mostly says ALL, and one table leaves it empty.

cols.DATEAPPROVED: The date the SBA approved the loan, stored as text like 05/01/2020.
cols.SBAOFFICECODE: The four-digit code of the SBA office that handled the loan. It needs a lookup.
cols.PROCESSINGMETHOD: Which loan program round the loan came through: PPP or PPS. The codes need a lookup.
cols.BORROWERNAME: The name of the business or nonprofit that got the loan.
cols.BORROWERCITY: The borrower's city. Capitals vary, so New York and NEW YORK both appear.
cols.BORROWERSTATE: The borrower's state, as two letters.
cols.BORROWERZIP: The borrower's ZIP code, sometimes with the four-digit extension like 15317-3246.
cols.LOANSTATUSDATE: The date the loan reached its current status, stored as text like 01/21/2021.
cols.LOANSTATUS: Where the loan stands: Paid in Full, Charged Off, or Exemption 4, a label that needs a lookup.
cols.TERM: The loan's length in months, stored as text. Mostly 24 or 60.
cols.SBAGUARANTYPERCENTAGE: The share of the loan the SBA guaranteed. Every row is 100.
cols.INITIALAPPROVALAMOUNT: The loan amount first approved, in dollars.
cols.CURRENTAPPROVALAMOUNT: The loan amount approved now, in dollars, after any changes. Use this column for the loan's size.
cols.UNDISBURSEDAMOUNT: Loan money approved but not paid out, in dollars. 0 for all but one loan.
cols.FRANCHISENAME: The franchise brand, like McDonalds or Subway, when the borrower is a franchise. Almost always blank.
cols.SERVICINGLENDERLOCATIONID: The SBA's ID for the bank branch servicing the loan.
cols.SERVICINGLENDERNAME: The bank servicing the loan now, like JPMorgan Chase Bank.
cols.SERVICINGLENDERADDRESS: The street address of the bank servicing the loan.
cols.SERVICINGLENDERCITY: The city of the bank servicing the loan.
cols.SERVICINGLENDERSTATE: The state of the bank servicing the loan, as two letters.
cols.SERVICINGLENDERZIP: The ZIP code of the bank servicing the loan.
cols.RURALURBANINDICATOR: U if the borrower is in an urban area, R if rural.
cols.HUBZONEINDICATOR: Y if the borrower is in a federal HUBZone, a low-income area favored for contracts.
cols.LMIINDICATOR: Y if the borrower is in a low- or moderate-income area.
cols.BUSINESSAGEDESCRIPTION: How old the business was, like Existing or more than 2 years old, or New Business. Some say Unanswered.
cols.PROJECTCITY: The city where the loan money was used. Capitals vary.
cols.PROJECTCOUNTYNAME: The county where the loan money was used, in capitals.
cols.PROJECTSTATE: The state where the loan money was used, as two letters.
cols.PROJECTZIP: The ZIP code where the loan money was used, often with the four-digit extension.
cols.CD: The congressional district where the loan money was used, like NY-12.
cols.JOBSREPORTED: How many jobs the borrower said the loan would keep, stored as text.
cols.NAICSCODE: The borrower's six-digit industry code, like 722511. The codes need a lookup; blank for under 1% of loans.
cols.REFINANCE_EIDL_PROCEED: Dollars used to pay off an earlier SBA disaster loan, stored as text. Almost always blank, and mostly 0 when filled.
cols.HEALTH_CARE_PROCEED: Dollars the borrower said went to employee health care, stored as text. Almost always blank.
cols.DEBT_INTEREST_PROCEED: Dollars the borrower said went to interest on other debt, stored as text. Almost always blank.
cols.BUSINESSTYPE: The borrower's legal form, like Corporation, LLC or Non-Profit Organization.
cols.ORIGINATINGLENDERLOCATIONID: The SBA's ID for the bank branch that made the loan.
cols.ORIGINATINGLENDER: The bank that made the loan, which can differ from the one servicing it now.
cols.ORIGINATINGLENDERCITY: The city of the bank that made the loan.
cols.ORIGINATINGLENDERSTATE: The state of the bank that made the loan, as two letters.
cols.VETERAN: Whether the owner is a veteran. Two thirds say Unanswered.
cols.NONPROFIT: Y if the borrower is a nonprofit. Blank for everyone else.
cols.FORGIVENESSAMOUNT: How many dollars of the loan were forgiven. Blank for about 25,000 loans.
cols.FORGIVENESSDATE: The date the loan was forgiven, stored as text like 11/03/2020.
