cols.PCT_DEBT_HELD_PUBLIC: The share of the debt held by the public, as a percent like 80.3. Blank for about a third of the days.
cols.PCT_INTRAGOV_HOLD: The share of the debt the government owes itself, as a percent like 19.7. Blank for about a third of the days.

ECONOMICS__FED_TREASURY_DEBT_TO_PENNY.summary: The U.S. national debt to the penny, one row per business day, split between debt the public holds and debt one part of the government owes another.
ECONOMICS__FED_TREASURY_DEBT_TO_PENNY.row: One day: the national debt as of one date.

cols.RECORD_DATE: The date the figure or record is as of, like the end of a month or day. Mostly Treasury tables plus one procurement table, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.TABLE_NBR: Which numbered table in the Treasury statement the row came from, like II or 4.
cols.SRC_LINE_NBR: The line number of this row in the original Treasury report.
cols.RECORD_FISCAL_YEAR: The federal budget year of the record, like 2025, which starts in October.
cols.RECORD_FISCAL_QUARTER: The quarter of the federal budget year, 1 to 4, stored as text.
cols.RECORD_CALENDAR_YEAR: The calendar year of the record, like 2025.
cols.RECORD_CALENDAR_QUARTER: The calendar quarter of the record, 1 to 4, stored as text.
cols.RECORD_CALENDAR_MONTH: The calendar month of the record, as two-digit text like 01 for January.
cols.RECORD_CALENDAR_DAY: The day of the month of the record, as two-digit text like 01.
cols.ACCOUNT_TYPE: Which Treasury account, like Federal Reserve Account or Treasury General Account.
cols.TRANSACTION_CATG: Category, like Justice Department programs or Deposits by States.
cols.TRANSACTION_CATG_DESC: More detail on the category, like Medicare Premiums. Mostly blank.
cols.TRANSACTION_TODAY_AMT: Amount on that day; small whole numbers suggest millions of dollars.
cols.TRANSACTION_MTD_AMT: Amount so far this month, same units as the daily amount.
cols.TRANSACTION_FYTD_AMT: Amount so far this fiscal year, same units as the daily amount.
cols.TABLE_NM: Name of the statement table; Deposits and Withdrawals of Operating Cash on every row.

ECONOMICS__FED_TREASURY_DTS_DEPOSITS.summary: Daily cash going into and out of the US Treasury's operating accounts, by category, from the Daily Treasury Statement, 478,149 lines.
ECONOMICS__FED_TREASURY_DTS_DEPOSITS.row: One statement line: one deposit or withdrawal category on one day.

cols.RECORD_DATE: The date the figure or record is as of, like the end of a month or day. Mostly Treasury tables plus one procurement table, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.TABLE_NBR: Which numbered table in the Treasury statement the row came from, like II or 4.
cols.SRC_LINE_NBR: The line number of this row in the original Treasury report.
cols.RECORD_FISCAL_YEAR: The federal budget year of the record, like 2025, which starts in October.
cols.RECORD_FISCAL_QUARTER: The quarter of the federal budget year, 1 to 4, stored as text.
cols.RECORD_CALENDAR_YEAR: The calendar year of the record, like 2025.
cols.RECORD_CALENDAR_QUARTER: The calendar quarter of the record, 1 to 4, stored as text.
cols.RECORD_CALENDAR_MONTH: The calendar month of the record, as two-digit text like 01 for January.
cols.RECORD_CALENDAR_DAY: The day of the month of the record, as two-digit text like 01.
cols.PARENT_ID: The ID of the line this one sits under in the table's outline. Blank for top-level lines.
cols.CLASSIFICATION_ID: The Treasury's ID for this line of the receipts table.
cols.CLASSIFICATION_DESC: What the line counts, like Federal Insurance Contributions Act Taxes or Estate and Gift Taxes.
cols.CURRENT_MONTH_GROSS_RCPT_AMT: Money taken in this month before refunds, in dollars. Blank for some lines.
cols.CURRENT_MONTH_REFUND_AMT: Refunds paid out this month, in dollars. Blank for most lines.
cols.CURRENT_MONTH_NET_RCPT_AMT: Money taken in this month after refunds, in dollars. Use this column for monthly totals; blank for some lines.
cols.CURRENT_FYTD_GROSS_RCPT_AMT: Money taken in so far this fiscal year before refunds, in dollars.
cols.CURRENT_FYTD_REFUND_AMT: Refunds paid so far this fiscal year, in dollars. Blank for most lines.
cols.CURRENT_FYTD_NET_RCPT_AMT: Money taken in so far this fiscal year after refunds, in dollars.
cols.PRIOR_FYTD_GROSS_RCPT_AMT: Money taken in by the same point last fiscal year before refunds, in dollars.
cols.PRIOR_FYTD_REFUND_AMT: Refunds paid by the same point last fiscal year, in dollars. Blank for most lines.
cols.PRIOR_FYTD_NET_RCPT_AMT: Money taken in by the same point last fiscal year after refunds, in dollars.
cols.PRINT_ORDER_NBR: The order the line prints in the published table.
cols.LINE_CODE_NBR: The Treasury's code number for the line.
cols.DATA_TYPE_CD: A one-letter code for the kind of line: D, T or S. The codes need a lookup.
cols.RECORD_TYPE_CD: A short code for the kind of record: RSG, SRS or SL. The codes need a lookup.
cols.SEQUENCE_LEVEL_NBR: How deep the line sits in the table's outline, from 1 to 4.

ECONOMICS__FED_TREASURY_MTS_RECEIPTS.summary: Money the federal government took in, month by month, from the Treasury's Monthly Treasury Statement: taxes and other receipts by type, with refunds and year-to-date totals.
ECONOMICS__FED_TREASURY_MTS_RECEIPTS.row: One receipt line: one line of the Treasury's receipts table, like payroll taxes, in one monthly statement.

cols.MODIFICATION_NUMBER: Which change to the award this row is, with 0 for the original. Formats are messy: 0, 0000 and P00003 all appear.
cols.FEDERAL_ACTION_OBLIGATION: The dollars the government committed or took back in this one transaction. Negative numbers are cuts or cancellations.
cols.TOTAL_OUTLAYED_AMOUNT_FOR_OVERALL_AWARD: Total dollars actually paid out on the whole award so far. Mostly blank, and 0 is common.
cols.DISASTER_EMERGENCY_FUND_CODES_FOR_OVERAL: Which emergency spending law funded the award, as a code plus words, like Q: Not Designated or Z: Emergency P.L. 117-58. Some rows list several codes, and it is mostly blank.
cols.OUTLAYED_AMOUNT_FROM_COVID_19_SUPPLEMENT: Dollars paid out on the award from COVID-19 relief money. Nearly always blank.
cols.OBLIGATED_AMOUNT_FROM_COVID_19_SUPPLEMEN: Dollars promised to the award from COVID-19 relief money. Nearly always blank, and can be negative after a cut.
cols.OUTLAYED_AMOUNT_FROM_IIJA_SUPPLEMENTAL_F: Dollars paid out on the award from the 2021 infrastructure law money. Nearly always blank.
cols.OBLIGATED_AMOUNT_FROM_IIJA_SUPPLEMENTAL_: Dollars promised to the award from the 2021 infrastructure law money. Nearly always blank.
cols.ACTION_DATE: The date of the award action, like a new contract or a change to one. Two tables store it as text.
cols.ACTION_DATE_FISCAL_YEAR: The federal fiscal year of the transaction, like 2007. Federal fiscal years start October 1.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_START_DATE: The date the work or grant was set to begin. Some tables store it as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_CURRENT_END_DATE: The date the work or grant is currently set to end, which can be in the future. Some tables store it as text.
cols.AWARDING_AGENCY_CODE: The three-digit code for the federal department that made the award, like 036. Stored as text to keep the leading zero.
cols.AWARDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency that made the award, like Department of Defense.
cols.AWARDING_SUB_AGENCY_CODE: The four-character code for the office inside the department that made the award, like 3600. Some contain letters, like 12K3.
cols.AWARDING_SUB_AGENCY_NAME: The office inside the agency that gave the award, like Department of the Navy or National Park Service.
cols.AWARDING_OFFICE_CODE: The code for the office that made the award, like 47QSSC or 12346T. Nearly a third of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.AWARDING_OFFICE_NAME: The name of the office that made the award, like DLA TROOP SUPPORT. Nearly a third of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_AGENCY_CODE: The three-digit code for the federal department paying for the award, like 047. About a quarter of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency whose money paid for the award. Can differ from the agency that made it.
cols.FUNDING_SUB_AGENCY_CODE: The four-character code for the office inside the department paying for the award, like 7300 or 97AS. About a quarter of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_SUB_AGENCY_NAME: The name of the office inside the department paying for the award, like Department of the Navy. About a quarter of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_OFFICE_CODE: The code for the office paying for the award, like 47QSSC or 12346T. Nearly a third of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_OFFICE_NAME: The name of the office paying for the award, like DLA TROOP SUPPORT. Nearly a third of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.TREASURY_ACCOUNTS_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: The Treasury accounts that paid for the award, as codes like 012-X-4336-000, several split by semicolons. About half the grant and loan rows fill it, most bulk contract rows are blank, and the full contracts table is empty.
cols.FEDERAL_ACCOUNTS_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: The federal budget accounts that paid for the award, like 073-1154, several split by semicolons. About half the grant and loan rows fill it, most bulk contract rows are blank, and the full contracts table is empty.
cols.OBJECT_CLASSES_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: What kind of spending paid for the award, as a budget category code plus words, like 26.0: Supplies and materials; some rows list several. About half the grant and loan rows fill it, and most contract rows are blank.
cols.PROGRAM_ACTIVITIES_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: The budget programs that paid for the award, as a code plus words, like 0101: FEDERAL PELL GRANTS. Mostly blank, and filler like 0000: UNKNOWN/OTHER or OPTN: FIELD IS OPTIONAL PRIOR TO FY21 shows up.
cols.RECIPIENT_UEI: The recipient's 12-character federal ID, the Unique Entity ID that replaced the DUNS number. Mostly blank in the federal assistance table and empty in one small API table.
cols.RECIPIENT_DUNS: The recipient's old 9-digit DUNS business number. Mostly blank in the federal assistance table, empty in the three newer tables, and an obvious filler like 123456787 shows up.
cols.RECIPIENT_NAME: Who received the money, like a company, agency or candidate. In the federal assistance table many rows say REDACTED or MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS instead of a name.
cols.RECIPIENT_NAME_RAW: The award recipient's name exactly as the source wrote it, not cleaned up. Grant and loan rows often hold stand-ins like REDACTED DUE TO PII or MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_UEI: The 12-character federal ID of the recipient's parent company. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_DUNS: The 9-digit DUNS number, the old business ID, of the recipient's parent company. Mostly blank in the grants table, empty in the bulk table, and the fake-looking 123456787 shows up often in contracts.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_NAME: The name of the recipient's parent company or government, in capitals. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_NAME_RAW: The name of the recipient's parent company or government, exactly as the source wrote it. Mostly blank in the grants and loans table.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTRY_CODE: The recipient's country as a three-letter code, like USA or GBR.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTRY_NAME: The country where the recipient is based, in capitals. The US shows up as both UNITED STATES and UNITED STATES OF AMERICA.
cols.RECIPIENT_ADDRESS_LINE_1: The first line of the recipient's street address.
cols.RECIPIENT_ADDRESS_LINE_2: The second line of the recipient's address, like a suite number. Mostly blank, and N/A shows up as filler.
cols.RECIPIENT_CITY_NAME: The city where the recipient is based, in capitals.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_COUNTY: The recipient's 5-digit county code, like 06037. Keep it as text for the leading zero.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTY_NAME: The recipient's county name, in capitals.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_STATE_: The recipient's state as a 2-digit code, like 06 for California. Keep it as text for the leading zero.
cols.RECIPIENT_STATE_CODE: The recipient's state, as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam appear too.
cols.RECIPIENT_STATE_NAME: The recipient's state spelled out, like MARYLAND.
cols.RECIPIENT_ZIP_CODE: The recipient's zip code, sometimes with the extra four digits after a dash. Blank in some grant rows.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_CD_ORI: The recipient's congressional district when the award was made, as state and number like MD-06.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_CD_CUR: The recipient's congressional district under today's district lines, as state and number like MD-06.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_COUNTRY_COD: The country where the work is done, as a three-letter code like USA.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_COUNTRY_NAM: The country where the work is done, spelled out, like UNITED STATES.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_CITY_NAME: The city where the work was actually done, in capitals. Can differ from where the recipient is based.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_PLACE_OF_PERFORM: The 5-digit county code where the work is done, like 06037 for Los Angeles. Keep it as text for the leading zero.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_COUNTY_NAME: The county where the work is done, in capitals.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_PLACE_OF_PERFORM: The state where the work is done, as a 2-digit code like 06 for California.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_STATE_NAME: The state where the work is done, spelled out.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_ZIP_4: The ZIP code where the work is done, often with the extra four digits, written like 600858337 or 48226-1906. Some grant rows say CITY-WIDE instead.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_PLACE_OF_PERFORM: The congressional district where the work is done, when the award was made, as state and number like IL-10.
The congressional district where the work is done, under today's district lines, like IL-10. Grant rows often show a 90 district like CA-90, which needs a lookup.
cols.CFDA_NUMBER: The federal assistance program number, like 93.778. Some rows list several, split by commas.
cols.CFDA_TITLE: The name of the federal aid program the money came from, like PAYCHECK PROTECTION LOAN PROGRAM or FEDERAL PELL GRANT PROGRAM. Empty in the USAspending API table.
cols.TRANSACTION_DESCRIPTION: A free-text note on what was bought or funded, often full of internal codes and abbreviations. Some rows just say DESCR N.A.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_BASE_TRANSACTION_DESCRIPTION: What the award is for, in the agency's own free-text words.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_1_NAME: The name of the recipient's top-paid executive. Mostly blank.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_1_AMOUNT: The yearly pay in dollars of the recipient's top-paid executive. Mostly blank, and some filled rows say 0.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_2_NAME: The name of the recipient's second top-paid executive. Mostly blank.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_2_AMOUNT: The yearly pay in dollars of the recipient's second top-paid executive. Mostly blank, and some filled rows say 0.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_3_NAME: The name of the third of the recipient's five top-paid officers.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_3_AMOUNT: Yearly pay in dollars of the third of the recipient's five top-paid officers. Mostly blank.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_4_NAME: The name of the fourth of the recipient's five top-paid officers. Mostly blank.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_4_AMOUNT: Yearly pay in dollars of the fourth of the recipient's five top-paid officers. Mostly blank.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_5_NAME: The name of the fifth of the recipient's five top-paid officers.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_5_AMOUNT: Yearly pay in dollars of the fifth of the recipient's five top-paid officers. Mostly blank.
cols.USASPENDING_PERMALINK: A web link to this award's page on usaspending.gov.
cols.INITIAL_REPORT_DATE: When the transaction was first reported to the federal spending system.
cols.LAST_MODIFIED_DATE: When the source last changed this record. Some tables add the time.
cols.ASSISTANCE_TRANSACTION_UNIQUE_KEY: The ID of this one transaction, built by gluing agency and award codes together. Each row has its own.
cols.ASSISTANCE_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY: The ID of the whole award this transaction belongs to, starting ASST_. Use it to add up all changes to one award.
cols.AWARD_ID_FAIN: The award number the agency gave the grant or loan. Sometimes blank.
cols.AWARD_ID_URI: A second award ID used for awards reported in bulk, mostly to individuals. Mostly blank.
cols.SAI_NUMBER: The state review number for the award. Almost always a placeholder like SAI EXEMPT or SAI NOT AVAILABLE, spelled many ways.
cols.TOTAL_OBLIGATED_AMOUNT: The total federal money promised on the whole award so far, in dollars. 0 is common.
cols.INDIRECT_COST_FEDERAL_SHARE_AMOUNT: The federal share of overhead costs, in dollars. Almost always blank or 0.
cols.NON_FEDERAL_FUNDING_AMOUNT: Money the recipient or others put in on this transaction, in dollars. Mostly 0 or blank.
cols.TOTAL_NON_FEDERAL_FUNDING_AMOUNT: Money the recipient or others put in across the whole award, in dollars. Mostly 0 or blank.
cols.FACE_VALUE_OF_LOAN: The loan amount on this transaction, in dollars. 0 when it is not a loan.
cols.ORIGINAL_LOAN_SUBSIDY_COST: What this loan transaction costs the government, in dollars. 0 when it is not a loan; can be negative.
cols.TOTAL_FACE_VALUE_OF_LOAN: The loan amount across the whole award, in dollars. 0 when it is not a loan.
cols.TOTAL_LOAN_SUBSIDY_COST: What the whole loan award costs the government, in dollars. 0 when it is not a loan; can be negative.
cols.GENERATED_PRAGMATIC_OBLIGATIONS: A single dollar figure for the transaction that uses the loan subsidy cost for loans and the obligation for everything else. Use this column to add up spending.
cols.RECIPIENT_CITY_CODE: A five-digit code for the recipient's city. 00000 is a common placeholder. Codes need a lookup.
cols.RECIPIENT_ZIP_LAST_4_CODE: The last four digits of the recipient's ZIP+4. Mostly blank, and 0000 shows up as filler.
cols.RECIPIENT_FOREIGN_CITY_NAME: The recipient's city when outside the US, like LONDON. Almost always blank; some say REMOVED TO PROTECT PII.
cols.RECIPIENT_FOREIGN_PROVINCE_NAME: The recipient's province when outside the US. Almost always blank, and fillers like PROVINCE and ANY VALUE are common.
cols.RECIPIENT_FOREIGN_POSTAL_CODE: The recipient's postal code when outside the US. Almost always blank; POSTAL_CODE shows up as filler.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_SCOPE: How wide the area served is, like SINGLE ZIP CODE, COUNTY-WIDE or STATE-WIDE.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_CODE: A code for where the work happens: two state letters plus a place or county number, like CA00000 or CA**037. Codes need a lookup.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_FOREIGN_LOC: Where the work happens when outside the US, in words. Almost always blank; UNKNOWN LOCATION DESCRIPTION is common.
cols.FUNDING_OPPORTUNITY_NUMBER: The number of the grant announcement the award came from, like PA-20-185. Almost always blank or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.FUNDING_OPPORTUNITY_GOALS_TEXT: The stated goals of the grant announcement, in words. Almost always blank or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.ASSISTANCE_TYPE_CODE: A two-digit code for the kind of help, like 06 or 10. The words are in ASSISTANCE_TYPE_DESCRIPTION.
cols.ASSISTANCE_TYPE_DESCRIPTION: The kind of help in words, like DIRECT LOAN, PROJECT GRANT or GUARANTEED/INSURED LOAN.
cols.BUSINESS_FUNDS_INDICATOR_CODE: Whether the money came from the 2009 Recovery Act: REC for yes, NON for no.
cols.BUSINESS_FUNDS_INDICATOR_DESCRIPTION: The Recovery Act flag in words: RECOVERY ACT or NOT RECOVERY ACT, with a few stray codes.
cols.BUSINESS_TYPES_CODE: A letter code for the kind of recipient, like P or Q. The words are in BUSINESS_TYPES_DESCRIPTION.
cols.BUSINESS_TYPES_DESCRIPTION: The kind of recipient in words, like INDIVIDUAL, SMALL BUSINESS or STATE GOVERNMENT.
cols.CORRECTION_DELETE_INDICATOR_CODE: A letter code, mostly C or L, marking a row that corrects or deletes an earlier one. Mostly blank; codes need a lookup.
cols.CORRECTION_DELETE_INDICATOR_DESCRIPTION: The correction flag in words, almost always CORRECT AN EXISTING RECORD. Mostly blank.
cols.ACTION_TYPE_CODE: A letter code for what this transaction did, like A or C. The words are in ACTION_TYPE_DESCRIPTION.
cols.ACTION_TYPE_DESCRIPTION: What this transaction did in words, like NEW, REVISION or CONTINUATION.
cols.RECORD_TYPE_CODE: A code 1, 2 or 3 for whether the row rolls up many small awards or is a single award. The words are in RECORD_TYPE_DESCRIPTION.
cols.RECORD_TYPE_DESCRIPTION: Whether the row is one award or a bundle of many: AGGREGATE RECORD, NON-AGGREGATE RECORD, or one to an individual.

ECONOMICS__FED_USASPENDING_ASSISTANCE_FU.summary: Every federal grant, loan, direct payment and other assistance transaction from USASpending, fiscal years 2007 to 2026, about 128 million rows with no row cap.
ECONOMICS__FED_USASPENDING_ASSISTANCE_FU.row: One award transaction: one new award, change or payment on one federal assistance award, on one day.

cols.CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY: USAspending's own key for the whole contract, built from the contract number and agency code, like CONT_AWD_FA527023F0101_9700.
cols.AWARD_ID_PIID: The government's contract number, like FA527023F0101. Some rows hold only a short order number like 0001.
cols.ACTION_DATE: The date of the award action, like a new contract or a change to one. Two tables store it as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_START_DATE: The date the work or grant was set to begin. Some tables store it as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_CURRENT_END_DATE: The date the work or grant is currently set to end, which can be in the future. Some tables store it as text.
cols.FEDERAL_ACTION_OBLIGATION: The dollars the government committed or took back in this one transaction. Negative numbers are cuts or cancellations.
cols.TOTAL_DOLLARS_OBLIGATED: The total dollars the government has committed to the whole contract so far, across all its transactions. Blank in many rows of the older tables.
cols.CURRENT_TOTAL_VALUE_OF_AWARD: What the whole contract is currently worth in dollars, counting options already used. Blank in many rows of the older tables.
cols.AWARDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency that made the award, like Department of Defense.
cols.AWARDING_SUB_AGENCY_NAME: The office inside the agency that gave the award, like Department of the Navy or National Park Service.
cols.FUNDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency whose money paid for the award. Can differ from the agency that made it.
cols.RECIPIENT_UEI: The recipient's 12-character federal ID, the Unique Entity ID that replaced the DUNS number. Mostly blank in the federal assistance table and empty in one small API table.
cols.RECIPIENT_DUNS: The recipient's old 9-digit DUNS business number. Mostly blank in the federal assistance table, empty in the three newer tables, and an obvious filler like 123456787 shows up.
cols.CAGE_CODE: The contractor's five-character Defense Department vendor code, like 1L027. Blank for many rows in some tables.
cols.RECIPIENT_NAME: Who received the money, like a company, agency or candidate. In the federal assistance table many rows say REDACTED or MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS instead of a name.
cols.RECIPIENT_DOING_BUSINESS_AS_NAME: The trade name the contractor goes by, if different from its legal name. Blank for most rows.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_UEI: The 12-character federal ID of the recipient's parent company. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_NAME: The name of the recipient's parent company or government, in capitals. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_CITY_NAME: The city where the recipient is based, in capitals.
cols.RECIPIENT_STATE_CODE: The recipient's state, as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam appear too.
cols.RECIPIENT_ZIP_4_CODE: The contractor's full nine-digit zip code, with no dash, like 070043561.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTRY_NAME: The country where the recipient is based, in capitals. The US shows up as both UNITED STATES and UNITED STATES OF AMERICA.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_STATE_CODE: The state where the work was actually done, as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam appear too.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_CITY_NAME: The city where the work was actually done, in capitals. Can differ from where the recipient is based.
cols.AWARD_TYPE: What kind of award: a contract type like PURCHASE ORDER or DELIVERY ORDER, or a grant type. Some rows use short forms like PO or DO, and the NIH table uses a one-digit code.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The industry code, usually six digits like 722110, which needs a lookup to read. Some tables hold shorter codes like 5416, the OSHA inspections table fills most rows with 000000, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.NAICS_DESCRIPTION: The industry in words, like Full-Service Restaurants, matching the NAICS code. One table leaves it empty.
cols.PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_CODE_DESCRIPTION: What kind of thing the government bought, in capitals, like OFFICE SUPPLIES or DRUGS AND BIOLOGICALS.
cols.TRANSACTION_DESCRIPTION: A free-text note on what was bought or funded, often full of internal codes and abbreviations. Some rows just say DESCR N.A.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_1_NAME: The name of the recipient's top-paid executive. Mostly blank.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_1_AMOUNT: The yearly pay in dollars of the recipient's top-paid executive. Mostly blank, and some filled rows say 0.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_2_NAME: The name of the recipient's second top-paid executive. Mostly blank.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_2_AMOUNT: The yearly pay in dollars of the recipient's second top-paid executive. Mostly blank, and some filled rows say 0.
cols.FOREIGN_OWNED: Whether the contractor is foreign-owned: t for true, f for false.
cols.USASPENDING_PERMALINK: A web link to this award's page on usaspending.gov.
cols.LAST_MODIFIED_DATE: When the source last changed this record. Some tables add the time.

ECONOMICS__FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS.summary: About 6.3 million federal contract actions from USAspending: which agency paid which company how much, for what.
ECONOMICS__FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS.row: One contract action: one award or change to a federal contract, with its dollars, agency and recipient.

cols.CONTRACT_TRANSACTION_UNIQUE_KEY: USAspending's ID for one contract action, built from agency codes, the contract number and the change number joined by underscores. -NONE- fills empty parts.
cols.CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY: USAspending's own key for the whole contract, built from the contract number and agency code, like CONT_AWD_FA527023F0101_9700.
cols.AWARD_ID_PIID: The government's contract number, like FA527023F0101. Some rows hold only a short order number like 0001.
cols.MODIFICATION_NUMBER: Which change to the award this row is, with 0 for the original. Formats are messy: 0, 0000 and P00003 all appear.
cols.TRANSACTION_NUMBER: A number that tells apart contract actions that would otherwise look the same. Almost always 0.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_AGENCY_ID: The 4-character code of the agency that owns the umbrella contract this order falls under, like 3600 for Veterans Affairs. Blank when there is no umbrella contract.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_AGENCY_NAME: The name of the agency that owns the umbrella contract this order falls under. Spelling varies, like DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS versus VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_ID_PIID: The contract number of the umbrella contract this order falls under, like GS03FGA010. Blank when there is none.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_MODIFICATION_NUMBER: Which change to the umbrella contract this refers to, like P00006 or 0 for the original.
cols.FEDERAL_ACTION_OBLIGATION: The dollars the government committed or took back in this one transaction. Negative numbers are cuts or cancellations.
cols.TOTAL_DOLLARS_OBLIGATED: The total dollars the government has committed to the whole contract so far, across all its transactions. Blank in many rows of the older tables.
cols.TOTAL_OUTLAYED_AMOUNT_FOR_OVERALL_AWARD: Total dollars actually paid out on the whole award so far. Mostly blank, and 0 is common.
cols.BASE_AND_EXERCISED_OPTIONS_VALUE: The dollar value the government has committed to so far, the base deal plus any extra options it chose to use. Can be negative when a change cuts it.
cols.CURRENT_TOTAL_VALUE_OF_AWARD: What the whole contract is currently worth in dollars, counting options already used. Blank in many rows of the older tables.
cols.BASE_AND_ALL_OPTIONS_VALUE: The dollar value if the government used every option in the contract. Can be negative when a change cuts it.
cols.POTENTIAL_TOTAL_VALUE_OF_AWARD: The most the whole contract could be worth in dollars. Sometimes blank in the full contracts table.
cols.DISASTER_EMERGENCY_FUND_CODES_FOR_OVERAL: Which emergency spending law funded the award, as a code plus words, like Q: Not Designated or Z: Emergency P.L. 117-58. Some rows list several codes, and it is mostly blank.
cols.OUTLAYED_AMOUNT_FROM_COVID_19_SUPPLEMENT: Dollars paid out on the award from COVID-19 relief money. Nearly always blank.
cols.OBLIGATED_AMOUNT_FROM_COVID_19_SUPPLEMEN: Dollars promised to the award from COVID-19 relief money. Nearly always blank, and can be negative after a cut.
cols.OUTLAYED_AMOUNT_FROM_IIJA_SUPPLEMENTAL_F: Dollars paid out on the award from the 2021 infrastructure law money. Nearly always blank.
cols.OBLIGATED_AMOUNT_FROM_IIJA_SUPPLEMENTAL_: Dollars promised to the award from the 2021 infrastructure law money. Nearly always blank.
cols.ACTION_DATE: The date of the award action, like a new contract or a change to one. Two tables store it as text.
cols.ACTION_DATE_FISCAL_YEAR: The federal fiscal year of the transaction, like 2007. Federal fiscal years start October 1.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_START_DATE: The date the work or grant was set to begin. Some tables store it as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_CURRENT_END_DATE: The date the work or grant is currently set to end, which can be in the future. Some tables store it as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_POTENTIAL_END_DATE: The latest date the work could run to if every option is used.
cols.ORDERING_PERIOD_END_DATE: The last date agencies can place orders under this umbrella contract. Mostly blank.
cols.SOLICITATION_DATE: The date the government asked for bids. Mostly blank in the full contracts table.
cols.AWARDING_AGENCY_CODE: The three-digit code for the federal department that made the award, like 036. Stored as text to keep the leading zero.
cols.AWARDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency that made the award, like Department of Defense.
cols.AWARDING_SUB_AGENCY_CODE: The four-character code for the office inside the department that made the award, like 3600. Some contain letters, like 12K3.
cols.AWARDING_SUB_AGENCY_NAME: The office inside the agency that gave the award, like Department of the Navy or National Park Service.
cols.AWARDING_OFFICE_CODE: The code for the office that made the award, like 47QSSC or 12346T. Nearly a third of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.AWARDING_OFFICE_NAME: The name of the office that made the award, like DLA TROOP SUPPORT. Nearly a third of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_AGENCY_CODE: The three-digit code for the federal department paying for the award, like 047. About a quarter of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency whose money paid for the award. Can differ from the agency that made it.
cols.FUNDING_SUB_AGENCY_CODE: The four-character code for the office inside the department paying for the award, like 7300 or 97AS. About a quarter of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_SUB_AGENCY_NAME: The name of the office inside the department paying for the award, like Department of the Navy. About a quarter of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_OFFICE_CODE: The code for the office paying for the award, like 47QSSC or 12346T. Nearly a third of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_OFFICE_NAME: The name of the office paying for the award, like DLA TROOP SUPPORT. Nearly a third of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.TREASURY_ACCOUNTS_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: The Treasury accounts that paid for the award, as codes like 012-X-4336-000, several split by semicolons. About half the grant and loan rows fill it, most bulk contract rows are blank, and the full contracts table is empty.
cols.FEDERAL_ACCOUNTS_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: The federal budget accounts that paid for the award, like 073-1154, several split by semicolons. About half the grant and loan rows fill it, most bulk contract rows are blank, and the full contracts table is empty.
cols.OBJECT_CLASSES_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: What kind of spending paid for the award, as a budget category code plus words, like 26.0: Supplies and materials; some rows list several. About half the grant and loan rows fill it, and most contract rows are blank.
cols.PROGRAM_ACTIVITIES_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: The budget programs that paid for the award, as a code plus words, like 0101: FEDERAL PELL GRANTS. Mostly blank, and filler like 0000: UNKNOWN/OTHER or OPTN: FIELD IS OPTIONAL PRIOR TO FY21 shows up.
cols.FOREIGN_FUNDING: Whether foreign money paid for the contract, as a letter: A foreign military sales, B other foreign funds, X not applicable.
cols.FOREIGN_FUNDING_DESCRIPTION: Whether foreign money paid for the contract, in words: NOT APPLICABLE, FOREIGN FUNDS FMS for foreign military sales, or FOREIGN FUNDS NON-FMS.
cols.SAM_EXCEPTION: A code for why the contractor did not have to register in the federal vendor system, SAM. Almost always blank.
cols.SAM_EXCEPTION_DESCRIPTION: Why the contractor did not have to register in SAM, the federal vendor system, in words like AWARDS TO FOREIGN ENTITIES. Almost always blank; the text NAN fills millions of rows and some hold stray letters like C or G.
cols.RECIPIENT_UEI: The recipient's 12-character federal ID, the Unique Entity ID that replaced the DUNS number. Mostly blank in the federal assistance table and empty in one small API table.
cols.RECIPIENT_DUNS: The recipient's old 9-digit DUNS business number. Mostly blank in the federal assistance table, empty in the three newer tables, and an obvious filler like 123456787 shows up.
cols.RECIPIENT_NAME: Who received the money, like a company, agency or candidate. In the federal assistance table many rows say REDACTED or MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS instead of a name.
cols.RECIPIENT_NAME_RAW: The award recipient's name exactly as the source wrote it, not cleaned up. Grant and loan rows often hold stand-ins like REDACTED DUE TO PII or MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS.
cols.RECIPIENT_DOING_BUSINESS_AS_NAME: The trade name the contractor goes by, if different from its legal name. Blank for most rows.
cols.CAGE_CODE: The contractor's five-character Defense Department vendor code, like 1L027. Blank for many rows in some tables.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_UEI: The 12-character federal ID of the recipient's parent company. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_DUNS: The 9-digit DUNS number, the old business ID, of the recipient's parent company. Mostly blank in the grants table, empty in the bulk table, and the fake-looking 123456787 shows up often in contracts.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_NAME: The name of the recipient's parent company or government, in capitals. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_NAME_RAW: The name of the recipient's parent company or government, exactly as the source wrote it. Mostly blank in the grants and loans table.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTRY_CODE: The recipient's country as a three-letter code, like USA or GBR.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTRY_NAME: The country where the recipient is based, in capitals. The US shows up as both UNITED STATES and UNITED STATES OF AMERICA.
cols.RECIPIENT_ADDRESS_LINE_1: The first line of the recipient's street address.
cols.RECIPIENT_ADDRESS_LINE_2: The second line of the recipient's address, like a suite number. Mostly blank, and N/A shows up as filler.
cols.RECIPIENT_CITY_NAME: The city where the recipient is based, in capitals.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_COUNTY: The recipient's 5-digit county code, like 06037. Keep it as text for the leading zero.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTY_NAME: The recipient's county name, in capitals.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_STATE_: The recipient's state as a 2-digit code, like 06 for California. Keep it as text for the leading zero.
cols.RECIPIENT_STATE_CODE: The recipient's state, as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam appear too.
cols.RECIPIENT_STATE_NAME: The recipient's state spelled out, like MARYLAND.
cols.RECIPIENT_ZIP_4_CODE: The contractor's full nine-digit zip code, with no dash, like 070043561.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_CD_ORI: The recipient's congressional district when the award was made, as state and number like MD-06.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_CD_CUR: The recipient's congressional district under today's district lines, as state and number like MD-06.
cols.RECIPIENT_PHONE_NUMBER: The contractor's phone number, 10 digits with no dashes, stored as text.
cols.RECIPIENT_FAX_NUMBER: The contractor's fax number, 10 digits with no dashes, stored as text.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_COUNTRY_COD: The country where the work is done, as a three-letter code like USA.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_COUNTRY_NAM: The country where the work is done, spelled out, like UNITED STATES.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_CITY_NAME: The city where the work was actually done, in capitals. Can differ from where the recipient is based.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_PLACE_OF_PERFORM: The 5-digit county code where the work is done, like 06037 for Los Angeles. Keep it as text for the leading zero.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_COUNTY_NAME: The county where the work is done, in capitals.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_PLACE_OF_PERFORM: The state where the work is done, as a 2-digit code like 06 for California.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_STATE_CODE: The state where the work was actually done, as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam appear too.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_STATE_NAME: The state where the work is done, spelled out.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_ZIP_4: The ZIP code where the work is done, often with the extra four digits, written like 600858337 or 48226-1906. Some grant rows say CITY-WIDE instead.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_PLACE_OF_PERFORM: The congressional district where the work is done, when the award was made, as state and number like IL-10.
The congressional district where the work is done, under today's district lines, like IL-10. Grant rows often show a 90 district like CA-90, which needs a lookup.
cols.AWARD_OR_IDV_FLAG: Whether the row is a regular contract, AWARD, or an umbrella deal other orders are placed under, IDV.
cols.AWARD_TYPE_CODE: What kind of contract it is, as a letter A to D, like a purchase order or delivery order. Needs a lookup.
cols.AWARD_TYPE: What kind of award: a contract type like PURCHASE ORDER or DELIVERY ORDER, or a grant type. Some rows use short forms like PO or DO, and the NIH table uses a one-digit code.
cols.IDV_TYPE_CODE: What kind of umbrella deal it is, as a letter A to E. Needs a lookup; blank for regular contracts.
cols.IDV_TYPE: What kind of umbrella deal it is, as a short name like IDC, BPA, FSS or GWAC. Blank for regular contracts.
cols.MULTIPLE_OR_SINGLE_AWARD_IDV_CODE: Whether the umbrella deal went to one company or several: S single, M multiple. Mostly blank.
cols.MULTIPLE_OR_SINGLE_AWARD_IDV: Whether the umbrella deal went to one company or several: SINGLE AWARD or MULTIPLE AWARD. Mostly blank.
cols.TYPE_OF_IDC_CODE: For open-ended delivery contracts, how the amount is set, as a letter A, B or C. Nearly always blank.
cols.TYPE_OF_IDC: For open-ended delivery contracts, how the amount is set, like INDEFINITE DELIVERY / INDEFINITE QUANTITY. Nearly always blank; the text NAN fills millions of rows.
cols.TYPE_OF_CONTRACT_PRICING_CODE: How the contract price is set, as a short code like J for firm fixed price. Needs a lookup.
cols.TYPE_OF_CONTRACT_PRICING: How the contract price is set, in words like FIRM FIXED PRICE, COST PLUS FIXED FEE or TIME AND MATERIALS.
cols.TRANSACTION_DESCRIPTION: A free-text note on what was bought or funded, often full of internal codes and abbreviations. Some rows just say DESCR N.A.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_BASE_TRANSACTION_DESCRIPTION: What the award is for, in the agency's own free-text words.
cols.ACTION_TYPE: What kind of change this contract action was, in words, like CHANGE ORDER, FUNDING ONLY ACTION or CLOSE OUT. Mostly blank.
cols.SOLICITATION_IDENTIFIER: The government's ID for the request for bids that led to this contract, like N0002406R5430. Mostly blank.
cols.NUMBER_OF_ACTIONS: How many contract actions this row stands for. Almost always 1.
cols.INHERENTLY_GOVERNMENTAL_FUNCTIONS: A code for whether the work is close to jobs only government should do: CL, CT, OT, or a combo like CL,CT. The words are in INHERENTLY_GOVERNMENTAL_FUNCTIONS_DESCRIPTION.
cols.INHERENTLY_GOVERNMENTAL_FUNCTIONS_DESCRI: Whether the work is close to jobs only government should do, in words, like CLOSELY ASSOCIATED, CRITICAL FUNCTIONS or OTHER FUNCTIONS.
cols.PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_CODE: A four-character code for what was bought, like 7110 or R499. All-number codes are goods, letter-first codes are services; needs a lookup.
cols.PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_CODE_DESCRIPTION: What kind of thing the government bought, in capitals, like OFFICE SUPPLIES or DRUGS AND BIOLOGICALS.
cols.CONTRACT_BUNDLING_CODE: A short code for whether several needs were bundled into one contract, like D, C or H. The words for it are in CONTRACT_BUNDLING.
cols.CONTRACT_BUNDLING: Whether several needs were bundled into one contract, in words, like NOT A BUNDLED REQUIREMENT or NOT BUNDLED.
cols.DOD_CLAIMANT_PROGRAM_CODE: A short code for the Defense Department spending category, like A3, C9E or S1. The words for it are in DOD_CLAIMANT_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION.
cols.DOD_CLAIMANT_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION: The Defense Department spending category in words, like SHIPS, SERVICES or COMBAT VEHICLES.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The industry code, usually six digits like 722110, which needs a lookup to read. Some tables hold shorter codes like 5416, the OSHA inspections table fills most rows with 000000, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.NAICS_DESCRIPTION: The industry in words, like Full-Service Restaurants, matching the NAICS code. One table leaves it empty.
cols.RECOVERED_MATERIALS_SUSTAINABILITY_CODE: A short code for which recycled-material or green-buying clauses the contract has, like A, B or C. The words for it are in RECOVERED_MATERIALS_SUSTAINABILITY.
cols.RECOVERED_MATERIALS_SUSTAINABILITY: Which recycled-material or green-buying clauses the contract has, in words, like FAR 52.223-4 INCLUDED or BIO-BASED. Some values are cut off mid-word.
cols.DOMESTIC_OR_FOREIGN_ENTITY_CODE: A short code for whether the contractor is U.S. or foreign owned, like A, C or D. The words for it are in DOMESTIC_OR_FOREIGN_ENTITY.
cols.DOMESTIC_OR_FOREIGN_ENTITY: Whether the contractor is U.S. or foreign owned, in words, like U.S. OWNED BUSINESS or FOREIGN-OWNED BUSINESS NOT INCORPORATED IN THE U.S.
cols.DOD_ACQUISITION_PROGRAM_CODE: A short code for the Defense weapons or buying program, like 234, DAL or 000. The words for it are in DOD_ACQUISITION_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION.
cols.DOD_ACQUISITION_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION: The Defense weapons or buying program in words, like TRIDENT II MISSILE or F-16. Mostly blank or NONE.
cols.INFORMATION_TECHNOLOGY_COMMERCIAL_ITEM_C: A short code for what kind of tech purchase this was, like Z, A or E. The words for it are in INFORMATION_TECHNOLOGY_COMMERCIAL_ITEM_CATEGORY.
What kind of tech purchase this was, in words, like NOT IT PRODUCTS OR SERVICES or COMMERCIAL SERVICE.
cols.EPA_DESIGNATED_PRODUCT_CODE: A short code for whether the goods had to meet EPA recycled-content rules, like A or E. The words for it are in EPA_DESIGNATED_PRODUCT.
cols.EPA_DESIGNATED_PRODUCT: Whether the goods had to meet EPA recycled-content rules, in words, like MEETS REQUIREMENTS or NOT REQUIRED.
cols.COUNTRY_OF_PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_ORIGIN_COD: The country the goods or services came from, as a three-letter code like USA, DEU or AFG. The text NAN shows up in place of a blank.
cols.COUNTRY_OF_PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_ORIGIN: The country the goods or services came from, spelled out, like UNITED STATES or IRAQ.
cols.PLACE_OF_MANUFACTURE_CODE: A short code for where the goods were made, like C, D or G. The words for it are in PLACE_OF_MANUFACTURE.
cols.PLACE_OF_MANUFACTURE: Where the goods were made, in words, like MFG IN U.S. or NOT A MANUFACTURED END PRODUCT. Some values are cut off.
cols.SUBCONTRACTING_PLAN_CODE: A short code for whether the contractor needed a plan to pass work to small businesses, like A, B or F. The words for it are in SUBCONTRACTING_PLAN.
cols.SUBCONTRACTING_PLAN: Whether the contractor needed a plan to pass work to small businesses, in words, like PLAN NOT REQUIRED.
cols.EXTENT_COMPETED_CODE: A short code for how much competition there was for the contract, like A, B, D or G. The words for it are in EXTENT_COMPETED.
cols.EXTENT_COMPETED: How much competition there was for the contract, in words, like FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION or NOT COMPETED.
cols.SOLICITATION_PROCEDURES_CODE: A short code for how bids were asked for, like SP1, NP or SSS. The words for it are in SOLICITATION_PROCEDURES.
cols.SOLICITATION_PROCEDURES: How bids were asked for, in words, like SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION, SEALED BID or ONLY ONE SOURCE.
cols.TYPE_OF_SET_ASIDE_CODE: A short code for which kind of business the contract was reserved for, like SBA, 8A or SDVOSBC; NONE means no set-aside, and it is the most common value in the big contracts table. The words for it are in TYPE_OF_SET_ASIDE.
cols.TYPE_OF_SET_ASIDE: Which kind of business the contract was reserved for, in words, like NO SET ASIDE USED. or HUBZONE SET-ASIDE.
cols.EVALUATED_PREFERENCE_CODE: A short code for a price edge given to certain small businesses, like HZE or SPS. Almost always NONE or blank.
cols.EVALUATED_PREFERENCE: Whether certain small businesses got a price edge when bids were judged, in words. Almost always NO PREFERENCE USED.
cols.RESEARCH_CODE: A short code for the small-business research program and phase, like SR1 or ST1. The words for it are in RESEARCH.
cols.RESEARCH: The small-business research program and phase in words, like SMALL BUSINESS INNOVATION RESEARCH PROGRAM PHASE II ACTION. Almost always blank or the text NAN.
cols.FAIR_OPPORTUNITY_LIMITED_SOURCES_CODE: A short code for why an order under an existing contract was or was not opened to other holders, like FAIR, ONE or FOO. The words for it are in FAIR_OPPORTUNITY_LIMITED_SOURCES.
cols.FAIR_OPPORTUNITY_LIMITED_SOURCES: Why an order under an existing contract was or was not opened to other holders, in words, like FAIR OPPORTUNITY GIVEN or URGENCY. The text NAN often stands in for blank.
cols.OTHER_THAN_FULL_AND_OPEN_COMPETITION_COD: A short code for the legal reason the contract skipped open bidding, like UNQ, OTH or ONE. The words for it are in OTHER_THAN_FULL_AND_OPEN_COMPETITION.
cols.OTHER_THAN_FULL_AND_OPEN_COMPETITION: The legal reason the contract skipped open bidding, in words, like UNIQUE SOURCE or AUTHORIZED BY STATUTE.
cols.NUMBER_OF_OFFERS_RECEIVED: How many bids came in. A 999 shows up and is likely filler, not a real count.
cols.COMMERCIAL_ITEM_ACQUISITION_PROCEDURES_C: A short code for whether off-the-shelf buying rules were used, like A, B or D. The words for it are in COMMERCIAL_ITEM_ACQUISITION_PROCEDURES.
cols.COMMERCIAL_ITEM_ACQUISITION_PROCEDURES: Whether off-the-shelf buying rules were used, in words, like COMMERCIAL ITEM or COMMERCIAL ITEM PROCEDURES NOT USED. The wording changed over time.
cols.SMALL_BUSINESS_COMPETITIVENESS_DEMONSTRA: Whether the contract fell under a small-business pilot program, as t or f. Always f where filled.
cols.SIMPLIFIED_PROCEDURES_FOR_CERTAIN_COMMER: Whether a shortcut buying process for commercial goods was used, as Y or N.
Whether a shortcut buying process for commercial goods was used, as YES or NO.
cols.A76_FAIR_ACT_ACTION_CODE: Whether the work came out of a review of jobs government could hand to contractors. Mixes N, Y, NO and YES in one column.
cols.A76_FAIR_ACT_ACTION: Whether the work came out of a review of jobs government could hand to contractors, as YES or NO. Almost always NO.
cols.FED_BIZ_OPPS_CODE: Whether the opportunity was posted on the federal bid website: Y, N, or X for not applicable.
cols.FED_BIZ_OPPS: Whether the opportunity was posted on the federal bid website, as YES, NO or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.LOCAL_AREA_SET_ASIDE_CODE: Whether the contract was reserved for local businesses in a disaster area, as Y or N.
cols.LOCAL_AREA_SET_ASIDE: Whether the contract was reserved for local businesses in a disaster area, as YES or NO.
cols.PRICE_EVALUATION_ADJUSTMENT_PREFERENCE_P: The percent price edge given to a favored bidder. Mostly blank, and almost always 0 where filled.
cols.CLINGER_COHEN_ACT_PLANNING_CODE: Whether the tech buy followed federal IT planning rules, as N or Y. Some rows write it N: NO or Y: YES instead.
cols.CLINGER_COHEN_ACT_PLANNING: Whether the tech buy followed federal IT planning rules, as YES or NO.
cols.MATERIALS_SUPPLIES_ARTICLES_EQUIPMENT_CO: Whether the federal wage law for goods contracts applies: Y, N, or X for not applicable.
cols.MATERIALS_SUPPLIES_ARTICLES_EQUIPMENT: Whether the federal wage law for goods contracts applies, as YES, NO or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.LABOR_STANDARDS_CODE: Whether federal wage rules for service workers apply: Y, N, or X for not applicable.
cols.LABOR_STANDARDS: Whether federal wage rules for service workers apply, as YES, NO or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.CONSTRUCTION_WAGE_RATE_REQUIREMENTS_CODE: Whether local-wage rules for construction workers apply: Y, N, or X for not applicable.
cols.CONSTRUCTION_WAGE_RATE_REQUIREMENTS: Whether local-wage rules for construction workers apply, as YES, NO or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.INTERAGENCY_CONTRACTING_AUTHORITY_CODE: The law that let one agency buy for another: A, B, or X for not applicable. The words are in INTERAGENCY_CONTRACTING_AUTHORITY.
cols.INTERAGENCY_CONTRACTING_AUTHORITY: The law that let one agency buy for another, in words, like ECONOMY ACT, OTHER STATUTORY AUTHORITY or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.OTHER_STATUTORY_AUTHORITY: The law cited when one agency bought for another under something other than the Economy Act, as free text like 40 U.S.C. 321. Almost always blank.
cols.PROGRAM_ACRONYM: The short name of the government-wide contract program used, like SEWP V or GWAC-VETS 2. Almost always blank.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_TYPE_CODE: A short code for the type of umbrella contract this order was placed under, like A, B or C. The words for it are in PARENT_AWARD_TYPE.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_TYPE: The type of umbrella contract this order was placed under, as an acronym like IDC, BPA, FSS or GWAC. Blank when there is no umbrella contract.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_SINGLE_OR_MULTIPLE_CODE: Whether the umbrella contract went to one company or several: S for single, M for multiple.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_SINGLE_OR_MULTIPLE: Whether the umbrella contract went to one company or several: SINGLE AWARD or MULTIPLE AWARD.
cols.MAJOR_PROGRAM: A program name typed in by the agency, free text like VETERANS FIRST CONTRACTING or JANSAN FSSI. Messy and mostly blank.
cols.NATIONAL_INTEREST_ACTION_CODE: A code for the national emergency the buy was tied to, like P20C or H05K. Almost always NONE or blank.
cols.NATIONAL_INTEREST_ACTION: The national emergency the buy was tied to, like COVID-19 2020 or HURRICANE KATRINA 2005. Almost always NONE or blank.
cols.COST_OR_PRICING_DATA_CODE: Whether the contractor had to hand over detailed cost data: Y, N, or W for waived.
cols.COST_OR_PRICING_DATA: Whether the contractor had to hand over detailed cost data, as YES, NO or NOT OBTAINED - WAIVED.
cols.COST_ACCOUNTING_STANDARDS_CLAUSE_CODE: Whether federal cost-accounting rules apply: Y, N, or X for exempt.
cols.COST_ACCOUNTING_STANDARDS_CLAUSE: Whether federal cost-accounting rules apply, in words, like YES - CAS CLAUSE INCLUDED or NOT APPLICABLE EXEMPT FROM CAS.
cols.GOVERNMENT_FURNISHED_PROPERTY_CODE: Whether the government lent the contractor equipment or property, as Y or N.
cols.GOVERNMENT_FURNISHED_PROPERTY: Whether the government lent the contractor equipment or property, in words: TRANSACTION USES GFE/GFP or TRANSACTION DOES NOT USE GFE/GFP.
cols.SEA_TRANSPORTATION_CODE: Whether goods were expected to ship by sea: Y, N, or U for unknown.
cols.SEA_TRANSPORTATION: Whether goods were expected to ship by sea, as YES, NO or UNKNOWN.
cols.UNDEFINITIZED_ACTION_CODE: Whether work started before the final terms were set: X, N, A or B. The words are in UNDEFINITIZED_ACTION.
cols.UNDEFINITIZED_ACTION: Whether work started before the final terms were set, in words, like NO, LETTER CONTRACT or OTHER UNDEFINITIZED ACTION.
cols.CONSOLIDATED_CONTRACT_CODE: Whether several needs were merged into one contract, as a letter like N, D, A, B or Y. N and D both line up with no; the words are in CONSOLIDATED_CONTRACT.
cols.CONSOLIDATED_CONTRACT: Whether several needs were merged into one contract, in words, like NO, YES or NOT CONSOLIDATED.
cols.PERFORMANCE_BASED_SERVICE_ACQUISITION_CO: Whether the service contract pays for results rather than hours: Y, N, or X for not applicable.
cols.PERFORMANCE_BASED_SERVICE_ACQUISITION: Whether the service contract pays for results rather than hours, in words, like YES - SERVICE WHERE PBA IS USED. or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.MULTI_YEAR_CONTRACT_CODE: Whether the contract covers several years of needs up front, as Y or N.
cols.MULTI_YEAR_CONTRACT: Whether the contract covers several years of needs up front, as YES or NO.
cols.CONTRACT_FINANCING_CODE: A short code for how the contractor gets paid before the work is done, like A, E or Z. The words for it are in CONTRACT_FINANCING.
cols.CONTRACT_FINANCING: How the contractor gets paid before the work is done, in words, like FAR 52.232-16 PROGRESS PAYMENTS or NOT APPLICABLE.

ECONOMICS__FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS_FUL.summary: Federal contract spending from USAspending, fiscal years 2007 to 2026, but cut off at exactly 1 million rows per year, so it is incomplete. Use the r2 reload for any total or trend.
ECONOMICS__FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS_FUL.row: One contract action: one new contract or change to a contract, on one day.

cols.CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY: USAspending's own key for the whole contract, built from the contract number and agency code, like CONT_AWD_FA527023F0101_9700.
cols.AWARD_ID_PIID: The government's contract number, like FA527023F0101. Some rows hold only a short order number like 0001.
cols.ACTION_DATE: The date of the award action, like a new contract or a change to one. Two tables store it as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_START_DATE: The date the work or grant was set to begin. Some tables store it as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_CURRENT_END_DATE: The date the work or grant is currently set to end, which can be in the future. Some tables store it as text.
cols.FEDERAL_ACTION_OBLIGATION: The dollars the government committed or took back in this one transaction. Negative numbers are cuts or cancellations.
cols.TOTAL_DOLLARS_OBLIGATED: The total dollars the government has committed to the whole contract so far, across all its transactions. Blank in many rows of the older tables.
cols.CURRENT_TOTAL_VALUE_OF_AWARD: What the whole contract is currently worth in dollars, counting options already used. Blank in many rows of the older tables.
cols.AWARDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency that made the award, like Department of Defense.
cols.AWARDING_SUB_AGENCY_NAME: The office inside the agency that gave the award, like Department of the Navy or National Park Service.
cols.FUNDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency whose money paid for the award. Can differ from the agency that made it.
cols.RECIPIENT_UEI: The recipient's 12-character federal ID, the Unique Entity ID that replaced the DUNS number. Mostly blank in the federal assistance table and empty in one small API table.
cols.RECIPIENT_DUNS: The recipient's old 9-digit DUNS business number. Mostly blank in the federal assistance table, empty in the three newer tables, and an obvious filler like 123456787 shows up.
cols.CAGE_CODE: The contractor's five-character Defense Department vendor code, like 1L027. Blank for many rows in some tables.
cols.RECIPIENT_NAME: Who received the money, like a company, agency or candidate. In the federal assistance table many rows say REDACTED or MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS instead of a name.
cols.RECIPIENT_DOING_BUSINESS_AS_NAME: The trade name the contractor goes by, if different from its legal name. Blank for most rows.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_UEI: The 12-character federal ID of the recipient's parent company. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_NAME: The name of the recipient's parent company or government, in capitals. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_CITY_NAME: The city where the recipient is based, in capitals.
cols.RECIPIENT_STATE_CODE: The recipient's state, as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam appear too.
cols.RECIPIENT_ZIP_4_CODE: The contractor's full nine-digit zip code, with no dash, like 070043561.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTRY_NAME: The country where the recipient is based, in capitals. The US shows up as both UNITED STATES and UNITED STATES OF AMERICA.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_STATE_CODE: The state where the work was actually done, as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam appear too.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_CITY_NAME: The city where the work was actually done, in capitals. Can differ from where the recipient is based.
cols.AWARD_TYPE: What kind of award: a contract type like PURCHASE ORDER or DELIVERY ORDER, or a grant type. Some rows use short forms like PO or DO, and the NIH table uses a one-digit code.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The industry code, usually six digits like 722110, which needs a lookup to read. Some tables hold shorter codes like 5416, the OSHA inspections table fills most rows with 000000, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.NAICS_DESCRIPTION: The industry in words, like Full-Service Restaurants, matching the NAICS code. One table leaves it empty.
cols.PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_CODE_DESCRIPTION: What kind of thing the government bought, in capitals, like OFFICE SUPPLIES or DRUGS AND BIOLOGICALS.
cols.TRANSACTION_DESCRIPTION: A free-text note on what was bought or funded, often full of internal codes and abbreviations. Some rows just say DESCR N.A.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_1_NAME: The name of the recipient's top-paid executive. Mostly blank.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_1_AMOUNT: The yearly pay in dollars of the recipient's top-paid executive. Mostly blank, and some filled rows say 0.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_2_NAME: The name of the recipient's second top-paid executive. Mostly blank.
cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_2_AMOUNT: The yearly pay in dollars of the recipient's second top-paid executive. Mostly blank, and some filled rows say 0.
cols.FOREIGN_OWNED: Whether the contractor is foreign-owned: t for true, f for false.
cols.USASPENDING_PERMALINK: A web link to this award's page on usaspending.gov.
cols.LAST_MODIFIED_DATE: When the source last changed this record. Some tables add the time.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_URL: The web address the data was downloaded from. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

ECONOMICS__FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS_FUL.summary: Federal contract spending from USAspending, 93 million transactions: who got paid, by which agency, for what, and how much.
ECONOMICS__FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS_FUL.row: One contract action: one transaction on one federal contract.

cols.AGENCY_NAME: The government agency's name, like Department of Housing and Urban Development. Empty in the grants table.
cols.AGENCY_ID: USAspending's internal number for the agency.
cols.TOPTIER_CODE: The Treasury code for the agency, like 086 or 513. Keep it as text so leading zeros stay.
cols.ABBREVIATION: The agency's short name, like HUD or FDIC.
cols.CONGRESSIONAL_JUSTIFICATION_URL: A web link to the agency's budget request to Congress.
cols.ACTIVE_FY: The fiscal year the money figures cover. 2026 on every row.
cols.ACTIVE_FQ: The fiscal quarter the money figures run through. 3 on every row.
cols.OUTLAY_AMOUNT: Dollars the agency has actually paid out so far this fiscal year.
cols.OBLIGATED_AMOUNT: Dollars the agency has committed to spend so far this fiscal year.
cols.BUDGET_AUTHORITY_AMOUNT: Dollars the agency is allowed to spend this fiscal year.
cols.CURRENT_TOTAL_BUDGET_AUTHORITY_AMOUNT: The whole federal government's spending authority this fiscal year, about 13.4 trillion dollars. The same number on every row.
cols.PERCENTAGE_OF_TOTAL_BUDGET_AUTHORITY: The agency's share of all federal spending authority, as a fraction, where 0.01 means 1 percent.
cols.AGENCY_SLUG: The agency's name as used in USAspending web addresses, like denali-commission.

ECONOMICS__FED_USASPENDING_TOPTIER_AGENC.summary: The 111 top-level federal agencies on USAspending.gov, with each one's budget, money committed and money paid out so far in fiscal year 2026.
ECONOMICS__FED_USASPENDING_TOPTIER_AGENC.row: One agency: one top-level federal department or agency and its fiscal 2026 money so far.

cols.ACCESSION_NUMBER: The SEC's unique number for one filing, like 0001193125-24-036425. The Health Canada drug table reuses the name for its own short codes like P9864 and leaves it mostly blank.
cols.CIK: The company's SEC filer number. Some tables pad it to 10 digits with leading zeros and some do not, so strip zeros before matching.
cols.TICKER: The company's stock ticker symbol, like AAPL. "--", "N/A" or blank means none was given.
cols.EIN: The organization's 9-digit federal tax ID number, stored as text. Some rows hold 000000000 as a filler or only 8 digits because a leading zero was lost, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.ENTITY_NAME: The name of the company, person or group the record is about. The two exclusion tables leave it mostly blank.
cols.FORM_TYPE: Which form was filed, like 8-K for the SEC or LM-2 for union reports; the codes depend on the agency. One IRS table just says EFILE.
cols.SIC_CODE: The four-digit industry code, like 2834 for drug makers. Kept as text so leading zeros like 0783 survive.
cols.PERIOD_OF_REPORT: The date the filing reports on, like the date of an insider's trade. One table stores it as text like 27-MAR-2026.
cols.DOCUMENT_URL: A web link to the original document, like the SEC filing or the enforcement order.
cols.SOURCE_ID: A short name for the source feed the row came from, like fed_cfpb_complaints. In the ITIS other-sources table it is a plain number instead, which needs a lookup.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.ISIN: The international securities code for the company's stock. Empty in this table.
cols.STATE_OF_INCORPORATION: The state where the company is incorporated, as two letters. Mostly DE, Delaware.
cols.BUSINESS_ADDRESS: The company's business address as one line of text. Only about 25 addresses appear.
cols.FILED_AT: The day the filing was made.
cols.FILED_YEAR: The year the filing was made.
cols.FILED_MONTH: The month the filing was made, 1 to 12.
cols.FILING_URL: A web link to the filing on the SEC's website.
cols.IS_REGISTRATION_OR_PROSPECTUS: True if the filing registers securities for sale or is a prospectus.
cols.IS_ANNUAL_REPORT: True if the filing is an annual report.
cols.IS_QUARTERLY_REPORT: True if the filing is a quarterly report.

ECONOMICS__FED_US_SEC_EDGAR.summary: Filings made to the SEC's EDGAR system by a small set of large companies, about 25 business addresses in all, mostly filed in 2025 and 2026, with a link to each filing.
ECONOMICS__FED_US_SEC_EDGAR.row: One filing: one document a company filed with the SEC on one day.

cols.AWARD_ID: The award's ID in the source's own system, like NNG15CR64C. The format differs by agency and country.
cols.RECIPIENT_UEI: The recipient's 12-character federal ID, the Unique Entity ID that replaced the DUNS number. Mostly blank in the federal assistance table and empty in one small API table.
cols.RECIPIENT_DUNS: The recipient's old 9-digit DUNS business number. Mostly blank in the federal assistance table, empty in the three newer tables, and an obvious filler like 123456787 shows up.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The industry code, usually six digits like 722110, which needs a lookup to read. Some tables hold shorter codes like 5416, the OSHA inspections table fills most rows with 000000, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.CFDA_NUMBER: The federal assistance program number, like 93.778. Some rows list several, split by commas.
cols.RECIPIENT_NAME: Who received the money, like a company, agency or candidate. In the federal assistance table many rows say REDACTED or MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS instead of a name.
cols.AWARDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency that made the award, like Department of Defense.
cols.FUNDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency whose money paid for the award. Can differ from the agency that made it.
cols.NAICS_DESCRIPTION: The industry in words, like Full-Service Restaurants, matching the NAICS code. One table leaves it empty.
cols.CFDA_TITLE: The name of the federal aid program the money came from, like PAYCHECK PROTECTION LOAN PROGRAM or FEDERAL PELL GRANT PROGRAM. Empty in the USAspending API table.
cols.AWARD_TYPE: What kind of award: a contract type like PURCHASE ORDER or DELIVERY ORDER, or a grant type. Some rows use short forms like PO or DO, and the NIH table uses a one-digit code.
cols.FISCAL_YEAR: The government fiscal year the row covers, like 2023, sometimes written as FY2026 or 2024 YTD. One ICE table holds small numbers that are not years, a DHS table leaves it mostly blank, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.AWARD_AMOUNT: The dollar amount of the award or grant. Some rows hold stand-in amounts of 0 or 1.
cols.START_DATE: The date it began, like an award, trial, listing or court. Mostly blank in several tables, and 1969-12-31 shows up in the offshore-leaks table as a stand-in date.
cols.END_DATE: The date it ended or is set to end, like an award or a listing. Some are in the future.
cols.LAST_MODIFIED_DATE: When the source last changed this record. Some tables add the time.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.GENERATED_UNIQUE_AWARD_ID: Meant to hold USAspending's unique award ID, but it is empty in this table.
cols.RECIPIENT_EIN: Meant to hold the recipient's tax ID, but it is empty in this table.
cols.TREASURY_ACCOUNT_SYMBOL: Meant to hold the Treasury account the money came from, but it is empty in this table.
cols.FEDERAL_ACCOUNT_CODE: Meant to hold the federal account code, but it is empty in this table.
cols.TOPTIER_AGENCY_CODE: The awarding agency as a three-digit code, like 075 or 097. Needs a lookup.
cols.PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_FIPS: Meant to hold the area code where the work happens, but it is empty in this table.
cols.RECIPIENT_LOCATION_FIPS: Meant to hold the recipient's area code, but it is empty in this table.
cols.DEF_CODE: Meant to hold the disaster or emergency funding code, but it is empty in this table.
cols.PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_STATE: The state where the work happens, as two letters. Blank on about a third of rows.
cols.PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_CITY: Meant to hold the city where the work happens, but it is empty in this table.
cols.RECIPIENT_LOCATION_STATE: Meant to hold the recipient's state, but it is empty in this table.
cols.TOTAL_OBLIGATION: Meant to hold the dollars promised, but it is empty in this table.
cols.TOTAL_OUTLAY: Meant to hold the dollars paid out, but it is empty in this table.
cols.TRANSACTION_COUNT: Meant to hold the number of changes to the award, but it is empty in this table.
cols.SUBAWARD_COUNT: Meant to hold the number of subawards, but it is empty in this table.
cols.AWARD_DURATION_DAYS: How many days the award runs. Blank on a third of rows, and a few say -1.
cols.AWARD_SIZE_BAND: The award size group. Always Large, 10 million dollars or more, in this table.

cols.TOPIC: A text description of what the dataset covers. Filled only in the FAO table; the FTC and Densho tables are empty.
cols.FILESIZE: The size of the download file, as text like 77KB.
cols.DATASETCODE: FAO's short code for the dataset, like TM or TCL.
cols.DATASETNAME: The dataset's name, like Trade: Trade Indices.
cols.DATASETDESCRIPTION: A written description of what the dataset holds. Blank on 3 rows.
cols.DATEUPDATE: When FAO last updated the dataset, as a date and time. Stored as text.
cols.FILELOCATION: Web address to download the dataset's bulk file.
cols.FILEROWS: How many rows the dataset's bulk file holds. Stored as text.

ECONOMICS__INTL_FAO_FAOSTAT.summary: The catalog of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization's FAOSTAT datasets: 69 datasets with names, descriptions, update dates and download links.
ECONOMICS__INTL_FAO_FAOSTAT.row: One dataset: one FAOSTAT dataset, like Trade Indices, with where to download it.

cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.UNIT: The unit the number is measured in, like %, GW, TWh or deaths per 100,000. One table writes percent as PC, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.NOTE: A free-text note about the record, blank for most rows. One housing table fills many rows with a bare tab character instead of text.
cols.AREA_CODE: The FAO's number for the country or region, like 5300. Codes need a lookup; AREA has the name.
cols.AREA_CODE_M49: The UN's M49 number for the country or region, with a leading apostrophe, like '062.
cols.AREA: The country or region name, like South America or Central Asia.
cols.ITEM_CODE: The FAO's code for the measure, like 210081; an F or M on the end marks the female or male version.
cols.ITEM: The measure in words, like Number of severely food insecure people.
cols.ELEMENT_CODE: A number code for the kind of figure, like 6121. The words are in ELEMENT.
cols.ELEMENT: Whether the number is the Value itself or the upper or lower bound of its confidence interval.
cols.YEAR_CODE: The years covered, glued together, like 20202022 for 2020 to 2022.
cols.VALUE: The number itself. Stored as text, and small values show as <0.1.
cols.FLAG: A letter marking how the number was made: E, X, O, Q or A. The letters need a lookup.

ECONOMICS__INTL_FAO_FAOSTAT_FOOD_SECURIT.summary: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization's food security numbers by country and region, like how many people go hungry or cannot get enough food, mostly as three-year averages.
ECONOMICS__INTL_FAO_FAOSTAT_FOOD_SECURIT.row: One measure for one country or region over one period, like the share of people severely food insecure in 2020 to 2022, or its upper or lower bound.
