ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_EGRID_PLANT_2022.summary: Every U.S. power plant in EPA's eGRID file for 2022: where it is, what fuel it burns, how much power it made and how much pollution it put out.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_EGRID_PLANT_2022.row: One power plant: its location, fuel, 2022 electricity output and 2022 emissions. One stray row holds the file's column codes, not a plant.

cols.TABLE_NAME: The name of the source table or report page the row came from, like S-52 or tri.tri_facility. Empty in the two DHS immigration tables.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state, as two letters like TX in some tables and as a number code like 48 or 06 in others, which needs a lookup and sometimes drops its leading zero. One table writes it like US_TX, and one leaves it empty.
cols.CITY_NAME: The city name. Casing varies, and some rows hold fillers like Not in a City, UNKNOWN or N/A.
cols.POSTAL_CODE: The ZIP or postal code, stored as text, as 5 or 9 digits or a foreign code. Fillers like 00000, UNKNOWN, N/A and -- mean none.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some tables add County, Parish or the state, like Garza County, TX, so clean it before matching. One table uses Undetermined as a filler, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.FRS_ID: The EPA's 12-digit facility registry number, starting 110. Empty in the TRI facility and Envirofacts tables.
cols.HANDLER_ID: The ID of a hazardous waste handler. In the RCRA table it is a 32-character scrambled code, not a readable EPA number; empty in the Envirofacts table.
cols.FACILITY_NAME: The name of the plant, site or building, as the agency wrote it. Generic fillers like RESIDENCE, UNKNOWN, WELL or HOME are common in some tables.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.PROGRAM_SCHEMA: The EPA program the row comes from. TRI, the toxic release program, on every row.
cols.CREATED_DATE: When the record was created. Empty.
cols.MEDIA_NAME: The part of the environment involved, like air or water. Empty.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_ENVIROFACTS.summary: A 5,000-row sample, not the full data: facility names from the EPA's toxic release program, pulled through its Envirofacts service. Good for testing only.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_ENVIROFACTS.row: One facility: one site from the EPA's toxic release program list.

cols.REGISTRY_ID: The EPA's 12-digit master ID for a facility, starting with 110. Links one site across EPA programs.
cols.FACILITY_NAME: The name of the plant, site or building, as the agency wrote it. Generic fillers like RESIDENCE, UNKNOWN, WELL or HOME are common in some tables.
cols.ADDRESS: The full address in one line of text, messy and not split into parts. Some rows hold notes instead, like UNKNOWN, Incarcerated or Moved Out of State, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.SUPPLEMENTAL_LOCATION: Extra free-text location notes, like a mining district, a suite number or directions to the site. Almost always blank; some rows hold the word NULL.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY: The county, usually as a name like Harris, though some tables add the word County and the federal court tables use five-digit number codes, including 88888, which needs a lookup. The UK company table holds UK counties, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.FIPS_CODE: The county's five-digit number code, like 06037, stored as text. One table mixes in state-letter codes like TX155, and one leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state, as two letters like TX in some tables and as a number code like 48 or 06 in others, which needs a lookup and sometimes drops its leading zero. One table writes it like US_TX, and one leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.POSTAL_CODE: The ZIP or postal code, stored as text, as 5 or 9 digits or a foreign code. Fillers like 00000, UNKNOWN, N/A and -- mean none.
cols.CONGRESSIONAL_DISTRICT: The congressional district, written differently per table: a bare number like 05, a state plus number like NJ-11 or AZ3, or a full phrase like Oklahoma, Congressional District 1.
cols.EPA_REGION: The EPA region number, 01 to 10, stored as two-digit text.
cols.FEDERAL_FACILITY_CODE: Whether the site is a federal facility. Written Y or N in some tables, Yes or blank in the EPA facility registry.
cols.FEDERAL_AGENCY: Whether the recipient or facility belongs to the federal government: a t or f flag in the spending tables, and the owning agency's name, like Defense: Army, in the EPA facilities table, where it is mostly blank.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.UPDATE_DATE: When the source last updated this record. Mostly a date; some tables store date and time, one as text.
cols.IS_FEDERAL_FACILITY: True if the facility is run by the federal government. Every row is false in the EPA facility registry, so the flag says nothing there.
cols.IS_ON_TRIBAL_LAND: True if the facility sits on tribal land. Every row is false in the EPA facility registry, so the flag says nothing there.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.SITE_TYPE: What kind of place it is, like STATIONARY, WATER SYSTEM, FACILITY or BROWNFIELDS SITE.
cols.TRIBAL_LAND_CODE: Yes when the site is on tribal land. Blank means not flagged; only about 13,000 rows say Yes.
cols.TRIBAL_LAND_NAME: The name of the tribal land, like NAVAJO NATION. Filled on only about 1,300 rows.
cols.PROGRAM_SYSTEM_ACRONYMS: The EPA programs that track this site and its ID in each, written like RCRAINFO:CAC003109842.
cols.CREATE_DATE: The date the site was added to the registry. 2000-03-01 is very common, likely the first bulk load.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_FRS_FACILITIES.summary: EPA's master list of every place it tracks, from factories and water systems to brownfields: 5.3 million sites with name, address, map point and which EPA programs cover them.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_FRS_FACILITIES.row: One registered facility: one place in EPA's registry, with its address and program IDs.

cols.REGISTRY_ID: The EPA's 12-digit master ID for a facility, starting with 110. Links one site across EPA programs.
cols.FAC_NAME: The name of the facility, like a business, school or clinic. Some rows just say RESIDENCE or UNKNOWN.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.FAC_STREET: The facility's street address. UNKNOWN and NOT AVAILABLE show up as fillers.
cols.FAC_CITY: The facility's city. UNKNOWN shows up as a filler.
cols.FAC_STATE: The facility's state, as two letters.
cols.FAC_ZIP: The facility's ZIP code. 00000, 70000 and UNKNO show up as fillers.
cols.FAC_EPA_REGION: EPA region number as two digits, 01 to 10. Blank on some rows.
cols.LATITUDE_MEASURE: Latitude of the facility's map point. Many facilities share the exact same point.
cols.LONGITUDE_MEASURE: Longitude of the facility's map point. Many facilities share the exact same point.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_FRS_FRS_FACILITIES.summary: EPA's national list of 3.28 million regulated facilities, with name, address, county and map point. It is a different cut from the larger FRS list and holds about 85,000 facilities that one lacks.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_FRS_FRS_FACILITIES.row: One facility: one site EPA tracks, by its registry ID.

cols.PGM_SYS_ID: The ID a specific EPA program uses for the facility, like a permit number. Formats differ by program.
cols.PGM_SYS_ACNRM: Short code for the EPA program that reported the facility, like TRIS, NPDES or AIR.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The industry code, usually six digits like 722110, which needs a lookup to read. Some tables hold shorter codes like 5416, the OSHA inspections table fills most rows with 000000, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.REGISTRY_ID: The EPA's 12-digit master ID for a facility, starting with 110. Links one site across EPA programs.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_FRS_FRS_NAICS_CODES.summary: Industry codes for facilities in the EPA's master facility registry, linking each site to what kind of business runs there.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_FRS_FRS_NAICS_CODES.row: One industry code: one industry code reported for one facility by one EPA program.

cols.PGM_SYS_ACRNM: The short name of the EPA database the record comes from, like ICIS, RCRAINFO, or TRIS.
cols.PGM_SYS_ID: The ID a specific EPA program uses for the facility, like a permit number. Formats differ by program.
cols.REGISTRY_ID: The EPA's 12-digit master ID for a facility, starting with 110. Links one site across EPA programs.
cols.LOCATION_ADDRESS: The street address of the facility. Filler like UNKNOWN or NO ADDRESS ON FILE is common, and some rows give a land survey spot like NW 1/4 SEC 13 T3N R22E instead.
cols.SUPPLEMENTAL_LOCATION: Extra free-text location notes, like a mining district, a suite number or directions to the site. Almost always blank; some rows hold the word NULL.
cols.CITY_NAME: The city name. Casing varies, and some rows hold fillers like Not in a City, UNKNOWN or N/A.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some tables add County, Parish or the state, like Garza County, TX, so clean it before matching. One table uses Undetermined as a filler, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.FIPS_CODE: The county's five-digit number code, like 06037, stored as text. One table mixes in state-letter codes like TX155, and one leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state, as two letters like TX in some tables and as a number code like 48 or 06 in others, which needs a lookup and sometimes drops its leading zero. One table writes it like US_TX, and one leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTRY_NAME: The country's full name, spelled different ways, like USA, US or UNITED STATES. The World Bank debt table also holds groups like Middle income.
cols.POSTAL_CODE: The ZIP or postal code, stored as text, as 5 or 9 digits or a foreign code. Fillers like 00000, UNKNOWN, N/A and -- mean none.
cols.PRIMARY_NAME: Facility name as listed in the program; sometimes a person's name, a street address or just RESIDENCE.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_FRS_FRS_PROGRAM_LIN.summary: EPA's Facility Registry links, 4.4 million of them: each facility's ID in each EPA program system, with name and address.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_FRS_FRS_PROGRAM_LIN.row: One link: one facility's record in one EPA program system.

cols.PGM_SYS_ACNRM: Short code for the EPA program that reported the facility, like TRIS, NPDES or AIR.
cols.SIC_CODE: The four-digit industry code, like 2834 for drug makers. Kept as text so leading zeros like 0783 survive.
cols.REGISTRY_ID: The EPA's 12-digit master ID for a facility, starting with 110. Links one site across EPA programs.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_FRS_FRS_SIC_CODES.summary: The older SIC industry codes attached to EPA-tracked facilities, from the EPA's facility registry, linking each facility's program records to an industry.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_FRS_FRS_SIC_CODES.row: One facility industry code: one SIC code listed for one facility record in one EPA program.

cols.REPORTING_YEAR: The year the report covers, like 2017.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

cols.EMISSION_RECORD_ID: A made-up ID for the row. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.FACILITY_ID: EPA's seven-digit ID for the reporting facility.
cols.SECTOR_ID: The industry sector, as a number code. The codes need a lookup.
cols.SUBSECTOR_ID: The industry subsector, as a number code. The codes need a lookup.
cols.GAS_ID: Which greenhouse gas, as a number code. The codes need a lookup.
cols.CO2E_EMISSION: The emissions, as CO2 equivalent. Blank on about 8% of rows.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_GHGRP_EMISSION.summary: Greenhouse gas emissions reported to the EPA by large US facilities from 2010 on, by gas, sector and subsector, as CO2 equivalent.

cols.REPORTING_YEAR: The year the report covers, like 2017.
cols.FRS_ID: The EPA's 12-digit facility registry number, starting 110. Empty in the TRI facility and Envirofacts tables.
cols.SUBMISSION_ID: The ID of one filing sent to the agency. The EPA table stores it as a decimal like 117560.0000000000.
cols.FACILITY_NAME: The name of the plant, site or building, as the agency wrote it. Generic fillers like RESIDENCE, UNKNOWN, WELL or HOME are common in some tables.
cols.PARENT_COMPANY: The company or body that owns this one. The greenhouse-gas table tacks on the ownership share, like 100%.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The industry code, usually six digits like 722110, which needs a lookup to read. Some tables hold shorter codes like 5416, the OSHA inspections table fills most rows with 000000, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.ADDRESS1: The first line of the street address. Almost always blank in the courthouses table.
cols.ADDRESS2: The second address line, like a suite number. Mostly blank in the research awards table and empty in the other two.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.ZIP: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Fillers like 00000, UNKNO or a lone dash show up, some codes lost a leading zero like 8721, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY: The county, usually as a name like Harris, though some tables add the word County and the federal court tables use five-digit number codes, including 88888, which needs a lookup. The UK company table holds UK counties, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY_FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 01001, stored as text. One table holds only the three-digit county part like 017, one holds N/A, and two leave it empty.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.FACILITY_YEAR_ID: A made-up ID for the facility and year. Each row has its own. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.FACILITY_ID: The EPA's greenhouse-gas program ID for the facility, like 1011659. Use it to follow one facility across years.
cols.EGGRT_FACILITY_ID: The facility's ID in the EPA's online reporting tool, stored as text with a trailing .0000000000.
cols.PROGRAM_SYS_ID: The facility's ID inside the program named in the next column, like 558417 or a 12-digit registry number.
cols.PROGRAM_NAME: Which EPA system the ID in the previous column comes from, like Green House Gas e-GGRT or FRS.
cols.TRIBAL_LAND_ID: A code for the tribal land the facility sits on, stored with a trailing .0000000000. Blank for almost every row; the codes need a lookup.
cols.REPORTED_INDUSTRY_TYPES: Letter codes for the kinds of industry reported, joined by commas, like C or C,D. The codes need a lookup.
cols.FACILITY_TYPES: What kind of reporter the facility is, like Direct Emitter, Supplier or Onshore Oil & Gas Production.
cols.REPORTED_SUBPARTS: Letter codes for the parts of the EPA rule the facility reported under, joined by commas, like C,W. The codes need a lookup.
cols.REPORTING_STATUS: Why the facility stopped reporting, with a valid or an unknown reason. Blank for most rows.
cols.EMISSION_CLASSIFICATION_CODE: A code for how emissions are grouped: DEFAULT, CU_OTHERS or CU_ONLY. The codes need a lookup.
cols.CEMS_USED: Y if the facility measured emissions with continuous monitors in the stack. Blank otherwise.
cols.CO2_CAPTURED: Y if the facility captured carbon dioxide. Blank otherwise.
cols.EMITTED_CO2_SUPPLIED: Y if the facility supplied carbon dioxide it would have emitted. Blank otherwise.
cols.BAMM_USED_DESC: A description of any stand-in measuring methods the facility used. Empty.
cols.BAMM_APPROVED: Whether stand-in measuring methods were approved. Empty.
cols.UU_RD_EXEMPT: Y if the facility was exempt for research and development. Filled on only 19 rows.
cols.PROCESS_STATIONARY_CML: A one-letter code about the facility's stationary combustion and process reporting, like H or Q. Almost always blank; the codes need a lookup.
cols.COMMENTS: A note from the EPA. Filled on only two rows.

cols.FACILITY_TYPE_CODE: The kind of owner, as a code like POF, NON or COR. Needs a lookup.
cols.CURRENT_HPV: Whether the facility has a serious air violation now, like No Violation Identified or Violation-Unresolved.

cols.SEASON_END_DATE: For seasonal systems, the month and day the season ends, like 09-30. Most say 12-31.
cols.PWS_ACTIVITY_CODE: Whether the system is running, as a one-letter code like A or I. The codes need a lookup.
cols.PWS_TYPE_CODE: The kind of system, as a code: CWS, TNCWS, NTNCWS or NP. The codes need a lookup.
cols.DBPR_SCHEDULE_CAT_CODE: The system's schedule group, 1 to 4, under the disinfection byproducts rule. Almost always blank.
cols.CDS_ID: An ID tied to the system that needs a lookup; 9999 shows up often as a placeholder. Almost always blank.
cols.GW_SW_CODE: GW if the water comes from underground, SW if from surface water like rivers and lakes.
cols.LT2_SCHEDULE_CAT_CODE: The system's schedule group, 1 to 5, under the surface water treatment rule. Almost always blank.
cols.OWNER_TYPE_CODE: Who owns the system, as a one-letter code like P, L or F. The codes need a lookup.
cols.POPULATION_SERVED_COUNT: How many people the system serves. 25 is by far the most common, and some say 0.
cols.POP_CAT_2_CODE: The system's size group when sizes are split into 2 groups, as a code 1 or 2 that needs a lookup.
cols.POP_CAT_3_CODE: The system's size group when sizes are split into 3 groups, as a code 1 to 3 that needs a lookup.
cols.POP_CAT_4_CODE: The system's size group when sizes are split into 4 groups, as a code 1 to 4 that needs a lookup.
cols.POP_CAT_5_CODE: The system's size group when sizes are split into 5 groups, as a code 1 to 5 that needs a lookup.
cols.POP_CAT_11_CODE: The system's size group when sizes are split into 11 groups, as a code 1 to 11 that needs a lookup.
cols.PRIMACY_TYPE: What kind of government oversees the system: State, Territory or Tribal.
cols.PRIMARY_SOURCE_CODE: The system's main water source, as a code like GW, SW or GU. The codes need a lookup.
cols.IS_GRANT_ELIGIBLE_IND: Y if the system can get federal grant money.
cols.IS_WHOLESALER_IND: Y if the system sells water to other systems.
cols.IS_SCHOOL_OR_DAYCARE_IND: Y if the system serves a school or daycare.
cols.SERVICE_CONNECTIONS_COUNT: How many pipe hookups the system serves. 1 is by far the most common, at nearly half of systems, and some say 0.
cols.EMAIL_ADDR: An email address for the system's contact. Mostly blank.
cols.PHONE_EXT_NUMBER: The contact's phone extension. Almost always blank, and some hold words like PLANT or just E.
cols.FAX_NUMBER: The contact's fax number. Almost always blank.
cols.ALT_PHONE_NUMBER: A second phone number. Almost always blank, and 9999999999 shows up as a placeholder.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE2: The second line of the contact's address. Mostly blank, and some say NOT AVAILABLE.
cols.SOURCE_WATER_PROTECTION_CODE: Y if the system has a plan to protect its water source. Mostly blank.
cols.SOURCE_PROTECTION_BEGIN_DATE: The date the source protection plan started. Almost always blank.
cols.OUTSTANDING_PERFORMER: Y if the state rated the system an outstanding performer. Almost always blank.
cols.OUTSTANDING_PERFORM_BEGIN_DATE: The date the outstanding performer rating started. Almost always blank.
cols.REDUCED_RTCR_MONITORING: How often the system tests for bacteria under a reduced schedule, like Annual or Quarterly. Capitals vary. Almost always blank.
cols.REDUCED_MONITORING_BEGIN_DATE: The date reduced bacteria testing started. Almost always blank.
cols.REDUCED_MONITORING_END_DATE: The date reduced bacteria testing ended. Almost always blank.
cols.SEASONAL_STARTUP_SYSTEM: For seasonal systems, whether pipes stay pressurized all year. Capitals vary. Almost always blank.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_PUB_WATER.summary: Every public drinking water system on file with the EPA, from city utilities to a campground well, with who runs it, whom it serves and where its water comes from. Most are marked inactive.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_PUB_WATER.row: One water system: one public drinking water system and its contact, size and source details.

cols.SUBMISSIONYEARQUARTER: Which quarterly EPA data release this row came from, like 2026Q2.
cols.PWSID: The public water system's ID, usually two state letters then seven characters, like OK2006367, though a few use longer prefixes like UTAH18050.
cols.FIRST_REPORTED_DATE: The date this record was first reported into the EPA's drinking-water system.
cols.LAST_REPORTED_DATE: The date this record was last reported into the EPA's drinking-water system.
cols.VISIT_ID: The visit's number within its water system, like 1 or #1. Use it together with the water system ID.
cols.AGENCY_TYPE_CODE: Who made the visit, as a two-letter code like ST, CN or DS. The codes need a lookup.
cols.VISIT_REASON_CODE: Why the visit happened, as a four-letter code like SNSV, RSCH or TECH. The codes need a lookup.
cols.MANAGEMENT_OPS_EVAL_CODE: Grade for the system's management and operations, as a letter like N, X, Z, R or M. The codes need a lookup.
cols.SOURCE_WATER_EVAL_CODE: Grade for the system's water source, as a letter like N, X, Z, R or M. The codes need a lookup.
cols.SECURITY_EVAL_CODE: Grade for the system's security, as a letter like N, X, Z, R or M. Mostly blank; the codes need a lookup.
cols.PUMPS_EVAL_CODE: Grade for the system's pumps, as a letter like N, X, Z, R or M. The codes need a lookup.
cols.OTHER_EVAL_CODE: Grade for the system's other items, as a letter like N, X, Z, R or M. The codes need a lookup.
cols.COMPLIANCE_EVAL_CODE: Grade for the system's rule compliance, as a letter like N, X, Z, R or M. The codes need a lookup.
cols.DATA_VERIFICATION_EVAL_CODE: Grade for the system's record checks, as a letter like N, X, Z, R or M. The codes need a lookup.
cols.TREATMENT_EVAL_CODE: Grade for the system's treatment, as a letter like N, X, Z, R or M. The codes need a lookup.
cols.FINISHED_WATER_STOR_EVAL_CODE: Grade for the system's treated-water storage, as a letter like N, X, Z, R or M. The codes need a lookup.
cols.DISTRIBUTION_EVAL_CODE: Grade for the system's pipes and distribution, as a letter like N, X, Z, R or M. The codes need a lookup.
cols.FINANCIAL_EVAL_CODE: Grade for the system's finances, as a letter like N, X, Z, R or M. Mostly blank; the codes need a lookup.
cols.VISIT_COMMENTS: Free-text notes from the visit. Mostly blank.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_SITE_VISI.summary: State and EPA visits to public drinking water systems, like sanitary surveys, with a grade for each part of the system checked.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_SITE_VISI.row: One site visit: one inspection of one water system on one day.

cols.SUBMISSIONYEARQUARTER: Which quarterly EPA data release this row came from, like 2026Q2.
cols.PWSID: The public water system's ID, usually two state letters then seven characters, like OK2006367, though a few use longer prefixes like UTAH18050.
cols.COMPL_PER_BEGIN_DATE: First day of the compliance period the violation covers.
cols.COMPL_PER_END_DATE: Last day of the compliance period the violation covers. Sometimes blank.
cols.NON_COMPL_PER_BEGIN_DATE: The date the water system fell out of compliance.
cols.NON_COMPL_PER_END_DATE: The date the water system got back into compliance. Sometimes blank.
cols.PWS_DEACTIVATION_DATE: The date the public water system was shut down. Blank when there is none, which is most rows in the violations table.
cols.CONTAMINANT_CODE: The EPA's code for the drinking-water contaminant, like PB90 for the lead test or CU90 for copper. Number codes like 2950 need the EPA lookup.
cols.UNIT_OF_MEASURE: The unit the amount is measured in, like Pounds or mg/L. Mostly blank in the drinking-water violations table.
cols.VIOLATION_ID: The number of the drinking water violation. Blank on rows that are only an enforcement action.
cols.FACILITY_ID: The number of the part of the water system involved, like a well or treatment plant. Numbered within each system, so 101 means different things in different systems. Mostly blank.
cols.VIOLATION_CODE: A code for the type of violation. The codes need a lookup.
cols.VIOLATION_CATEGORY_CODE: A short code for the violation group, like MR, MCL, MON or TT. The codes need a lookup.
cols.IS_HEALTH_BASED_IND: Y if the violation was about water quality that can affect health, N if not.
cols.VIOL_MEASURE: The measured amount of the contaminant that broke the limit. Zero is common. A number stored as text. Mostly blank.
cols.FEDERAL_MCL: The federal limit for the contaminant, with units, like 0.005 mg/L, or 5% of samples.
cols.STATE_MCL: The state's limit for the contaminant, when it has its own. Zero is common and likely means none given. Mostly blank.
cols.IS_MAJOR_VIOL_IND: Y if the violation counts as major.
cols.SEVERITY_IND_CNT: A severity count for the violation. Mostly blank.
cols.CALCULATED_RTC_DATE: The date the system came back into compliance, as calculated by EPA. Year-end dates like December 31 are very common.
cols.VIOLATION_STATUS: Where the violation stands: resolved, archived, addressed, or unaddressed.
cols.PUBLIC_NOTIFICATION_TIER: How urgently the public must be told, 1 for most urgent up to 3 for least.
cols.CALCULATED_PUB_NOTIF_TIER: EPA's calculated public notice urgency, 1 to 3. Matches the reported tier in the profile.
cols.VIOL_ORIGINATOR_CODE: A letter code for who recorded the violation, mostly S. The codes need a lookup.
cols.SAMPLE_RESULT_ID: The number of the water test result tied to the violation. Mostly blank.
cols.CORRECTIVE_ACTION_ID: The number of the fix required for the violation. Mostly blank.
cols.RULE_CODE: A three-digit code for the specific drinking water rule broken. The codes need a lookup.
cols.RULE_GROUP_CODE: A three-digit code for the broad group of drinking water rules. The codes need a lookup.
cols.RULE_FAMILY_CODE: A three-digit code for the family of drinking water rules. The codes need a lookup.
cols.VIOL_FIRST_REPORTED_DATE: When the violation was first reported to EPA.
cols.VIOL_LAST_REPORTED_DATE: When the violation record was last updated with EPA.
cols.ENFORCEMENT_ID: The number of the enforcement action. Blank on rows that are only a violation. Placeholder-looking numbers like 9999900000000000001 appear.
cols.ENFORCEMENT_DATE: The day the enforcement action was taken.
cols.ENFORCEMENT_ACTION_TYPE_CODE: A three-letter code for the kind of enforcement action, like SOX or SIE. The codes need a lookup.
cols.ENF_ACTION_CATEGORY: The weight of the action: informal, formal, or resolving.
cols.ENF_ORIGINATOR_CODE: A letter code for who took the action, mostly S. The codes need a lookup.
cols.ENF_FIRST_REPORTED_DATE: When the enforcement action was first reported to EPA.
cols.ENF_LAST_REPORTED_DATE: When the enforcement action record was last updated with EPA.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_VIOLATION.summary: Safe Drinking Water Act violations by public water systems, and the enforcement actions taken against them, from EPA; each row is a violation, an enforcement action, or the two joined, so neither side is filled on every row.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_VIOLATION.row: One violation matched to one enforcement action, or a violation with no action, or an action with no violation.

cols.SITE_NAME: The name of the place, whether a Superfund cleanup site, a mine, a stream gauge, or a health clinic. Many mine rows just say Unknown or Unnamed.
cols.EPA_REGION_CODE: Which of EPA's 10 regions the site is in. Stored as text, sometimes with a leading zero like 02 and sometimes without.
cols.FEDERAL_FACILITY_CODE: Whether the site is a federal facility. Written Y or N in some tables, Yes or blank in the EPA facility registry.
cols.STREET_ADDRESS: The street address, like 4201 IVAR AVE. Some rows hold fillers or directions instead, like TBD, LAT/LONG_USED, PORTABLE SOURCE or 5 MI NE OF.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY: The county, usually as a name like Harris, though some tables add the word County and the federal court tables use five-digit number codes, including 88888, which needs a lookup. The UK company table holds UK counties, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state, as two letters like TX in some tables and as a number code like 48 or 06 in others, which needs a lookup and sometimes drops its leading zero. One table writes it like US_TX, and one leaves it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.PROJECTION: The map coordinate system the location uses, like NAD83 or WGS84.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.BOUNDARY_FEATURE_ID: EPA's number for this boundary feature.
cols.EPA_ID: EPA's ID for the site, like WAD988466355. One site can have several features. Links to other EPA records.
cols.EPA_PROGRAM: The EPA program the feature falls under, mostly Superfund Remedial.
cols.SITE_FEATURE_CLASS: Feature class number: 5, 51 or 52; 5 on almost every row. The codes need a lookup.
cols.SITE_FEATURE_TYPE: What the outline shows, like Comprehensive Site Area or Extent of Contamination.
cols.SITE_FEATURE_NAME: The feature's name, often just Site Boundary.
cols.SITE_FEATURE_DESCRIPTION: A description of the feature, in words.
cols.NPL_STATUS_CODE: The site's status on the national Superfund priority list, as a letter like F, D, N, P or R. The codes need a lookup.
cols.LAST_CHANGE_AT: When the feature was last changed.
cols.ORIGINALLY_CREATED_AT: When the feature was first drawn.
cols.SITE_FEATURE_SOURCE: Where the outline came from, like an EPA region office or a state map. Some say Unknown.
cols.ADDRESS_COMMENT: Notes on where the site is. Mostly blank, with placeholders like N/A and <Null>.
cols.SITE_CONTACT_NAME: The EPA contact person for the site.
cols.SITE_URL: EPA's web page for the site.
cols.FEATURE_INFO_URL: A link to a document about the boundary.
cols.GIS_AREA: Size of the area, in the unit given in GIS_AREA_UNITS. Some are 0.
cols.GIS_AREA_UNITS: The unit for GIS_AREA: mostly Acres, also Square Miles or Miles, in mixed spelling.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SUPERFUND_SITE_BOUN.summary: EPA Superfund site boundary records, 2,114 features across 1,908 sites; only the details were loaded, not the map shapes.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SUPERFUND_SITE_BOUN.row: One boundary feature: one mapped outline or area at one Superfund site.

cols.FACILITY_NAME: The name of the plant, site or building, as the agency wrote it. Generic fillers like RESIDENCE, UNKNOWN, WELL or HOME are common in some tables.
cols.STREET_ADDRESS: The street address, like 4201 IVAR AVE. Some rows hold fillers or directions instead, like TBD, LAT/LONG_USED, PORTABLE SOURCE or 5 MI NE OF.
cols.CITY_NAME: The city name. Casing varies, and some rows hold fillers like Not in a City, UNKNOWN or N/A.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some tables add County, Parish or the state, like Garza County, TX, so clean it before matching. One table uses Undetermined as a filler, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.STATE_COUNTY_FIPS_CODE: The county's five-digit government code, where the first two digits are the state. Kept as text so leading zeros survive.
cols.STATE_ABBR: The state, as two letters like TX. Territories like PR and GU show up, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.MAIL_CITY: The city of the mailing address.
cols.MAIL_ZIP_CODE: The mailing zip code, stored as text. ATF's feed drops leading zeros; that table zero-fills them back to 5 digits, or 9 for a zip+4.
cols.FRS_ID: The EPA's 12-digit facility registry number, starting 110. Empty in the TRI facility and Envirofacts tables.
cols.EPA_REGISTRY_ID: EPA's 12-digit ID for the facility, starting 110. Stored as text.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.TRI_FACILITY_ID: EPA's 15-character ID for the facility in the Toxics Release Inventory. Each row has its own value.
cols.REGION: The EPA region the facility sits in, a number from 1 to 10.
cols.FAC_CLOSED_IND: Whether the facility has closed, as code 0, 1 or 2 that needs a lookup. Most are 0.
cols.MAIL_NAME: The name on the facility's mailing address.
cols.MAIL_STREET_ADDRESS: The facility's mailing street address, often a P.O. box.
cols.MAIL_STATE_ABBR: State of the mailing address, as two letters.
cols.MAIL_PROVINCE: Province of the mailing address, for the handful outside the US. Almost always blank.
cols.MAIL_COUNTRY: Country of the mailing address, United States or Canada. Almost always blank.
cols.ASGN_FEDERAL_IND: Whether the facility is federal, as code C, F or G that needs a lookup. Almost all are C.
cols.ASGN_AGENCY: The federal agency that runs the facility, like DOD, DOJ or TVA. Blank for all but a few hundred facilities.
cols.PARENT_CO_DB_NUM: The parent company's nine-digit Dun & Bradstreet number. Blank for about 4 in 10.
cols.PARENT_CO_NAME: The parent company's name as the facility wrote it. Blank for about a third.
cols.FAC_LATITUDE: The facility's latitude as reported, packed as degrees, minutes and seconds like 474045, not decimal. 0 is a placeholder.
cols.FAC_LONGITUDE: The facility's longitude as reported, packed as degrees, minutes and seconds like 1191659, with no minus sign. 0 is a placeholder.
cols.PREF_LATITUDE: EPA's preferred latitude for the facility, in decimal degrees. Blank for about 4 in 10.
cols.PREF_LONGITUDE: EPA's preferred longitude in decimal degrees, stored without the minus sign, so western US longitudes read positive. Blank for about 4 in 10.
cols.PREF_ACCURACY: The stated accuracy of the preferred coordinates, stored as text like 150.00. 99999.00 looks like a placeholder.
cols.PREF_COLLECT_METH: How the preferred coordinates were collected, as a code like A1 or I1 that needs a lookup. UN is the most common value.
cols.PREF_DESC_CATEGORY: What spot on the site the coordinates mark, as a code like PG or FC that needs a lookup. UN is the most common value.
cols.PREF_HORIZONTAL_DATUM: The map reference system of the coordinates, code 1, 2 or U that needs a lookup.
cols.PREF_SOURCE_SCALE: Map scale of the coordinate source, code U, J or E that needs a lookup.
cols.PREF_QA_CODE: Quality-check code for the coordinates, like 1010 or 0000, which needs a lookup.
cols.ASGN_PARTIAL_IND: Whether the report covers only part of the facility, 0 or 1. Almost all are 0.
cols.ASGN_PUBLIC_CONTACT: Name of the facility's public contact person, sometimes a department instead.
cols.ASGN_PUBLIC_PHONE: Phone number of the public contact, ten digits.
cols.ASGN_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL: Email of the public contact. Blank for about 4 in 10.
cols.BIA_CODE: Bureau of Indian Affairs tribe code for facilities on tribal land; the codes need a lookup. Almost always blank.
cols.STANDARDIZED_PARENT_COMPANY: The parent company's name cleaned up by EPA so spellings match across facilities. Blank for about 6 in 10.
cols.ASGN_PUBLIC_PHONE_EXT: Phone extension for the public contact. Mostly blank.
cols.ASGN_TECHNICAL_CONTACT: Name of the facility's technical contact. Empty in this table.
cols.ASGN_TECHNICAL_PHONE: Phone of the technical contact. Empty in this table.
cols.ASGN_TECHNICAL_PHONE_EXT: Phone extension of the technical contact. Empty in this table.
cols.MAIL: A mail column with no values; the name does not say what it held. Empty in this table.
cols.ASGN_TECHNICAL_CONTACT_EMAIL: Email of the technical contact. Empty in this table.
cols.FOREIGN_PARENT_CO_NAME: The foreign parent company's name as written, like CRH PLC or CEMEX SAB DE CV. Almost always blank.
cols.FOREIGN_PARENT_CO_DB_NUM: The foreign parent's Dun & Bradstreet number. Almost always blank.
cols.STANDARDIZED_FOREIGN_PARENT_COMPANY: The foreign parent's name cleaned up by EPA so spellings match. Almost always blank.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_TRI_FACILITY.summary: Every facility that reports toxic chemical releases to EPA's Toxics Release Inventory, with its address, contacts, parent companies and map coordinates.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_TRI_FACILITY.row: One toxic-release reporting facility: its location, contacts and parent companies.

cols.DISCLOSURE_ID: FracFocus's long ID for one fracking chemical disclosure, a random-looking code with dashes. Use it to join FracFocus tables.
cols.API_NUMBER: The well's 14-digit API number, the standard U.S. oil and gas well ID. Keep it as text; the first two digits are the state.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some tables add County, Parish or the state, like Garza County, TX, so clean it before matching. One table uses Undetermined as a filler, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.OPERATOR_NAME: The company that runs the well, pipeline, or mine.
cols.WELL_NAME: The name the operator gave the oil or gas well, like Kothmann Ranch 26H. Some orphaned-well rows just say NO NAME or FEE.
cols.PROJECTION: The map coordinate system the location uses, like NAD83 or WGS84.
cols.FF_VERSION: Which version of the FracFocus form was used, 1 to 4.
cols.FEDERAL_WELL: True if the well is on federal land. Stored as the text True or False.
cols.INDIAN_WELL: True if the well is on tribal land. Stored as the text True or False.
cols.JOB_START_DATE: The date the fracking job started. Empty in both FracFocus tables.
cols.JOB_END_DATE: The date the fracking job ended. Empty in both FracFocus tables.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.TVD: How deep the well goes straight down, likely in feet. Some rows show 0.
cols.TOTAL_BASE_WATER_VOLUME: How much water was pumped into the well, likely in gallons.
cols.TOTAL_BASE_NON_WATER_VOLUME: How much non-water base fluid was pumped into the well. Often 0.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_FILE: The name of the source file this row was read from, like 2___Plant_Y2024.xlsx. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_FRACFOCUS_DISCLOSURE_LI.summary: Every fracking job disclosure filed with the FracFocus registry, with the operator, well number, location, and how much water and other fluid was used. The job start and end date columns are empty.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_FRACFOCUS_DISCLOSURE_LI.row: One disclosure: one well's fracking job, as reported by the operator.

cols.PURPOSE_ID: FracFocus's code for the additive and purpose this ingredient belongs to. Several ingredients share one.
cols.INGREDIENTS_ID: FracFocus's code for this ingredient entry. Blank for about 11% of rows.
cols.CAS_NUMBER: The chemical's standard registry number, like 7732-18-5 for water. Many rows say Proprietary or Confidential instead, hiding the chemical.
cols.SUPPLIER: The company that supplied the additive, like Halliburton. Many rows hold stand-ins like Ingredient Container or Listed Above.
cols.PURPOSE: What the additive does, like Friction Reducer or Biocide. Many rows hold stand-ins like Ingredient Container Purpose or a note pointing to the trade name list.
cols.INGREDIENT_COMMON_NAME: The chemical's plain name, like Water or Hydrochloric acid. Typos appear, like Methyl Alchol. Blank for about 30%.
cols.INGREDIENT_COMMENT: Free-text notes on the ingredient, like Proprietary CAS. Almost always blank.
cols.INGREDIENT_MSDS: True if the chemical is listed on the product's safety data sheet. Blank for about 11%.
cols.CLAIMANT_COMPANY: The company claiming the chemical as a trade secret, like Halliburton. Almost always blank, and some say Null or just a dash.
cols.PERCENT_HIGH_ADDITIVE: The most this chemical can make up of its additive product, as a percent.
cols.PERCENT_HF_JOB: How much of the whole fracking fluid this chemical makes up, as a percent. 0 is common.
cols.MASS_INGREDIENT: How much of the chemical was used, by weight; the unit is not stated. 0 shows up for about a quarter of rows.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_FRACFOCUS_REGISTRY.summary: Every chemical that oil and gas operators disclosed pumping into wells during fracking, as reported to the FracFocus registry, with the well, supplier and amounts. Many chemical ID numbers are hidden as trade secrets.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_FRACFOCUS_REGISTRY.row: One ingredient line: one chemical in one additive, used for one purpose, in one well's fracking job.

cols.DISCLOSURE_ID: FracFocus's long ID for one fracking chemical disclosure, a random-looking code with dashes. Use it to join FracFocus tables.
cols.API_NUMBER: The well's 14-digit API number, the standard U.S. oil and gas well ID. Keep it as text; the first two digits are the state.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some tables add County, Parish or the state, like Garza County, TX, so clean it before matching. One table uses Undetermined as a filler, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.OPERATOR_NAME: The company that runs the well, pipeline, or mine.
cols.WELL_NAME: The name the operator gave the oil or gas well, like Kothmann Ranch 26H. Some orphaned-well rows just say NO NAME or FEE.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_FILE: The name of the source file this row was read from, like 2___Plant_Y2024.xlsx. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.WATER_SOURCE_ID: FracFocus's long code for the water source line.
cols.DESCRIPTION: The kind of water, like groundwater, surface water or produced water, and whether it had under or over 1000 of total dissolved solids.
cols.PERCENT: The share of the job's base water that came from this source, in percent. 100 is most common.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_FRACFOCUS_WATER_SOURCE.summary: Where the water came from for fracking jobs reported to FracFocus, the national fracking chemical registry, like groundwater, surface water or recycled oilfield water, with each source's share.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_FRACFOCUS_WATER_SOURCE.row: One water source: one source of water used in one well's fracking job, with its share of the water.

cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY: The county, usually as a name like Harris, though some tables add the word County and the federal court tables use five-digit number codes, including 88888, which needs a lookup. The UK company table holds UK counties, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.CONGRESSIONAL_DISTRICT: The congressional district, written differently per table: a bare number like 05, a state plus number like NJ-11 or AZ3, or a full phrase like Oklahoma, Congressional District 1.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.NID_ID: The national dam ID, two state letters and five digits, like OH00433. Blank on two rows.
cols.OTHER_STRUCTURE_ID: A tag like S001 for an extra structure that belongs to a dam. Almost always blank.
cols.FEDERAL_ID: The federal dam ID, in the same form as NID_ID, like OH00433.
cols.DAM_NAME: The dam's name, like Lake Milton Dam.
cols.OTHER_NAMES: Other names the dam or its lake goes by. Mostly blank.
cols.FORMER_NAMES: Names the dam used to have. Mostly blank, and 0 shows up as a placeholder.
cols.OWNER_NAMES: Who owns the dam, like BUREAU OF RECLAMATION or a local district. Several owners can share one cell.
cols.OWNER_TYPES: The kind of owner, like Private or Local Government. Several types are joined with a semicolon.
cols.PRIMARY_OWNER_TYPE: The main kind of owner: Private, Local Government, State, Federal, Public Utility, Tribal Government or Not Listed.
cols.IS_ASSOCIATED_STRUCTURE: True when this row is an extra structure tied to a main dam rather than a dam itself.
cols.PRIMARY_PURPOSE: What the dam is mainly for, like Recreation or Flood Risk Reduction.
cols.PURPOSES: All the dam's uses, joined in one cell.
cols.SOURCE_AGENCY: The state that sent in the dam's record, like Texas.
cols.RIVER_OR_STREAM: The river or creek the dam sits on. Unknown and Tr-, meaning a tributary, are common.
cols.IS_STATE_REGULATED: True when a state agency regulates the dam.
cols.IS_FEDERALLY_REGULATED: True when a federal agency regulates the dam.
cols.STATE_REGULATORY_AGENCY: The state agency that regulates the dam, spelled many ways, like Owrb or Iowa DNR.
cols.FEDERAL_AGENCY_OWNERS: The federal agency that owns the dam, like US Army Corps of Engineers. Almost always blank.
cols.PRIMARY_DAM_TYPE: What the dam is built of or how, like Earth or Concrete. Earth is by far the most common.
cols.NID_HEIGHT_CATEGORY: The dam's height as a band, like Less than 25 feet.
cols.YEAR_COMPLETED: The year the dam was finished.
cols.NID_STORAGE_ACRE_FT: How much water the dam can hold, in acre-feet.
cols.MAX_STORAGE_ACRE_FT: The most water the dam can hold at the top of the dam, in acre-feet.
cols.NORMAL_STORAGE_ACRE_FT: How much water the dam usually holds, in acre-feet. 0 is common.
cols.SURFACE_AREA_ACRES: The size of the lake behind the dam at normal level, in acres.
cols.DRAINAGE_AREA_SQ_MILES: How much land drains into the dam, in square miles. 0 is common.
cols.MAX_DISCHARGE_CFS: The most water the spillway can release, in cubic feet per second. Mostly blank, and 0 is common.
cols.SPILLWAY_TYPE: Whether the spillway has gates: Controlled or Uncontrolled. Blank on about half of rows.
cols.DATA_LAST_UPDATED: When the dam's record was last updated.
cols.LAST_INSPECTION_DATE: When the dam was last inspected. 1980-01-01 shows up often and looks like a placeholder.
cols.INSPECTION_FREQUENCY: How often the dam is supposed to be inspected, in years, like 5. 0 is common.
cols.HAZARD_POTENTIAL: How bad it would be if the dam failed: High, Significant, Low or Undetermined.
cols.CONDITION_ASSESSMENT: The dam's condition: Satisfactory, Fair, Poor, Unsatisfactory, Not Rated or Not Available.
cols.CONDITION_ASSESSMENT_DATE: When the condition was last rated. Mostly blank.
cols.OPERATIONAL_STATUS: Whether problems are being worked on, like Under Remediation or Enforcement Pending. Mostly blank.
cols.HAS_EMERGENCY_ACTION_PLAN: True when the dam has an emergency plan for a failure.
cols.EAP_LAST_REVISION_DATE: When the emergency plan was last updated. Mostly blank.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_NID_DAMS.summary: Every dam in the Army Corps of Engineers' National Inventory of Dams, with its owner, size, hazard rating, condition and inspection dates.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_NID_DAMS.row: One dam or structure: its name, owner, size, hazard rating and last inspection.

cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.STATE_FIPS: The state's number code, like 48 or 06, which needs a lookup. Several tables drop the leading zero so 6 means 06, some rows hold other codes like C1, TX, 00 or N/A, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.MONTH_NAME: The month spelled out, like January. One calendar table uses short forms like Jan.
cols.BEGIN_YEARMONTH: Year and month the event began, as a six-digit number like 200806.
cols.BEGIN_DAY: Day of the month the event began.
cols.BEGIN_TIME: Local clock time the event began, as a number like 1200 for noon; 0 is midnight.
cols.END_YEARMONTH: Year and month the event ended, as a six-digit number like 200806.
cols.END_DAY: Day of the month the event ended.
cols.END_TIME: Local clock time the event ended, as a number like 1800; 2359 is common for all-day events.
cols.EPISODE_ID: ID of the larger storm episode; several events can belong to one episode.
cols.EVENT_ID: ID of this single event. Each row has its own value.
cols.EVENT_TYPE: Kind of weather, like Thunderstorm Wind, Hail or Flash Flood.
cols.CZ_TYPE: Place type code, C, Z or M; codes need a lookup.
cols.CZ_FIPS: County or zone number within the state, without leading zeros.
cols.CZ_NAME: Name of the county or forecast zone.
cols.WFO: Three-letter code of the Weather Service office that logged it, like LWX.
cols.BEGIN_DATE_TIME: Start date and time as text, like 13-JUN-17 17:00:00, with a two-digit year.
cols.CZ_TIMEZONE: Time zone of the listed times, written two ways, like CST-6 and CST.
cols.END_DATE_TIME: End date and time as text, like 24-NOV-00 12:00:00, with a two-digit year.
cols.INJURIES_DIRECT: People injured directly by the event. 0 on almost all rows.
cols.INJURIES_INDIRECT: People injured indirectly, like in a crash on an icy road. 0 on almost all rows.
cols.DEATHS_DIRECT: People killed directly by the event. 0 on almost all rows.
cols.DEATHS_INDIRECT: People killed indirectly. 0 on almost all rows.
cols.DAMAGE_PROPERTY: Property damage as text with a letter for scale, like 10.00K; convert before adding up. Blank on about a third of rows.
cols.DAMAGE_CROPS: Crop damage as text with a letter for scale, like 5.00K or 5K; convert before adding up. Blank on about 4 in 10 rows, and almost always 0 when filled.
cols.SOURCE: Who reported the event, like Trained Spotter or Public; the same source appears in both upper and mixed case.
cols.MAGNITUDE: Strength of the event: a wind speed like 50 or a hail size like 0.75, depending on event type. Blank on about half of rows.
cols.MAGNITUDE_TYPE: How the wind speed was measured, codes like EG, MG or E that need a lookup. Blank on most rows.
cols.FLOOD_CAUSE: Cause of a flood, like Heavy Rain or Ice Jam. Blank for non-flood events.
cols.CATEGORY: Storm category, 1 to 5. Filled on only 560 rows.
cols.TOR_F_SCALE: Tornado strength on the F or EF scale, like EF0 or F2; EFU needs a lookup. Blank for non-tornado events.
cols.TOR_LENGTH: Tornado path length in miles. Blank for non-tornado events.
cols.TOR_WIDTH: Tornado path width in yards, stored as text. Blank for non-tornado events.
cols.TOR_OTHER_WFO: Weather office for the next area a tornado crossed into. Filled on few rows.
cols.TOR_OTHER_CZ_STATE: State of the next area a tornado crossed into, as two letters. Filled on few rows.
cols.TOR_OTHER_CZ_FIPS: County number of the next area a tornado crossed into, three digits. Filled on few rows.
cols.TOR_OTHER_CZ_NAME: County name of the next area a tornado crossed into. Filled on few rows.
cols.BEGIN_RANGE: Distance in miles from the reference place to where the event began. Mostly blank.
cols.BEGIN_AZIMUTH: Compass direction from the reference place to where the event began, like N or SW. Mostly blank.
cols.BEGIN_LOCATION: Reference place for where the event began, like a town; COUNTYWIDE is common.
cols.END_RANGE: Distance in miles from the reference place to where the event ended. Mostly blank.
cols.END_AZIMUTH: Compass direction from the reference place to where the event ended. Mostly blank.
cols.END_LOCATION: Reference place for where the event ended, like a town; COUNTYWIDE is common.
cols.BEGIN_LAT: Latitude where the event began, stored as text. Blank on about 40% of rows.
cols.BEGIN_LON: Longitude where the event began, negative in the US, stored as text. Blank on about 40% of rows.
cols.END_LAT: Latitude where the event ended, stored as text. Blank on about 40% of rows.
cols.END_LON: Longitude where the event ended, stored as text. Blank on about 40% of rows.
cols.EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Written summary of the whole storm episode.
cols.EVENT_NARRATIVE: Written account of this event, like Trees down.
cols.DATA_SOURCE: Which NOAA file format the row came from: CSV, PDS or PDC.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_NOAA_STORM_EVENTS.summary: Every storm and severe weather event logged by the National Weather Service, 1.78 million events, with where and when it hit, deaths, injuries, damage and a written account.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_NOAA_STORM_EVENTS.row: One storm event: one kind of weather in one county or forecast zone, from start time to end time.

cols.GEOMETRY: The shape of the area on a map, as GeoJSON map coordinates. Mostly blank in the NOAA weather table.
cols.TEMPERATURE: The air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit when the rail incident happened. Empty in the weather table.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.FIPS_CODE: The county's five-digit number code, like 06037, stored as text. One table mixes in state-letter codes like TX155, and one leaves it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.ID: The alert's web address at the National Weather Service, which works as its ID.
cols.EVENT: The kind of alert, like Heat Advisory or Flood Warning.
cols.STATUS: Actual for real alerts; one row is a Test.
cols.MESSAGE_TYPE: Alert for a new alert, Update for a change to one.
cols.SEVERITY: How severe the weather is: Severe, Moderate, Minor or Unknown.
cols.CERTAINTY: How sure forecasters are: Observed, Likely, Possible or Unknown.
cols.URGENCY: How soon people need to act: Immediate, Expected, Future, Past or Unknown.
cols.AREA_DESC: The counties or zones covered, in words, separated by semicolons.
cols.ONSET: When the weather is expected to start.
cols.ENDS: When the weather is expected to end. Blank on some rows.
cols.HEADLINE: The alert's one-line headline.
cols.DESCRIPTION: The full alert text: what, where, when and impacts.
cols.INSTRUCTION: What the Weather Service tells people to do, like drink plenty of fluids. Blank on about 30% of rows.
cols.SENDER_NAME: The Weather Service office that sent the alert, like NWS Anchorage AK.
cols.ZONE_UGC: Web links to the forecast zones the alert covers.
cols.STATION_ID: Meant for a weather station ID. Empty in this table.
cols.WIND_SPEED: Meant for wind speed. Empty in this table.
cols.WIND_DIRECTION: Meant for wind direction. Empty in this table.
cols.TIMESTAMP: Meant for an observation time. Empty in this table.
cols.FORECAST_OFFICE: Meant for the forecast office. Empty in this table.
cols.GRID_X: Meant for the forecast grid column. Empty in this table.
cols.GRID_Y: Meant for the forecast grid row. Empty in this table.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_NOAA_WEATHER_API.summary: A small pull of 287 National Weather Service alerts from early July 2026, like heat advisories, flood warnings and small craft advisories.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_NOAA_WEATHER_API.row: One weather alert, or one update to an alert, from one Weather Service office.

cols.REPORT_NUMBER: The agency's ID number for the incident or bad-reaction report. The format differs by source.
cols.REPORT_RECEIVED_DATE: The date the agency received the report.
cols.INCIDENT_YEAR: The year the incident happened, like 2005. The rail crossing table holds two-digit values like 13 instead.
cols.OPERATOR_NAME: The company that runs the well, pipeline, or mine.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.SUPPLEMENTAL_NUMBER: A number for the latest version of the report, since operators file updates.
cols.REPORT_TYPE: Whether this is the first or an updated report, and whether it is final, like SUPPLEMENTAL FINAL or ORIGINAL.
cols.NRC_REPORT_NUMBER: The report number from the National Response Center, where spills are first phoned in. A few are blank.
cols.LOCAL_DATETIME: The local date and time the accident happened.
cols.TIME_ZONE: The time zone of the accident, like CENTRAL or EASTERN. Blank for most rows.
cols.PHMSA_OPERATOR_ID: The pipeline safety agency's ID number for the company running the pipeline. Use it to join to other pipeline tables.
cols.OPERATOR_STREET_ADDRESS: The street address of the pipeline company.
cols.OPERATOR_CITY: The city of the pipeline company, mostly Houston.
cols.OPERATOR_STATE: The state of the pipeline company, as two letters.
cols.OPERATOR_POSTAL_CODE: The ZIP code of the pipeline company.
cols.LOCATION_LATITUDE: The latitude of the accident site.
cols.LOCATION_LONGITUDE: The longitude of the accident site.
cols.COMMODITY_RELEASED_TYPE: What escaped, almost always NATURAL GAS, sometimes hydrogen or landfill gas.
cols.COMMODITY_DETAILS: More detail on what escaped when it was not plain natural gas, like DRY GAS. Blank for almost every row.
cols.UNINTENTIONAL_RELEASE_VOLUME: How much gas leaked by accident. The unit is not stated in the table.
cols.INTENTIONAL_RELEASE_VOLUME: How much gas was let out on purpose, such as to make the line safe. Mostly 0; the unit is not stated in the table.
cols.FATALITY_IND: YES if anyone died, NO if not.
cols.NUM_EMPLOYEE_FATALITIES: How many of the operator's employees died. Filled only when someone died, so blank for almost every row.
cols.NUM_CONTRACTOR_FATALITIES: How many contractors died. Filled on only about 20 rows, and most of those say 0.
cols.NUM_EMERGENCY_RESPONDER_FATALITIES: How many firefighters or other responders died. Filled only when someone died, and 0 on every filled row.
cols.NUM_WORKER_FATALITIES: How many workers died. Filled only when someone died, so blank for almost every row.
cols.NUM_PUBLIC_FATALITIES: How many members of the public died. Filled only when someone died, so blank for almost every row.
cols.TOTAL_FATALITIES: How many people died in all. Use this column to count deaths; almost all rows are 0.
cols.INJURY_IND: YES if anyone was hurt, NO if not.
cols.NUM_EMPLOYEE_INJURIES: How many of the operator's employees were hurt. Filled only when someone was hurt.
cols.NUM_CONTRACTOR_INJURIES: How many contractors were hurt. Filled only when someone was hurt.
cols.NUM_EMERGENCY_RESPONDER_INJURIES: How many responders were hurt. Filled only when someone was hurt, and 0 on every filled row.
cols.NUM_WORKER_INJURIES: How many workers were hurt. Filled only when someone was hurt.
cols.NUM_PUBLIC_INJURIES: How many members of the public were hurt. Filled only when someone was hurt.
cols.STATUS_WHEN_IDENTIFIED: What the pipeline was doing when the problem was found, like normal operation or idle. Blank for most rows.
cols.SHUTDOWN_DUE_ACCIDENT_IND: YES if the pipeline was shut down because of the accident, NO if not.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_PHMSA_FLAGGED_INCIDENTS.summary: Serious accidents on natural gas transmission and gathering pipelines since 2010, as reported to the federal pipeline safety agency: who ran the pipe, where, how much gas escaped, and who was killed or hurt. Other kinds of pipelines are not in this table yet.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_PHMSA_FLAGGED_INCIDENTS.row: One incident report: one pipeline accident, as filed by the operator.

cols.SEQNOS: The National Response Center's report number. A number stored as text.
cols.CALL_TYPE: The kind of call to the National Response Center, almost always INC for an incident. A few rows say DRL, which needs a lookup.
cols.RESPONSIBLE_COMPANY: The company named as responsible for the spill or incident, like CHEVRON or BP. Often blank.
cols.RESPONSIBLE_ORG_TYPE: What kind of party was responsible, like PRIVATE ENTERPRISE, MILITARY or UNKNOWN.
cols.RESPONSIBLE_CITY: The city of the responsible party. Often blank.
cols.RESPONSIBLE_STATE: The responsible party's state, as two letters. XX means unknown.
cols.RESPONSIBLE_ZIP: The responsible party's zip code, stored as text. Mostly blank, and some carry a stray .0 on the end like 30303.0.
cols.DATE_TIME_RECEIVED: When the National Response Center got the call, date and time.
cols.DATE_TIME_COMPLETE: When the call report was finished, date and time.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.SOURCE: How the report came in, like TELEPHONE or WEB REPORT. UNAVAILABLE fills about a third of rows.
cols.SRC_YEAR: The year of the yearly file the report came from.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_USCG_NRC_INCIDENTS.summary: Spills, leaks and chemical releases reported to the Coast Guard's National Response Center.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_USCG_NRC_INCIDENTS.row: One call to the National Response Center: the type of incident, the company responsible, and when it came in.
