ENVIRONMENT__FED_USCG_NRC_INCIDENT_REPOR.summary: A secondary copy of Coast Guard National Response Center reports of spills and other incidents, 116,662 reports; the main copy of the same feed is a separate million-row table.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_USCG_NRC_INCIDENT_REPOR.row: One incident report: one call to the National Response Center.

cols.COUNTRY: The country, written different ways by table: a full name, a two- or three-letter code, or a number code that needs a lookup. Some rows hold a region like World or a UK nation like England, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 06037. One table holds two-digit state codes instead, and nine tables leave it empty.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.RANK: The row's place in a ranked list, where 1 is first. Empty in the USGS minerals table.
cols.VALUE_USD: A dollar value. Filled in the SEC 13F holdings table, empty in the USGS minerals table.
cols.URL: A web link to the record's own page at the source.
cols.SITE_NAME: The name of the place, whether a Superfund cleanup site, a mine, a stream gauge, or a health clinic. Many mine rows just say Unknown or Unnamed.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY: The county, usually as a name like Harris, though some tables add the word County and the federal court tables use five-digit number codes, including 88888, which needs a lookup. The UK company table holds UK counties, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COMMODITY: Meant for the commodity; use COMMOD1 to COMMOD3. Empty in this table.
cols.PRODUCTION_QUANTITY: Meant for how much was produced. Empty in this table.
cols.PRODUCTION_UNIT: Meant for the unit for production. Empty in this table.
cols.RESERVES: Meant for reserves. Empty in this table.
cols.IMPORT_RELIANCE_PCT: Meant for import reliance as a percent. Empty in this table.
cols.US_STATE: Meant for the US state. Empty in this table.
cols.DATA_SOURCE_NOTES: Meant for notes on the data source. Empty in this table.
cols.DEP_ID: The USGS ID for the site. Nearly every row has its own.
cols.MRDS_ID: The site's ID in the USGS Mineral Resources Data System, like DC04243. Filled on about half of rows.
cols.MAS_ID: An older 10-digit federal mine-file ID for the site. Filled on about 63% of rows.
cols.REGION: World region for sites outside the US, as two letters like SA, AS, EU or AF. Mostly blank; the codes need a lookup.
cols.COM_TYPE: Kind of commodity, as one letter: M, N, B or E. The codes need a lookup.
cols.COMMOD1: The main commodities at the site, like Gold or Copper; several can be listed together.
cols.COMMOD2: Secondary commodities at the site. Mostly blank.
cols.COMMOD3: Minor commodities at the site. Mostly blank.
cols.OPER_TYPE: How the site is or was worked, like Surface, Underground or Placer. Unknown on about half of rows.
cols.DEP_TYPE: The kind of deposit, like Vein or Placer. Mostly blank.
cols.PROD_SIZE: How big the site's production was, as a letter like S, N, Y, U or M. Mostly blank; the codes need a lookup.
cols.DEV_STAT: How far the site got: Producer, Past Producer, Prospect, Occurrence or Unknown.
cols.ORE: The ore minerals found, like Gold or Chromite. Mostly blank.
cols.GANGUE: The worthless minerals mixed in with the ore, like Quartz. Mostly blank.
cols.OTHER_MATL: Other minerals present at the site. Mostly blank.
cols.OREBODY_FM: The shape of the ore body, like TABULAR or IRREGULAR. Mostly blank.
cols.WORK_TYPE: Kind of mine workings, like Underground or Surface. Mostly blank.
cols.MODEL: The geologic deposit model, as a number plus a name, like '85: Polymetallic veins'. Mostly blank.
cols.ALTERATION: How the rock around the ore was changed, like Silicification. Mostly blank.
cols.CONC_PROC: What concentrated the ore, like Hydrothermal. Mostly blank.
cols.NAMES: Other names for the site. Mostly blank.
cols.ORE_CTRL: What controls where the ore sits, like a Shear Zone or Fault. Mostly blank.
cols.REPORTER: Who recorded the site: a person or a federal field office.
cols.HROCK_UNIT: The named rock formation that holds the deposit. Mostly blank.
cols.HROCK_TYPE: The kind of rock that holds the deposit, like Limestone. Mostly blank.
cols.AROCK_UNIT: A named rock formation near the deposit. Mostly blank.
cols.AROCK_TYPE: The kind of rock near the deposit, like Diorite. Mostly blank.
cols.STRUCTURE: Local geologic structure, like a fault or batholith. Mostly blank.
cols.TECTONIC: The broad geologic setting, like Basin And Range. Mostly blank.
cols.REF: Source references for the site's information, in free text.
cols.YFP_BA: Marks the first production year as before or after: < or >. Filled on under 1% of rows.
cols.YR_FST_PRD: Year the site first produced. Mostly blank.
cols.YLP_BA: Marks the last production year as before or after: < or >. Filled on under 1% of rows.
cols.YR_LST_PRD: Year the site last produced. Mostly blank.
cols.DY_BA: Marks the discovery year as before or after: < or >. Filled on under 1% of rows.
cols.DISC_YR: Year the site was discovered. Mostly blank.
cols.PROD_YRS: Years of production, as free text like '1901 - 1948'. Mostly blank.
cols.DISCR: Who discovered the site. Mostly blank.
cols.SCORE: A record-quality grade from A to E; D covers most rows. The grades need a lookup.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_USGS_MINERALS.summary: The USGS list of mineral sites around the world, mostly in the US: mines, past mines, prospects and known deposits, with what they hold and the rock around them.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_USGS_MINERALS.row: One mineral site: one mine, prospect or known deposit.

cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY: The county, usually as a name like Harris, though some tables add the word County and the federal court tables use five-digit number codes, including 88888, which needs a lookup. The UK company table holds UK counties, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.WELL_NAME: The name the operator gave the oil or gas well, like Kothmann Ranch 26H. Some orphaned-well rows just say NO NAME or FEE.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.WELL_RECORD_ID: A made-up ID for one well record. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.WELL_IDENTIFIER: The well's ID with a label in front, like API:37121270180000 or USGSID:KS4969. Usually the API well number.
cols.WELL_NUMBER: The well's number on its lease, like 1 or 2. Blank on more than half the rows.
cols.TYPE: The kind of well, spelled many ways, like OIL, O or Oil Well. Codes like WI and NT need a lookup; blank on about half the rows.
cols.STATUS: The well's status, spelled many ways, like Orphan, OR or orphan. Codes like HP and UN need a lookup.
cols.PRIME_MERIDIAN: The survey meridian for the land location, like Indian or 6th. Blank on most rows.
cols.TOWNSHIP: The survey township number. Blank on more than half the rows.
cols.RANGE: The survey range number. Blank on more than half the rows.
cols.R_DIR: Range direction, E or W. One row holds 3.
cols.SECTION: The survey section number. Blank on more than half the rows.
cols.QTR: The quarter of the section, like NE or NW4. Spelled two ways; blank on most rows.
cols.QTR_QTR: The quarter of that quarter, like NE4 or SE. Blank on most rows.
cols.QTR_QTR_QTR: A third level of quarter, like SW4. Blank on most rows.
cols.SOURCE: The state agency that reported the well, like Ohio Department of Natural Resources.
cols.DATA_FILE_DATE: The date of the state file the record came from.
cols.WELL_INFO_NOTES: Free-text notes on the well, like Priority 1C Well. Blank on most rows.
cols.LOCATION_NOTES: Free-text notes on where the well is or how its coordinates were made. Blank on more than half the rows.
cols.OTHER_NOTES: Other free-text notes, like Operator Unknown. Blank on most rows.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_USGS_ORPHANED_OIL_GAS_W.summary: Oil and gas wells left with no owner to plug them, as documented by state agencies and gathered by the USGS.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_USGS_ORPHANED_OIL_GAS_W.row: One orphaned well: its ID, state, type, status, location and the agency that reported it.

cols.SITE_NAME: The name of the place, whether a Superfund cleanup site, a mine, a stream gauge, or a health clinic. Many mine rows just say Unknown or Unnamed.
cols.STATE_CD: The state: two letters like FL in the CMS tables, a 2-digit number code like 06 in the USGS table.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.SITE_NO: The USGS number for the stream gauge, like 06041000. Keep it as text so leading zeros stay.
cols.PARAMETER_CD: A five-digit code for what was measured, like 00065 or 00060. The plain words are in the parameter name column.
cols.PARAMETER_NAME: What was measured: gage height in feet, streamflow in cubic feet per second, water temperature, or pH. Some symbols show up as web codes like ³.
cols.DATETIME: The date and time of the reading.
cols.VALUE: The measured number. -999999 is a placeholder for no value, not a real reading.
cols.UNIT_CD: The unit of the value: ft, ft3/s, deg C or std units.
cols.QUALIFIER: Letter codes on the reading's quality, like P, P,Ssn or P,ZFL. Almost all are plain P. The codes need a lookup.
cols.COUNTY_CD: The gauge's county as a five-digit federal code, state plus county.
cols.HUC_CD: The 8-digit, sometimes 12-digit, code for the watershed the gauge is in.
cols.AGENCY_CD: The agency that runs the gauge. Almost always USGS.
cols.DATA_TYPE: real-time for instant readings, daily for daily summaries. Almost all are real-time.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_USGS_WATER.summary: About 6.5 million readings from USGS river and stream gauges: water height, flow, temperature and pH, mostly from late June and early July 2026.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_USGS_WATER.row: One reading: one measurement at one stream gauge at one moment.

cols.STATES: The state or states the record covers. A list of two-letter codes like MA,ME,NH in the watershed table, where CN means Canada; code plus name like AK Alaska in the HUD table.
cols.SOURCE_ORIGINATOR: The agency or source that supplied the record, like U.S. Geological Survey.
cols.LOAD_DATE: When the record was loaded, as the table itself reports it: a date or a date and time.
cols.SHAPE_LENGTH: The length of the shape's outline, from the map software. Units differ by table: meters in the watershed table, map degrees in the tribal table.
cols.SHAPE_AREA: The area of the shape, from the map software. Units differ by table: square meters in the watershed table, square map degrees in the tribal table.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.HUC8: Eight-digit watershed code. Each row has its own value.
cols.TNM_ID: USGS National Map feature ID, in curly braces.
cols.GLOBAL_ID: Another USGS feature ID, in curly braces.
cols.OBJECT_ID: Row number from the source map file.
cols.WATERSHED_NAME: Name of the watershed, like a river basin or an island.
cols.REFERENCE_GNIS_IDS: ID of the named place in the federal place-name database.
cols.META_SOURCE_ID: ID of the source metadata record; one value covers most rows.
cols.SOURCE_DATA_DESC: Source the boundary was drawn from, mostly Watershed Boundary Dataset.
cols.SOURCE_FEATURE_ID: Feature ID in the source data. Empty in this table: filled 0.
cols.AREA_ACRES: Area of the watershed in acres.
cols.AREA_SQ_KM: Area of the watershed in square kilometers.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_USGS_WBD_HUC8.summary: The USGS list of 2,456 HUC-8 watersheds, with names, states and areas; the key for joining water and environmental data by watershed.

cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTRY_CODE: The country as a code, usually two letters like US, but some tables use three letters like AGO. The World Bank debt table also holds group codes like MIC and LMC that need a lookup.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state, as two letters like TX in some tables and as a number code like 48 or 06 in others, which needs a lookup and sometimes drops its leading zero. One table writes it like US_TX, and one leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY_CODE: The county's number code, written different ways: three digits like 001, sometimes without leading zeros like 3, five digits with the state like 11001, or state letters plus digits like FL095. One table uses name codes like US_SD_CLARK, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.ORGANIZATION_IDENTIFIER: A short code for the group that runs the spot, like USGS-MA or RIDEM.
cols.ORGANIZATION_FORMAL_NAME: The full name of the group that runs the spot, like the USGS Massachusetts Water Science Center.
cols.MONITORING_LOCATION_IDENTIFIER: The portal's ID for the spot, starting with the group's code. Nearly every row has its own.
cols.MONITORING_LOCATION_NAME: The spot's name, like a river, bay or road crossing.
cols.MONITORING_LOCATION_TYPE_NAME: What kind of spot it is: Well on most rows, then streams, estuaries, lakes and others.
cols.MONITORING_LOCATION_DESCRIPTION_TEXT: Free-text notes about the spot. Mostly blank.
cols.HUC_EIGHT_DIGIT_CODE: The 8-digit code for the watershed the spot sits in. Names need a lookup.
cols.DRAINAGE_AREA_MEASURE_VALUE: How much land drains to the spot, in square miles. Mostly blank.
cols.DRAINAGE_AREA_MEASURE_UNIT_CODE: The unit for drainage area, always sq mi when filled. Mostly blank.
cols.CONTRIBUTING_DRAINAGE_AREA_MEASURE_VALUE: How much of that land actually feeds water to the spot, in square miles. Nearly always blank.
cols.CONTRIBUTING_DRAINAGE_AREA_MEASURE_UNIT_: The unit for that area, always sq mi when filled. Nearly always blank.
cols.SOURCE_MAP_SCALE_NUMERIC: The scale of the map used to place the spot, like 24000 for a 1:24,000 map. About half blank, and a few say 0.
cols.HORIZONTAL_ACCURACY_MEASURE_VALUE: How precise the spot's map position is, read with the unit column. Some values are negative, like -5, which can't be a real accuracy.
cols.HORIZONTAL_ACCURACY_MEASURE_UNIT_CODE: The unit for position accuracy: mostly seconds, some hours, some Unknown.
cols.HORIZONTAL_COLLECTION_METHOD_NAME: How the spot's position was found, like read off a map or taken by GPS.
cols.HORIZONTAL_DATUM_NAME: The map reference system for the coordinates, mostly NAD83. Some say OTHER or UNKWN.
cols.VERTICAL_MEASURE_VALUE: The spot's height, read with the unit column.
cols.VERTICAL_MEASURE_UNIT_CODE: The unit for height: feet, written both feet and ft, or m for meters.
cols.VERTICAL_ACCURACY_MEASURE_VALUE: How precise the height is, in the unit next to it.
cols.VERTICAL_ACCURACY_MEASURE_UNIT_CODE: The unit for height accuracy: feet or m.
cols.VERTICAL_COLLECTION_METHOD_NAME: How the height was found, like read off a topographic map or surveyed.
cols.VERTICAL_DATUM_NAME: The sea-level reference for the height, mostly NGVD29. Some say Unknown or UNKWN.
cols.AQUIFER_NAME: The regional underground water layer a well draws from, mostly glacial sand and gravel. Blank for most spots.
cols.LOCAL_AQUIFER_NAME: Meant to hold the local name of the well's water layer, but empty on every row.
cols.FORMATION_TYPE_TEXT: The ground a well sits in, like outwash, till or bedrock. Mostly blank.
cols.AQUIFER_TYPE_NAME: Whether the well's water layer is confined or unconfined. Mostly blank.
cols.CONSTRUCTION_DATE_TEXT: When the well was built, stored as text in mixed forms: some just a year, some a full date like 20220510. Blank on about half the rows.
cols.WELL_DEPTH_MEASURE_VALUE: How deep the well is, in feet.
cols.WELL_DEPTH_MEASURE_UNIT_CODE: The unit for well depth, always ft.
cols.WELL_HOLE_DEPTH_MEASURE_VALUE: How deep the drilled hole is, in feet. Mostly blank.
cols.WELL_HOLE_DEPTH_MEASURE_UNIT_CODE: The unit for hole depth, always ft. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_NAME: Which database supplied the record: NWIS or STORET.

ENVIRONMENT__FED_WQP_MONITORING_STATIONS.summary: Water-quality monitoring spots in Rhode Island from the national Water Quality Portal, mostly wells run by the USGS Massachusetts office, with who runs them, where they sit and well details.
ENVIRONMENT__FED_WQP_MONITORING_STATIONS.row: One monitoring spot: a stream, lake, estuary or well where water gets sampled.

cols.COUNTRY: The country, written different ways by table: a full name, a two- or three-letter code, or a number code that needs a lookup. Some rows hold a region like World or a UK nation like England, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 06037. One table holds two-digit state codes instead, and nine tables leave it empty.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.DOI: The DOI, a permanent web ID for a paper or dataset, like 10.2813/0758057.
cols.MODEL_VERSION: The version of the Global Earthquake Model release. 2023.1 on every row.
cols.PGA_10PCT_50YR: The ground shaking level with a 10 percent chance of being passed in 50 years. Empty in this table.
cols.VS30: The ground stiffness the model assumes, in meters per second of shear-wave speed in the top 30 meters. 760 on every row. A number stored as text.
cols.HAZARD_MODEL_ID: A short code for the region the model covers, like USA, JPN or AFR.

ENVIRONMENT__INTL_GEM_HAZARD.summary: A 12-row index of the Global Earthquake Model's 2023 earthquake hazard models, one per world region or country, like the USA, Japan or Africa.
ENVIRONMENT__INTL_GEM_HAZARD.row: One hazard model: the Global Earthquake Model's shaking-risk model for one region or country.

cols.COUNTRY: The country, written different ways by table: a full name, a two- or three-letter code, or a number code that needs a lookup. Some rows hold a region like World or a UK nation like England, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.GENDER: The person's sex, written differently by table: Male or Female, M or F, m or f, or Male Owned for businesses. Some rows say Unknown or Unanswered, the clinical trials table mostly says ALL, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.DEFENDER_NAME: The name of the defender. Empty in this table.
cols.REGION: The region where it happened. Empty in this table.
cols.INCIDENT_TYPE: What happened, like attack, killing, threat or arrest. Filled on under half the rows.
cols.SECTOR: The industry involved: mining, dam or logging. Almost always blank.
cols.INDIGENOUS_STATUS: Yes when the defender was Indigenous. Mostly blank, and blank does not mean no.
cols.PERPETRATOR: Who carried out the attack. Empty in this table.
cols.SOURCE_REPORT: The web link to the Global Witness page the passage came from.
cols.NOTES_CONTEXT: The passage of text itself, as written on the page.

ENVIRONMENT__INTL_GLOBAL_WITNESS_DEFENDE.summary: A small set of 232 notes pulled from Global Witness web pages about land and environmental defenders who were attacked, threatened or killed. Names, regions and perpetrators are empty.
ENVIRONMENT__INTL_GLOBAL_WITNESS_DEFENDE.row: One passage from a Global Witness page about attacks on land and environmental defenders.

cols.EPA_REGISTRY_ID: EPA's 12-digit ID for the facility, starting 110. Stored as text.
cols.FACILITY_NAME: The name of the plant, site or building, as the agency wrote it. Generic fillers like RESIDENCE, UNKNOWN, WELL or HOME are common in some tables.
cols.MATCH_METHOD: How this row was matched to another list, like exact, fuzzy, brand, or surname plus state; some rows say unmatched. Mostly blank in the EPA crosswalk and excluded-providers tables.
cols.MATCH_CONFIDENCE: How sure the name match is, from 0 to 1. Only 1.00, 0.85 or 0.80 appear; mostly blank in the crosswalk.
cols.PARENT_UEI: The 12-character federal contractor ID of the parent company. Mostly blank in the crosswalk.
cols.MATCHED_LEI: Global company ID of the company matched to the facility by name. Blank for about 19 in 20 facilities.
cols.MATCHED_LEGAL_NAME: Legal name of the matched company, like CVS HEALTH CORPORATION. Blank when there is no match, most rows.
cols.ULTIMATE_PARENT_LEI: Global company ID of the top parent company. Almost always blank.
cols.PARENT_LEGAL_NAME: Legal name of the parent company. Blank when there is no match, most rows.
cols.PARENT_CIK: The parent company's SEC filer number. Almost always blank.
cols.REVIEW_FLAG: Meant to flag matches for a human to check, but every filled row is false. Blank on most rows.

ENVIRONMENT__XC_EPA_CORPORATE_CROSSWALK.summary: A lookup your pipeline built that links EPA facilities to the companies behind them through global company IDs and SEC filer numbers; most facilities have no match because most have no public-company parent.
ENVIRONMENT__XC_EPA_CORPORATE_CROSSWALK.row: One EPA facility: its matched company, parent company and SEC ID when one was found.

cols.ENTITY: The country or region name, like Albania or World.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.CODE: The three-letter country code, like USA. Groupings use codes starting with OWID_, like OWID_WRL for the whole world. Blank for some regions.
cols.ANNUAL_CO_EMISSIONS: Carbon dioxide put out that year, likely in tonnes. The column name cuts off the 2. Stored as text.

ENVIRONMENT__XC_OWID_CO2.summary: Yearly carbon dioxide emissions for each country and world region, from Our World in Data.
ENVIRONMENT__XC_OWID_CO2.row: One country-year: one country's or region's carbon dioxide emissions for one year.

cols.ENTITY: The country or region name, like Albania or World.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.CODE: Three-letter country code; codes starting OWID_ are regions like the world. Blank for some regions.
cols.FOSSIL_FUELS: Percent of energy from fossil fuels, stored as text.

ENVIRONMENT__XC_OWID_FOSSIL_SHARE.summary: Share of each country's energy that comes from fossil fuels, by year, from Our World in Data.
ENVIRONMENT__XC_OWID_FOSSIL_SHARE.row: One country-year: fossil fuel share of energy for one country or region in one year.

cols.ENTITY: The country or region name, like Albania or World.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.CODE: Our World in Data's code for the area: OWID_WRL, OWID_NH or OWID_SH.
cols.AVERAGE: How far the year's average temperature was from the long-term average, in degrees, stored as text.
cols.LOWER_BOUND: The low end of the likely range for that difference, in degrees, stored as text.
cols.UPPER_BOUND: The high end of the likely range for that difference, in degrees, stored as text.

ENVIRONMENT__XC_OWID_TEMP_ANOMALY.summary: How much warmer or colder each year was than a long-term average, for the world and each hemisphere, from Our World in Data.
ENVIRONMENT__XC_OWID_TEMP_ANOMALY.row: One area in one year: the temperature difference for the world or one hemisphere in one year.

cols.PAGE_URL: The web address of the page this row came from.
cols.CAPTURED_AT: When the web page snapshot was taken, date and time.
cols.PAGE_DIGEST: A 32-character fingerprint of a web page's content. The same code means the same page content.
cols.VERSION_KEY: An ID for the snapshot, built from the page's web address. Nearly every snapshot has its own. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.DATASET_NO: Which numbered Epstein document set the page belongs to, 1 to 12.
cols.PAGER_PAGES: How many result pages the page's list showed. Blank on some snapshots.
cols.APPROX_FILES_FROM_PAGER: Rough file count, worked out from the number of result pages. An estimate, not an exact count. Blank on some snapshots.
cols.FILES_ON_PAGE_ONE: How many files showed on the first result page, usually about 50.

FCT_DATASET_SIZE_HISTORY.summary: A time-lapse of the Justice Department's Epstein document pages: 339 snapshots of how many files each page seemed to hold, kept to catch files being quietly added or removed.
FCT_DATASET_SIZE_HISTORY.row: One snapshot: one Epstein document page at one moment, with the file count read off its page list.

cols.DATASET_NAME: The name of the dataset. One table stores it web-encoded, like DataSet%201 for DataSet 1, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.FILE_URL: The web address of the document file, mostly on justice.gov. Each row has its own.
cols.EFTA_FILE_NUMBER: The number from the file's EFTA label. Blank on a few rows.
cols.FIRST_OBSERVED_AT: When the file was first seen.
cols.LAST_OBSERVED_AT: When the file was last seen.
cols.OBSERVATIONS: How many times the file has been seen.
cols.SOURCES_OBSERVING: How many sources have seen the file: 1 or 2.
cols.OBSERVED_BY: Which sources saw the file: wayback_replay, live_snapshot, or both, listed in either order.

FCT_LIBRARY_SNAPSHOT.summary: A watch list of 619 public Epstein document files, tracking each file's web address and when it was first and last seen, to catch files that appear, change or vanish.
FCT_LIBRARY_SNAPSHOT.row: One document file being watched: its link and sighting history, not its contents.

cols.URLKEY: The saved web address in the Wayback Machine's flipped format, starting gov,justice and then the page path. Long ones are cut off.
cols.URL: A web link to the record's own page at the source.
cols.CAPTURED_AT: When the web page snapshot was taken, date and time.
cols.CONTENT_DIGEST: A 32-character fingerprint of the saved page. Same fingerprint means the page did not change.
cols.MIMETYPE: The kind of file saved, almost always text/html, a web page. A few rows say warc/revisit or unk.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CHANGE_KIND: What changed since the last snapshot: first_capture, content_changed, or content_and_status_changed.
cols.HTTP_STATUS: The web server's answer: 200 for the page loaded, 404 for not found, 403 or 401 for blocked, 301 for moved.
cols.PREV_HTTP_STATUS: The server's answer at the snapshot before. Blank for first snapshots.
cols.PREV_DIGEST: The fingerprint of the page at the snapshot before. If it differs from this one, the page changed. Blank for first snapshots.
cols.CONTENT_BYTES: The size of the saved page, in bytes.
cols.PREV_CAPTURED_AT: When the snapshot before was taken. Blank for first snapshots.
cols.HOURS_SINCE_PREV_CAPTURE: How many hours passed since the snapshot before, often about 24.

FCT_WAYBACK_PAGE_CHANGES.summary: A change log of web pages tracked for the Epstein investigation, built from Internet Archive snapshots, flagging when a page first appeared, changed, or started returning an error.
FCT_WAYBACK_PAGE_CHANGES.row: One snapshot: one saved copy of one tracked web page, compared with the copy before it.

cols.TRADERS_DEALER_SHORT_ALL: How many dealers, meaning big banks held contracts betting the price falls. A lone dot means no number. Stored as text with leading spaces.

cols.ACTIVITY_ID: The ID number for one activity: an EPA inspection, violation or enforcement action, or one reported spending item in the Texas lobby tables.
cols.CASE_NUMBER: The agency's ID number for one case, in a format that depends on the agency, like 05-2014-5064 or I-200-19058-315794. In the OSHA injury tables it is a small running number like 1, 2 or 3 that repeats across work sites, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.ICIS_FACILITY_INTEREST_ID: EPA's enforcement-system ID for the facility, a number stored as text.
cols.FACILITY_UIN: EPA's 12-digit registry ID for the facility, starting 110. Stored as text.
cols.FACILITY_NAME: The name of the plant, site or building, as the agency wrote it. Generic fillers like RESIDENCE, UNKNOWN, WELL or HOME are common in some tables.
cols.FACILITY_CITY: The city where the facility is.
cols.FACILITY_STATE: The facility's state. Two letters in the EPA table, full name like TEXAS in the ICE table.
cols.ENF_CONCLUSION_ID: EPA's ID for the case outcome, like a settlement or order, that covers this facility.
cols.FACILITY_ZIP: The facility's ZIP code in mixed forms: five digits, ZIP+4 with a dash, or nine digits run together.

cols.ACTIVITY_ID: The ID number for one activity: an EPA inspection, violation or enforcement action, or one reported spending item in the Texas lobby tables.
cols.CASE_NUMBER: The agency's ID number for one case, in a format that depends on the agency, like 05-2014-5064 or I-200-19058-315794. In the OSHA injury tables it is a small running number like 1, 2 or 3 that repeats across work sites, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.REGISTRY_ID: The EPA's 12-digit master ID for a facility, starting with 110. Links one site across EPA programs.
cols.FACILITY_NAME: The name of the plant, site or building, as the agency wrote it. Generic fillers like RESIDENCE, UNKNOWN, WELL or HOME are common in some tables.
cols.LOCATION_ADDRESS: The street address of the facility. Filler like UNKNOWN or NO ADDRESS ON FILE is common, and some rows give a land survey spot like NW 1/4 SEC 13 T3N R22E instead.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state, as two letters like TX in some tables and as a number code like 48 or 06 in others, which needs a lookup and sometimes drops its leading zero. One table writes it like US_TX, and one leaves it empty.
cols.ZIP: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Fillers like 00000, UNKNO or a lone dash show up, some codes lost a leading zero like 8721, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.PRIMARY_SIC_CODE: The facility's main industry, as a 4-digit SIC code. Blank on about 4 in 10 rows; the codes need a lookup.
cols.PRIMARY_NAICS_CODE: The facility's main industry, as a 6-digit NAICS code. Mostly blank, and 999999 is a placeholder.

FINANCE__FED_EPA_ICIS_FEC_CASE_FACILITIE.row: One facility tied to one EPA enforcement case.

cols.PGM_SYS_ACRNM: The short name of the EPA database the record comes from, like ICIS, RCRAINFO, or TRIS.
cols.PGM_SYS_ID: The ID a specific EPA program uses for the facility, like a permit number. Formats differ by program.
cols.REGISTRY_ID: The EPA's 12-digit master ID for a facility, starting with 110. Links one site across EPA programs.
cols.AGENCY: The government agency tied to the record, written differently by table: EPA or State, a full department name, a bracketed list in the Federal Register, or number codes in the federal appeals table, where most rows hold -9.
cols.ACTIVITY_TYPE_CODE: The EPA code for the kind of action: INS inspection, AIF informal action, AFR administrative formal action, JDC court case. One table also has OSR, INF and INV, which need a lookup.
cols.ENF_TYPE_CODE: A short code for the kind of enforcement action, like NOV for notice of violation or CIV for a civil court case. The matching words are in ENF_TYPE_DESC.
cols.ENF_TYPE_DESC: The kind of enforcement action in words, like Notice of Violation or Civil Judicial Action.
cols.ACHIEVED_DATE: The date the EPA's informal enforcement step, like a warning letter, was completed.
cols.ENF_IDENTIFIER: The EPA's case number for the enforcement action, in several formats like 02-2003-A006.
cols.STATUTE: The environmental law involved, as an acronym like SDWA, TSCA or RCRA.

cols.GIIN: The ID a foreign bank registers with the IRS under the FATCA offshore-account law, like X5PYX1.00000.LE.076. The last three digits are the country code.
cols.INSTITUTION_NAME: The name of the college, bank, or financial firm. Some FDIC rows say Redacted.
cols.COUNTRY_NAME: The country's full name, spelled different ways, like USA, US or UNITED STATES. The World Bank debt table also holds groups like Middle income.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

FINANCE__FED_FATCA_FFI.summary: The IRS list of foreign banks, funds and other financial institutions registered for FATCA reporting, with their GIIN ID and country.

cols.CERT: The bank's FDIC certificate number, a number that identifies one bank.
cols.NAME: The name of whatever the row is about: a person, company, bank, county, address or dataset, depending on the table. Spelling is not cleaned, fillers like UNNAMED or None show up, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.ZIP: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Fillers like 00000, UNKNO or a lone dash show up, some codes lost a leading zero like 8721, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 06037. One table holds two-digit state codes instead, and nine tables leave it empty.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LEI: The company's Legal Entity Identifier, a 20-character global ID. The FDIC table's values are only 16 characters, so they look cut short.
cols.HOLDING_COMPANY_NAME: The name of the company that owns the bank. Often blank.
cols.HOLDING_COMPANY_CITY: The city where the bank's owning company is based.
cols.ADDRESS: The full address in one line of text, messy and not split into parts. Some rows hold notes instead, like UNKNOWN, Incarcerated or Moved Out of State, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY: The county, usually as a name like Harris, though some tables add the word County and the federal court tables use five-digit number codes, including 88888, which needs a lookup. The UK company table holds UK counties, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.INSURED_DATE: The date the bank or credit union got federal deposit insurance. The credit union table has placeholder dates like 1900-01-01, and the failed-banks table is empty.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.STALP: The bank's state, as two letters.
cols.BKCLASS: Charter class code, like NM, N, SL or SM; codes need a lookup.
cols.ACTIVE: 1 if the institution is still open, 0 if not; most rows are 0.
cols.DATEUPDT: Date the FDIC last updated the record.
cols.ESTYMD: Date the institution was founded; some go back to the 1880s.
cols.ENDEFYMD: Date the institution stopped existing, by closing or merging. Blank for open banks.
cols.ASSET: Total assets on the latest financial report. Blank on about 14% of rows.
cols.DEP: Total deposits on the latest financial report.
cols.DEPDOM: Deposits held in US offices on the latest financial report.
cols.NETINC: Net income on the latest financial report; can be negative.
cols.REPDTE: Date of the financial report the dollar figures come from.
cols.RSSDID: Federal Reserve ID for the institution; 0 is a placeholder.
cols.CHRTAGNT: Who granted the charter: STATE, OCC, OTS or SOVER.
cols.SPECGRP: Specialty group code, like 4.0 or 8.0; codes need a lookup.
cols.HCTMULT: Holding company flag, always 1 when filled. Mostly blank.
cols.DOCKET: Savings institution docket number; 0 is a placeholder on most rows.
cols.FDIC_ID: The FDIC's internal ID for the institution.
cols.CBSA: Metro or micro area where the bank is based, like Chicago-Naperville-Elgin, IL-IN-WI.
cols.CBSA_METRO_NAME: Metro area name; blank for banks outside a metro area.
cols.CHARTER: National bank charter number; 0 is a placeholder on most rows.
cols.CLCODE: Numeric bank class code, like 21 or 3; codes need a lookup.
cols.FDIC_REGION: FDIC regional office, like Dallas or Chicago.
cols.FDIC_SUPERVISOR: FDIC office that supervises the bank.
cols.OCC_DISTRICT: District of the national bank regulator, like SOUTHERN DISTRICT. Mostly blank.
cols.IN_CONSERVATORSHIP: Y if the bank was placed under government control, N if not.
cols.INSURANCE_DROPPED_DATE: Date FDIC insurance ended. Filled on only 161 rows.
cols.MDI_STATUS_CODE: Minority-owned bank code, like 03 or 01; the words are in MDI_STATUS_DESC. Filled on only 301 rows.
cols.MDI_STATUS_DESC: Minority ownership in words, like Black or African American owned; NONE for most banks.
cols.SUCCESSOR_CERT: FDIC certificate number of the bank that took this one over; 0 means none.
cols.PARENT_CERT: Certificate number of a parent bank. 0, meaning none, on nearly every filled row; blank on about 14% of rows.
cols.OFFICES: Number of offices. Mostly blank; OFFICES_DOMESTIC is fuller.

FINANCE__FED_FDIC_BANK_DATA.summary: A partial pull of the FDIC's directory of insured banks and savings institutions, open and closed; the notes flag it as a sample, not the full list, so do not count from it.
FINANCE__FED_FDIC_BANK_DATA.row: One bank: one FDIC-insured institution, open or closed.

cols.SURVEY_YEAR: The year the survey covers, like 2009 or 1994.
cols.FDIC_CERT: The FDIC's certificate number for a bank, like 30965. Use it to join bank tables. Blank for some failed banks.
cols.INSTITUTION_NAME: The name of the college, bank, or financial firm. Some FDIC rows say Redacted.
cols.BANK_CLASS: A short code for the kind of bank and who charters it, like N, NM, SM, SB or SL. Needs the FDIC lookup to read.
cols.CHARTER_TYPE: Who chartered the bank: FED for a national charter or STATE. Empty in the failed-banks table.
cols.HOLDING_COMPANY_NAME: The name of the company that owns the bank. Often blank.
cols.HOLDING_COMPANY_CITY: The city where the bank's owning company is based.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.BRANCH_YEAR_KEY: A made-up ID joining year, bank number and branch number, like 2025-59112-1. Each row has its own. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.BRANCH_NUMBER: The branch's number within its bank. 0 is the most common value and looks like the bank's main office.
cols.BRANCH_UNINUM: The FDIC's permanent ID number for the branch, the same from year to year. A few rows are blank.
cols.RECORD_ID: An ID joining year, bank number and branch number with underscores, like 2025_59112_1. Close to one per row.
cols.RSSD_ID: The Federal Reserve's ID number for the bank that owns the branch.
cols.HOLDING_COMPANY_RSSD: The Federal Reserve's ID number for the bank's parent holding company. 0 means no holding company is listed.
cols.OTS_DOCKET: The old savings-and-loan regulator's docket number for the bank. About 45% of rows hold 0 or 0.0, which means none; the zeros are stored two ways as text.
cols.BRANCH_NAME: The branch's name, like Lexington Branch.
cols.BRANCH_ADDRESS: The branch's street address. Some just say Main Street.
cols.BRANCH_CITY: The city the branch is in.
cols.BRANCH_CITY_ALT: A second spelling of the branch's city, often the bigger city name the post office uses.
cols.BRANCH_STATE: The branch's state, as two letters.
cols.BRANCH_STATE_FIPS: The branch's state as a federal number code, like 6 for California, stored without the leading zero.
cols.BRANCH_COUNTY_FIPS: The branch's county number within its state, without the state part or leading zeros.
cols.BRANCH_STATE_COUNTY_FIPS: The branch's county as a five-digit federal code, stored without the leading zero, like 6037 for Los Angeles.
cols.BRANCH_COUNTRY: The branch's country or territory, like United States or Puerto Rico. Spellings vary, like UNITED STATES.
cols.BRANCH_PLACE_CODE: A federal code for the town the branch is in. 0 means none, and some codes end in .0 because they are numbers stored as text.
cols.BRANCH_MSA_CODE: The code for the branch's metro area. 0 means the branch is outside a metro area; the codes need a lookup.
cols.BRANCH_MSA_NAME: The name of the branch's metro area, like New York-Newark-Jersey City.
cols.BRANCH_CSA_CODE: The code for the branch's larger combined metro region. 0 means none; the codes need a lookup.
cols.BRANCH_CSA_NAME: The name of the branch's larger combined metro region, like New York-Newark, NY-NJ-CT-PA.
cols.BRANCH_CBSA_DIVISION_CODE: The code for a sub-area inside a very big metro area. 0 for most branches, which means none.
cols.BRANCH_CBSA_DIVISION_NAME: The name of the sub-area inside a very big metro area, like New York-Jersey City-White Plains. Blank for most branches.
cols.BRANCH_NECTA_CODE: The code for a New England town-based metro area. 0 for almost all branches, which means none.
cols.BRANCH_NECTA_NAME: The name of the New England town-based metro area, like Boston-Cambridge-Quincy. Blank for almost all branches.
cols.BRANCH_METRO_FLAG: 1 if the branch is in a metro area, 0 if not.
cols.BRANCH_MICRO_FLAG: 1 if the branch is in a smaller micro area, 0 if not.
cols.BRANCH_SERVICE_TYPE: A number code for what kind of branch it is, like a full-service office; 11 is by far the most common. The codes need a lookup.
cols.BRANCH_DEPOSIT_REPORTING_METHOD: A letter code for how the bank assigned deposits to this branch, like M, E or C, sometimes two joined like M,E. Blank for most rows; the codes need a lookup.
cols.MAIN_OFFICE_FLAG: 1 if this branch is the bank's main office, 0 if not.
cols.BRANCH_DEPOSITS_THOUSANDS: How much money was on deposit at this branch, in thousands of dollars. Use this column to add up deposits; some branches show 0.
cols.SIMS_LATITUDE: The branch's latitude on a map. Blank for some rows.
cols.SIMS_LONGITUDE: The branch's longitude on a map. Blank for some rows.
cols.SIMS_PROJECTION: How precisely the branch was placed on the map, like US_RoofTop, US_Streets or US_Zipcode. Values mix words and numbers like 0 and 100.
cols.SIMS_DESCRIPTION: A short code describing the map match, like M, S01 or POINTADDRESS. Values mix styles; the codes need a lookup.
cols.SIMS_ACQUIRED_DATE: The date the branch was acquired from another bank. Blank for about half the rows.
cols.SIMS_ESTABLISHED_DATE: The date the branch opened. Round dates like 1889-01-01 look like stand-ins for an unknown day.
cols.INSTITUTION_ADDRESS: The street address of the bank's head office.
cols.INSTITUTION_CITY: The city of the bank's head office, like Charlotte or Sioux Falls.
cols.INSTITUTION_STATE: The state of the bank's head office, as two letters.
cols.INSTITUTION_STATE_NAME: The state of the bank's head office, spelled out. Spelling mixes capitals, like Ohio and OHIO.
cols.INSTITUTION_ZIP: The ZIP code of the bank's head office.
cols.INSTITUTION_STATE_COUNTY_FIPS: The county of the bank's head office, as a five-digit federal code stored without the leading zero.
cols.INSTITUTION_COUNTRY: The country of the bank's head office, mostly United States.
cols.INSTITUTION_ASSETS_THOUSANDS: The whole bank's total assets that year, in thousands of dollars. It repeats on every branch of the bank, so do not add it up across branches.
cols.INSTITUTION_DEPOSITS_THOUSANDS: The whole bank's total deposits, in thousands of dollars. It shows 0 on most rows, so it looks filled only on a main-office row.
cols.INSTITUTION_DOMESTIC_DEPOSITS_THOUSANDS: The whole bank's deposits in U.S. offices, in thousands of dollars. It repeats on every branch, so do not add it up across branches.
cols.INSURED_BRANCH_DEMAND_DEPOSITS_THOUSANDS: Checking-type deposits at a foreign bank's insured U.S. branch, in thousands of dollars. Blank or 0 on almost every row.
cols.INSURED_BRANCH_TIME_SAVINGS_DEPOSITS_THO: Savings and time deposits at a foreign bank's insured U.S. branch, in thousands of dollars. Blank or 0 on almost every row.
cols.ESCROW_DEPOSITS_THOUSANDS: Escrow money the bank holds, in thousands of dollars. Blank for most rows.
cols.CLASS_CODE: A number code for the bank's charter class; 3 and 21 are the most common. The codes need a lookup.
cols.CHARTER_AGENCY: Who granted the bank's charter: STATE, OCC or OTS.
cols.CHARTER_AGENCY_NAME: Who granted the bank's charter, spelled out: a state agency, the Comptroller of the Currency, or the Office of Thrift Supervision.
cols.COMMUNITY_BANK_FLAG: 1 if the bank counts as a community bank, 0 if not. Blank for most rows.
cols.INSURED_STATUS: A two-letter code for the bank's insurance status, like CB or SA. The codes need a lookup.
cols.INSURANCE_AGENCY: Which FDIC insurance fund covers the bank: DIF, BIF or SAIF.
cols.REGULATOR: The bank's main federal regulator: OCC, FDIC, FED or OTS.
cols.CALL_REPORT_CODE: Which kind of money report the bank files: CALL or TFR.
cols.FED_DISTRICT_CODE: The number of the Federal Reserve district the bank is in, 1 to 12.
cols.FED_DISTRICT_NAME: The Federal Reserve district the bank is in, like Cleveland or Richmond.
cols.FDIC_REGION_CODE: The number of the FDIC region that oversees the bank. The numbers match the region names in the next column.
cols.FDIC_REGION_NAME: The FDIC region that oversees the bank, like Chicago or Atlanta.
cols.OCC_DISTRICT_CODE: The number of the OCC district for the bank. Some are stored with .0, like 6.0.
cols.OCC_DISTRICT_NAME: The name of the OCC district for the bank, like Central District or Large Bank.
cols.SPECIALIZATION_GROUP_CODE: A number code for the bank's main line of business. Some are stored with .0, like 4.0; the next column spells them out.
cols.SPECIALIZATION_GROUP_DESC: The bank's main line of business, like COMMERCIAL LENDING, MORTGAGE LENDING or AGRICULTURAL.
cols.MULTIBANK_HOLDING_FLAG: Whether the bank's holding company owns several banks, one, or none: MULT, ONE or NONE.
cols.HOLDING_COMPANY_STATE: The state of the bank's parent holding company, as two letters.
cols.DENOVO_FLAG: 1 if the bank is brand new, 0 if not. Zeros are stored two ways, 0 and 0.0.
cols.CONSOLIDATED_REPORTING_CODE: A number code about consolidated reporting, stored with .0 like 3.0. Blank for almost all rows; the codes need a lookup.
cols.UNIT_BANK_FLAG: 1 if the bank has only one office, 0 if it has branches. Values are stored two ways, like 1 and 1.0.
cols.DOMESTIC_FLAG: 1 if the branch is in the U.S., 0 if it is abroad.

FINANCE__FED_FDIC_SOD_BRANCH_DEPOSITS.summary: Every FDIC-insured bank branch in the country, year by year from 1994 to 2025, with how much money was on deposit there and who owned the bank.
FINANCE__FED_FDIC_SOD_BRANCH_DEPOSITS.row: One branch-year: one bank branch in one yearly FDIC deposit survey.

cols.FEC_CMTE_ID: The FEC's ID for a political committee, a C followed by 8 digits.
cols.CMTE_NM: The political committee's name, like a PAC or a campaign, in capitals.
cols.TRES_NM: The name of the committee's treasurer, usually last name first. Some rows hold the filler N, N N.
cols.CMTE_ST1: The first street line of the political committee's address.
cols.CMTE_ST2: The second street line of the committee's address, like a suite number. Mostly blank.
cols.CMTE_CITY: The city of the political committee's mailing address.
cols.CMTE_ST: The political committee's state, as two letters.
cols.CMTE_ZIP: The committee's zip code, five or nine digits with no dash.
cols.CMTE_DSGN: One letter for the committee's role: P is a candidate's main campaign, A authorized, J joint fundraiser, U unauthorized, B lobbyist PAC, D leadership PAC.
cols.CMTE_TP: One letter for the committee's type, like H House campaign, S Senate, P President, Q or N a PAC, O a super PAC. Needs the FEC lookup for the rest.
cols.CMTE_PTY_AFFILIATION: The committee's party, as a short code like DEM, REP, or UNK for unknown; odd values like W and NNE need a lookup. Blank for most committees.
cols.CMTE_FILING_FREQ: How often the committee files reports, one letter: M monthly, Q quarterly, T terminated, A administratively terminated, D debt.
cols.ORG_TP: A one-letter code for what kind of group backs the committee, like C for corporation or L for labor union. Needs a lookup; often blank.
cols.CONNECTED_ORG_NM: The company, union, or group that sponsors the political committee, in capitals. Often blank, and most filled rows just say NONE.
cols.FEC_CAND_ID: The FEC's ID for a candidate. The first letter shows the race: H House, S Senate, P President. Mostly blank.

cols.TRES_NM: The name of the committee's treasurer, usually last name first. Some rows hold the filler N, N N.

FINANCE__FED_FEC_COMMITTEES_DIM.summary: One clean line for every federal political committee, with name, treasurer, type, party and linked candidate, built to attach committee names to money records without making duplicates.

cols.CMTE_ID: The Federal Election Commission's ID for the political committee, a C and eight digits like C00493783.
cols.AMNDT_IND: Whether the filing is new or a fix. N is new; other codes like A1 or T mark amendments or termination.
cols.IMAGE_NUM: The FEC's 18-digit number for the scanned page of the filing. Starts with the date it was filed.
cols.NAME: The name of whatever the row is about: a person, company, bank, county, address or dataset, depending on the table. Spelling is not cleaned, fillers like UNNAMED or None show up, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.EMPLOYER: The donor's employer, as written, like RETIRED or NOT EMPLOYED; placeholders like N/A are common. Almost always blank in the committee-to-candidate table.
cols.OCCUPATION: The person's job as they wrote it, like RETIRED or Attorney, not cleaned. The mine accident table uses NO VALUE FOUND as a filler, and one FEC table leaves it almost always blank.
cols.TRANSACTION_AMT: The dollar amount of the transaction. Some rows in the committee-to-candidate table are 0 or negative, like -1 or -5.
cols.OTHER_ID: The FEC ID of the other committee or candidate in the transaction, usually a C followed by 8 digits. Often blank in the individual donations table.
cols.CAND_ID: The Federal Election Commission's ID for the candidate. The first letter says the race: H for House, S for Senate, P for President.
cols.TRAN_ID: The filer's own ID for one transaction line in the filing. Formats vary by filer.
cols.FILE_NUM: The FEC's number for the report this row came from.
cols.MEMO_CD: X marks a memo line, not new money. Leave X rows out when adding up dollars. Almost always blank.
cols.IS_MEMO_TRANSACTION: True if the row is a memo line, not new money. Leave these out when adding up dollars.
cols.MEMO_TEXT: A free-text note on the transaction, like EARMARKED FOR a named committee or DIRECT CONTRIBUTION. Often blank, and mostly blank in the committee-to-candidate table.
cols.SUB_ID: The FEC's unique 19-digit ID for this one transaction row.
cols.CYCLE: The two-year election cycle, named by its end year, like 2026.
cols.RPT_TP: The kind of report the transaction was filed on, as a code like YE, Q3 or 30G that needs a lookup.
cols.TRANSACTION_PGI: Which election the money was for: a letter like P or G, often with the year, like G2024. The letters need a lookup.
cols.TRANSACTION_TP: Transaction type, a code like 24K or 24E that needs a lookup.
cols.ENTITY_TP: Kind of recipient, as a code like CCM, ORG, IND or PAC that needs a lookup.
cols.TRANSACTION_DT: Date of the transaction, stored as text in month-day-year order, like 11202024. Blank on a few rows.

cols.CAND_NAME: The candidate's name, last name first. Mostly in capitals, but the independent spending table mixes styles like Trump, Donald and TRUMP, DONALD J.
cols.FILE_NUM: The FEC's number for the report this row came from.
cols.AMNDT_IND: Whether the filing is new or a fix. N is new; other codes like A1 or T mark amendments or termination.
cols.TRAN_ID: The filer's own ID for one transaction line in the filing. Formats vary by filer.
cols.IMAGE_NUM: The FEC's 18-digit number for the scanned page of the filing. Starts with the date it was filed.
cols.FEC_ELECTION_YR: The two-year election cycle, named by its ending year like 2024.
cols.CYCLE_FILE: The election cycle of the FEC file, an even year like 2018.
cols.SPE_ID: The FEC committee ID of the group that spent the money, like C00756569.
cols.SPE_NAM: The name of the group that spent the money.
cols.ELE_TYPE: A letter for the election the money was aimed at, like G, P, R, O or S; the codes need a lookup.
cols.CAN_OFFICE_STATE: The two-letter state of the race. Blank on about one in ten rows.
cols.CAN_OFFICE_DIS: The congressional district number of the race. 00 is used for statewide and presidential races.
cols.CAN_OFFICE: The office sought: H for House, S for Senate, P for President.
cols.CAND_PTY_AFF: The candidate's party, like DEMOCRATIC PARTY or REPUBLICAN PARTY. Blank on about one in seven rows.
cols.EXP_AMO: How much was spent on this line, in dollars. Stored as text.
cols.EXP_DATE: The date the money was spent, written like 05-SEP-24. Stored as text. Blank on about a quarter of rows.
cols.AGG_AMO: The running total the group had spent in this race so far, in dollars. Stored as text.
cols.SUP_OPP: S if the money supported the candidate, O if it opposed them.
cols.PUR: What the money was for, in the group's words, like Payroll or Digital Advertising.
cols.PAY: Who got paid, like Google or a consulting firm.
cols.RECEIPT_DAT: The date the FEC received the report, written like 22-FEB-21. Stored as text.
cols.PREV_FILE_NUM: The number of an earlier report this one amends. Blank on most rows.
cols.DISSEM_DT: The date the ad or message went out to the public, written like 23-OCT-18. Stored as text.
cols.IS_SUSPECT_FILING: True for a filing flagged as suspect, False otherwise. Only a few dozen rows are True.
cols.IS_SUPERSEDED: True when a later filing replaced this line, so it may double-count. About one in eight rows are True.

FINANCE__FED_FEC_INDEPENDENT_EXPENDITURE.summary: Money that outside groups like super PACs spent on their own to support or oppose federal candidates, as reported to the Federal Election Commission.
FINANCE__FED_FEC_INDEPENDENT_EXPENDITURE.row: One spending line: one payment by one outside group for or against one candidate.

cols.SUB_ID: The FEC's unique 19-digit ID for this one transaction row.
cols.CMTE_ID: The Federal Election Commission's ID for the political committee, a C and eight digits like C00493783.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.EMPLOYER: The donor's employer, as written, like RETIRED or NOT EMPLOYED; placeholders like N/A are common. Almost always blank in the committee-to-candidate table.
cols.OCCUPATION: The person's job as they wrote it, like RETIRED or Attorney, not cleaned. The mine accident table uses NO VALUE FOUND as a filler, and one FEC table leaves it almost always blank.
cols.TRANSACTION_DATE: The date the money moved or the trade or shipment happened.
cols.TRANSACTION_AMT: The dollar amount of the transaction. Some rows in the committee-to-candidate table are 0 or negative, like -1 or -5.
cols.OTHER_ID: The FEC ID of the other committee or candidate in the transaction, usually a C followed by 8 digits. Often blank in the individual donations table.
cols.MEMO_TEXT: A free-text note on the transaction, like EARMARKED FOR a named committee or DIRECT CONTRIBUTION. Often blank, and mostly blank in the committee-to-candidate table.
cols.MEMO_CD: X marks a memo line, not new money. Leave X rows out when adding up dollars. Almost always blank.
cols.IS_MEMO_TRANSACTION: True if the row is a memo line, not new money. Leave these out when adding up dollars.
cols.CYCLE_FILE: The election cycle of the FEC file, an even year like 2018.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.DONOR_NAME: The giver's name, last name first, like JOHNSON, THOMAS. Spelled as filed, so one person can appear many ways.
cols.TRANSACTION_TYPE: A short code for the kind of contribution, like 15, 15E or 24T. Codes need a lookup.
cols.ENTITY_TYPE: A code for the kind of giver: IND, ORG, CAN, PAC, CCM, COM, PTY or TRB. Almost all IND; codes need a lookup.

FINANCE__FED_FEC_INDIV_CONTRIBUTIONS.summary: Every itemized contribution to federal campaigns and committees from the FEC's bulk files, about 284 million rows. About 1.6 million are memo rows that repeat money already counted, so leave them out when adding up.
FINANCE__FED_FEC_INDIV_CONTRIBUTIONS.row: One itemized contribution: one giver, one committee, one date and amount.

cols.CAND_ELECTION_YR: The election year the candidate is running in, like 2024.
cols.FEC_ELECTION_YR: The two-year election cycle, named by its ending year like 2024.
cols.CMTE_TP: One letter for the committee's type, like H House campaign, S Senate, P President, Q or N a PAC, O a super PAC. Needs the FEC lookup for the rest.
cols.CMTE_DSGN: One letter for the committee's role: P is a candidate's main campaign, A authorized, J joint fundraiser, U unauthorized, B lobbyist PAC, D leadership PAC.
cols.LINKAGE_ID: The FEC's ID number for one link between a candidate and a committee.
cols.FEC_CANDIDATE_ID: The FEC's ID for the candidate, like S8NY00249.
cols.FEC_COMMITTEE_ID: The FEC's ID for the committee, like C00750935.

cols.CU_NUMBER: The federal regulator's charter number for the credit union. A number stored as text.
cols.CYCLE_DATE: The quarter-end date the credit union report covers, like 2026-03-31.
cols.JOIN_NUMBER: A number for linking a credit union's rows across the report files. Text in one table, a number in the other.
cols.RSSD: The Federal Reserve's ID number for the bank or credit union.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state, as two letters like TX in some tables and as a number code like 48 or 06 in others, which needs a lookup and sometimes drops its leading zero. One table writes it like US_TX, and one leaves it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY_CODE: The county's number code, written different ways: three digits like 001, sometimes without leading zeros like 3, five digits with the state like 11001, or state letters plus digits like FL095. One table uses name codes like US_SD_CLARK, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.CONG_DIST: The congressional district. Just the number in the credit union table; state plus number like WI-02 in the NIH table.
cols.STREET: The street address line, like 925 DAYNA ST or PO BOX 505. Some rows hold UNKNOWN instead.
cols.INSURED_DATE: The date the bank or credit union got federal deposit insurance. The credit union table has placeholder dates like 1900-01-01, and the failed-banks table is empty.

cols.CU_TYPE: The kind of credit union charter, as a code 1, 2 or 3. Needs a lookup.
cols.CU_NAME: The credit union's name, like GROW FINANCIAL.
cols.CHARTERSTATE: The state where the credit union is chartered, as two letters.
cols.SMSA: A metro area code. 9998 fills almost every row and looks like a placeholder; the rest need a lookup.
cols.ATTENTION_OF: An attention line for mail, like a person or a PO box. Blank on almost every row.
cols.REGION: The NCUA region, as a number 1, 2, 3 or 8. Needs a lookup.
cols.SE: A one-letter NCUA code, like A to L. Needs a lookup.
cols.DISTRICT: The NCUA district, as a number. Needs a lookup.
cols.YEAR_OPENED: The year the credit union opened.
cols.TOM_CODE: A two-digit NCUA code, like 99 or 00. Needs a lookup.
cols.LIMITED_INC: 1 or 0, a limited-income flag. Needs a lookup to be sure what it means.
cols.ISSUE_DATE: The date the charter was issued. Many are January 1 of a year, so the exact day may be a stand-in.
cols.PEER_GROUP: The size group NCUA puts the credit union in, 1 to 6. Needs a lookup.
cols.QUARTER_FLAG: Always 0 in this table, so it tells you nothing.
cols.ISMDI: True if the credit union is minority-owned, False if not.
cols.AM_DATEHELD: The date and time of the credit union's annual meeting, mostly in spring 2026.

FINANCE__FED_NCUA_CALL_REPORTS_FS220.summary: The main financial statement of every federally insured credit union for the March 2026 quarter, as filed with the credit union regulator NCUA: about 245 money lines per credit union.
FINANCE__FED_NCUA_CALL_REPORTS_FS220.row: One credit union: its full quarterly financial statement, one line item per column.

cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.REGION: The NCUA region number that handled the merger: 1, 2 or 3.
cols.CONTINUING_CREDIT_UNION_CHARTER: The charter number of the credit union that survives the merger.
cols.CONTINUING_NAME: The name of the credit union that survives the merger.
cols.CONTINUING_LOCATION: City and state of the surviving credit union, like LOMBARD, IL.
cols.CONTINUING_ASSETS: Total assets of the surviving credit union, in dollars.
cols.MERGING_CREDIT_UNION_CHARTER: The charter number of the credit union that is folded in. Each row has its own value.
cols.MERGING_CREDIT_UNION_NAME: The name of the credit union that is folded in.
cols.MERGING_LOCATION: City and state of the credit union that is folded in.
cols.MERGING_ASSETS: Total assets of the credit union that is folded in, in dollars.
cols.MERGING_REASON: Why it merged: EXPANDED SERVICES, INABILITY TO OBTAIN OFFICIALS or POOR FINANCIAL CONDITION.
cols.CONTINUING_FIELD_OF_MEMBERSHIP: Who can join the surviving credit union, in its own words.
cols.MERGING_FIELD_OF_MEMBERSHIP: Who could join the folded-in credit union, in its own words.

FINANCE__FED_NCUA_CHARTER_MERGER_EVENTS.row: One merger: one credit union folding into another.

cols.MEMBERS: How many members the credit union or labor union has.
cols.TOTAL_ASSETS: Total assets in dollars, whether of a credit union, hospital, bankruptcy filer, or labor union.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CHARTER_NUMBER: The credit union's NCUA charter number, its main ID.
cols.YEAR_AND_QUARTER: The quarter the numbers cover. Every row reads 2026.1, the first quarter of 2026.
cols.STREET_MAILING_ADDRESS: The street or P.O. box of the mailing address.
cols.CITY_MAILING_ADDRESS: The city of the mailing address.
cols.STATE_MAILING_ADDRESS: The two-letter state of the mailing address.
cols.ZIP_CODE_MAILING_ADDRESS: The ZIP code of the mailing address.
cols.CREDIT_UNION_TYPE: FCU for a federally chartered credit union, FISCU for a state-chartered one with federal insurance.
cols.NCUA_REGION: The NCUA region number that oversees the credit union: 1, 2, 3 or 8.
cols.LOW_INCOME_DESIGNATION: Yes if NCUA has marked it as serving mostly low-income members, No if not.
cols.RETURN_ON_AVERAGE_ASSETS: Profit as a percent of average assets.
cols.NET_WORTH_RATIO_EXCLUDES_CECL_TRANSITION: Net worth as a percent of assets, leaving out a temporary accounting relief.
cols.LOAN_TO_SHARE_RATIO: Loans as a percent of member deposits. Over 100 means it has lent out more than it holds.
cols.TOTAL_DEPOSITS_4_QUARTER_GROWTH: Percent change in deposits over the past year.
cols.TOTAL_LOANS_4_QUARTER_GROWTH: Percent change in loans over the past year. Can be negative.
cols.TOTAL_ASSETS_4_QUARTER_GROWTH: Percent change in total assets over the past year.
cols.MEMBERS_4_QUARTER_GROWTH: Percent change in membership over the past year. Can be negative.
cols.NET_WORTH_4_QUARTER_GROWTH_EXCLUDES_CECL: Percent change in net worth over the past year, leaving out a temporary accounting relief.
cols.NCUA_INTERNAL_ID_JOIN_NUMBER: NCUA's internal ID number for the credit union, used to join its other files.

FINANCE__FED_SENATE_EFD_PTR.summary: Stock, bond and other asset trades senators reported on periodic transaction reports, scraped from the Senate's filing website.
FINANCE__FED_SENATE_EFD_PTR.row: One trade line on one filing: who owned the asset, what it was, and whether it was bought or sold.

cols.TRANSACTION_DATE: The date the money moved or the trade or shipment happened.
cols.TICKER: The company's stock ticker symbol, like AAPL. "--", "N/A" or blank means none was given.
cols.ASSET_DESCRIPTION: The stock, bond, or fund the senator bought or sold, as typed on the form. Some rows only say the filing was a scanned PDF, and some carry web leftovers like &.
cols.ASSET_TYPE: What kind of asset was traded, like Stock, Corporate Bond, or Municipal Security. PDF Disclosed Filing means the details are only in a scanned form.
cols.AMOUNT: The dollar amount. In the Senate stock table it is a text range like $1,001 - $15,000 or the word Unknown, not an exact number.
cols.COMMENT: The filer's free-text note on the trade. Two dashes mean no comment.
cols.SENATOR: The senator's name. One table writes Last, First plus Senator; the others write First Last.
cols.PTR_LINK: A web link to the senator's stock trade report on the Senate disclosure site.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.OWNER: Whose account made the trade: Self, Spouse, Joint or Child. N/A shows up as a placeholder.
cols.TYPE: The kind of trade: Purchase, full Sale, partial Sale or Exchange. N/A shows up as a placeholder.

FINANCE__FED_SENATE_STOCK_WATCHER.summary: Stock and other trades US senators reported in their periodic transaction reports, gathered by the Senate Stock Watcher project.
FINANCE__FED_SENATE_STOCK_WATCHER.row: One reported trade: one asset bought or sold by a senator or their family on one day.

cols.LEI: The company's Legal Entity Identifier, a 20-character global ID. The FDIC table's values are only 16 characters, so they look cut short.
cols.ACRONYM: A short name or abbreviation for the organization. Mostly blank; in the French portal table some cells hold a full name instead.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.WEBSITE: The organization's website address, with or without www or https. A few rows in the energy-efficiency table hold a sentence of text instead.
cols.LAST_UPDATE_DATE: The date the record was last updated at the source.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.MIC: The market's four-letter code, like XNAS. Each row has its own value.
cols.OPERATING_MIC: The code of the main venue that runs this market. Segments carry their parent's code.
cols.OPRT_SGMT: OPRT if this code is a main operating venue, SGMT if it is a segment of one.
cols.MARKET_NAME_INSTITUTION_DESCRIPTION: The market's name, like BULGARIAN STOCK EXCHANGE - MAIN MARKET.
cols.LEGAL_ENTITY_NAME: The company that legally runs the market, like NASDAQ STOCKHOLM AB. Blank for more than half.
cols.MARKET_CATEGORY_CODE: The kind of market, as a four-letter code like NSPD, MLTF or ATSS. The codes need a lookup.
cols.ISO_COUNTRY_CODE_ISO_3166: The market's country, as two letters like GB or US.
cols.STATUS: Whether the code is ACTIVE, EXPIRED or UPDATED.
cols.CREATION_DATE: The date the code was created.
cols.LAST_VALIDATION_DATE: The date the entry was last checked. Mostly blank.
cols.EXPIRY_DATE: The date the code expired. Filled only for expired codes.
cols.COMMENTS: Free-text notes on the market, like DARK POOL or SYSTEMATIC INTERNALISER. Blank for almost half.

FINANCE__INTL_ISO_MIC_REGISTRY.summary: Every stock exchange, trading platform and market segment in the world with an official ISO market identifier code, with its operator, country and status.
FINANCE__INTL_ISO_MIC_REGISTRY.row: One market code: one trading venue or one segment of a venue.

cols.COMPANY_NAME: The company's name as the source wrote it, so one company can show up several ways, like Wal-Mart Stores and Walmart Inc. One table leaves it empty.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_1: The first line of the street address, like 13 STATION ROAD.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_2: The second address line, often a suite or floor but sometimes a street or area name. Blank for many rows, one table leaves it empty, and two fill it with a lone dash.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.OSFI_FI_RECORD_ID: A code for the institution record. Each row has its own.
cols.FI_TYPE_NAME: The broad kind of institution: a federally regulated financial institution or a foreign bank representative office.
cols.FI_GROUP_NAME: The group the institution falls in, like banks, life insurers, or property and casualty insurers.
cols.FI_INDUSTRY_NAME: The narrower industry, like domestic banks, foreign bank branches, or Canadian life insurers.
cols.CANADIAN_TRADE_COMPANY_NAME: The name the company trades under in Canada, when different. Mostly blank.
cols.REPRESENTATIVE_NAME: The person named as the institution's top contact. Some names have double spaces.
cols.TITLE: That person's job title, like chief executive officer or chief agent. The same title is written several ways.
cols.PROVINCE_STATE: The province of the head office in Canada, mostly Ontario.
cols.POSTAL_ZIP_CODE: The head office's postal code, like M5H 1J8.
cols.AUTHORIZED_INSURANCE_CLASSES: The kinds of insurance an insurer may sell, listed with semicolons, like life, and accident and sickness.

FINANCE__INTL_OSFI_REGULATED_FI.summary: Canada's register of federally regulated financial companies kept by OSFI, its bank and insurance regulator: banks, insurers, trust and loan companies and fraternal benefit societies, with head-office contacts.
FINANCE__INTL_OSFI_REGULATED_FI.row: One institution: one bank, insurer or other financial company regulated by Canada's federal government.
