FINANCE__INTL_WB_IDS.summary: World Bank International Debt Statistics: what poorer countries owe foreign lenders and pay back each year, one yearly column from 1970 to 2032, with the later years being scheduled payments.
FINANCE__INTL_WB_IDS.row: One country and one debt measure: a series like loans from multilateral lenders to the government, with a value for every year.

cols.FILING_ID: The ID of one filing or report. Some tables use long random-looking codes, others plain numbers.
cols.BIOGUIDE: The member of Congress's official ID, a letter and six digits like A000383.
cols.MATCH_NOTE: A note on how the row was matched to other data, like last name or ambiguous: 2 people share it. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.TRANSACTION_DATE: The date the money moved or the trade or shipment happened.
cols.FILED_DATE: The date the filing was submitted. One table includes the time too, and the Senate trades table is mostly blank.
cols.TICKER: The company's stock ticker symbol, like AAPL. "--", "N/A" or blank means none was given.
cols.ASSET_DESCRIPTION: The stock, bond, or fund the senator bought or sold, as typed on the form. Some rows only say the filing was a scanned PDF, and some carry web leftovers like &.
cols.ASSET_TYPE: What kind of asset was traded, like Stock, Corporate Bond, or Municipal Security. PDF Disclosed Filing means the details are only in a scanned form.
cols.AMOUNT_RANGE: The dollar range of the trade, like $1,001 - $15,000. Senators report ranges, not exact amounts; some rows say Unknown.
cols.COMMENT: The filer's free-text note on the trade. Two dashes mean no comment.
cols.PTR_LINK: A web link to the senator's stock trade report on the Senate disclosure site.
cols.FILING_KIND: How the Senate stock-trade disclosure was filed: ptr for an online trade report, or paper.
cols.IS_AMENDMENT: True if the filing amends an earlier one, False if not. Stored as text.
cols.SOURCE_ID: A short name for the source feed the row came from, like fed_cfpb_complaints. In the ITIS other-sources table it is a plain number instead, which needs a lookup.
cols.SENATOR_RAW: The senator's name as written on the filing, in many styles.
cols.SENATOR_NAME: The senator's cleaned-up name, like Tommy Tuberville. Use this to group by senator.
cols.OWNER: Who owned the asset: Self, Spouse, Joint or Child. N/A on a few rows.
cols.TRANSACTION_TYPE: Purchase, a full sale, a partial sale, or Exchange. N/A on a few rows.

FINANCE__SENATE_TRADES.summary: Stock trades US senators reported, from mid-2012 on, joined from two sources: Senate Stock Watcher up to 2020 and the Senate filing site from 2021.
FINANCE__SENATE_TRADES.row: One reported trade line: one senator, one asset, one buy or sell, with a dollar range.

cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit National Provider Identifier, stored as text. Some tables leave it mostly blank or empty, and the SAM exclusions table uses 0000000000 as a filler.
cols.EXCLUSION_TYPE: Why the person or company is barred. HHS tables use the law section as a code like 1128a1; the SAM tables use words like Voluntary Exclusion. It is almost always blank in the health-center people table.
cols.EXCLUSION_DATE: The date the provider was barred from federal health programs. One table writes it as 8 digits like 20260720, and it is almost always blank in the health-center staff table.
cols.FACILITY_TYPE: What kind of facility it is, like Hospital, Nursing home, Health Center, or Apartment in the HUD housing table. One table leaves it empty.
cols.EXCLUDED_LAST: The banned worker's last name, as the federal exclusion list spells it.
cols.EXCLUDED_FIRST: The banned worker's first name, as the federal exclusion list spells it.
cols.FACILITY_CCN: The Medicare certification number of the facility the worker is tied to, six characters. Use it to join to other Medicare facility tables.

EXCLUDED_PROVIDER_AT_FACILITY.summary: A story lead, not a finding: 39 health workers banned from federal health programs who still show up as tied to a Medicare facility, matched on their exact provider number; the facility list was only partly loaded, so the count will grow.
EXCLUDED_PROVIDER_AT_FACILITY.row: One match: one banned health worker paired with one Medicare facility they are listed at.

cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit National Provider Identifier, stored as text. Some tables leave it mostly blank or empty, and the SAM exclusions table uses 0000000000 as a filler.
cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.EXCLUSION_TYPE: Why the person or company is barred. HHS tables use the law section as a code like 1128a1; the SAM tables use words like Voluntary Exclusion. It is almost always blank in the health-center people table.
cols.EXCLUSION_YEAR: The year the provider was banned from federal health programs.
cols.POST_EXCLUSION_PAYMENTS: How many payments the banned provider got after the ban.
cols.TOTAL_PAID_AFTER_EXCLUSION: Total dollars paid to the banned provider after the ban.
cols.FIRST_PAID_YEAR: The first year the banned provider got paid after the ban, 2023 or 2024.
cols.LAST_PAID_YEAR: The last year the banned provider got paid after the ban, 2023 or 2024.
cols.DISTINCT_PAYERS: How many different companies paid the banned provider.

EXCLUDED_PROVIDER_PAID_AFTER_EXCLUSION.summary: A lead list of 287 providers banned from federal health programs who still got drug- or device-company payments in a year after their ban; it needs human review before use.
EXCLUDED_PROVIDER_PAID_AFTER_EXCLUSION.row: One banned provider: their ban and the industry payments that came after it.

cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit National Provider Identifier, stored as text. Some tables leave it mostly blank or empty, and the SAM exclusions table uses 0000000000 as a filler.
cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.EXCLUSION_TYPE: Why the person or company is barred. HHS tables use the law section as a code like 1128a1; the SAM tables use words like Voluntary Exclusion. It is almost always blank in the health-center people table.
cols.EXCLUSION_YEAR: The year the provider was banned from federal health programs.
cols.POST_EXCLUSION_PAYMENTS: How many payments the banned provider got after the ban.
cols.TOTAL_PAID_AFTER_EXCLUSION: Total dollars paid to the banned provider after the ban.
cols.FIRST_PAID_YEAR: The first year the banned provider got paid after the ban, 2023 or 2024.
cols.LAST_PAID_YEAR: The last year the banned provider got paid after the ban, 2023 or 2024.
cols.DISTINCT_PAYERS: How many different companies paid the banned provider.
cols.ZIP5: The 5-digit ZIP code, stored as text so leading zeros like 00623 survive.
cols.COUNTY_FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 01001, stored as text. One table holds only the three-digit county part like 017, one holds N/A, and two leave it empty.
cols.IN_DESIGNATED_SHORTAGE_COUNTY: True if the county is officially short of health workers.
cols.EXCL_STATE: State on the provider's exclusion record, as two letters.
cols.SHORTAGE_PRIMARY_CARE: 1 if the county is a primary care shortage area, 0 if not.
cols.SHORTAGE_MENTAL_HEALTH: 1 if the county is a mental health shortage area, 0 if not.
cols.SHORTAGE_DENTAL: 1 if the county is a dental care shortage area, 0 if not.

EXCLUDED_PROVIDER_PAID_AFTER_EXCLUSION_I.summary: A lead for review, not a finding: 287 providers banned from federal health programs who still got drug or device industry payments after their ban, with whether their county is a federal health shortage area; the notes flag a caveat on how the county was matched.
EXCLUDED_PROVIDER_PAID_AFTER_EXCLUSION_I.row: One excluded provider: one banned doctor or clinician paid by industry after exclusion.

cols.PARENT_UEI: The 12-character federal contractor ID of the parent company. Mostly blank in the crosswalk.
cols.COMPANY_NAME: The company's name as the source wrote it, so one company can show up several ways, like Wal-Mart Stores and Walmart Inc. One table leaves it empty.
cols.MATCH_CONFIDENCE: How sure the name match is, from 0 to 1. Only 1.00, 0.85 or 0.80 appear; mostly blank in the crosswalk.
cols.VIOLATING_FACILITIES: How many of the company's facilities were penalized or cited; 1 for all but one company.
cols.ANY_SNC: Y or N: whether any facility is a serious violator. N on every row, so none are.
cols.TOTAL_EPA_PENALTIES: Total EPA penalty dollars across the company's facilities. 0 for 23 companies.
cols.TOTAL_FORMAL_ACTIONS: How many formal EPA enforcement actions hit the company's facilities.
cols.FEDERAL_DOLLARS_OBLIGATED: Total federal contract dollars promised to the company.
cols.N_AWARDS: How many federal contracts the company holds.
cols.N_AGENCIES: How many federal agencies gave the company contracts.

FEDERAL_CONTRACTOR_EPA_VIOLATOR.summary: A lead list, not a finding: 57 companies that hold federal contracts and also own EPA facilities that were penalized or cited. It only covers facilities matched to a parent company, so it misses many.
FEDERAL_CONTRACTOR_EPA_VIOLATOR.row: One company: one federal contractor tied to at least one penalized or cited EPA facility.

cols.CCN: The facility's 6-character Medicare certification number, stored as text; some hold letters, like 38T061. It is almost always blank in the three Open Payments tables.
cols.HOSPITAL_NAME: The hospital's name. In the officer-pay table some rows are foundations or other groups, not hospitals.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP5: The 5-digit ZIP code, stored as text so leading zeros like 00623 survive.
cols.COUNTY_FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 01001, stored as text. One table holds only the three-digit county part like 017, one holds N/A, and two leave it empty.
cols.TYPE_OF_CONTROL: A number code for who owns or runs the hospital, like church, for-profit or government. Needs the CMS lookup to read; stored as text.
cols.NET_PATIENT_REVENUE: The hospital's patient income for the year, in dollars, after discounts.
cols.IN_DESIGNATED_SHORTAGE_COUNTY: True if the county is officially short of health workers.
cols.IS_RURAL: True when the hospital is in a rural area.
cols.FY_END: The last day of the hospital's fiscal year used here, written like 12/31/2023. Stored as text.
cols.OPERATING_INCOME: What the hospital made or lost on patient care that year, in dollars. Negative means a loss.
cols.OPERATING_MARGIN_PCT: Patient-care profit or loss as a percent of patient revenue, like -2.4.
cols.MEDICAID_REVENUE: Money the hospital got from Medicaid that year, in dollars. Blank for about a quarter of hospitals.
cols.MEDICAID_DEPENDENCE_PCT: Medicaid's share of the hospital's patient revenue, in percent, like 8.6.
cols.UNCOMPENSATED_CARE: The cost of care the hospital gave and was not paid for, in dollars.
cols.NEGATIVE_OPERATING_MARGIN: True when the hospital lost money on patient care. True for almost every row.
cols.MEDICAID_DEPENDENT: True when Medicaid makes up a large share of the hospital's revenue.
cols.RISK_TIER: The closure-risk label this analysis gave the hospital: elevated, high or critical.

HOSPITAL_CLOSURE_RISK.summary: A lead that still needs human review: Medicare hospitals that lose money on patient care or lean heavily on Medicaid, flagged by closure risk and whether they are rural, from their latest cost reports.
HOSPITAL_CLOSURE_RISK.row: One hospital: its latest-year operating margin, Medicaid dependence and closure-risk tier.

cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.AT_RISK_HOSPITALS: How many hospitals in the state are flagged at risk of closing.
cols.CRITICAL: How many at-risk hospitals are in the critical tier.
cols.HIGH: How many at-risk hospitals are in the high tier. 0 in most states.
cols.RURAL: How many at-risk hospitals are rural.
cols.IN_SHORTAGE_COUNTY: How many at-risk hospitals sit in a county short of health workers.

HOSPITAL_CLOSURE_RISK_BY_STATE.summary: Counts of hospitals at risk of closing in each state, by risk level; an early lead that needs human review before anything is published.
HOSPITAL_CLOSURE_RISK_BY_STATE.row: One state or territory and its counts of at-risk hospitals.

cols.BIOGUIDE: The member of Congress's official ID, a letter and six digits like A000383.
cols.FULL_NAME: The full name of the person, like Nancy Pelosi. In the court table it is the court's full name.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.CHAMBER: Which chamber of Congress: House or Senate. Some tables write rep or sen, and one also has President.
cols.IDEOLOGY_LABEL: A plain label for the member's politics: left/liberal, right/conservative or unknown, with a handful marked centrist.
cols.N_PAC_DONORS: How many different PACs gave money to the member of Congress.
cols.BILLS_SPONSORED: How many bills the member of Congress introduced as lead sponsor.
cols.BILLS_ENACTED: How many of the member's bills became law.
cols.MISSED_VOTE_PCT: The percent of votes the member of Congress missed.
cols.PARTY_UNITY_PCT: The percent of votes where the member voted with their party.
cols.REVIEW_TIER: How strongly the row is flagged for a closer look: high, medium, low, or context_only.
cols.PARTY: The member's party: Republican, Democrat or Independent.
cols.TOTAL_SUPPORT_USD: All money backing the member: PAC gifts plus outside spending for them, in dollars, summed across election cycles.
cols.PAC_USD: Money PACs gave the member, in dollars, summed across cycles.
cols.OUTSIDE_FOR_USD: Outside group spending in the member's favor, in dollars, summed across cycles. Often 0.
cols.BILLS_SUBSTANTIVE: How many real bills the member sponsored, not counting ceremonial ones.
cols.ADVANCED_PAST_COMMITTEE: How many of the member's bills got past committee.
cols.COSPONSORED: How many bills the member signed onto as a cosponsor.
cols.MONEY_PCTILE: Where the member ranks on money, from 0 to 1; higher means more money.
cols.ABSENTEE_PCTILE: Where the member ranks on missed votes, from 0 to 1; higher means more missed.
cols.HIGH_MONEY_ZERO_OUTPUT: True for members with lots of money and no bill output. Only a handful are true.

MEMBER_MONEY_VS_OUTPUT.summary: A lead list, not a finding: 635 members of Congress ranked by campaign money against how many bills they moved and how many votes they missed. Low bill counts can have innocent reasons, so a person must review each one.
MEMBER_MONEY_VS_OUTPUT.row: One member: one member of Congress, with their money totals, bill counts and percentile ranks.

cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit National Provider Identifier, stored as text. Some tables leave it mostly blank or empty, and the SAM exclusions table uses 0000000000 as a filler.
cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.SPECIALTY: The provider's medical specialty or job, like Family Practice or Pharmacist.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP5: The 5-digit ZIP code, stored as text so leading zeros like 00623 survive.
cols.TOTAL_CLAIMS: How many prescriptions the prescriber wrote that Medicare Part D paid for, counting refills.
cols.REVIEW_TIER: How strongly the row is flagged for a closer look: high, medium, low, or context_only.
cols.OPIOID_RATE: Percent of the prescriber's Medicare drug claims that were for opioids.
cols.OPIOID_CLAIMS: How many Medicare opioid claims the prescriber wrote.
cols.RATE_PCTILE_IN_SPECIALTY: Where the prescriber's opioid rate ranks within their specialty, as a fraction. 0.9 or higher means the top tenth.
cols.OPIOID_PAY_USD: Dollars the prescriber received from companies tied to opioid or pain products.
cols.OPIOID_PAY_COUNT: How many such payments the prescriber received.
cols.DISTINCT_OPIOID_PAYERS: How many different companies made those payments.
cols.COUNTY_FIPS_2015: The five-digit code of the prescriber's county, as of 2015.
cols.OVERDOSE_BAND_2015: The county's 2015 drug overdose death rate, as a range like 14.1-16.
cols.OVERDOSE_BAND_LO_2015: The low end of that overdose rate range, as a number.
cols.IN_HIGH_OVERDOSE_COUNTY_2015: true when the prescriber's county had a high overdose rate in 2015.

OPIOID_PRESCRIBER_PAID_HIGH_RX.summary: A lead list, not a finding: Medicare drug-plan prescribers who took opioid or pain-drug company money in 2022 to 2024 and rank in the top tenth of opioid prescribers in their own specialty. It needs human review before anything is published.
OPIOID_PRESCRIBER_PAID_HIGH_RX.row: One prescriber: one doctor or other prescriber with their opioid prescribing, drug company payments and home county overdose level.

cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.FLAGGED_PRESCRIBERS: How many heavy opioid prescribers in the state took opioid-maker money.
cols.HIGH_TIER: How many of the flagged prescribers fall in the highest tier. 0 in most states.
cols.MEDIUM_TIER: How many of the flagged prescribers fall in the middle tier.
cols.IN_HIGH_OVERDOSE_COUNTY_2015: How many of the flagged prescribers practice in a county with high overdose deaths in 2015.
cols.TOTAL_OPIOID_PAY_USD: The total opioid-maker money paid to the state's flagged prescribers, in dollars.
cols.AVG_OPIOID_RATE: The average opioid prescribing rate of the state's flagged prescribers, as a percent like 51.9.

OPIOID_PRESCRIBER_PAID_HIGH_RX_BY_STATE.summary: A state-by-state count of heavy opioid prescribers who also took money from opioid painkiller makers, with the total paid, built as a map layer. These are leads, and a person must check them before anything is published.
OPIOID_PRESCRIBER_PAID_HIGH_RX_BY_STATE.row: One state: the flagged-prescriber totals for one state.

cols.CMTE_ID: The Federal Election Commission's ID for the political committee, a C and eight digits like C00493783.
cols.CMTE_NAME: The committee's name, like ZINC COLLECTIVE PAC or a candidate's own campaign committee.
cols.CONNECTED_ORG: The company, union or group behind the committee, as the committee wrote it. Blank for about a quarter; some say NONE.
cols.CMTE_TYPE: A one-letter FEC code for the kind of committee, like Q, N or H. The codes need a lookup.
cols.MEMBERS_FUNDED: How many different members of Congress the committee gave to.
cols.DEM_MEMBERS: How many of those members are Democrats.
cols.REP_MEMBERS: How many of those members are Republicans.
cols.TOTAL_USD: Total dollars the committee gave to members, both parties.
cols.TOTAL_TO_DEMS: Dollars the committee gave to Democrats.
cols.TOTAL_TO_REPS: Dollars the committee gave to Republicans.
cols.BIPARTISAN_BALANCE: How evenly the committee split between parties, from 0 for all one side to 1 for an even split.
cols.BOTH_SIDES_FLAG: True when the committee gave to a real number of members in both parties. True for about half.

PAC_FUNDS_BOTH_SIDES.summary: A lead list, not a finding: for each federal political committee, how many members of Congress it gave to in each party and how much, to spot committees that fund both sides. Needs a human check before use.
PAC_FUNDS_BOTH_SIDES.row: One committee: one political committee's giving to sitting members of Congress, split by party.

cols.EIN: The organization's 9-digit federal tax ID number, stored as text. Some rows hold 000000000 as a filler or only 8 digits because a leading zero was lost, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.ORG_NAME: The name of the organization, like a charity, campaign committee, university or pharmacy chain. In the drinking-water table it often holds a person's name instead, and two tables leave it mostly blank.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.NTEE_CODE: The nonprofit's category code, a letter plus two or three more characters like E22 for hospitals or X20 for Christian groups. Needs a lookup.
cols.REVOCATION_DATE: The date the IRS took away the group's tax-exempt status. One table stores it as text like 15-NOV-2010.
cols.REVENUE_AMT: The nonprofit's total yearly revenue in dollars, from its latest filing. Zero often means not reported, and one table stores it as text.
cols.ASSET_AMT: The nonprofit's total assets in dollars, from its latest filing. Zero often means not reported, and one table stores it as text.
cols.REVOKED_EXEMPTION_TYPE: The kind of tax exemption the group lost, as a two-digit code like 03 or 08. The codes need a lookup.
cols.REVIEW_BUCKET: long_tail for smaller groups, or whale_review_individually for big ones that need a closer look.

REVOKED_BUT_DEDUCTIBLE.summary: A lead list, not a finding: 22,512 nonprofits the IRS stripped of tax-exempt status that its own master file still lists as tax-deductible. Needs a person's review before use.
REVOKED_BUT_DEDUCTIBLE.row: One nonprofit: one organization, matched by EIN, that lost tax-exempt status but still shows as deductible.

cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ORGS: Number of revoked but still-deductible charities in the state.
cols.LONG_TAIL_ORGS: Count of the smaller charities in the long tail; the cutoff is not stated.
cols.WHALE_ORGS: Count of the biggest charities, the whales; the cutoff is not stated. Most states have 0.
cols.REVENUE_MILLIONS: Their total reported revenue, in millions of dollars.

REVOKED_BUT_DEDUCTIBLE_BY_STATE.summary: A state-by-state count of charities the IRS stripped of tax-exempt status, never reinstated, yet still lists as tax-deductible, with their reported revenue.
REVOKED_BUT_DEDUCTIBLE_BY_STATE.row: One state: how many such charities it has and their revenue.

cols.PERSON_NAME: The name of the person tied to the record. Some tables mix in company names or court case names, some leave it mostly blank, and four leave it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.TERMINATION_DATE: The date the thing ended, like a registration, recall or judge's service, and blank when it has not ended. Some rows hold far-future dates like 2101-01-04 or 2200-12-30.
cols.REGISTRANT_NAME: The name of whoever registered, like a lobbying firm, fund, foreign agent, aircraft owner or offender, with people often last name first. The aircraft table also uses REGISTRATION PENDING as a filler.
cols.DOCUMENT_TYPE: What kind of document it is, like SEC insider Form 4 or a FARA Supplemental Statement; categories depend on the source. It is almost always blank in the slave narratives table and empty in one table.
cols.ADDRESS_1: The first line of the street address. In the foreign-agent table it is mostly blank and sometimes holds just a city like Washington.
cols.ADDRESS_2: The second line of the address, like a suite or floor, blank for many rows. The FDA recall tables often say N/A instead.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.ZIP: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Fillers like 00000, UNKNO or a lone dash show up, some codes lost a leading zero like 8721, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.SOURCE_FILE: The file or link the row was loaded from, like FARA_All_Registrants.csv or a quarter like 2024q2.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.FARA_REGISTRATION_KEY: A made-up ID for the row. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.REGISTRATION_NUMBER: The FARA registration number of the agent or firm, like 3301. Use it to tie records to one registrant.
cols.COMPANY_ID: Despite the name, holds firm names like LS2group, not IDs. Filled on only 221 rows.
cols.DATE: The date on the record; what it marks depends on the file. Mostly blank.
cols.REGISTRANT_DATE: When the agent or firm registered. Mostly blank, filled only on foreign-client records.
cols.DOC_URL: A web link to the filed document. Some say Available-FARA-Public-Office instead of a link.
cols.SHORT_FORM_NAME: The full name of a person who filed a short form as an agent. Name order and capitals vary.
cols.SHORT_FORM_LAST_NAME: The last name of a person who filed a short form. Mostly blank.
cols.SHORT_FORM_FIRST_NAME: The first name of a person who filed a short form. Mostly blank.
cols.SHORT_FORM_DATE: When the person filed the short form. Mostly blank.
cols.SHORT_FORM_TERMINATION_DATE: When the person stopped being an agent. Mostly blank.
cols.FOREIGN_PRINCIPAL: The foreign client, like Government of Mexico. Mostly blank.
cols.FOREIGN_PRINCIPAL_NAME: The foreign client's name, like Royal Embassy of Saudi Arabia. Mostly blank.
cols.FOREIGN_PRINCIPAL_COUNTRY: The foreign client's country, in capitals, like SAUDI ARABIA. Mostly blank.
cols.FOREIGN_PRINCIPAL_REGISTRATION_DATE: When the foreign client was first listed. Mostly blank.
cols.FOREIGN_PRINCIPAL_TERMINATION_DATE: When the work for the foreign client ended. Mostly blank.
cols.COUNTRY_LOCATION_REPRESENTED: The country the agent represents, in capitals, like JAPAN. Mostly blank.
cols.IS_ACTIVE_REGISTRATION: True if the agent's registration is still active.
cols.IS_ACTIVE_FOREIGN_PRINCIPAL: True if the work for the foreign client is still going.
cols.SOURCE_LINK: Which of the four FARA bulk files the row came from, as a web link.
cols.DATE_STAMPED: When FARA stamped the document as received. Filled only on document records.

FOREIGN_INFLUENCE__FED_FARA_BULK.summary: The Justice Department's foreign agent filings: who registered to lobby or do PR for a foreign government or group, who they worked for, and the documents they filed, from four bulk files stacked together.
FOREIGN_INFLUENCE__FED_FARA_BULK.row: One FARA record: a registrant, a filed document, an individual agent's short form, or a foreign client, depending on which bulk file it came from.

cols.AGENCY: The government agency tied to the record, written differently by table: EPA or State, a full department name, a bracketed list in the Federal Register, or number codes in the federal appeals table, where most rows hold -9.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.POSITION_KEY: A made-up ID for each job, one per row. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.INDUSTRY_SECTOR: The main industry tied to the job, like Real Estate, Energy or Defense. Same values as SECTOR1.
cols.POSITION_TYPE: Whether the job is Senate-confirmed or appointed without a Senate vote. Two rows say nan, a placeholder for blank.
cols.POSITION_NAME: The job title, like Director or General Counsel.
cols.POSITION_DEPARTMENT: The department or office the job sits in, like the Department of the Treasury.
cols.POSITION_DESCRIPTION: A short written description of what the job does.
cols.SECTOR1: The first industry tied to the job, like Real Estate or Energy. Matches INDUSTRY_SECTOR.
cols.SECTOR1_INTEREST: A score of 1, 2 or 3 for how strong the tie to the first industry is; the scale needs a lookup. Some rows say nan, a placeholder for blank.
cols.SECTOR2: The second industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills many rows.
cols.SECTOR2_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the second industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills many rows.
cols.SECTOR3: The third industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills many rows.
cols.SECTOR3_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the third industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills many rows.
cols.SECTOR4: The fourth industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR4_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the fourth industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR5: The fifth industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR5_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the fifth industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR6: The sixth industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR6_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the sixth industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR7: The seventh industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR7_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the seventh industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR8: The eighth industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR8_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the eighth industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR9: The ninth industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR9_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the ninth industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR10: The tenth industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR10_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the tenth industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR11: The eleventh industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR11_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the eleventh industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills most rows.
cols.SECTOR12: The twelfth industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills almost every row.
cols.SECTOR12_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the twelfth industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills almost every row.
cols.SECTOR14: The fourteenth industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills almost every row.
cols.SECTOR14_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the fourteenth industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills almost every row.
cols.SECTOR14_1: An extra industry slot named like a second SECTOR14; there is no SECTOR13 column. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills almost every row.
cols.SECTOR14_INTEREST_1: The 1-to-3 tie score for that extra industry slot. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills almost every row.
cols.SECTOR15: The fifteenth industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills almost every row.
cols.SECTOR15_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the fifteenth industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills almost every row.
cols.SECTOR16: The sixteenth industry tied to the job, if any. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills almost every row.
cols.SECTOR16_INTEREST: The 1-to-3 tie score for the sixteenth industry; the scale needs a lookup. The text nan, a placeholder for blank, fills almost every row.
cols.SECTOR_COUNT: Meant to count the industries tied to the job, but it says 16 on every row, so it counts slots, not ties.
cols.IS_SENATE_CONFIRMED: True when the job needs Senate confirmation.
cols._SOURCE_ID: The name of the source feed, the same on every row. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

GOVERNANCE__FED_REVOLVINGDOOR_PROJECT.summary: 405 federal appointee jobs, each tagged with the industries the person in it came from, a map of the revolving door between government and business.
GOVERNANCE__FED_REVOLVINGDOOR_PROJECT.row: One appointed federal job: the post, its agency, and the industries tied to the person holding it.

cols.RECORD_DATE: The date the figure or record is as of, like the end of a month or day. Mostly Treasury tables plus one procurement table, and one table leaves it empty.

cols.ARCHIVAL_RECORD_SK: A made-up key, a long scrambled string, shared by many rows. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.RECORD_ID: Meant to be the record's ID. Empty on every row.
cols.GEO_LOCATION: Meant to be the record's place. Empty on every row.
cols.FIPS_GEO: Meant to be the place's census code. Empty on every row.
cols.RECORD_GROUP_NUMBER: Meant to be the Archives record group number. Empty on every row.
cols.SERIES_TITLE: Meant to be the series title. Empty on every row.
cols.DESCRIPTION_TEXT: Filled on only 4 rows, and each holds an HTTP 404 error message, not a description.
cols.RAW_FIELDS_JSON: The raw text scraped from the page, stored as JSON. It holds search-form labels like with the exact phrase, not record data.

GOVERNMENT_RECORDS__FED_NARA_AAD.summary: A failed scrape of the National Archives' Access to Archival Databases site: 554 rows, mostly search-page text and error messages, with no real archival records.
GOVERNMENT_RECORDS__FED_NARA_AAD.row: One scraped page fragment: a bit of text pulled from one Archives web page, not a real record.

cols.NODE_ID: The ID of this item as a point in a linked network. In the Offshore Leaks tables it links people, companies, and addresses through the relationships table; in the spending tree it is an agency code like 005.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.DESCRIPTION: The agency's name, like Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.
cols.ANCESTORS: The levels above this one in the tree; an empty list on every row, since these are the top.
cols.ACCOUNT_COUNT: How many federal accounts sit under the agency.
cols.CHILD_COUNT: Meant to hold how many branches sit under the agency, but empty on every row.

GOVERNMENT_RECORDS__FED_USASPENDING_TAS_.summary: The top level of USAspending's tree of federal accounts: 92 agencies, each with how many accounts it holds.
GOVERNMENT_RECORDS__FED_USASPENDING_TAS_.row: One agency at the top of the account tree.

cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit National Provider Identifier, stored as text. Some tables leave it mostly blank or empty, and the SAM exclusions table uses 0000000000 as a filler.
cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.PRESCRIBER_TYPE: The prescriber's specialty, like Internal Medicine or Nurse Practitioner.
cols.DATA_YEAR: The year the data covers, like 2024. One table runs into future years like 2032.
cols.PRESCRIBER_NAME: The prescriber's name, last name first.
cols.ADDICTION_CLAIMS: How many Medicare drug claims the prescriber wrote for addiction drugs in 2022.
cols.ADDICTION_DRUG_COST: What Medicare paid for those addiction drug claims, in dollars.
cols.ADDICTION_DRUG_COUNT: How many different addiction drugs the prescriber wrote for, from 1 to 6.
cols.ADDICTION_DRUGS: The addiction drugs the prescriber wrote for, like Methadone Hcl. Several are joined with a | when there is more than one.
cols.WAS_PAID_2022: True if the prescriber got any drug or device company payment in 2022.
cols.TOTAL_PAYMENTS: All company payments to the prescriber in 2022, of every kind, in dollars. 0 if none. Use this column to add up money.
cols.PAYMENT_COUNT: How many company payments the prescriber got in 2022. 0 if none.
cols.MANUFACTURER_COUNT: How many different companies paid the prescriber in 2022. 0 if none.
cols.TOP_MANUFACTURER: The company that paid the prescriber the most in 2022, like ABBVIE INC. Blank for prescribers who got nothing.
cols.TOP_MANUFACTURER_PAYMENTS: How much that top company paid the prescriber in 2022, in dollars. Blank for prescribers who got nothing.

HEALTH__ADDICTION_PRESCRIBERS_PAID.summary: Medicare drug-plan prescribers of the addiction drugs buprenorphine, naltrexone or methadone in 2022, matched to drug and device company payments they got that same year.
HEALTH__ADDICTION_PRESCRIBERS_PAID.row: One prescriber: one doctor or other clinician who prescribed an addiction drug in 2022.

cols.INDICATOR: What is being measured in this row, in words, like Symptoms of Anxiety Disorder or Heroin overdose deaths. Empty in the Eurostat table.

cols.SUBGROUP: The group of people the number is for, like an education level such as High school diploma or GED, or a race group.
cols.TIME_PERIOD: The survey round number, 1, 2, 3 and up. Stored as text; use the label column for the dates.

cols.TIME_PERIOD_END_DATE: Last day of the survey round. A date stored as text.

HEALTH__FED_CDC_ANXIETY_DEPRESSION.summary: Survey estimates of anxiety and depression symptoms in US adults from the CDC's Household Pulse Survey, by state and by groups like age, race and education, across survey phases.
HEALTH__FED_CDC_ANXIETY_DEPRESSION.row: One estimate: one measure for one group in one survey period.

cols.PARENT_DATASET_ID: The ID of the dataset this item is built from, as a list in brackets. Empty brackets, [], on most rows.
cols.ATTRIBUTION: The CDC office credited with the data, like NCHS/DVS. Blank for about one in five.
cols.PROVENANCE: Whether the item is official. Every row says official, so it tells you nothing.
cols.UPDATED_AT: When the catalog entry last changed, data or description.
cols.DATA_UPDATED_AT: When the data itself was last updated.
cols.METADATA_UPDATED_AT: When the description and other details were last updated.
cols.DOWNLOAD_COUNT: How many times the item has been downloaded.
cols.CATEGORIES: Site-wide topic labels, as a list in brackets, like ["health"]. Empty brackets on most rows.
cols.DOMAIN_CATEGORY: The CDC's own topic for the item, like NNDSS, Vaccinations or 500 Cities & Places.
cols.DOMAIN_TAGS: Keywords the CDC attached, as a list in brackets. Some are empty brackets.
cols.OWNER_DISPLAY_NAME: The account that published the item, an office name, a person, or a cdc.gov email address.
cols.PERMALINK: A short permanent web link to the item, like https://data.cdc.gov/d/jgyr-4kbb.
cols.LINK: The full web address of the item's page. Each row has its own.

HEALTH__FED_CDC_DATA_PORTAL.summary: The catalog of everything published on the CDC's open data website, 1,471 entries pulled on August 11, 2026.
HEALTH__FED_CDC_DATA_PORTAL.row: One catalog entry: one dataset, file, chart, filtered view or link on data.cdc.gov.

cols.FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 06037. One table holds two-digit state codes instead, and nine tables leave it empty.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY: The county, usually as a name like Harris, though some tables add the word County and the federal court tables use five-digit number codes, including 88888, which needs a lookup. The UK company table holds UK counties, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.POPULATION: How many people live in the area or group the row covers, like a county or census tract; the CDC WONDER table holds national figures around 160 million.
cols.ESTIMATED_AGE_ADJUSTED_DEATH_RATE_11_CAT: Estimated age-adjusted drug-poisoning death rate, given only as a band like 6.1-8, not an exact number.

HEALTH__FED_CDC_DRUG_POISONING_COUNTY.summary: CDC estimates of drug-poisoning death rates for every US county by year, given as rate bands.
HEALTH__FED_CDC_DRUG_POISONING_COUNTY.row: One county in one year: its population and estimated drug-poisoning death rate band.

cols.INDICATOR: What is being measured in this row, in words, like Symptoms of Anxiety Disorder or Heroin overdose deaths. Empty in the Eurostat table.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.SUBGROUP: The group of people the number is for, like an education level such as High school diploma or GED, or a race group.
cols.TIME_PERIOD: The survey round number, 1, 2, 3 and up. Stored as text; use the label column for the dates.
cols.TIME_PERIOD_LABEL: The survey round's dates in words, like Apr 23 - May 5, 2020.
cols.TIME_PERIOD_START_DATE: First day of the survey round. A date stored as text.
cols.TIME_PERIOD_END_DATE: Last day of the survey round. A date stored as text.
cols.LOWCI: The low end of the likely range for the percent. A number stored as text.
cols.HIGHCI: The high end of the likely range for the percent. A number stored as text.
cols.CONFIDENCE_INTERVAL: The likely range for the percent, low to high, as one piece of text like 22.7 - 24.3.
cols.QUARTILE_RANGE: Which quarter of all values this one falls in, shown as that quarter's low-to-high range like 16.6-19.4. Often blank, and some rows say Estimate not reliable.
cols.C_GROUP: How the people are grouped, like By State, By Age or By Education.
cols.PHASE: Which phase of the survey, like 1, 3.1 or 3 with dates. Written several ways.
cols.VALUE: The estimate, as a percent like 9.1. A number stored as text; blank where hidden.
cols.QUARTILE_NUMBER: Which quarter of all states the value falls in, 1 to 4. -1 is a filler; blank for rows not by state.
cols.SUPPRESSION_FLAG: 1 when the estimate was hidden as unreliable. Filled on only 299 rows.

HEALTH__FED_CDC_HEALTH_INSURANCE.summary: Survey estimates of how many U.S. adults had health insurance, by state and by groups like age, race and education, from the CDC's Household Pulse Survey rounds starting in 2020.
HEALTH__FED_CDC_HEALTH_INSURANCE.row: One estimate: one insurance measure for one group of people in one survey round.

cols.GEOID: The Census code for the place: 2 digits for a state, 5 for a county, like 04005. Keep it as text for the leading zero.
cols.NAME: The name of whatever the row is about: a person, company, bank, county, address or dataset, depending on the table. Spelling is not cleaned, fillers like UNNAMED or None show up, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.PERIOD: The time span the row covers. The SEC tables write a statement end date like 20231231, while others use a quarter number, a year, TTM, or 12 month-ending.
cols.ST_GEOID: The state as a two-digit federal code, like 48 for Texas.
cols.INTENT: Cause of death: Drug_OD, All_Suicide, All_Homicide, FA_Deaths, FA_Suicide or FA_Homicide, where FA means firearm.
cols.COUNT_SUP: Number of deaths. Blank on over half the rows, and 0 is the most common value.
cols.RATE: Death rate. -999 is a placeholder on about 6,500 rows, and 0 is common.
cols.RATE_M: A 1 or 0 flag; the 0 rows line up with the rows that have a count, so 1 appears to mark a missing or hidden count.
cols.RATE_M_CI: Filled only on the rows where the rate is -999, and always -999 itself, so it holds no real values.
cols.DATA_AS_OF: Date CDC last updated the data, as text; one of two dates in 2026.
cols.TTM_DATE_RANGE: The 12-month window for rolling rows, as text like February, 2025 to January, 2026. Mostly blank.

HEALTH__FED_CDC_INJURY_VIOLENCE_COUNTY.summary: CDC death counts and rates by county for six causes: drug overdose, all suicide, all homicide, and firearm deaths, suicides and homicides.
HEALTH__FED_CDC_INJURY_VIOLENCE_COUNTY.row: One county cause period: one county, one cause of death, one time period.

cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CAUSE_NAME: The cause of death in plain words, like Cancer or Suicide.
cols.ICD_113_CAUSE_NAME: The official cause name with its disease codes, like Malignant neoplasms, C00-C97.
cols.AGE_ADJUSTED_DEATH_RATE: Deaths per 100,000 people, adjusted so places with older or younger people compare fairly.

HEALTH__FED_CDC_LEADING_CAUSES_STATE.summary: Deaths and age-adjusted death rates for the leading causes of death in each state, 1999 to 2017, plus a United States total each year.
HEALTH__FED_CDC_LEADING_CAUSES_STATE.row: One cause of death in one state, or the whole U.S., in one year.

cols.GEOCODE: The map point as text, like POINT with longitude then latitude. POINT 0 0 means no location. Often blank.
cols.REPORTING_AREA: The state, territory or region reporting, like ALABAMA or a region name, in capitals.
cols.MMWR_WEEK: The CDC reporting week of the year, 1 to 53. Stored as text.
cols.LABEL: The disease, like Toxic shock syndrome or a named arboviral disease.
cols.CURRENT_WEEK: Cases reported this week. Mostly blank; see CURRENT_WEEK_FLAG for why. Stored as text.
cols.CURRENT_WEEK_FLAG: A mark on the week's count: - is by far the most common, with N and U also used. The marks need a lookup.
cols.PREVIOUS_52_WEEK_MAX: The highest weekly count over the past 52 weeks. Stored as text.
cols.PREVIOUS_52_WEEKS_MAX_FLAG: A mark on the 52-week high: - or NC. The marks need a lookup.
cols.CUMULATIVE_YTD_CURRENT_MMWR_YEAR: Cases so far this year. Mostly blank.
cols.CUMULATIVE_YTD_CURRENT_MMWR_YEAR_FLAG: A mark on this year's total: -, N or U. The marks need a lookup.
cols.CUMULATIVE_YTD_PREVIOUS_MMWR_YEAR: Cases by this point last year. Mostly blank.
cols.CUMULATIVE_YTD_PREVIOUS_MMWR_YEAR_FLAG: A mark on last year's total: -, N, NN, NP or U. The marks need a lookup.
cols.LOCATION1: The state or territory name when the row is a single place.
cols.LOCATION2: The region name, like NEW ENGLAND, or TOTAL or US RESIDENTS, when the row is a group of places. Mostly blank.
cols.SORT_ORDER: A long number CDC uses to order the rows. Each row has its own.

HEALTH__FED_CDC_NNDSS_WEEKLY_2024.summary: CDC's weekly counts of nationally notifiable diseases, like toxic shock syndrome or meningococcal disease, by state and region. Despite the 2024 in the name, it holds 2022 through 2026.
HEALTH__FED_CDC_NNDSS_WEEKLY_2024.row: One disease in one state or region for one week: that week's case count plus year-to-date totals.

cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.MONTH: The month, in many formats: January, 01, 1998-11, 10-2011, a mid-month date like 2026-03-15, or Total. One table leaves it empty.
cols.PERIOD: The time span the row covers. The SEC tables write a statement end date like 20231231, while others use a quarter number, a year, TTM, or 12 month-ending.
cols.INDICATOR: What is being measured in this row, in words, like Symptoms of Anxiety Disorder or Heroin overdose deaths. Empty in the Eurostat table.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.DATA_VALUE: The reported number, stored as text. Blank on about one in six rows.
cols.PERCENT_COMPLETE: How complete the data is, as text: 100 on nearly every row, 99.5 on a few.
cols.PERCENT_PENDING_INVESTIGATION: Percent of deaths still waiting on a cause ruling, stored as text.
cols.FOOTNOTE: Note on the number, like Numbers may differ from published reports or Underreported due to incomplete data.
cols.PREDICTED_VALUE: CDC's estimate after adjusting for late reports, stored as text. Blank on about a third of rows.

HEALTH__FED_CDC_OVERDOSE.summary: CDC's monthly counts of drug overdose deaths by state, with the reported number, CDC's predicted number and how complete the data is.
HEALTH__FED_CDC_OVERDOSE.row: One state month measure: one overdose measure for one state and one reporting month.

cols.INDICATOR: What is being measured in this row, in words, like Symptoms of Anxiety Disorder or Heroin overdose deaths. Empty in the Eurostat table.
cols.UNIT: The unit the number is measured in, like %, GW, TWh or deaths per 100,000. One table writes percent as PC, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.AGE: The person's age in years, or an age group like 15-24 years in the CDC table. Stored as text in some tables.
cols.UNIT_NUM: A number code for the kind of rate, 1 or 2; the unit column spells it out.
cols.STUB_NAME: How the population is split for this row, like by sex and age, or by sex and race.
cols.STUB_NAME_NUM: A number code for how the population is split; the stub name column spells it out.
cols.STUB_LABEL: The exact group the rate is for, like Female: Black or African American.
cols.STUB_LABEL_NUM: A number code for the exact group, like 4.22; the stub label column spells it out.
cols.YEAR_NUM: A running number for the year, from 1 up to 42; the year column gives the real year.
cols.AGE_NUM: A number code for the age group, like 0 for all ages; the age column spells it out.
cols.ESTIMATE: The suicide death rate for the group. A number stored as text; blank where CDC flags the value.
cols.FLAG: A mark explaining a missing or shaky rate, either ... or *. The marks need a lookup. Mostly blank.

HEALTH__FED_CDC_SUICIDE_RATES.summary: CDC suicide death rates for the US by year, broken out by sex, age, race and Hispanic origin; for 9 rows in 2018 CDC itself publishes two different rates for the same group.
HEALTH__FED_CDC_SUICIDE_RATES.row: One rate: the suicide death rate for one group of people, like Black women aged 45 to 64, in one year.

cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.SEX: Male or Female. Some tables also have All.
cols.POPULATION: How many people live in the area or group the row covers, like a county or census tract; the CDC WONDER table holds national figures around 160 million.
cols.CRUDE_RATE: Deaths per 100,000 people, not adjusted for age. Blank in about half the VA rows.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.ICD_CHAPTER: The broad cause-of-death group, like Diseases of the musculoskeletal system.

HEALTH__FED_CDC_WONDER.summary: US deaths by year, sex and broad cause, with population and death rate, from CDC WONDER. Counts under 10 are hidden.
HEALTH__FED_CDC_WONDER.row: One year, one sex and one cause group: deaths, population and the death rate.

cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit National Provider Identifier, stored as text. Some tables leave it mostly blank or empty, and the SAM exclusions table uses 0000000000 as a filler.
cols.START_DATE: The date it began, like an award, trial, listing or court. Mostly blank in several tables, and 1969-12-31 shows up in the offshore-leaks table as a stand-in date.
cols.GENDER: The person's sex, written differently by table: Male or Female, M or F, m or f, or Male Owned for businesses. Some rows say Unknown or Unanswered, the clinical trials table mostly says ALL, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.KEYWORDS: Keywords tagged on the record. Formats differ: a list of words where [] means none, numbers split by semicolons that need a lookup, or words per language.
cols.SOURCE_ID: A short name for the source feed the row came from, like fed_cfpb_complaints. In the ITIS other-sources table it is a plain number instead, which needs a lookup.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.NCT_ID: The study's ClinicalTrials.gov ID, like NCT04040296. Each study has its own.
cols.ORG_STUDY_ID: The sponsor's own ID for the study, typed freely.
cols.EUDRACT_NUMBER: The study's European trial registry number, like 2006-005604-14. Almost always blank.
cols.OFFICIAL_TITLE: Full official title of the study.
cols.OVERALL_STATUS: Where the study stands, like COMPLETED, RECRUITING, TERMINATED or UNKNOWN.
cols.PHASE: Trial phase as a text list, like ["PHASE2"] or ["PHASE1", "PHASE2"]; NA means phases do not apply.
cols.STUDY_TYPE: Kind of study: INTERVENTIONAL, OBSERVATIONAL or EXPANDED_ACCESS.
cols.FIRST_POSTED_DATE: Date the study first appeared on ClinicalTrials.gov.
cols.PRIMARY_COMPLETION_DATE: Date the main results were or will be collected. Can be in the future; many are the last day of a year.
cols.COMPLETION_DATE: Date the whole study ended or is expected to end. Can be in the future.
cols.RESULTS_FIRST_POSTED_DATE: Date results were first posted. Blank for most studies because most never post results.
cols.LAST_UPDATE_POSTED_DATE: Date the study record was last updated.
cols.STUDY_DURATION_DAYS: How many days the study ran or is planned to run. Blank on about half the rows.
cols.DAYS_TO_RESULTS_POSTING: Days between the study and its results being posted. Blank unless results were posted.
cols.ENROLLMENT: How many people were or will be enrolled. Some rows say 0.
cols.LEAD_SPONSOR_NAME: The main organization running the study, like AstraZeneca or Mayo Clinic.
cols.LEAD_SPONSOR_CLASS: Kind of sponsor, like INDUSTRY, NIH, FED or OTHER.
cols.RESPONSIBLE_PARTY: Who is responsible for the study record, stored as a block of JSON text.
cols.OVERSIGHT_HAS_DMC: True or false: whether a data monitoring committee watches the study.
cols.IS_FDA_REGULATED_DRUG: True or false: whether the study tests an FDA-regulated drug. Blank on over a third of rows.
cols.IS_FDA_REGULATED_DEVICE: True or false: whether the study tests an FDA-regulated device. Blank on over a third of rows.
cols.MINIMUM_AGE: Youngest age allowed to join, as text like 18 Years.
cols.MAXIMUM_AGE: Oldest age allowed to join, as text like 65 Years. Blank when there is no upper limit.
cols.ELIGIBILITY_CRITERIA: Who can and cannot join the study, as long free text.
cols.HAS_RESULTS: True or false: whether results have been posted. False for most studies.
cols.WHY_STOPPED: Why the study stopped early, in free text like Lack of funding. Almost always blank.
cols.CONDITIONS: Diseases or conditions studied, as a text list like ["Breast Cancer"].
cols.INTERVENTIONS: Drugs, devices or other treatments tested, stored as JSON text. [] means none listed.
cols.PRIMARY_OUTCOMES: Main things the study measures, stored as JSON text.
cols.SECONDARY_OUTCOMES: Other things the study measures, stored as JSON text. [] on many rows.
cols.COLLABORATORS: Other organizations helping with the study, stored as JSON text. [] on most rows.
cols.LOCATIONS: Sites where the study runs, stored as JSON text. [] means none listed.
cols.REFERENCES: Published papers tied to the study, stored as JSON text. [] on most rows.
cols.SECONDARY_IDS: Other ID numbers for the study, like NIH grant numbers, stored as JSON text. [] on most rows.
cols.STATUS_CATEGORY: A grouping of study status, but it says Other / Unknown on every row, so it tells you nothing.
cols.PHASE_CATEGORY: A grouping of study phase, but it says Unknown on every row, so it tells you nothing.

HEALTH__FED_CLINICALTRIALS.summary: Registered clinical studies from ClinicalTrials.gov: who sponsors them, the drug or condition, the phase, and whether results were posted.
HEALTH__FED_CLINICALTRIALS.row: One study: one registered clinical trial or observational study.

cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit National Provider Identifier, stored as text. Some tables leave it mostly blank or empty, and the SAM exclusions table uses 0000000000 as a filler.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ASM_COHORT: Which condition the clinician is measured on: Low Back Pain or Heart Failure.
cols.ORGANIZATION_LEGAL_NAME: The legal name of the clinician's practice.
cols.ASM_CY27_PARTICIPANT: Whether the clinician takes part in 2027. Yes on every row.
cols.ASM_CY27_SMALLPRACTICE: Yes if the clinician counts as a small practice in 2027, No if not.
cols.ASM_CY28_PARTICIPANT: Meant for whether the clinician takes part in 2028. Every row holds the text Null, so it is not filled yet.
cols.ASM_CY28_SMALLPRACTICE: Meant for small-practice status in 2028. Every row holds the text Null, so it is not filled yet.
cols.ASM_CY29_PARTICIPANT: Meant for whether the clinician takes part in 2029. Every row holds the text Null, so it is not filled yet.
cols.ASM_CY29_SMALLPRACTICE: Meant for small-practice status in 2029. Every row holds the text Null, so it is not filled yet.
cols.ASM_CY30_PARTICIPANT: Meant for whether the clinician takes part in 2030. Every row holds the text Null, so it is not filled yet.
cols.ASM_CY30_SMALLPRACTICE: Meant for small-practice status in 2030. Every row holds the text Null, so it is not filled yet.
cols.ASM_CY31_PARTICIPANT: Meant for whether the clinician takes part in 2031. Every row holds the text Null, so it is not filled yet.
cols.ASM_CY31_SMALLPRACTICE: Meant for small-practice status in 2031. Every row holds the text Null, so it is not filled yet.

HEALTH__FED_CMS_AMBULATORY_SPECIALTY_MOD.summary: Clinicians picked for Medicare's Ambulatory Specialty Model, a payment test for low back pain and heart failure care, with their practice and small-practice status for 2027.
HEALTH__FED_CMS_AMBULATORY_SPECIALTY_MOD.row: One clinician in one condition group of the model.

cols.CCN: The facility's 6-character Medicare certification number, stored as text; some hold letters, like 38T061. It is almost always blank in the three Open Payments tables.
cols.FACILITY_NAME: The name of the plant, site or building, as the agency wrote it. Generic fillers like RESIDENCE, UNKNOWN, WELL or HOME are common in some tables.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_1: The first line of the street address, like 13 STATION ROAD.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_2: The second address line, often a suite or floor but sometimes a street or area name. Blank for many rows, one table leaves it empty, and two fill it with a lone dash.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY_PARISH: The county name, or parish in Louisiana. Casing varies.
cols.TELEPHONE_NUMBER: The facility's phone number, written with the area code in brackets and a dash in some tables and as bare digits in others. Some rows hold a lone dash instead of a number.
cols.CERTIFICATION_DATE: The date the facility was certified to take Medicare. In the NPI registry it is when the provider last confirmed their record.
cols.NETWORK: The regional kidney-care network the clinic belongs to, as a number from 1 to 18.
cols.FIVE_STAR_DATE: The time window the star rating measure covers. Every clinic has the same value: Jan 2021 to Dec 2024.
cols.FIVE_STAR: The clinic's Medicare star rating, 1 to 5 stars. Blank for a few hundred clinics.
cols.FIVE_STAR_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the star rating score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.PROFIT_OR_NON_PROFIT: Whether the clinic is run for profit or as a non-profit. Most are for-profit.
cols.CHAIN_OWNED: Yes when the clinic belongs to a chain. Most do.
cols.CHAIN_ORGANIZATION: The chain that owns the clinic, like DaVita or Fresenius Medical Care. Says Independent when there is no chain.
cols.LATE_SHIFT: Yes when the clinic runs a late-day dialysis shift.
cols.OF_DIALYSIS_STATIONS: How many dialysis chairs or stations the clinic has.
cols.OFFERS_IN_CENTER_HEMODIALYSIS: Yes when patients can get blood-filtering dialysis at the clinic itself.
cols.OFFERS_PERITONEAL_DIALYSIS: Yes when the clinic offers peritoneal dialysis, the kind done through the belly, usually at home.
cols.OFFERS_HOME_HEMODIALYSIS_TRAINING: Yes when the clinic trains patients to do hemodialysis at home.
cols.CLAIMS_DATE: The time window of Medicare claims behind some measures. Every clinic has the same value: Jul 2024 to Jun 2025.
cols.EQRS_DATE: The time window of clinic-reported patient records behind some measures. Every clinic has the same value: Jul 2024 to Jun 2025.
cols.SMR_DATE: The time window the death rate measure covers. Every clinic has the same value: Jan 2021 to Dec 2024.
cols.PATIENT_SURVIVAL_CATEGORY_TEXT: How the clinic did on patient survival next to what Medicare expected: As Expected, Better than Expected, Worse than Expected or Not Available.
cols.PATIENT_SURVIVAL_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the survival score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PATIENTS_INCLUDED_IN_SURVIVAL_: How many patients the clinic's death rate is based on.
cols.MORTALITY_RATE_FACILITY: The clinic's patient death rate, adjusted for how sick its patients are. Blank when it could not be reported.
cols.MORTALITY_RATE_UPPER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_97: The high end of the likely range for the clinic's death rate.
cols.MORTALITY_RATE_LOWER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_2_: The low end of the likely range for the clinic's death rate.
cols.SHR_DATE: The time window the hospital-stay measure covers. Every clinic has the same value: Jan 2024 to Dec 2024.
cols.PATIENT_HOSPITALIZATION_CATEGORY_TEXT: How the clinic did on hospital stays next to what Medicare expected: As Expected, Better than Expected, Worse than Expected or Not Available.
cols.PATIENT_HOSPITALIZATION_DATA_AVAILABILIT: A code saying whether the hospital-stay score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PATIENTS_INCLUDED_IN_HOSPITALI: How many patients the clinic's hospital-stay rate is based on.
cols.HOSPITALIZATION_RATE_FACILITY: How often the clinic's patients ended up in the hospital, adjusted for how sick they are.
cols.HOSPITALIZATION_RATE_UPPER_CONFIDENCE_LI: The high end of the likely range for the clinic's hospital-stay rate.
cols.HOSPITALIZATION_RATE_LOWER_CONFIDENCE_LI: The low end of the likely range for the clinic's hospital-stay rate.
cols.SRR_DATE: The time window the readmission measure covers. Every clinic has the same value: Jan 2024 to Dec 2024.
cols.PATIENT_HOSPITAL_READMISSION_CATEGORY: How the clinic did on patients going back into the hospital next to what Medicare expected: As Expected, Better than Expected, Worse than Expected or Not Available.
cols.PATIENT_HOSPITAL_READMISSION_DATA_AVAILA: A code saying whether the readmission score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_HOSPITALIZATIONS_INCLUDED_IN_H: How many hospital discharges the clinic's readmission rate is based on.
cols.READMISSION_RATE_FACILITY: The share of the clinic's patients who went back into the hospital soon after leaving, adjusted for how sick they are.
cols.READMISSION_RATE_UPPER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_: The high end of the likely range for the clinic's readmission rate.
cols.READMISSION_RATE_LOWER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_: The low end of the likely range for the clinic's readmission rate.
cols.STRR_DATE: The time window the blood transfusion measure covers. Every clinic has the same value: Jan 2024 to Dec 2024.
cols.PATIENT_TRANSFUSION_CATEGORY_TEXT: How the clinic did on blood transfusions next to what Medicare expected: As Expected, Better than Expected, Worse than Expected or Not Available.
cols.PATIENT_TRANSFUSION_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CO: A code saying whether the transfusion score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PATIENTS_INCLUDED_IN_THE_TRANS: How many patients the clinic's transfusion rate is based on.
cols.TRANSFUSION_RATE_FACILITY: How often the clinic's patients needed blood transfusions, adjusted for how sick they are. Blank for about four in ten clinics.
cols.TRANSFUSION_RATE_UPPER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_: The high end of the likely range for the clinic's transfusion rate.
cols.TRANSFUSION_RATE_LOWER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_: The low end of the likely range for the clinic's transfusion rate.
cols.FYSWR_DATE: The time window the first-year transplant waitlist measure covers. Every clinic has the same value: Jan 2021 to Dec 2023.
cols.FYSWR_CATEGORY_TEXT: How the clinic did on getting new patients onto the kidney transplant waitlist in their first year next to what Medicare expected: As Expected, Better than Expected, Worse than Expected or Not Available.
cols.PATIENT_TRANSPLANT_WAITLIST_DATA_AVAILAB: A code saying whether the first-year transplant waitlist score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PATIENTS_IN_THIS_FACILITY_FOR_: How many new patients the first-year transplant waitlist score is based on.
cols.FIRST_YEAR_STANDARDIZED_KIDNEY_TRANSPLAN: How often new patients got onto the kidney transplant waitlist within a year, next to the expected number. 1 means as expected; higher is better.
cols.C_95_C_I_UPPER_LIMIT_FOR_FYSWR: The high end of the likely range for the first-year transplant waitlist score.
cols.C_95_C_I_LOWER_LIMIT_FOR_FYSWR: The low end of the likely range for the first-year transplant waitlist score.
cols.PPPW_CATEGORY_TEXT: How the clinic did on keeping its patients on the kidney transplant waitlist next to what Medicare expected: As Expected, Better than Expected, Worse than Expected or Not Available.
cols.PATIENT_PREVALENT_TRANSPLANT_WAITLIST_DA: A code saying whether the transplant waitlist score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PATIENTS_FOR_PPPW: How many patients the transplant waitlist percentage is based on.
cols.PERCENTAGE_OF_PREVALENT_PATIENTS_WAITLIS: Percent of the clinic's patients who are on the kidney transplant waitlist, adjusted for patient mix.
cols.C_95_C_I_UPPER_LIMIT_FOR_PPPW: The high end of the likely range for the transplant waitlist percentage.
cols.C_95_C_I_LOWER_LIMIT_FOR_PPPW: The low end of the likely range for the transplant waitlist percentage.
cols.SEDR_DATE: The time window the emergency room visit measure covers. Every clinic has the same value: Jan 2024 to Dec 2024.
cols.SEDR_CATEGORY_TEXT: How the clinic did on emergency room visits next to what Medicare expected: As Expected, Better than Expected, Worse than Expected or Not Available.
cols.EMERGENCY_DEPARTMENT_ENCOUNTER_DATA_AVAI: A code saying whether the emergency room visit score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PATIENTS_INCLUDED_IN_SEDR_SUMM: How many patients the emergency room visit score is based on.
cols.STANDARDIZED_ED_VISITS_RATIO_FACILITY: How often the clinic's patients went to the emergency room, next to the expected number. 1 means as expected; lower is better.
cols.SEDR_UPPER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_97_5: The high end of the likely range for the emergency room visit score.
cols.SEDR_LOWER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_2_5: The low end of the likely range for the emergency room visit score.
cols.ED30_DATE: The time window the post-hospital emergency room measure covers. Every clinic has the same value: Jan 2023 to Dec 2024.
cols.ED30_CATEGORY_TEXT: How the clinic did on emergency room visits within 30 days of leaving the hospital next to what Medicare expected: As Expected, Better than Expected, Worse than Expected or Not Available.
cols.EMERGENCY_DEPARTMENT_ENCOUNTER_RATIO_OCC: A code saying whether the post-hospital emergency room score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_HOSPITALIZATIONS_INCLUDED_IN_E: How many hospital discharges the post-hospital emergency room score is based on.
cols.STANDARDIZED_ED_VISITS_WITHIN_30_DAYS_OF: How often patients went to the emergency room within 30 days of leaving the hospital, next to the expected number. 1 means as expected; lower is better.
cols.ED30_UPPER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_97_5: The high end of the likely range for the post-hospital emergency room score.
cols.ED30_LOWER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_2_5: The low end of the likely range for the post-hospital emergency room score.
cols.YEARS_MODALITY_SWITCH_BASED_UPON: The time window the switch-to-home-dialysis measure covers. Every clinic has the same value: Jan 2021 to Dec 2023.
cols.SMOSR_CLASSIFICATION_CATEGORY_FACILITY: How the clinic did on moving patients to home dialysis or a transplant next to what Medicare expected: As Expected, Better than Expected, Worse than Expected or Not Available.
cols.MODALITY_SWITCH_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the switch-to-home-dialysis score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.SMOSR_NUMBER_OF_ELIGIBLE_PATIENTS_FACILI: How many patients the switch-to-home-dialysis score is based on.
cols.SMOSR_STANDARDIZED_MODALITY_SWITCH_RATIO: How often patients moved to home dialysis or a transplant, next to the expected number. 1 means as expected; higher is better.
cols.SMOSR_UPPER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_FACILITY: The high end of the likely range for the switch-to-home-dialysis score.
cols.SMOSR_LOWER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_FACILITY: The low end of the likely range for the switch-to-home-dialysis score.
cols.SIR_DATE: The time window the bloodstream infection measure covers. Every clinic has the same value: Jan 2024 to Dec 2024.
cols.PATIENT_INFECTION_CATEGORY_TEXT: How the clinic did on bloodstream infections next to what Medicare expected: As Expected, Better than Expected, Worse than Expected or Not Available.
cols.PATIENT_INFECTION_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the infection score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.STANDARD_INFECTION_RATIO: How many bloodstream infections the clinic's patients got, next to the expected number. 1 means as expected; lower is better, and 0 is common.
cols.SIR_UPPER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_97_5: The high end of the likely range for the infection score.
cols.SIR_LOWER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_2_5: The low end of the likely range for the infection score. Blank for about four in ten clinics.
cols.FISTULA_CATEGORY_TEXT: How the clinic did on using a fistula, an artery joined to a vein in the arm, for dialysis next to what Medicare expected: As Expected, Better than Expected, Worse than Expected or Not Available.
cols.FISTULA_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the fistula score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PATIENTS_INCLUDED_IN_FISTULA_S: How many patients the fistula score is based on.
cols.FISTULA_RATE_FACILITY: Percent of the clinic's patients getting dialysis through a fistula, adjusted for patient mix. Higher is better.
cols.FISTULA_RATE_UPPER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_97_5: The high end of the likely range for the fistula percentage.
cols.FISTULA_RATE_LOWER_CONFIDENCE_LIMIT_2_5: The low end of the likely range for the fistula percentage.
cols.HCP_VACCINATION_DATA_COLLECTION_DATES: The time window for the staff vaccination measure. Every clinic has the same value: Apr 2025 to Jun 2025.
cols.HCP_VACCINATION_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the staff vaccination score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.HEALTHCARE_WORKER_COVID_19_VACCINATION_A: Percent of the clinic's staff up to date on COVID-19 shots. Zero at most clinics.
cols.ADULT_HD_KT_V_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the adult hemodialysis cleaning score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_ADULT_HD_PATIENTS_WITH_KT_V_DA: How many adult hemodialysis patients had a test showing how well dialysis cleaned their blood.
cols.NUMBER_OF_ADULT_HD_PATIENT_MONTHS_WITH_K: How many patient-months of those blood-cleaning tests the clinic reported for adult hemodialysis.
cols.PERCENT_OF_ADULT_HD_PATIENTS_WITH_KT_V_1: Percent of adult hemodialysis patients whose blood was cleaned well enough, a Kt/V score of 1.2 or more. Blank for about four in ten clinics.
cols.ADULT_PD_KT_V_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the adult peritoneal dialysis cleaning score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_ADULT_PD_PATIENTS_WITH_KT_V_DA: How many adult peritoneal dialysis patients had a test showing how well dialysis cleaned their blood. Zero at about half of clinics.
cols.NUMBER_OF_ADULT_PD_PATIENT_MONTHS_WITH_K: How many patient-months of blood-cleaning tests the clinic reported for adult peritoneal dialysis. Blank for about half of clinics.
cols.PERCENTAGE_OF_ADULT_PD_PTS_WITH_KT_V_1_7: Percent of adult peritoneal dialysis patients whose blood was cleaned well enough, a Kt/V score of 1.7 or more. Blank for most clinics.
cols.PEDIATRIC_HD_KT_V_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the child hemodialysis cleaning score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PEDIATRIC_HD_PATIENTS_WITH_KT_: How many child hemodialysis patients had a blood-cleaning test. Zero at almost every clinic.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PEDIATRIC_HD_PATIENT_MONTHS_WI: How many patient-months of blood-cleaning tests the clinic reported for child hemodialysis. Blank for almost every clinic.
cols.PERCENTAGE_OF_PEDIATRIC_HD_PATIENTS_WITH: Percent of child hemodialysis patients whose blood was cleaned well enough, a Kt/V score of 1.2 or more. Filled for only 20 clinics.
cols.PEDIATRIC_PD_KT_V_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the child peritoneal dialysis cleaning score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PEDIATRIC_PD_PATIENTS_WITH_KT_: How many child peritoneal dialysis patients had a blood-cleaning test. Zero at almost every clinic.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PEDIATRIC_PD_PATIENT_MONTHS_WI: How many patient-months of blood-cleaning tests the clinic reported for child peritoneal dialysis. Blank for almost every clinic.
cols.PERCENTAGE_OF_PEDIATRIC_PD_PATIENTS_WITH: Percent of child peritoneal dialysis patients whose blood was cleaned well enough, a Kt/V score of 1.8 or more. Filled for only 26 clinics.
cols.PERCENTAGE_OF_MEDICARE_PATIENTS_WITH_HGB: Percent of Medicare patients whose hemoglobin, a blood count, fell below 10. Blank for about a quarter of clinics.
cols.HGB_10_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the low hemoglobin score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.PERCENTAGE_OF_MEDICARE_PATIENTS_WITH_HGB: Percent of Medicare patients whose hemoglobin, a blood count, ran above 12. Zero at most clinics.
cols.HGB_12_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the high hemoglobin score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_DIALYSIS_PATIENTS_WITH_HGB_DAT: How many patients the hemoglobin percentages are based on.
cols.HYPERCALCEMIA_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the high calcium score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PATIENTS_IN_HYPERCALCEMIA_SUMM: How many patients the high-calcium percentage is based on.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PATIENT_MONTHS_IN_HYPERCALCEMI: How many patient-months of calcium tests the high-calcium percentage is based on.
cols.PERCENTAGE_OF_ADULT_PATIENTS_WITH_HYPERC: Percent of adult patients with too much calcium in their blood, above 10.2. Lower is better. Blank for about four in ten clinics.
cols.SERUM_PHOSPHORUS_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE: A code saying whether the blood phosphorus score could be reported, like 001 or 258. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PATIENTS_IN_SERUM_PHOSPHORUS_S: How many patients the blood phosphorus percentages are based on.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PATIENT_MONTHS_IN_SERUM_PHOSPH: How many patient-months of phosphorus tests the phosphorus percentages are based on.
cols.PERCENTAGE_OF_ADULT_PATIENTS_WITH_SERUM_: Percent of adult patients with blood phosphorus below 3.5. Blank for about four in ten clinics.
