HEALTH__FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PROVIDER.summary: Medicare payments and patient counts for 1.3 million doctors and other providers, with totals for services, drugs and patient mix.
HEALTH__FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PROVIDER.row: One provider: one doctor or organization, by NPI, with a year of Medicare totals.

cols.EFFECTIVE_DATE: The date something took effect, like a merger, a drug price, or a suspension.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.NDC: The drug's 11-digit National Drug Code, stored as text.
cols.DRUG_DESCRIPTION: The drug name, strength and form, like METFORMIN HCL 1,000 MG TABLET.
cols.NADAC_PER_UNIT: What pharmacies paid on average for one unit, in dollars. Check the pricing unit before comparing.
cols.PRICING_UNIT: What one unit is: EA for each pill, ML for milliliter, GM for gram.
cols.PHARMACY_TYPE: Always C/I in this table. The code needs a lookup.
cols.IS_OTC: Y for over-the-counter drugs, N for prescription.
cols.EXPLANATION_CODE: Notes on how the price was set, as numbers like 1 or 1, 5. The codes need a lookup.
cols.RATE_CLASSIFICATION: G for generic or B for brand, with B-ANDA and B-BIO as variants. The variants need a lookup.
cols.GENERIC_NADAC_PER_UNIT: The average generic price per unit for the same drug, for brand rows. Blank on almost every row.
cols.GENERIC_EFFECTIVE_DATE: The date the generic price took effect. Blank on almost every row.
cols.AS_OF_DATE: The week's file the price came from, mostly in 2024.
cols.BRAND_TO_GENERIC_RATIO: How many times more the brand costs than the generic. Blank on almost every row.

HEALTH__FED_CMS_NADAC.summary: Weekly average prices US pharmacies pay to buy each drug, from Medicaid's national drug price survey.
HEALTH__FED_CMS_NADAC.row: One drug on one weekly price file: its code, name and average price per unit.

cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit National Provider Identifier, stored as text. Some tables leave it mostly blank or empty, and the SAM exclusions table uses 0000000000 as a filler.
cols.PROVIDER_MIDDLE_NAME: The provider's middle name or initial. Often blank.
cols.LAST_UPDATE_DATE: The date the record was last updated at the source.
cols.NPI_DEACTIVATION_DATE: The date the provider's 10-digit national ID was shut off. Almost always blank.
cols.CERTIFICATION_DATE: The date the facility was certified to take Medicare. In the NPI registry it is when the provider last confirmed their record.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.ENTITY_TYPE_CODE: 1 or 2: 1 marks a person and 2 an organization; the counts line up with the person and organization name columns. Blank on a few hundred thousand rows.
cols.REPLACEMENT_NPI: The newer NPI that replaced this one. Almost always blank; filled on only about 80 rows.
cols.EMPLOYER_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER_EIN: Meant to hold the organization's federal tax ID, but it is empty in this table.
cols.PROVIDER_ORGANIZATION_NAME_LEGAL_BUSINES: The organization's legal business name, like WALGREEN CO. Filled only for organizations, so blank on most rows.
cols.PROVIDER_LAST_NAME_LEGAL_NAME: The person's legal last name. Filled only for individual providers.
cols.PROVIDER_NAME_PREFIX_TEXT: Name prefix like DR., MRS. or MS. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_NAME_SUFFIX_TEXT: Name suffix like JR., II or III. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_TEXT: The person's credentials as typed, like MD, M.D., RN or LCSW. Free text, so the same degree is spelled many ways.
cols.PROVIDER_OTHER_ORGANIZATION_NAME: Meant to hold another name the organization uses, but every filled row just says <UNAVAIL>. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_OTHER_ORGANIZATION_NAME_TYPE_CO: Type code for the other organization name; always 6 when filled, and the code needs a lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_OTHER_LAST_NAME: Another last name the person has used, such as a maiden name. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_OTHER_FIRST_NAME: First name that goes with the person's other name. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_OTHER_MIDDLE_NAME: Middle name or initial that goes with the person's other name. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_OTHER_NAME_PREFIX_TEXT: Prefix like DR. or MS. on the person's other name. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_OTHER_NAME_SUFFIX_TEXT: Suffix like JR. on the person's other name. Almost always blank.
cols.PROVIDER_OTHER_CREDENTIAL_TEXT: Credentials typed with the person's other name, like MD or RN. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_OTHER_LAST_NAME_TYPE_CODE: A code for what kind of other name this is: 1, 5, 2 or 3; the codes need a lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_FIRST_LINE_BUSINESS_MAILING_ADD: First line of the provider's mailing address. Many providers share one address, including P.O. boxes like PO BOX 7004.
cols.PROVIDER_SECOND_LINE_BUSINESS_MAILING_AD: Second line of the mailing address, usually a suite number. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_BUSINESS_MAILING_ADDRESS_CITY_N: City of the provider's mailing address.
cols.PROVIDER_BUSINESS_MAILING_ADDRESS_STATE_: State of the mailing address, mostly as two letters. Over a thousand distinct values, so foreign and misspelled entries are mixed in.
cols.PROVIDER_BUSINESS_MAILING_ADDRESS_POSTAL: ZIP code of the mailing address, often 9 digits run together, stored as text.
cols.PROVIDER_BUSINESS_MAILING_ADDRESS_COUNTR: Country of the mailing address as two letters; US on nearly every row.
cols.PROVIDER_BUSINESS_MAILING_ADDRESS_TELEPH: Phone number for the mailing address, 10 digits as text. Many providers share one number.
cols.PROVIDER_BUSINESS_MAILING_ADDRESS_FAX_NU: Fax number for the mailing address, 10 digits as text. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_FIRST_LINE_BUSINESS_PRACTICE_LO: First line of the street address where the provider actually practices.
cols.PROVIDER_SECOND_LINE_BUSINESS_PRACTICE_L: Second line of the practice address, usually a suite number. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_BUSINESS_PRACTICE_LOCATION_ADDR: State where the provider practices, mostly as two letters. Over a thousand distinct values, so foreign and misspelled entries are mixed in.
ZIP code of the practice address, often 9 digits run together, stored as text.
Country of the practice address as two letters; US on nearly every row.
Phone number at the practice location, 10 digits as text. Many providers share one number.
Fax number at the practice location, 10 digits as text. Mostly blank.
cols.PROVIDER_ENUMERATION_DATE: The date the provider was first given this NPI. The earliest dates are in 2006 and 2007, when the system started.
cols.NPI_DEACTIVATION_REASON_CODE: Meant to hold why an NPI was shut off, but it is empty in this table.
cols.NPI_REACTIVATION_DATE: The date a shut-off NPI was turned back on. Almost always blank.
cols.PROVIDER_SEX_CODE: The person's sex as F, M, X or U. Filled only for individual providers.
cols.AUTHORIZED_OFFICIAL_LAST_NAME: Last name of the person who signs for the organization, like its owner or president. Filled only for organizations.
cols.AUTHORIZED_OFFICIAL_FIRST_NAME: First name of the person who signs for the organization. Filled only for organizations.
cols.AUTHORIZED_OFFICIAL_MIDDLE_NAME: Middle name or initial of the person who signs for the organization. Mostly blank.
cols.AUTHORIZED_OFFICIAL_TITLE_OR_POSITION: Job title of the person who signs for the organization, like OWNER, PRESIDENT or CEO. Free text.
cols.AUTHORIZED_OFFICIAL_TELEPHONE_NUMBER: Phone number of the person who signs for the organization, 10 digits as text.

cols.IS_SOLE_PROPRIETOR: Y or N: whether the person works as a sole proprietor; some rows say X. Filled only for individual providers.
cols.IS_ORGANIZATION_SUBPART: Y or N: whether the organization is a branch or unit of a bigger one. Filled only for organizations.
cols.PARENT_ORGANIZATION_LBN: Legal name of the parent organization, like WALGREENS BOOTS ALLIANCE INC. Filled only for branches, so almost always blank.
cols.PARENT_ORGANIZATION_TIN: Meant to hold the parent organization's tax ID, but every filled row just says <UNAVAIL>. Mostly blank.
cols.AUTHORIZED_OFFICIAL_NAME_PREFIX_TEXT: Prefix like DR. or MR. for the person who signs for the organization. Mostly blank.
cols.AUTHORIZED_OFFICIAL_NAME_SUFFIX_TEXT: Suffix like JR. for the person who signs for the organization. Almost always blank.
cols.AUTHORIZED_OFFICIAL_CREDENTIAL_TEXT: Credentials of the person who signs for the organization, like MD or DDS. Mostly blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_1: Group type for specialty 1, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Mostly blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_2: Group type for specialty 2, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Mostly blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_3: Group type for specialty 3, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Mostly blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_4: Group type for specialty 4, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Mostly blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_5: Group type for specialty 5, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Mostly blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_6: Group type for specialty 6, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Mostly blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_7: Group type for specialty 7, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Almost always blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_8: Group type for specialty 8, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Almost always blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_9: Group type for specialty 9, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Almost always blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_10: Group type for specialty 10, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Almost always blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_11: Group type for specialty 11, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Almost always blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_12: Group type for specialty 12, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Almost always blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_13: Group type for specialty 13, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Almost always blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_14: Group type for specialty 14, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Almost always blank.
cols.HEALTHCARE_PROVIDER_TAXONOMY_GROUP_15: Group type for specialty 15, like 193200000X MULTI-SPECIALTY GROUP. Almost always blank.

HEALTH__FED_CMS_NPPES.summary: Every US health care provider with a National Provider Identifier, all 9.6 million doctors, nurses, clinics, pharmacies and suppliers, with names, addresses, specialties and licenses.
HEALTH__FED_CMS_NPPES.row: One provider: one person or organization that holds one NPI.

cols.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN: The nursing home's six-digit Medicare ID. Kept as text so leading zeros like 015073 survive.
cols.COUNTY_FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 01001, stored as text. One table holds only the three-digit county part like 017, one holds N/A, and two leave it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.OWNERSHIP_TYPE: Who owns it: for-profit, non-profit, government, cooperative and so on, with wording that differs by table. Some rows say Unavailable.
cols.ADDRESS: The full address in one line of text, messy and not split into parts. Some rows hold notes instead, like UNKNOWN, Incarcerated or Moved Out of State, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY_PARISH: The county name, or parish in Louisiana. Casing varies.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.PHONE_NUMBER: A phone number, typed in mixed formats: with or without dashes, and with country codes for foreign numbers. Blank for many rows, and some are just stubs like 501-   -.
cols.DATE_FIRST_APPROVED_TO_PROVIDE_MEDICARE_: The date the nursing home was first approved to take Medicare and Medicaid patients.
cols.PROCESSING_DATE: The date CMS put out this batch of the file. The same date on every row of a table.
cols.PROVIDER_RESIDES_IN_HOSPITAL: Whether the nursing home is inside a hospital, Y or N.
cols.CONTINUING_CARE_RETIREMENT_COMMUNITY: Whether the nursing home is part of a retirement community with several levels of care, Y or N.
cols.SPECIAL_FOCUS_STATUS: Whether CMS put the nursing home on its watch list for homes with a record of serious problems: SFF means on it, SFF Candidate means in line for it. Blank for about 96% of homes.
cols.ABUSE_ICON: Y if the nursing home is marked with CMS's abuse warning icon, N if not.
cols.MOST_RECENT_HEALTH_INSPECTION_MORE_THAN_: Y if the home's last health inspection was more than two years ago, N if not.
cols.WITH_A_RESIDENT_AND_FAMILY_COUNCIL: Which kind of council the home has, like Resident or Both. Blank for about 6% of homes.
cols.NUMBER_OF_CERTIFIED_BEDS: How many beds the nursing home is certified to fill.
cols.AVERAGE_NUMBER_OF_RESIDENTS_PER_DAY: How many residents the home had on an average day, with a decimal.
cols.CHAIN_NAME: The nursing-home chain that owns or runs the home. Some chains are named after a person, like BENJAMIN LANDA.
cols.CHAIN_ID: CMS's ID number for the nursing-home chain. Blank when the home is not in a chain.
cols.NUMBER_OF_FACILITIES_IN_CHAIN: How many nursing homes are in the chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_OVERALL_5_STAR_RATING: The average overall star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_HEALTH_INSPECTION_RATING: The average inspection star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_STAFFING_RATING: The average staffing star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_QM_RATING: The average quality-of-care star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.OVERALL_RATING: The home's overall star rating from CMS, 1 to 5 stars. 5 is best.
cols.HEALTH_INSPECTION_RATING: The home's inspection star rating from CMS, 1 to 5 stars. 5 is best.
cols.STAFFING_RATING: The home's staffing star rating from CMS, 1 to 5 stars. 5 is best.
cols.REPORTED_NURSE_AIDE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_R: Nurse aide hours worked per resident per day, as the home reported them. 2.5 means two and a half hours.
cols.REPORTED_LPN_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT: Licensed practical nurse hours worked per resident per day, as the home reported them.
cols.REPORTED_RN_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT_: Registered nurse hours worked per resident per day, as the home reported them.
cols.REPORTED_LICENSED_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RES: Hours per resident per day from licensed nurses, registered and practical combined, as the home reported them.
cols.REPORTED_TOTAL_NURSE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_: All nursing hours per resident per day, aides and licensed nurses together, as the home reported them.
cols.TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_NURSE_STAFF_HOURS_PER_RE: All nursing hours per resident per day on weekends only. Usually lower than the weekday number.
cols.REGISTERED_NURSE_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT_PER_: Registered nurse hours per resident per day on weekends only.
cols.REPORTED_PHYSICAL_THERAPIST_STAFFING_HOU: Physical therapist hours per resident per day, as the home reported them. Usually a small fraction of an hour.
cols.NURSING_CASE_MIX_INDEX: A score for how much nursing care the home's residents need. Higher means sicker, needier residents.
cols.NURSING_CASE_MIX_INDEX_RATIO: The home's care-needs score divided by the national average. Above 1 means needier residents than average.
cols.TOTAL_NURSING_STAFF_TURNOVER: The percent of nursing staff who left over a year, from 0 to 100.
cols.REGISTERED_NURSE_TURNOVER: The percent of registered nurses who left over a year, from 0 to 100.
cols.NUMBER_OF_ADMINISTRATORS_WHO_HAVE_LEFT_T: How many administrators, the person running the home, left during the period CMS counts.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_STANDARD_SURVEY_HEALTH_DA: The date of the home's most recent routine health inspection. One table stores it as a date, the other as a date with a midnight time.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_DE: How many problems inspectors cited in the most recent inspection cycle, routine and complaint visits together.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_NUMBER_OF_STANDARD_HEALTH: How many problems the most recent routine inspection cited.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_NUMBER_OF_COMPLAINT_HEALT: How many problems were cited from complaint visits in the most recent inspection cycle.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_REVISITS: How many times inspectors had to come back to check fixes in the most recent inspection cycle.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_STANDARD_HEALTH_SURVEY_DA: The date of the home's second most recent routine health inspection. One table stores it as a date, the other as a date with a midnight time.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_: How many problems inspectors cited in the two earlier inspection cycles, routine and complaint visits together.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_NUMBER_OF_STANDARD_HEALTH: How many problems the second most recent routine inspection cited.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_NUMBER_OF_COMPLAINT_HEA: How many problems were cited from complaint visits in the two earlier inspection cycles.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_REVISI: How many times inspectors came back to check fixes in the two earlier inspection cycles.
cols.NUMBER_OF_FINES: How many fines the home was hit with in the period CMS counts.
cols.TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_FINES_IN_DOLLARS: The total of those fines, in dollars. Zero when there were none.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PAYMENT_DENIALS: How many times Medicare refused to pay the home for new admissions as a penalty.
cols.TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_PENALTIES: Fines plus payment denials, added together.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.PROVIDER_NUMBER: Meant for the provider number; use CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN. Empty in this table.
cols.PROVIDER_SSA_COUNTY_CODE: The home's county as a three-digit Social Security county code, like 200. Repeats across states, and the codes need a lookup.
cols.LEGAL_BUSINESS_NAME: The legal name of the company that runs the home. Some rows say 'Legal Business Name Not Available' instead of a name.
cols.PROVIDER_TYPE: Which programs pay the home: Medicare and Medicaid, Medicare only, or Medicaid only.
cols.URBAN: Y if the home is in an urban area, N if not.
cols.LOCATION: The home's full address on one line: street, city, state and ZIP.
cols.GEOCODING_FOOTNOTE: A footnote code on the map location; the only value is 22, on 808 rows. The code needs a lookup.
cols.DATE_OF_MOST_RECENT_HEALTH_INSPECTION: Meant for the date of the latest health inspection. Empty in this table.
cols.AUTOMATIC_SPRINKLER_SYSTEMS_IN_ALL_REQUI: Whether the home has sprinklers in every required area: Yes, Partial, or Data Not Available.
cols.NUMBER_OF_RESIDENTS_IN_CERTIFIED_BEDS: Meant for the count of residents in certified beds. Empty in this table.
cols.QUALITY_MEASURE_RATING: The home's quality-of-care star rating, 1 to 5.
cols.LONG_STAY_QM_RATING: Quality-of-care star rating for long-stay residents, 1 to 5.
cols.SHORT_STAY_QM_RATING: Quality-of-care star rating for short-stay residents, 1 to 5.
cols.CASE_MIX_NURSE_AIDE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_R: Expected nurse aide hours per resident per day for a home with these residents' care needs.
cols.CASE_MIX_LPN_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT: Expected licensed practical nurse hours per resident per day for a home with these residents' care needs.
cols.CASE_MIX_RN_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT_: Expected registered nurse hours per resident per day for a home with these residents' care needs.
cols.CASE_MIX_TOTAL_NURSE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_: Expected total nurse staff hours per resident per day for a home with these residents' care needs.
cols.CASE_MIX_WEEKEND_TOTAL_NURSE_STAFFING_HO: Expected weekend total nurse staff hours per resident per day for a home with these residents' care needs.
cols.ADJUSTED_NURSE_AIDE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_R: Reported nurse aide hours per resident per day, adjusted for how much care the residents need.
cols.ADJUSTED_LPN_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT: Reported licensed practical nurse hours per resident per day, adjusted for how much care the residents need.
cols.ADJUSTED_RN_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT_: Reported registered nurse hours per resident per day, adjusted for how much care the residents need.
cols.ADJUSTED_TOTAL_NURSE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_: Reported total nurse staff hours per resident per day, adjusted for how much care the residents need.
cols.ADJUSTED_WEEKEND_TOTAL_NURSE_STAFFING_HO: Reported weekend total nurse staff hours per resident per day, adjusted for how much care the residents need.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_HEALTH_DEFICIENCY_SCORE: Points for problems found in the latest inspection cycle; higher is worse.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_HEALTH_REVISIT_SCORE: Points for repeat visits inspectors needed in the latest cycle; 0 at most homes.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_TOTAL_HEALTH_SCORE: Total inspection points for the latest cycle; higher is worse.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_HEALTH_DEFICIENCY_SCORE: Points for problems found in the two inspection cycles before the latest; higher is worse.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_HEALTH_REVISIT_SCORE: Points for repeat visits in the two earlier cycles; 0 at most homes.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_TOTAL_HEALTH_SCORE: Total inspection points for the two earlier cycles; higher is worse.
cols.TOTAL_WEIGHTED_HEALTH_SURVEY_SCORE: Weighted inspection score across all three cycles; higher is worse.
cols.NUMBER_OF_CITATIONS_FROM_INFECTION_CONTR: Citations from infection-control inspections. Filled for only about 14% of homes.
cols.TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_DEFICIENCIES: Meant for the total count of health problems cited. Empty in this table.
cols.TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_FIRE_SAFETY_DEFICIENCIES: Meant for the total count of fire safety problems cited. Empty in this table.
cols.OVERALL_RATING_BAND: The overall star rating grouped as Low, Average, High or Not Rated. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.HAS_FINANCIAL_PENALTY: true if the home has been fined. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

HEALTH__FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME.summary: Every Medicare and Medicaid nursing home in the US, with star ratings, staffing, inspection scores, fines and abuse flags.

cols.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN: The nursing home's six-digit Medicare ID. Kept as text so leading zeros like 015073 survive.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.SURVEY_DATE: The date of the inspection that found this problem.
cols.SURVEY_TYPE: What kind of inspection it was. Always Health in the health table and Fire Safety in the fire table.
cols.DEFICIENCY_PREFIX: The letter in front of the rule number: F for health rules, K or E for fire and emergency rules.
cols.DEFICIENCY_CATEGORY: The broad group the broken rule falls in, like Pharmacy Service Deficiencies or Smoke Deficiencies.
cols.DEFICIENCY_TAG_NUMBER: The four-digit number of the rule that was broken, kept as text so leading zeros stay. Put the prefix letter in front to get the full tag, like F0725.
cols.DEFICIENCY_DESCRIPTION: The rule that was broken, in plain words, like Provide enough nursing staff every day.
cols.SCOPE_SEVERITY_CODE: One letter from A to L grading how serious and how widespread the problem was. Later letters are worse.
cols.DEFICIENCY_CORRECTED: Where the fix stands, like has a date of correction, has a plan of correction, Past Non-Compliance, or waiver granted.
cols.CORRECTION_DATE: The date the home fixed or promised to fix the problem.
cols.INSPECTION_CYCLE: Which inspection round the finding came from: 1 is the most recent, then 2, then 3. Stored as text.
cols.STANDARD_DEFICIENCY: Y if the problem was found on a routine inspection, N if not. Nearly always Y in the fire table.
cols.COMPLAINT_DEFICIENCY: Y if the problem was found on a visit sparked by a complaint, N if not. Nearly always N in the fire table.
cols.INFECTION_CONTROL_INSPECTION_DEFICIENCY: Y if the problem was found on an infection-control inspection, N if not. Nearly always N in both tables.
cols.CITATION_UNDER_IDR: Y if the home is disputing this citation through the informal appeal process, N if not. Nearly always N.
cols.CITATION_UNDER_IIDR: Y if the citation is under the independent appeal process, N if not. Nearly always N.
cols.PROCESSING_DATE: The date CMS put out this batch of the file. The same date on every row of a table.
cols.LOCATION: The home's full address on one line: street, city, state and ZIP.

cols.COVERED_RECIPIENT_LAST_NAME: The last name of the doctor or practitioner who got paid.
cols.RECIPIENT_CITY: The city of whoever received the payment.
cols.RECIPIENT_STATE: The state of whoever received the payment, as two letters.
cols.RECIPIENT_ZIP_CODE: The recipient's zip code, sometimes with the extra four digits after a dash. Blank in some grant rows.
cols.COVERED_RECIPIENT_PRIMARY_TYPE_1: The paid person's main profession, like Medical Doctor or Nurse Practitioner.
cols.COVERED_RECIPIENT_SPECIALTY_1: The paid person's specialty, as a broad group and a specialty split by a | bar.

cols.NATURE_OF_PAYMENT_OR_TRANSFER_OF_VALUE: What the payment was for, like Food and Beverage or Consulting Fee.

cols.TEACHING_HOSPITAL_NAME: The teaching hospital that got the payment.

cols.CITY_NAME: The city name. Casing varies, and some rows hold fillers like Not in a City, UNKNOWN or N/A.
cols.FAC_NAME: The name of the facility, like a business, school or clinic. Some rows just say RESIDENCE or UNKNOWN.
cols.CCN: The facility's 6-character Medicare certification number, stored as text; some hold letters, like 38T061. It is almost always blank in the three Open Payments tables.
cols.STATE_CD: The state: two letters like FL in the CMS tables, a 2-digit number code like 06 in the USGS table.
cols.FIPS_STATE_CD: The state as a two-digit federal code, like 48 for Texas. Stored as text.
cols.FIPS_CNTY_CD: The county as a three-digit federal code, kept as text with leading zeros. Only unique when paired with the state code.
cols.PRVDR_CTGRY_SBTYP_CD: The facility's subtype within its provider type, as a two-digit code that needs a lookup.
cols.PRVDR_CTGRY_CD: The type of provider, as a two-digit code that needs a lookup. Only five codes appear, led by 21, 01 and 12.
cols.CHOW_CNT: How many times the facility has changed owners on Medicare's record. Most show 0.
cols.CHOW_DT: Date of the most recent change of owner. Mostly blank, and some facilities with a change of owner on record have no date here.
cols.ACPTBL_POC_SW: Whether the facility has an accepted plan to fix problems found at inspection, Y or N.
cols.CMPLNC_STUS_CD: The facility's compliance status, as code A or B that needs a lookup. Blank for about 4 in 10.
cols.SSA_CNTY_CD: The county, as a three-digit Social Security county code that needs a lookup. It is not the FIPS county code.
cols.CROSS_REF_PROVIDER_NUMBER: Another Medicare provider number this facility is cross-referenced to. Mostly blank.
cols.CRTFCTN_DT: Date the facility was certified for Medicare.
cols.ELGBLTY_SW: A Y or N eligibility flag from Medicare's file; the name does not say eligible for what.
cols.INTRMDRY_CARR_CD: The Medicare contractor that handles the facility's claims, as a five-digit code that needs a lookup. 00000 is a placeholder.
cols.MDCD_VNDR_NUM: The facility's Medicaid vendor number. Blank for about 9 in 10. Mostly blank.
cols.ORGNL_PRTCPTN_DT: Date the facility first joined Medicare. 1966-07-01 is the most common date.
cols.CHOW_PRIOR_DT: Date of the change of owner before the most recent one. Mostly blank.
cols.INTRMDRY_CARR_PRIOR_CD: The claims contractor the facility used before its current one, as a code that needs a lookup. Blank for about 4 in 10.
cols.RGN_CD: The federal health region the facility sits in, as a two-digit code from 01 to 10.

cols.SSA_STATE_CD: The state, as a two-digit Social Security state code that needs a lookup. It is not the FIPS state code.

cols.PHNE_NUM: The facility's phone number, ten digits with no punctuation.
cols.PGM_TRMNTN_CD: Whether and why the facility left Medicare, as a two-digit code that needs a lookup. 00 is the most common value.
cols.TRMNTN_EXPRTN_DT: Date the facility's Medicare participation ended or expires. Mostly blank.
cols.CRTFCTN_ACTN_TYPE_CD: The kind of certification action on file, as a code from 1 to 8 that needs a lookup.
cols.GNRL_CNTL_TYPE_CD: Who owns or controls the facility, as a code like 03 or 2B that needs a lookup.
cols.ZIP_CD: The facility's ZIP code, five digits.
cols.CBSA_URBN_RRL_IND: Whether the facility is in an urban or rural area: U or R.

cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit National Provider Identifier, stored as text. Some tables leave it mostly blank or empty, and the SAM exclusions table uses 0000000000 as a filler.
cols.RURAL_STATUS: Whether the area or practice is rural. One table uses True or False; the others use Rural, Non-Rural, Partially Rural, Unknown or Not Applicable.
cols.PROVIDER_KEY: A number for the clinician record; each row has its own value.
cols.PRACTICE_STATE_OR_US_TERRITORY: The state or US territory where the clinician practices, as two letters.
cols.PRACTICE_SIZE: How many clinicians work in the practice, stored as text. Runs from 1 to over 11,000 for the biggest groups.
cols.CLINICIAN_TYPE: What kind of clinician this is, like Doctor of Medicine, Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant.
cols.CLINICIAN_SPECIALTY: The clinician's specialty as Medicare lists it, like Physician/Internal Medicine or Nurse Practitioner.
cols.YEARS_IN_MEDICARE: How many years the clinician has billed Medicare, stored as text.
cols.NON_REPORTING: True if the clinician sent in no data to be scored, stored as the text True or False.
cols.PARTICIPATION_OPTION: How the clinician took part: as a Group, APM Entity, Individual, Subgroup or Virtual Group.
cols.REPORTING_OPTION: Which scoring track was used: Traditional MIPS, APM Performance Pathway or MIPS Value Pathways.
cols.MIPS_VALUE_PATHWAY_ID: The code for the specialty track used, like G0058 or M0005. Mostly blank; only filled when the MIPS Value Pathways track was used.
cols.MIPS_VALUE_PATHWAY_TITLE: The name of the specialty track used, like Value in Primary Care. Mostly blank; only filled for the MIPS Value Pathways track.
cols.MEDICARE_PATIENTS: How many Medicare patients were counted for this score, stored as text. Often a whole group's total, not one person's.
cols.ALLOWED_CHARGES: Dollars Medicare allowed for the patients counted in this score. Often a whole group's total, running into the hundreds of millions.
cols.SERVICES: How many Medicare services were counted for this score, stored as text. Often a whole group's total.
cols.OPTED_INTO_MIPS: True if the clinician chose to be scored even though they could have sat out, stored as the text True or False.
cols.SMALL_PRACTICE_STATUS: True if the practice counts as small, stored as the text True or False.
cols.HEALTH_PROFESSIONAL_SHORTAGE_AREA_STATUS: True if the clinician works in an area short on health workers, stored as the text True or False.
cols.AMBULATORY_SURGICAL_CENTER_BASED_STATUS: True if the clinician works mainly at an outpatient surgery center, stored as the text True or False. Almost always False.
cols.HOSPITAL_BASED_STATUS: True if the clinician works mainly in a hospital, stored as the text True or False.
cols.NON_PATIENT_FACING_STATUS: True if the clinician rarely sees patients face to face, like a radiologist, stored as the text True or False.
cols.FACILITY_BASED_STATUS: True if the clinician works mainly in a facility like a hospital, stored as the text True or False.
cols.RECEIVED_FACILITY_SCORE: True if the clinician was scored using their hospital's score instead of their own, stored as the text True or False.
cols.DUAL_ELIGIBILITY_RATIO: Share of the clinician's patients who are on both Medicare and Medicaid, from 0 to 1.
cols.SAFETY_NET_STATUS: True if the clinician counts as a safety-net provider serving many low-income patients, stored as the text True or False.
cols.EXTREME_UNCONTROLLABLE_CIRCUMSTANCE_EUC: True if the clinician got relief for a disaster or other event outside their control, stored as the text True or False.
cols.FINAL_SCORE: The clinician's overall score, 0 to 100. This is the number that sets their Medicare pay change.
cols.PAYMENT_ADJUSTMENT_PERCENTAGE: The percent their Medicare payments go up or down because of the score. 0 means no change.
cols.COMPLEX_PATIENT_BONUS: Bonus points for treating sicker or poorer patients, stored as text. About half the rows get 0.00.
cols.QUALITY_CATEGORY_SCORE: The score for the quality part, 0 to 100.
cols.QUALITY_IMPROVEMENT_SCORE: Extra quality points for doing better than last year. Most rows get 0.
cols.QUALITY_CATEGORY_WEIGHT: How much the quality part counts toward the final score, as a share like 0.30, stored as text.
cols.QUALITY_REWEIGHTING_EUC: True if the quality part was dropped from the score because of a disaster or similar event, stored as the text True or False.
cols.SMALL_PRACTICE_BONUS: Bonus points for small practices: either 0.00 or 6.00, stored as text.

cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.

cols.TRANSACTION_ID: The seller's own line number on its report. It repeats across sellers and years, so it is not a row ID: use ARCOS_ROW_KEY.
cols.TRANSACTION_DATE: The day the shipment happened. Runs from January 2006 to December 2012.
cols.BUYER_NAME: The buyer's business name, like a specific pharmacy.
cols.INGREDIENT_NAME: The exact chemical form of the drug, like "oxycodone hydrochloride".
cols.COMPANY_NAME: The company that makes or sells the product.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: Which load run brought this row in. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.TRANSACTION_CODE: What kind of transaction it was. Always "S", a sale, except 5 broken rows where the columns slid over.
cols.REPORTER_DEA_NO: The seller's DEA license number. Every business allowed to handle these drugs has one.
cols.REPORTER_BUSINESS_ACTIVITY: What kind of business the seller is. Almost all are distributors; about 0.3% are drug makers.
cols.REPORTER_NAME: The seller's business name, as typed on its DEA registration.
cols.REPORTER_STATE: The seller's state, as two letters.
cols.REPORTER_COUNTY_FIPS: The seller's county, as a standard 5-digit government code.
cols.BUYER_DEA_NO: The buyer's DEA license number. The buyer is the pharmacy or doctor who received the pills.
cols.BUYER_BUSINESS_ACTIVITY: What kind of place the buyer is: a chain pharmacy, an independent pharmacy, or a doctor. "DW/30" marks a doctor licensed to treat 30 addiction patients.
cols.BUYER_STATE: The buyer's state, as two letters.
cols.BUYER_COUNTY_FIPS: The buyer's county, as a standard 5-digit government code.
cols.DRUG_CODE: The DEA's number for the drug.
cols.DRUG_NAME: The drug: hydrocodone or oxycodone. Nothing else is in this table.
cols.PRODUCT_NAME: The product as it's sold, with the strength, like "oxycodone hydrochloride tablets 5mg".
cols.QUANTITY: How many bottles or boxes were shipped. Not pills: 8 bottles of 100 is 8 here.
cols.DOSAGE_UNITS: How many pills were shipped. Use this column to count pills.
cols.BASE_WEIGHT_GRAMS: Grams of the pure drug in the shipment, not counting filler or the salt it's bound to.
cols.MME_CONVERSION_FACTOR: How strong this drug is next to morphine: 1.5 for oxycodone, 1 for hydrocodone.
cols.DOSAGE_STRENGTH: Milligrams of drug in each pill, like 5 or 10.
cols.MEASURE: The form the drug comes in. TAB, a tablet, on every row except the 5 broken ones.
cols.TOTAL_MME: The shipment's total strength counted as morphine: pills times milligrams times the conversion factor. The fairest way to compare shipments.
cols.LABELER_NAME: The company whose label is on the bottle.
cols.REPORTER_FAMILY: The seller's parent company, which rolls branches up to one name, like McKesson or Cardinal Health.
cols.ARCOS_ROW_KEY: A unique ID for each row, one per row across all 178,598,026. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

HEALTH__FED_DEA_ARCOS.row: One shipment line: one pill product, from one seller to one buyer, on one day.

cols.REPORT_NUMBER: The agency's ID number for the incident or bad-reaction report. The format differs by source.
cols.PRODUCTS: A list of the products tied to this record, packed as JSON text you have to unpack to read.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.REPORT_TYPE: How the report came in: Pre-MoCRA, the older system, Expedited 15-day reports, Direct reports, or Periodic ones.
cols.REPORT_VERSION: Which version of the report this is. 1 is the first; higher numbers are follow-ups.
cols.INITIAL_RECEIVED_DATE: The day the FDA first got the report.
cols.LATEST_RECEIVED_DATE: The day the FDA got the newest version of the report.
cols.MEDDRA_VERSION: The version of the medical word list used to name the reactions. Every row says 28, so it tells you nothing.
cols.PATIENT: The patient's age, age unit and gender, packed together in one block of text, like {"gender":"Female"}.
cols.REACTIONS: What happened to the patient, as a list, like ["Ovarian Cancer"] or ["Death","Injury"]. Ovarian cancer claims fill a big share.
cols.OUTCOMES: How bad it got, as a list, like ["Death"] or ["Hospitalization"].
cols.PRODUCT_BRAND_NAME: Empty on every row. The product details sit in the PRODUCTS column, as a list.
cols.PRIMARY_REACTION_TEXT: Empty on every row. Use the reactions column instead.

cols.K_NUMBER: The FDA clearance number for a device, usually K plus six digits. DEN and BK numbers also show up. Mostly blank in the establishment table.

cols.DECISION_CODE: FDA's short code for its decision, like SESE in the clearance table or APPR and OK30 in the high-risk approval table. Needs a lookup.
cols.THIRD_PARTY_FLAG: Y if an outside reviewer, not FDA staff, could review the device, N if not. Mostly N in both tables, and a few classification rows are blank.

cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.POSTAL_CODE: The ZIP or postal code, stored as text, as 5 or 9 digits or a foreign code. Fillers like 00000, UNKNOWN, N/A and -- mean none.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTRY_CODE: The country as a code, usually two letters like US, but some tables use three letters like AGO. The World Bank debt table also holds group codes like MIC and LMC that need a lookup.
cols.OPENFDA: A bundle of extra FDA details for the product, like device class, brand name, or facility numbers, stored as JSON, a nested list. Always empty braces in the device enforcement table and mostly empty braces in the drug enforcement table.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CLEARANCE_TYPE: Kind of 510k review: Traditional, Special, Abbreviated or a few rarer types.
cols.DECISION_DESCRIPTION: The FDA decision in words, almost always Substantially Equivalent; Unknown on some.
cols.STATEMENT_OR_SUMMARY: Whether the maker filed a Summary or a Statement with the clearance. Blank on about a third of rows.
cols.REVIEW_ADVISORY_COMMITTEE: Two-letter code for the FDA panel that reviewed the device, like SU or CV; the codes need a lookup.

cols.PRODUCT_CODE: The FDA's three-letter code for the type of medical device, like GEX. Needs a lookup; empty in the device enforcement table.
cols.DEVICE_NAME: The name of the medical device, like CRYOSURGICAL DEVICE 2000 or Osmolality Of Tears.

cols.REGISTRATION_NUMBER_LIST: A comma-separated list of FDA registration numbers for the facilities that make this kind of device. Some lists start with a stray comma, and the column is empty in the device recall table.

cols.FEI_NUMBER_LIST: A comma-separated list of FDA facility ID numbers for the places that make this kind of device. Some lists start with a stray comma, and the column is empty in the device recall table.

cols.DEVICE_CLASS: The device type's risk class, mostly 1, 2 or 3, plus N, U and f codes that need a lookup.
cols.REGULATION_NUMBER: The federal rule number that covers the device, like 876.1500.
cols.MEDICAL_SPECIALTY: Two-letter code for the medical specialty, like GU or CV; the description column spells it out.
cols.MEDICAL_SPECIALTY_DESCRIPTION: The medical specialty in words, like Clinical Chemistry. Unknown on about 900 rows.
cols.REVIEW_PANEL: Two-letter code for the FDA panel that reviews the device, like GU or SU; the codes need a lookup.
cols.SUBMISSION_TYPE_ID: Code for the kind of FDA review needed, a number from 1 to 8; the codes need a lookup.
cols.UNCLASSIFIED_REASON: Code for why a device is not classified, like 1 or 3; the codes need a lookup. Almost always blank.
cols.DEFINITION: Free-text definition or notes for the device type. Mostly blank.

cols.LIFE_SUSTAIN_SUPPORT_FLAG: Y or N: whether the device keeps a patient alive.
cols.PMA_NUMBER_LIST: FDA premarket approval numbers tied to the device, as a comma list like P010061. Mostly blank.

cols.CENTER_CLASSIFICATION_DATE: The date FDA ranked how dangerous the recall is.
cols.REPORT_DATE: The date the report was issued. One CMS table stores it as text like Q2, 2026.
cols.TERMINATION_DATE: The date the thing ended, like a registration, recall or judge's service, and blank when it has not ended. Some rows hold far-future dates like 2101-01-04 or 2200-12-30.

cols.PRODUCT_TYPE: The kind of product. Always Drugs in this table.

cols.GENERIC_NAME_LIST: The generic names of the recalled drugs, like LEVOTHYROXINE SODIUM. Mostly blank.

cols.ITIS_TSN: The plant or animal's ID in ITIS, the US species list. Mostly blank.
cols.NCBI_TAXON_ID: The species ID in the NCBI taxonomy, like 9606. Mostly blank.
cols.USDA_PLANTS_ID: The plant's ID in the USDA PLANTS database, like ABFR2. Mostly blank.
cols.POWO_ID: The plant's ID in Kew's Plants of the World Online, like 326889-2. Mostly blank.
cols.GRIN_ID: The plant's ID in the USDA GRIN plant database. Mostly blank.
cols.MPNS_ID: The plant's ID in the Medicinal Plant Names Services list, like WCS-355112. Mostly blank.
cols.INN_ID: The drug's ID in the World Health Organization's list of generic drug names. Mostly blank.
cols.USAN_ID: The drug's US Adopted Name ID, like DE-66. Mostly blank.
cols.DAILYMED_NAME: Despite the name, the values look like FDA substance codes, not names. Mostly blank.
cols.DISPLAY_NAME: The substance's name, in capitals, like POTASSIUM CREOSOTESULFONATE.
cols.MOLECULAR_FORMULA: The chemical formula, like C10H18O. Blank for non-chemicals.
cols.INCHIKEY: A standard fingerprint code for the chemical structure. Blank for non-chemicals.
cols.SMILES: The chemical structure written as a line of text. Blank for non-chemicals.
cols.INGREDIENT_TYPE: What role the substance plays, like INGREDIENT SUBSTANCE or IONIC MOIETY.
cols.SUBSTANCE_TYPE: What kind of substance it is, like chemical, protein, mixture or polymer.

HEALTH__FED_FDA_UNII_GSRS_SUBSTANCES.summary: The FDA's master list of 168,046 substances, from drugs and chemicals to plants and proteins, each with its FDA ID and matching IDs in other databases.
HEALTH__FED_FDA_UNII_GSRS_SUBSTANCES.row: One substance: one FDA substance ID, with its name, chemical formula and IDs in other databases.

cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.MIDDLE_NAME: The person's middle name, or just an initial.
cols.BUSINESS_NAME: The name of the business, when the row is a business. Mostly blank in the exclusion list, where most rows are people, and the firearms-license table often holds the word None instead.
cols.SPECIALTY: The provider's medical specialty or job, like Family Practice or Pharmacist.
cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit National Provider Identifier, stored as text. Some tables leave it mostly blank or empty, and the SAM exclusions table uses 0000000000 as a filler.
cols.EXCLUSION_TYPE: Why the person or company is barred. HHS tables use the law section as a code like 1128a1; the SAM tables use words like Voluntary Exclusion. It is almost always blank in the health-center people table.
cols.EXCLUSION_DATE: The date the provider was barred from federal health programs. One table writes it as 8 digits like 20260720, and it is almost always blank in the health-center staff table.
cols.REINSTATEMENT_DATE: The date a revoked status was restored, like a charity's tax exemption given back. Mostly blank, and empty in the OIG exclusions table.
cols.ADDRESS: The full address in one line of text, messy and not split into parts. Some rows hold notes instead, like UNKNOWN, Incarcerated or Moved Out of State, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Fillers like 00000, UNKNO or a lone dash show up, some codes lost a leading zero like 8721, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.WAS_REINSTATED: Whether the group or person later got back what they lost, like a tax exemption: True or False. Always False in the health-fraud exclusion list sample.
cols.IS_ENTITY_NOT_INDIVIDUAL: True if the barred party is a business or group, False if it is a person.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.EXCLUSION_SK: A code built for this exclusion record. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.GENERAL_CATEGORY: The kind of person or business excluded, in cut-off capitals, like IND- LIC HC SERV PRO or NURSING PROFESSION.
cols.UPIN: The person's old Medicare doctor ID from before NPI numbers, like G71212. Mostly blank.
cols.NPI_IS_REAL: True if the row holds a real National Provider Identifier, false if the NPI is missing or a placeholder. Mostly false.
cols.HAS_WAIVER: True if the exclusion has a waiver letting the person keep working in some federal programs. Only 4 rows say true.

HEALTH__FED_HHS_OIG_LEIE.summary: The federal list of people and businesses banned from Medicare, Medicaid and other federal health programs, kept by the HHS Inspector General.
HEALTH__FED_HHS_OIG_LEIE.row: One exclusion: one person or business barred from federal health programs, from one start date.

cols.HPSA_ID: The ID of a federally named doctor-shortage area, ten characters, sometimes ending in a letter. Stored as text.
cols.BHCMIS_ORGANIZATION_ID: The federal ID for a community health center organization, as text with leading zeros. Mostly blank in the shortage-area table.
cols.HPSA_NAME: The name of the doctor-shortage area, like a county, a neighborhood, a low-income group, or a clinic.
cols.HPSA_DISCIPLINE_CLASS: Which kind of care is short: Primary Care, Dental Health, or Mental Health. Always Primary Care in the primary-care table.
cols.DISCIPLINE_CLASS_NUMBER: A number for which kind of care is short: 1 lines up with Primary Care, 6 with Dental Health, 7 with Mental Health. Always 1 in the primary-care table.
cols.HPSA_SCORE: How severe the doctor shortage is, 0 to 25. Higher means worse. Stored as text in one table.
cols.PC_MCTA_SCORE: A score for how short the area is on maternity care. Mostly blank, and stored as text with stray leading spaces in one table.
cols.HPSA_STATUS: Where the shortage designation stands: Designated, Proposed For Withdrawal, or Withdrawn.
cols.HPSA_STATUS_CODE: The same status as one letter: D Designated, P Proposed For Withdrawal, W Withdrawn.
cols.HPSA_TYPE_CODE: What kind of shortage area it is, like Hpsa Geo for a place, Hpsa Pop for a group of people, or a facility type like FQHC or ITU. Needs a lookup.
cols.WITHDRAWN_DATE: The date the shortage designation was withdrawn. Blank if still active. A real date in one table, month/day/year text in the other.
cols.BREAK_IN_DESIGNATION: Y if the shortage designation had a gap in time, N if not. Every row in both tables is N.
cols.HPSA_FTE: How many full-time doctors the area has, counted in full-time equivalents, so 0.5 is one half-time doctor. Stored as text in one table.
cols.HPSA_SHORTAGE: How many more full-time doctors the area needs to end the shortage. Stored as text in one table, often blank.
cols.METROPOLITAN_INDICATOR: Whether the area is Metropolitan, Non-Metropolitan, Frontier, or Unknown.
cols.RURAL_STATUS: Whether the area or practice is rural. One table uses True or False; the others use Rural, Non-Rural, Partially Rural, Unknown or Not Applicable.
cols.RURAL_STATUS_CODE: A one-letter rural code: R rural, N not rural, P partly rural, U unknown, plus a rare A that needs a lookup. Sometimes blank.
cols.US_MEXICO_BORDER_100KM_INDICATOR: Y if the place is within 100 kilometers of the Mexico border, N if not, U if unknown.
cols.US_MEXICO_BORDER_COUNTY_INDICATOR: Y if the place is in a county on the Mexico border, N if not, U if unknown.
cols.HPSA_ADDRESS: The street address of the shortage area, only when it is a single facility. Blank for about 90% of rows.
cols.HPSA_CITY: The city of the shortage area, only when it is a single facility. Blank for about 90% of rows.
cols.HPSA_POSTAL_CODE: The zip code of the shortage area, only when it is a single facility. Blank for about 90% of rows, sometimes with the four-digit add-on.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.PRIMARY_STATE_ABBREVIATION: The area's state or territory, as two letters. Includes places like GU for Guam and MH for the Marshall Islands.
cols.PRIMARY_STATE_NAME: The area's state or territory, spelled out.
cols.PRIMARY_STATE_FIPS_CODE: The area's state as a two-digit federal code, kept as text with leading zeros.
cols.STATE_ABBREVIATION: The state as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam and AS for American Samoa appear too.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_FIPS_CODE: The state as a 2-digit Census code, like 06 for California. Territories use codes 60 and up.
cols.COMMON_STATE_ABBREVIATION: The area's state or territory, as two letters. Nearly the same as the primary state column, but a few rows differ.
cols.COMMON_STATE_NAME: The area's state or territory, spelled out.
cols.COMMON_STATE_FIPS_CODE: The area's state as a two-digit federal code, kept as text with leading zeros.
cols.COMMON_COUNTY_NAME: The county with its state tacked on, like Polk County, FL.
cols.COMMON_STATE_COUNTY_FIPS_CODE: The county as a five-digit federal code, state plus county, kept as text with leading zeros.
cols.COMMON_POSTAL_CODE: The five-digit zip code of the shortage area. Blank for about 90% of rows.
cols.COMMON_REGION_NAME: The federal health department region, like Region 4.
cols.COUNTY_EQUIVALENT_NAME: The county name, or the local equivalent in territories, like Rongelap in the Marshall Islands.
cols.STATE_COUNTY_FIPS_CODE: The county's five-digit government code, where the first two digits are the state. Kept as text so leading zeros survive.
cols.RECORD_CREATE_DATE: The date the source built the file. It is 2026-08-07 on every row, so it says nothing about the individual record.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.HPSA_COMPONENT_ID: A made-up ID for each area-and-piece pair. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.HPSA_GEOGRAPHY_ID: The code for the piece of land, like a census tract or county code. Stand-alone clinics say POINT instead.
cols.HPSA_COMPONENT_SOURCE_ID: An ID for a stand-alone clinic piece, filled only on those rows. Mostly blank.
cols.DESIGNATION_TYPE: The kind of shortage label, like HPSA Population, Geographic HPSA, or a clinic type such as Rural Health Clinic.
cols.DESIGNATION_DATE: When the area was first named a shortage area. Some dates go back to 1978.
cols.DESIGNATION_LAST_UPDATE_DATE: When the shortage label was last changed.
cols.WITHDRAWN_DATE_STRING: The date the label was withdrawn, stored as text like 2024/01/02. Blank on the rest of the rows.
cols.DEGREE_OF_SHORTAGE: How severe the shortage is. Almost every filled row says Not applicable; the few real values are numbers stored as text.
cols.DESIGNATION_POPULATION: How many people live in the shortage area. It is a figure for the whole area, carried on each of its pieces, so do not add it up across rows; some say 0.
cols.PCT_POPULATION_BELOW_POVERTY: Share of the area's people below the poverty line, as a percent. Some say 0.
cols.FORMAL_RATIO: People per primary-care doctor in the area, written as text like 3853:1. Some say 0:1.
cols.PROVIDER_RATIO_GOAL: The people-per-doctor mark the area is measured against, written as text like 3000:1 or 3500:1.
cols.ESTIMATED_SERVED_POPULATION: How many people the area's current doctors can serve.
cols.ESTIMATED_UNDERSERVED_POPULATION: How many people are left without enough care. Some values are negative, like -3500.
cols.RESIDENT_CIVILIAN_POPULATION: The area's civilian population. Mostly blank, and some say 0.
cols.POPULATION_TYPE: Which group the shortage covers, like the whole local population or low-income residents.
cols.POPULATION_TYPE_CODE: A short code for that group, like LI or TRC; POPULATION_TYPE spells it out.
cols.DESIGNATION_POPULATION_TYPE_DESCRIPTION: The group the shortage covers, or the clinic type for clinic labels.
cols.PROVIDER_TYPE: Says Not Applicable on every filled row, so it tells you nothing.
cols.METROPOLITAN_INDICATOR_CODE: Whether the area is urban or rural, as a code: 0, M, N or F. The codes need a lookup.
cols.COMPONENT_NAME: The name of the piece, like a census tract or a town. Some are bare numbers.
cols.COMPONENT_TYPE_CODE: A short code for the kind of piece: CT, CSD, SCTY or UNK.
cols.COMPONENT_TYPE_DESCRIPTION: The kind of piece: Census Tract, County Subdivision, Single County, or Unknown.
cols.COMPONENT_STATE_ABBREVIATION: The piece's state, as two letters.
cols.COUNTY_FIPS_CODE: The 3-digit county code within the state; it needs the state to point at one county.
cols.RECORD_CREATE_DATE_TEXT: The date the file was made, stored as text; 2026/08/07 on every row.

HEALTH__FED_HRSA_HPSA_PRIMARY_CARE.summary: Places the federal government has named short of primary-care doctors, with each area's scores, population and poverty figures, split into the census tracts, towns and counties that make it up.

cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.

cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.PRF_ROW_ID: A row number for the line. Each row has its own. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.PROVIDER_NAME: The name of the doctor, practice or hospital that got the money, as written in the file.
cols.PAYMENT_AMOUNT: The payment in whole dollars. Use this column to add up money.
cols.PAYMENT_RAW: The payment as it was written in the file, with a dollar sign and commas, like $1,017.
cols.NAME_KEY: The provider name cleaned up for matching: capitals, punctuation removed. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.NAME_WORDS: How many words are in the cleaned name. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

cols.SITE_NAME: The name of the place, whether a Superfund cleanup site, a mine, a stream gauge, or a health clinic. Many mine rows just say Unknown or Unnamed.
cols.SITE_ADDRESS: The street address of the site, like the workplace OSHA inspected or the health center's clinic.
cols.HEALTH_CENTER_NAME: The name of the community health center organization.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.

cols.STATE_COUNTY_FIPS_CODE: The county's five-digit government code, where the first two digits are the state. Kept as text so leading zeros survive.
cols.COUNTY_EQUIVALENT_NAME: The county name, or the local equivalent in territories, like Rongelap in the Marshall Islands.
cols.STATE_FIPS_CODE: The state as a 2-digit Census code, like 06 for California. Territories use codes 60 and up.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.RECORD_CREATE_DATE: The date the source built the file. It is 2026-08-07 on every row, so it says nothing about the individual record.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.HEALTH_CENTER_NUMBER: The federal grant number of the parent health center, like H80CS00293. Many sites share one.
cols.FQHC_SITE_MEDICARE_BILLING_NUMBER: The site's Medicare billing number. Blank for more than half of sites.
cols.FQHC_SITE_NPI_NUMBER: The site's own 10-digit NPI. Blank for about two thirds of sites.
cols.SITE_STATE_ABBREVIATION: The site's state, as two letters.
cols.SITE_POSTAL_CODE: The site's ZIP code, as 5 digits or 9 with a dash.
cols.SITE_TELEPHONE_NUMBER: The site's phone number, sometimes with an extension.
cols.SITE_WEB_ADDRESS: The health center's website. Blank for about half of sites.
cols.OPERATING_HOURS_PER_WEEK: How many hours a week the site is open, like 40.
cols.LOCATION_SETTING_ID: A number code for the kind of setting. The next column spells it out.
cols.LOCATION_SETTING_DESCRIPTION: The kind of setting, like School, Hospital or All Other Clinic Types.
cols.SITE_STATUS_ID: A status code. It is 1 on every row.
cols.SITE_STATUS_DESCRIPTION: The site's status. Active on every row.
cols.LOCATION_TYPE_ID: A number code for permanent, seasonal or mobile. The next column spells it out.
cols.LOCATION_TYPE_DESCRIPTION: Whether the site is Permanent, Seasonal, or a Mobile Van.
cols.SITE_TYPE_ID: A number code for what the site does. The next column spells it out.
cols.SITE_TYPE_DESCRIPTION: Whether the site sees patients, is an office, or both.
cols.OPERATOR_ID: A number code for who runs the site. The next column spells it out.
cols.OPERATOR_DESCRIPTION: Who runs the site: the health center itself, a subrecipient, or a contractor.
cols.OPERATING_SCHEDULE_ID: A number code for full- or part-time. The next column spells it out.
cols.OPERATING_SCHEDULE_DESCRIPTION: Whether the site is open Full-Time or Part-Time. Unknown for most sites.
cols.OPERATING_CALENDAR_ID: A number code for year-round or seasonal. The next column spells it out.
cols.OPERATING_CALENDAR: Whether the site is open Year-Round or Seasonal. Unknown for most sites.
cols.SITE_ADDED_TO_SCOPE_DATE: The date the site was added to the health center's federal grant.
cols.HEALTH_CENTER_TYPE: The kind of health center. Most rows are a Federally Qualified Health Center; 963 are FQHC Look-Alikes, which meet the same rules but get no federal health center grant.
cols.HEALTH_CENTER_STREET_ADDRESS: The parent health center's street address.
cols.HEALTH_CENTER_STATE: The parent health center's state, as two letters.
cols.HEALTH_CENTER_ZIP_CODE: The parent health center's ZIP code, as 5 digits or 9 with a dash.
cols.GRANTEE_ORGANIZATION_TYPE: What kind of organization got the grant, like a tax-exempt corporation or a government body.
cols.COMPLETE_COUNTY_NAME: The site's county with the word County, like Los Angeles County.
cols.COUNTY_DESCRIPTION: What the local area is called, like County, Parish, Borough or Municipio.
cols.HHS_REGION_CODE: The federal health department's region number for the site, 01 to 10.
cols.HHS_REGION_NAME: The federal health department's region, like Region 4.
cols.STATE_FIPS_CONGRESSIONAL_DISTRICT_CODE: The congressional district as a four-digit code: two for the state, two for the district, like 5401.
cols.CONGRESSIONAL_DISTRICT_NUMBER: The congressional district number within the state, like 02.
cols.CONGRESSIONAL_DISTRICT_NAME: The congressional district in words, like West Virginia District 01 or Alaska At Large.
cols.CONGRESSIONAL_DISTRICT_CODE: The congressional district as state letters and number, like WV-01. At-large seats use 00.
cols.US_REPRESENTATIVE_NAME: The member of the House for the site's district.
cols.US_SENATOR_ONE_NAME: One of the two U.S. senators for the site's state.
cols.US_SENATOR_TWO_NAME: The other U.S. senator for the site's state.

cols.SERVICE_UNIT: The Indian Health Service district the facility belongs to, like CROW or ANCHORAGE.
cols.FACILITY_NAME: The name of the plant, site or building, as the agency wrote it. Generic fillers like RESIDENCE, UNKNOWN, WELL or HOME are common in some tables.
cols.FACILITY_TYPE: What kind of facility it is, like Hospital, Nursing home, Health Center, or Apartment in the HUD housing table. One table leaves it empty.
cols.STREET: The street address line, like 925 DAYNA ST or PO BOX 505. Some rows hold UNKNOWN instead.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Fillers like 00000, UNKNO or a lone dash show up, some codes lost a leading zero like 8721, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.PHONE: A phone number, in mixed formats, sometimes with an extension like x1102. Empty in the labor union table, and the FCC table has one value, just I.
cols.APC_FLAG: A flag the Indian Health Service calls APC; it needs a lookup. Yes or No in the facilities list, but mostly blank in the other table, where it holds 1, 2, Y, N, 0, or A.
cols.ITU_CODE: Who runs the facility, as one letter: I for Indian Health Service, T for a tribe, U for an urban Indian program. N and ? also show up in one table.
cols.LOCATION_TYPE: Who runs the facility, spelled out, like IHS, Urban, Title 1 Tribal, Title 5 Tribal 638, or Non-IHS. Mostly blank in the larger facility table, which also has a stray 9.
cols.BED_COUNT: How many beds the facility has. Zero for places with no beds.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.WEBSITE: The organization's website address, with or without www or https. A few rows in the energy-efficiency table hold a sentence of text instead.

cols.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN: The nursing home's six-digit Medicare ID. Kept as text so leading zeros like 015073 survive.
