cols.AVERAGE_NUMBER_OF_RESIDENTS_PER_DAY: How many residents the home had on an average day, with a decimal.
cols.PROVIDER_RESIDES_IN_HOSPITAL: Whether the nursing home is inside a hospital, Y or N.
cols.DATE_FIRST_APPROVED_TO_PROVIDE_MEDICARE_: The date the nursing home was first approved to take Medicare and Medicaid patients.
cols.CHAIN_NAME: The nursing-home chain that owns or runs the home. Some chains are named after a person, like BENJAMIN LANDA.
cols.CHAIN_ID: CMS's ID number for the nursing-home chain. Blank when the home is not in a chain.
cols.NUMBER_OF_FACILITIES_IN_CHAIN: How many nursing homes are in the chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_OVERALL_5_STAR_RATING: The average overall star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_HEALTH_INSPECTION_RATING: The average inspection star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_STAFFING_RATING: The average staffing star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_QM_RATING: The average quality-of-care star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CONTINUING_CARE_RETIREMENT_COMMUNITY: Whether the nursing home is part of a retirement community with several levels of care, Y or N.
cols.SPECIAL_FOCUS_STATUS: Whether CMS put the nursing home on its watch list for homes with a record of serious problems: SFF means on it, SFF Candidate means in line for it. Blank for about 96% of homes.
cols.ABUSE_ICON: Y if the nursing home is marked with CMS's abuse warning icon, N if not.
cols.MOST_RECENT_HEALTH_INSPECTION_MORE_THAN_: Y if the home's last health inspection was more than two years ago, N if not.
cols.WITH_A_RESIDENT_AND_FAMILY_COUNCIL: Which kind of council the home has, like Resident or Both. Blank for about 6% of homes.
cols.OVERALL_RATING: The home's overall star rating from CMS, 1 to 5 stars. 5 is best.
cols.HEALTH_INSPECTION_RATING: The home's inspection star rating from CMS, 1 to 5 stars. 5 is best.
cols.STAFFING_RATING: The home's staffing star rating from CMS, 1 to 5 stars. 5 is best.
cols.REPORTED_NURSE_AIDE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_R: Nurse aide hours worked per resident per day, as the home reported them. 2.5 means two and a half hours.
cols.REPORTED_LPN_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT: Licensed practical nurse hours worked per resident per day, as the home reported them.
cols.REPORTED_RN_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT_: Registered nurse hours worked per resident per day, as the home reported them.
cols.REPORTED_LICENSED_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RES: Hours per resident per day from licensed nurses, registered and practical combined, as the home reported them.
cols.REPORTED_TOTAL_NURSE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_: All nursing hours per resident per day, aides and licensed nurses together, as the home reported them.
cols.TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_NURSE_STAFF_HOURS_PER_RE: All nursing hours per resident per day on weekends only. Usually lower than the weekday number.
cols.REGISTERED_NURSE_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT_PER_: Registered nurse hours per resident per day on weekends only.
cols.REPORTED_PHYSICAL_THERAPIST_STAFFING_HOU: Physical therapist hours per resident per day, as the home reported them. Usually a small fraction of an hour.
cols.TOTAL_NURSING_STAFF_TURNOVER: The percent of nursing staff who left over a year, from 0 to 100.
cols.REGISTERED_NURSE_TURNOVER: The percent of registered nurses who left over a year, from 0 to 100.
cols.NUMBER_OF_ADMINISTRATORS_WHO_HAVE_LEFT_T: How many administrators, the person running the home, left during the period CMS counts.
cols.NURSING_CASE_MIX_INDEX: A score for how much nursing care the home's residents need. Higher means sicker, needier residents.
cols.NURSING_CASE_MIX_INDEX_RATIO: The home's care-needs score divided by the national average. Above 1 means needier residents than average.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_STANDARD_SURVEY_HEALTH_DA: The date of the home's most recent routine health inspection. One table stores it as a date, the other as a date with a midnight time.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_DE: How many problems inspectors cited in the most recent inspection cycle, routine and complaint visits together.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_NUMBER_OF_STANDARD_HEALTH: How many problems the most recent routine inspection cited.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_NUMBER_OF_COMPLAINT_HEALT: How many problems were cited from complaint visits in the most recent inspection cycle.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_REVISITS: How many times inspectors had to come back to check fixes in the most recent inspection cycle.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_STANDARD_HEALTH_SURVEY_DA: The date of the home's second most recent routine health inspection. One table stores it as a date, the other as a date with a midnight time.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_: How many problems inspectors cited in the two earlier inspection cycles, routine and complaint visits together.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_NUMBER_OF_STANDARD_HEALTH: How many problems the second most recent routine inspection cited.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_NUMBER_OF_COMPLAINT_HEA: How many problems were cited from complaint visits in the two earlier inspection cycles.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_REVISI: How many times inspectors came back to check fixes in the two earlier inspection cycles.
cols.NUMBER_OF_FINES: How many fines the home was hit with in the period CMS counts.
cols.TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_FINES_IN_DOLLARS: The total of those fines, in dollars. Zero when there were none.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PAYMENT_DENIALS: How many times Medicare refused to pay the home for new admissions as a penalty.
cols.TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_PENALTIES: Fines plus payment denials, added together.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.PROCESSING_DATE: The date CMS put out this batch of the file. The same date on every row of a table.
cols.OWNERSHIP_TYPE_DETAIL: Ownership in detail, like For profit - Corporation or Government - County.
cols.PROVIDER_TYPE: Which programs it takes: Medicare and Medicaid, Medicare only or Medicaid only.
cols.PROBLEM_FACILITIES_SFFS_CANDIDATES_ONE_S: Yes if the home is a flagged problem facility, a special focus candidate or one-star; No if not.
cols.PROVIDER_CHANGED_OWNERSHIP_IN_LAST_12_MO: Y if the home changed owners in the last 12 months, N if not; only a few dozen say Y.
cols.EXPECTED_NURSE_AIDE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_R: Nurse aide hours per resident per day that CMS expects, given how sick the residents are.
cols.DEVIATION_FROM_EXPECTED_NURSE_AIDE_STAFF: Gap between reported and expected nurse aide hours; negative means fewer hours than expected.
cols.EXPECTED_RN_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT_: Registered nurse hours per resident per day that CMS expects, given how sick the residents are.
cols.DEVIATION_FROM_EXPECTED_RN_STAFFING: Gap between reported and expected registered nurse hours; negative means fewer hours than expected.
cols.EXPECTED_TOTAL_NURSE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_: Total nurse staff hours per resident per day that CMS expects, given how sick the residents are.
cols.DEVIATION_FROM_EXPECTED_TOTAL_NURSE_HOUR: Gap between reported and expected total nurse hours; negative means fewer hours than expected.
cols.NUMBER_OF_FACILITY_REPORTED_INCIDENTS: Number of incidents the home reported about itself.
cols.LOCATION: Full address in one string: street, city, state and ZIP.

HEALTH__FED_NURSINGHOME411.summary: Every nursing home certified for Medicare or Medicaid, 14,713 homes, with star ratings, staffing, inspections, complaints, chain and ownership details from CMS.
HEALTH__FED_NURSINGHOME411.row: One nursing home: one certified facility and its current ratings.

cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.COHORT: The group of people the row counts, like Veteran, Other Veteran, or Non-Veteran.
cols.SEX: Male or Female. Some tables also have All.
cols.RANK: The row's place in a ranked list, where 1 is first. Empty in the USGS minerals table.
cols.CRUDE_RATE: Deaths per 100,000 people, not adjusted for age. Blank in about half the VA rows.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CAUSE_OF_DEATH: The cause of death, like Malaria or Whooping cough.
cols.PERCENT_OF_DEATHS: This cause's share of all deaths in the group, as a percent. Blank on some rows.
cols.UNADJUSTED_RATE: Deaths per 100,000 people, not adjusted for age. Blank on almost every row.
cols.AGE_ADJUSTED_RATE: Deaths per 100,000 people, adjusted for age so groups compare fairly. Mostly blank.
cols.YPLL: Years of potential life lost: how many years early these deaths came, added up. Blank on some rows.
cols.YPLL_PCT: This cause's share of all years of life lost, as a percent. Blank on some rows.

HEALTH__FED_VA_ALLCAUSE_MORTALITY.summary: Leading causes of death among veterans, 2018 to 2023, with counts, rates and years of life lost, by group and sex, from the VA.
HEALTH__FED_VA_ALLCAUSE_MORTALITY.row: One cause-year: one cause of death, for one veteran group and sex, in one year.

cols.YEAR_OF_DEATH: The year the deaths happened, like 2021.
cols.COHORT: The group of people the row counts, like Veteran, Other Veteran, or Non-Veteran.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.AGE_GROUP: Age band: All, 18-34, 35-54, 55-74 or 75+. Blank on some rows.
cols.POPULATION_ESTIMATE: Estimated population the rate is based on.
cols.UNADJUSTED_RATE_PER_100K: Suicide deaths per 100,000 people, not adjusted for age.
cols.AGE_ADJUSTED_RATE_PER_100K: Suicide deaths per 100,000, adjusted for age so groups compare fairly. Filled on only about 1 in 6 rows.
cols.MALE_SUICIDE_DEATHS: Male suicide deaths. Blank on about a third of rows.
cols.MALE_POPULATION_ESTIMATE: Estimated male population. Blank on about a third of rows.
cols.MALE_UNADJUSTED_RATE_PER_100K: Male suicide deaths per 100,000, not adjusted for age. Blank on about a third of rows.
cols.MALE_AGE_ADJUSTED_RATE_PER_100K: Male suicide deaths per 100,000, adjusted for age. Filled on only about 1 in 6 rows.
cols.FEMALE_SUICIDE_DEATHS: Female suicide deaths. Blank on about 4 in 10 rows.
cols.FEMALE_POPULATION_ESTIMATE: Estimated female population. Blank on about 4 in 10 rows.
cols.FEMALE_UNADJUSTED_RATE_PER_100K: Female suicide deaths per 100,000, not adjusted for age. Blank on about 4 in 10 rows.
cols.FEMALE_AGE_ADJUSTED_RATE_PER_100K: Female suicide deaths per 100,000, adjusted for age. Filled on only about 1 in 6 rows.

HEALTH__FED_VA_SUICIDE_NATIONAL.summary: National veteran suicide deaths and rates per 100,000 by year, group and age band, with male and female splits, from the VA's annual suicide prevention report.
HEALTH__FED_VA_SUICIDE_NATIONAL.row: One group in one year: suicide deaths, population and rates for one cohort and age band.

cols.YEAR_OF_DEATH: The year the deaths happened, like 2021.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.GEOGRAPHIC_REGION: The region the state belongs to: Southern, Western, Midwestern or Northeastern. All marks the national total.
cols.VETERAN_SUICIDES: How many veterans died by suicide. Blank on a few rows.
cols.VETERAN_POPULATION_ESTIMATE: Estimated number of veterans living in the state, rounded to the thousand.
cols.VETERAN_SUICIDE_RATE_PER_100K: Veteran suicides per 100,000 veterans. Blank on about one row in eleven.
cols.GENERAL_POPULATION_SUICIDES: Meant to be suicides in the general population. Empty on every row.
cols.GENERAL_POPULATION_RATE_PER_100K: Meant to be the general population suicide rate. Empty on every row.

HEALTH__FED_VA_SUICIDE_STATE.summary: Veteran suicide counts and rates by state and year, from the VA's annual suicide prevention report. The general-population comparison columns are empty here.
HEALTH__FED_VA_SUICIDE_STATE.row: One state-year: veteran suicides and the veteran population for one state, or the nation, in one year.

cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit National Provider Identifier, stored as text. Some tables leave it mostly blank or empty, and the SAM exclusions table uses 0000000000 as a filler.
cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.CREDENTIAL: The letters after the person's name, like MD, RN, or D.D.S., typed however the source typed them. Mostly blank in the exclusions table.
cols.TAXONOMY_CODE_1: The person's main medical specialty as a ten-character code, like 207R00000X. Needs a lookup. Mostly blank in the exclusions table.
cols.BPHC_ASSIGNED_NUMBER: The federal ID for one health center site, like BPS-H80-000156.
cols.SITE_NAME: The name of the place, whether a Superfund cleanup site, a mine, a stream gauge, or a health clinic. Many mine rows just say Unknown or Unnamed.
cols.HEALTH_CENTER_NAME: The name of the community health center organization.
cols.SITE_ADDRESS: The street address of the site, like the workplace OSHA inspected or the health center's clinic.
cols.SITE_STATE: The state where the site is, as two letters.
cols.NPI_DEACTIVATION_DATE: The date the provider's 10-digit national ID was shut off. Almost always blank.
cols.EXCLUSION_DATE: The date the provider was barred from federal health programs. One table writes it as 8 digits like 20260720, and it is almost always blank in the health-center staff table.
cols.EXCLUSION_TYPE: Why the person or company is barred. HHS tables use the law section as a code like 1128a1; the SAM tables use words like Voluntary Exclusion. It is almost always blank in the health-center people table.
cols.OPTOUT_EFFECTIVE_DATE: The date the doctor's opt-out from Medicare billing took effect. Nearly always blank in the health-center people table.
cols.OPTOUT_END_DATE: The date the doctor's Medicare opt-out runs out. Nearly always blank in the health-center people table.
cols.MATCH_NOTE: A note on how the row was matched to other data, like last name or ambiguous: 2 people share it. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.SITE_ZIP5: The health center site's five-digit ZIP code.
cols.PEOPLE_AT_SITE: How many providers matched to this site's address. Very large counts mean a big shared campus.
cols.NPPES_LAST_UPDATE_DATE: The date the provider last updated their entry in the national provider file. 2007-07-08 is very common, likely the file's first load date.
cols.IS_EXCLUDED: true when the provider is on the federal list of people barred from Medicare and Medicaid. 117 rows are true.
cols.LEIE_SPECIALTY: The provider's specialty as the exclusion list gives it, like FAMILY PRACTICE. Filled only for excluded providers.
cols.IS_OPTED_OUT: true when the provider has opted out of billing Medicare.
cols.IS_HIGH_DENSITY_CAMPUS: true when the site has so many matched providers that it is likely a big shared campus. About a third of rows are true.

HEALTH__FQHC_SITE_PEOPLE.summary: People in the national provider file whose listed practice address matches a community health center site, checked against the federal exclusion list and the Medicare opt-out list. This is an address match, not an official staff roster.
HEALTH__FQHC_SITE_PEOPLE.row: One person-site match: one provider whose practice street and ZIP match one health center site.

cols.EIN: The organization's 9-digit federal tax ID number, stored as text. Some rows hold 000000000 as a filler or only 8 digits because a leading zero was lost, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.HOSPITAL_NAME: The hospital's name. In the officer-pay table some rows are foundations or other groups, not hospitals.
cols.FILER_NAME: The name of whoever filed the form: an organization like a hospital in one table, a lobbyist written last name first in the other.
cols.NTEE_CODE: The nonprofit's category code, a letter plus two or three more characters like E22 for hospitals or X20 for Christian groups. Needs a lookup.
cols.TAX_YEAR: The tax year the filing covers. The 990 table writes year and month together, like 202506 for June 2025.
cols.PERSON_NAME: The name of the person tied to the record. Some tables mix in company names or court case names, some leave it mostly blank, and four leave it empty.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_URL: The web address the data was downloaded from. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.OBJECT_ID: The IRS's ID for the electronic tax return this person was listed on. Many people share one return.
cols.PERSON_SEQ: The person's place in the return's list: 1 for the first person listed, 2 for the second and so on.
cols.HOSPITAL_CITY: The hospital's city, in capitals, from the IRS master list of charities.
cols.HOSPITAL_STATE: The hospital's state, as two letters.
cols.TAX_PERIOD_END: The last day of the tax year the return covers, often December 31 or June 30.
cols.TITLE: The person's job title as written on the return, like DIRECTOR, TRUSTEE or PHYSICIAN. Spelling and capitals vary.
cols.IS_SCHEDULE_J_POINTER: A true or false flag tied to the return's Schedule J pay detail. True for about 1% of rows.
cols.IS_GROUP_RETURN: True if the return covers a group of related hospitals. Almost always false.
cols.AVG_HOURS_PER_WEEK: Average hours a week the person worked for the hospital. 1 is the most common value.
cols.AVG_HOURS_PER_WEEK_RELATED_ORG: Average hours a week the person worked for related organizations. 0 is the most common value; blank for about a fifth.
cols.IS_TRUSTEE_OR_DIRECTOR: True if the person sits on the board.
cols.IS_INSTITUTIONAL_TRUSTEE: True if the board member is an institution, like a bank, rather than a person. Very rare.
cols.IS_OFFICER: True if the person is an officer, like the chief executive or treasurer.
cols.IS_KEY_EMPLOYEE: True if the person is a key employee, a manager with real control.
cols.IS_HIGHEST_COMPENSATED: True if the person is one of the hospital's highest-paid employees.
cols.IS_FORMER: True if the person is a former officer, director or employee still being reported.
cols.REPORTABLE_COMP_FROM_ORG: Pay from the hospital itself, in dollars, as reported on the W-2 or 1099. 0 for most people listed.
cols.REPORTABLE_COMP_FROM_RELATED_ORGS: Pay from related organizations, in dollars. 0 for most people listed.
cols.OTHER_COMPENSATION: Other pay like retirement money and benefits, in dollars. 0 for more than half.
cols.TOTAL_COMPENSATION: All three kinds of pay added up, in dollars. Use this column to rank pay; about half the people listed get $0.
cols.BMF_ASSET_AMT: The hospital's total assets, in dollars, from the IRS master list of charities. The same for every person on one return.
cols.BMF_REVENUE_AMT: The hospital's total revenue, in dollars, from the IRS master list of charities. The same for every person on one return.
cols.SCHEMA_VERSION: The version of the IRS electronic form layout the return used, like 2022v5.0.
cols.SOURCE_ZIP: The IRS download file the return came from, like 2021_TEOS_XML_01A.zip. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

HEALTH__HOSPITAL_OFFICER_PAY.summary: The officers, directors, top employees and highest-paid staff that nonprofit hospitals list on their IRS Form 990 tax returns, with titles, hours and pay. Returns filed in 2016 through 2018 are missing because the IRS no longer posts them.
HEALTH__HOSPITAL_OFFICER_PAY.row: One person on one return: one person listed on one hospital's Form 990 for one tax year. Board members sit at $0 next to paid executives.

cols.BRAND_NAME: The name the drug or medical device is sold under, like DEXCOM G6. The Part D table often gives the generic name like Gabapentin, and the device ID table often gives a company name or NA or N/A instead.
cols.ACCESSION_NUMBER: The SEC's unique number for one filing, like 0001193125-24-036425. The Health Canada drug table reuses the name for its own short codes like P9864 and leaves it mostly blank.
cols.LAST_UPDATE_DATE: The date the record was last updated at the source.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.DRUG_CODE: Health Canada's internal number for the drug product. Nearly every row has its own.
cols.DRUG_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER: The eight-digit Drug Identification Number printed on the package, with leading zeros.
cols.PRODUCT_CATEGORIZATION: Category for low-risk products, like CAT IV - SUNBURN PROTECTANTS. Mostly blank.
cols.DESCRIPTOR: Extra wording on the product, like SINGLE USE VIAL. Mostly blank.
cols.PEDIATRIC_FLAG: Y if the product is for children; Y on only 9 rows.
cols.NUMBER_OF_AIS: How many active ingredients the product has.
cols.AI_GROUP_NO: A 10-digit number for the product's set of active ingredients. Products with the same ingredients share it.
cols.BRAND_NAME_F: The brand name in French. Mostly blank.
cols.DESCRIPTOR_F: The descriptor in French. Mostly blank.

HEALTH__INTL_HEALTHCANADA_DPD_DRUG.summary: Health Canada's Drug Product Database: drug products sold in Canada, with drug ID number, brand name, class and ingredient group; one record is missing because the loader read it as the header.

cols.CHAIN_ID: CMS's ID number for the nursing-home chain. Blank when the home is not in a chain.
cols.CHAIN_NAME: The nursing-home chain that owns or runs the home. Some chains are named after a person, like BENJAMIN LANDA.
cols.NUMBER_OF_FACILITIES_IN_CHAIN: How many nursing homes are in the chain.
cols.HOMES_IN_ROSTER: How many nursing homes the chain has on its roster.
cols.MATCHED_HOMES: How many of the chain's homes were found by name in the relief payment list. 0 for most chains.
cols.MATCHED_HOME_SHARE: Share of the chain's homes that matched by name, from 0 to 1.
cols.MATCHED_RELIEF_DOLLARS: Provider Relief Fund dollars matched to the chain's homes by name. A floor; 0 means no name match, not no money.
cols.RELIEF_PER_MATCHED_HOME: Matched relief dollars divided by matched homes. Blank when no home matched.
cols.EXACT_MATCH_DOLLARS: Relief dollars where the payee name matched a home's name exactly.
cols.PRF_STARTS_WITH_HOME_DOLLARS: Relief dollars where the payee name starts with a home's name.
cols.HOME_STARTS_WITH_PRF_DOLLARS: Relief dollars where a home's name starts with the payee name.
cols.PRF_CONTAINS_HOME_DOLLARS: Relief dollars where the payee name contains a home's name.
cols.HOSPITAL_BASED_HOMES: How many of the chain's homes sit inside a hospital.
cols.HOSPITAL_BASED_DOLLARS_EXCLUDED: Relief dollars left out because the matched home sits inside a hospital.
cols.PAYEE_SHORTER_HOMES: How many homes matched a payee name shorter than the home's own name.
cols.PAYEE_SHORTER_DOLLARS: Relief dollars from matches where the payee name was shorter than the home's name.
cols.CHAIN_AVG_OVERALL_RATING: The chain's average overall star rating, 1 to 5.
cols.CHAIN_AVG_HEALTH_INSPECTION_RATING: The chain's average inspection star rating, 1 to 5.
cols.CHAIN_AVG_STAFFING_RATING: The chain's average staffing star rating, 1 to 5.
cols.CHAIN_AVG_QM_RATING: The chain's average quality-of-care star rating, 1 to 5.
cols.TOTAL_FINES_COUNT: How many fines the chain's homes got.
cols.TOTAL_FINES_DOLLARS: Total dollars of fines on the chain's homes.
cols.FINES_PER_BED: Fine dollars per certified bed across the chain.
cols.TOTAL_CERTIFIED_BEDS: Total certified beds across the chain's homes.
cols.SPECIAL_FOCUS_HOMES: How many of the chain's homes are on Medicare's special focus list for poor care.
cols.ABUSE_ICON_HOMES: How many of the chain's homes carry the abuse warning icon.
cols.ONE_STAR_HOMES: How many of the chain's homes have a one-star overall rating.

HEALTH__NURSING_HOME_RELIEF_BY_CHAIN.summary: Covid Provider Relief Fund dollars matched by name to each nursing home chain, next to the chain's ratings, fines and warning flags; the dollars are a floor, and 0 means no name match, not no money.

cols.PROGRAM_YEAR: The year the drug or device company payments were made, like 2024.
cols.MEAL_CAP_KEY: A made-up key for the maker-year, a long scrambled string. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.PAYMENT_MAKER_NAME: The drug or device company that paid for the meals.
cols.PAYMENT_MAKER_ID: The company's Open Payments ID number.
cols.TOTAL_FB_PAYMENTS: How many food and drink payments the company made that year.
cols.TOTAL_FB_AMOUNT_USD: Total dollars the company spent on food and drink for doctors that year.
cols.AVG_FB_AMOUNT_USD: The average food and drink payment, in dollars.
cols.MEDIAN_FB_AMOUNT_USD: The middle food and drink payment, in dollars.
cols.N_MEAL_CAP: How many payments landed just under the $125 cap. 0 for about four in ten companies.
cols.N_EXACTLY_124_99: How many payments were exactly $124.99. 0 for most companies.
cols.N_JUST_ABOVE: How many payments landed just over the $125 cap.
cols.MEAL_CAP_SHARE: Share of the company's meal payments that landed just under the cap, as a fraction.
cols.CLIFF_RATIO: Payments just under the cap divided by payments just over it. Higher means more bunching under the line. Blank for about half the companies.
cols.EXACTLY_124_99_SHARE: Share of the company's meal payments that were exactly $124.99, as a fraction.
cols.IS_PRONOUNCED_FINGERPRINT: true when the company's bunching under the cap is strong enough to flag. 84 maker-years are true.

HEALTH__PHARMA_MEAL_CAP_FINGERPRINT.summary: Drug and device makers ranked by whether the meals they buy doctors bunch just under the $125 reporting cap, one maker per year, built from Open Payments.
HEALTH__PHARMA_MEAL_CAP_FINGERPRINT.row: One maker-year: one drug or device company's food and drink payments to doctors in one program year.

cols.SAM_NUMBER: The federal contracting system's own ID for an exclusion, a long random-looking code, one per row.
cols.UEI: The 12-character Unique Entity ID the federal government gives each business, which replaced DUNS. Often blank.
cols.EXCLUDING_AGENCY: The federal agency that barred the person or company, as a short abbreviation like HHS, DOJ, or EPA.
cols.EXCLUSION_TYPE: Why the person or company is barred. HHS tables use the law section as a code like 1128a1; the SAM tables use words like Voluntary Exclusion. It is almost always blank in the health-center people table.
cols.EXCLUSION_PROGRAM: What the ban covers: Procurement, NonProcurement, or Reciprocal.
cols.IS_ENTITY_NOT_INDIVIDUAL: True if the barred party is a business or group, False if it is a person.
cols.ENTITY_NAME: The name of the company, person or group the record is about. The two exclusion tables leave it mostly blank.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ACTIVATION_DATE: The date the ban took effect.
cols.TERMINATION_DATE_RAW: The date the ban ends, or the word Indefinite. Stored as text, so it will not sort as a date.
cols.IS_CURRENTLY_EXCLUDED: True if the ban is still in force, False if it has ended.

cols.PERSON_NAME: The name of the person tied to the record. Some tables mix in company names or court case names, some leave it mostly blank, and four leave it empty.
cols.STATE_FIPS: The state's number code, like 48 or 06, which needs a lookup. Several tables drop the leading zero so 6 means 06, some rows hold other codes like C1, TX, 00 or N/A, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.DOCUMENT_TYPE: What kind of document it is, like SEC insider Form 4 or a FARA Supplemental Statement; categories depend on the source. It is almost always blank in the slave narratives table and empty in one table.
cols.SUBJECTS: Subject tags for the item, several in one field split by | or ;.
cols.FULL_TEXT: Meant to hold the document's full text, but in the WPA table it holds photo catalog descriptions like 1 photographic print, and in the AustLII table it is empty.
cols.SOURCE_ID: A short name for the source feed the row came from, like fed_cfpb_complaints. In the ITIS other-sources table it is a plain number instead, which needs a lookup.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.LOC_ITEM_ID: The Library of Congress item number.
cols.INTERVIEW_DATE: The interview date, but always January 1 of 1937 or 1938, so only the year is real.
cols.INTERVIEW_YEAR: The year of the interview, 1937 or 1938.
cols.INTERVIEW_MONTH: Always 1, a stand-in rather than the real month.
cols.TITLE: The Library of Congress title, like Bill McRay, ex-slave, Beaumont.
cols.INTERVIEWER: Meant to hold the interviewer's name, but it is empty.
cols.FORMAT_LABEL: Always photo, print, drawing: these records are photographs, not interview texts.
cols.FULL_TEXT_CHAR_LENGTH: How many characters of text the row holds, only 49 to 57, so the full interview text is not here.
cols.DIGITAL_URL: The link to the item on the Library of Congress website.
cols.THUMBNAIL_URL: The link to a small preview image.

cols.ACTIVITY_YEAR: The year of the mortgage data, like 2022.
cols.LEI: The company's Legal Entity Identifier, a 20-character global ID. The FDIC table's values are only 16 characters, so they look cut short.
cols.DERIVED_MSA_MD: The metro area code for the property, 5 digits like 47894 for the Washington DC area. 99999 means not in a metro area.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state, as two letters like TX in some tables and as a number code like 48 or 06 in others, which needs a lookup and sometimes drops its leading zero. One table writes it like US_TX, and one leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY_CODE: The county's number code, written different ways: three digits like 001, sometimes without leading zeros like 3, five digits with the state like 11001, or state letters plus digits like FL095. One table uses name codes like US_SD_CLARK, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.CENSUS_TRACT: The census tract, a neighborhood-sized area. Mortgage tables give the full 11-digit code with state and county first; the HUD table gives only the 6-digit tract part.
cols.CONFORMING_LOAN_LIMIT: C if the loan is under the size limit for standard government-backed mortgages, NC if it is over.
cols.DERIVED_LOAN_PRODUCT_TYPE: The loan type and lien position together, like FHA:First Lien.
cols.DERIVED_DWELLING_CATEGORY: The kind of home, like Single Family 1-4 Units:Site-Built or Multifamily.
cols.DERIVED_ETHNICITY: The borrowers' ethnicity as summed up by the CFPB: Hispanic or Latino, Not Hispanic or Latino, Joint, Ethnicity Not Available, or rarely Free Form Text Only.
cols.DERIVED_RACE: The borrowers' race as summed up by the CFPB, like White, Asian, Joint or Race Not Available.
cols.DERIVED_SEX: The borrowers' sex as summed up by the CFPB: Male, Female, Joint or Sex Not Available.
cols.ACTION_TAKEN: What the lender did with the mortgage application, as a number code: 1 means the loan was made; others like denied or withdrawn need a lookup.
cols.PURCHASER_TYPE: Who bought the mortgage from the lender, as a number code. 0 means it was not sold; others like Fannie Mae need a lookup.
cols.PREAPPROVAL: Whether the borrower asked for preapproval: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.LOAN_TYPE: The kind of mortgage: 1 regular, 2 FHA, 3 VA, 4 USDA rural.
cols.LOAN_PURPOSE: What the mortgage was for. HMDA tables use number codes like 1 for buying a home that need a lookup; the HUD table says it in words like Purchase.
cols.LIEN_STATUS: Where the loan stands in line to be paid back if the home is sold: 1 first, 2 second. The historic table adds 3 and 4, which need a lookup.
cols.REVERSE_MORTGAGE: 1 if it is a reverse mortgage, 2 if not, 1111 if the lender is exempt from reporting it.
cols.OPEN_END_LINE_OF_CREDIT: 1 if it is an open-ended credit line like a home equity line, 2 if not, 1111 if the lender is exempt.
cols.BUSINESS_OR_COMMERCIAL_PURPOSE: 1 if the loan is mainly for business, 2 if not, 1111 if the lender is exempt.
cols.LOAN_AMOUNT: The loan amount in dollars, rounded to the middle of a $10,000 band, so 515000 covers 510,000 to 519,999.
cols.LOAN_TO_VALUE_RATIO: The loan as a percent of the property's value, like 80.0 or 95.0. About a third of rows are blank.
cols.INTEREST_RATE: The mortgage interest rate, as a percent like 6.125. Blank for loans not made, and stored as text in some tables.
cols.RATE_SPREAD: How many percentage points the loan's rate sits above the typical rate for a prime borrower. Can be negative, mostly blank, some rows say Exempt, and stored as text in some tables.
cols.HOEPA_STATUS: Whether it was a high-cost loan under federal rules: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.TOTAL_LOAN_COSTS: Total closing costs the borrower paid, in dollars. Often blank, and some rows say Exempt instead of a number.
cols.TOTAL_POINTS_AND_FEES: Total points and fees on the loan, in dollars. Almost always blank; some rows say Exempt instead of a number.
cols.ORIGINATION_CHARGES: The lender's fees for making the loan, in dollars. Often blank, and some rows say Exempt instead of a number.
cols.DISCOUNT_POINTS: Dollars the borrower paid up front to get a lower interest rate. Mostly blank, and some rows say Exempt instead of a number.
cols.LENDER_CREDITS: Dollars the lender paid toward the borrower's closing costs. Mostly blank; stored as text in some tables, where it can read Exempt.
cols.LOAN_TERM: How long the loan runs, in months, like 360 for 30 years. Stored as text; some rows say Exempt instead of a number.
cols.PREPAYMENT_PENALTY_TERM: How many months the loan charges a penalty for paying it off early, like 36. Mostly blank; can read Exempt in the text versions.
cols.INTRO_RATE_PERIOD: How many months the loan's starting teaser rate lasts before it can change, like 60 or 84. Blank for fixed-rate loans; can read Exempt.
cols.NEGATIVE_AMORTIZATION: Whether the loan balance can grow even when you pay: 1 yes, 2 no, 1111 exempt from reporting.
cols.INTEREST_ONLY_PAYMENT: Whether the loan lets you pay only interest for a while: 1 yes, 2 no, 1111 exempt from reporting.
cols.BALLOON_PAYMENT: Whether the loan ends with one big lump payment: 1 yes, 2 no, 1111 exempt from reporting.
cols.OTHER_NONAMORTIZING_FEATURES: Whether the loan has some other feature that keeps the balance from paying down normally: 1 yes, 2 no, 1111 exempt.
cols.PROPERTY_VALUE: The home's value in dollars, rounded to the middle of a 10,000 band, so values end in 5000. Stored as text in some tables.
cols.CONSTRUCTION_METHOD: How the home was built, as a code: 1 site-built, 2 manufactured home.
cols.OCCUPANCY_TYPE: How the borrower will use the home, as a code: 1 main home, 2 second home, 3 rental or investment.
cols.MANUFACTURED_HOME_SECURED_PROPERTY_TYPE: For manufactured homes, whether the loan covers the home and land or just the home, as a code. 3 means not a manufactured home; 1111 means exempt.
cols.MANUFACTURED_HOME_LAND_PROPERTY_INTEREST: For manufactured homes, whether the borrower owns or leases the land underneath, as a code. 5 means not a manufactured home; 1111 means exempt.
cols.TOTAL_UNITS: How many homes or apartments are in the property. The mortgage tables store it as text with ranges like 5-24.
cols.MULTIFAMILY_AFFORDABLE_UNITS: For apartment buildings, how many units are income-restricted affordable housing. Almost always blank; can read Exempt in the text versions.
cols.DEBT_TO_INCOME_RATIO: The borrower's monthly debt as a share of income. Mixes bands like 30%-<36% with exact numbers like 41, plus Exempt, so it is text, not a number.
cols.APPLICANT_CREDIT_SCORE_TYPE: Which credit scoring model the lender used for the borrower, as a number code like 1 or 3; 9 not applicable, 1111 exempt. Needs a lookup.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_CREDIT_SCORE_TYPE: Which credit scoring model the lender used for the co-borrower, as a number code; 10 means no co-borrower, 9 not applicable, 1111 exempt. Needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_1: The borrower's first listed ethnicity, as a number code like 1 Hispanic or 2 not Hispanic, with subgroups like 11 to 14. Needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_2: The borrower's second listed ethnicity, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_3: The borrower's third listed ethnicity, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_4: The borrower's fourth listed ethnicity, as a number code. Filled on just one row per table.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_5: The borrower's fifth listed ethnicity, as a number code. Filled on just one row per table.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_1: The co-borrower's first listed ethnicity, as a number code; 5 means no co-borrower. Needs a lookup.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_2: The co-borrower's second listed ethnicity, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_3: The co-borrower's third listed ethnicity, as a number code. Nearly always blank, and empty in the 2023 loan table.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_4: The co-borrower's fourth listed ethnicity, as a number code. Empty in every table.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_5: The co-borrower's fifth listed ethnicity, as a number code. Empty in every table.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's ethnicity by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the co-borrower's ethnicity by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 4 no co-borrower.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_1: The borrower's first listed race, as a number code like 5 for White or 3 for Black. Two-digit codes are subgroups; needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_2: The borrower's second listed race, as a number code like 5 for White. Blank for almost everyone.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_3: The borrower's third listed race, as a number code. Blank for almost everyone.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_4: The borrower's fourth listed race, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_5: The borrower's fifth listed race, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_1: The co-applicant's race as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup, like 5 for White or 3 for Black. 8 means there is no co-applicant.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_2: A second race the co-applicant picked, as a number code like 22 or 5. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_3: A third race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_4: A fourth race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_5: A fifth race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Nearly always blank, and empty in two of the four tables.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's race by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the co-borrower's race by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 4 no co-borrower.
cols.APPLICANT_SEX: The applicant's sex as a number code: 1 male, 2 female, 3 not provided, 4 not applicable. The newer file also uses 6 for picked both.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_SEX: The co-applicant's sex as a number code: 1 male, 2 female, 3 not provided, 4 not applicable, 5 no co-applicant. The newer files also use 6 for picked both.
cols.APPLICANT_SEX_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's sex by looks or name: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_SEX_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the co-borrower's sex by looks or name: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 4 no co-borrower.
cols.APPLICANT_AGE: The applicant's age as a range like 25-34, not an exact age. Bands differ by source, and 8888 means not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_AGE: The co-borrower's age band, like 25-34 or >74. 9999 means no co-borrower and 8888 means not applicable.
cols.APPLICANT_AGE_ABOVE_62: Whether the borrower is over 62, as Yes or No. Sometimes blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_AGE_ABOVE_62: Whether the co-borrower is over 62, as Yes or No. Mostly blank, since most loans have no co-borrower.
cols.SUBMISSION_OF_APPLICATION: Whether the borrower applied straight to this lender, as a code: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 1111 exempt.
cols.INITIALLY_PAYABLE_TO_INSTITUTION: Whether the loan was first owed to this lender, as a code: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 1111 exempt.
cols.AUS_1: The first automated underwriting system the lender ran the loan through, as a number code like 1 or 2; 6 not applicable, 1111 exempt. Needs a lookup.
cols.AUS_2: A second automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Mostly blank.
cols.AUS_3: A third automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.AUS_4: A fourth automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.AUS_5: A fifth automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_1: The main reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. 10 means not applicable and 1111 means the lender is exempt; the older file is blank unless denied.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_2: A second reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_3: A third reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. Almost always blank.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_4: A fourth reason the loan was turned down, as a number code like 4 or 9. Nearly always blank. Needs a lookup.
cols.TRACT_POPULATION: How many people live in the home's census tract, the neighborhood-sized area the Census counts. A few rows hold 0, likely meaning missing.
cols.TRACT_MINORITY_POPULATION_PERCENT: The share of the home's census tract that is minority, as a percent from 0 to 100. A few rows hold 0, likely meaning missing.
cols.FFIEC_MSA_MD_MEDIAN_FAMILY_INCOME: The median family income in dollars for the home's metro area, the same for every loan in that area. 0 shows up where there is no metro area.
cols.TRACT_TO_MSA_INCOME_PERCENTAGE: The census tract's median family income as a percent of its metro area's, so 100 is average and 50 is half. 0 means missing.
cols.TRACT_OWNER_OCCUPIED_UNITS: How many homes in the census tract are lived in by their owners. A few rows hold 0, likely meaning missing.
cols.TRACT_ONE_TO_FOUR_FAMILY_HOMES: How many houses in the census tract hold one to four families. Some rows hold 0, likely meaning missing.
cols.TRACT_MEDIAN_AGE_OF_HOUSING_UNITS: The typical age in years of homes in the census tract. 0 likely means missing.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.INCOME: The applicant's yearly income in thousands of dollars, so 110 means 110,000 dollars. Zero appears.

cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_1: The borrower's first listed ethnicity, as a number code like 1 Hispanic or 2 not Hispanic, with subgroups like 11 to 14. Needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_2: The borrower's second listed ethnicity, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_3: The borrower's third listed ethnicity, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_4: The borrower's fourth listed ethnicity, as a number code. Filled on just one row per table.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_5: The borrower's fifth listed ethnicity, as a number code. Filled on just one row per table.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_1: The co-borrower's first listed ethnicity, as a number code; 5 means no co-borrower. Needs a lookup.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_2: The co-borrower's second listed ethnicity, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_3: The co-borrower's third listed ethnicity, as a number code. Nearly always blank, and empty in the 2023 loan table.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_4: The co-borrower's fourth listed ethnicity, as a number code. Empty in every table.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_5: The co-borrower's fifth listed ethnicity, as a number code. Empty in every table.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's ethnicity by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the co-borrower's ethnicity by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 4 no co-borrower.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_1: The borrower's first listed race, as a number code like 5 for White or 3 for Black. Two-digit codes are subgroups; needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_2: The borrower's second listed race, as a number code like 5 for White. Blank for almost everyone.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_3: The borrower's third listed race, as a number code. Blank for almost everyone.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_4: The borrower's fourth listed race, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_5: The borrower's fifth listed race, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_1: The co-applicant's race as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup, like 5 for White or 3 for Black. 8 means there is no co-applicant.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_2: A second race the co-applicant picked, as a number code like 22 or 5. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_3: A third race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_4: A fourth race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_5: A fifth race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Nearly always blank, and empty in two of the four tables.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's race by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the co-borrower's race by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 4 no co-borrower.
cols.APPLICANT_SEX: The applicant's sex as a number code: 1 male, 2 female, 3 not provided, 4 not applicable. The newer file also uses 6 for picked both.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_SEX: The co-applicant's sex as a number code: 1 male, 2 female, 3 not provided, 4 not applicable, 5 no co-applicant. The newer files also use 6 for picked both.
cols.APPLICANT_SEX_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's sex by looks or name: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_SEX_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the co-borrower's sex by looks or name: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 4 no co-borrower.
cols.APPLICANT_AGE: The applicant's age as a range like 25-34, not an exact age. Bands differ by source, and 8888 means not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_AGE: The co-borrower's age band, like 25-34 or >74. 9999 means no co-borrower and 8888 means not applicable.
cols.APPLICANT_AGE_ABOVE_62: Whether the borrower is over 62, as Yes or No. Sometimes blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_AGE_ABOVE_62: Whether the co-borrower is over 62, as Yes or No. Mostly blank, since most loans have no co-borrower.
cols.SUBMISSION_OF_APPLICATION: Whether the borrower applied straight to this lender, as a code: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 1111 exempt.
cols.INITIALLY_PAYABLE_TO_INSTITUTION: Whether the loan was first owed to this lender, as a code: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 1111 exempt.
cols.AUS_1: The first automated underwriting system the lender ran the loan through, as a number code like 1 or 2; 6 not applicable, 1111 exempt. Needs a lookup.
cols.AUS_2: A second automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Mostly blank.
cols.AUS_3: A third automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.AUS_4: A fourth automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.AUS_5: A fifth automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_1: The main reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. 10 means not applicable and 1111 means the lender is exempt; the older file is blank unless denied.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_2: A second reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_3: A third reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. Almost always blank.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_4: A fourth reason the loan was turned down, as a number code like 4 or 9. Nearly always blank. Needs a lookup.
cols.TRACT_POPULATION: How many people live in the home's census tract, the neighborhood-sized area the Census counts. A few rows hold 0, likely meaning missing.
cols.TRACT_MINORITY_POPULATION_PERCENT: The share of the home's census tract that is minority, as a percent from 0 to 100. A few rows hold 0, likely meaning missing.
cols.FFIEC_MSA_MD_MEDIAN_FAMILY_INCOME: The median family income in dollars for the home's metro area, the same for every loan in that area. 0 shows up where there is no metro area.
cols.TRACT_TO_MSA_INCOME_PERCENTAGE: The census tract's median family income as a percent of its metro area's, so 100 is average and 50 is half. 0 means missing.
cols.TRACT_OWNER_OCCUPIED_UNITS: How many homes in the census tract are lived in by their owners. A few rows hold 0, likely meaning missing.
cols.TRACT_ONE_TO_FOUR_FAMILY_HOMES: How many houses in the census tract hold one to four families. Some rows hold 0, likely meaning missing.
cols.TRACT_MEDIAN_AGE_OF_HOUSING_UNITS: The typical age in years of homes in the census tract. 0 likely means missing.
cols.INCOME: The applicant's yearly income in thousands of dollars, like 110 for $110,000. 0 shows up often.

HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_DC_ONLY.summary: Mortgage applications reported under the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act, but only for Washington DC: the load pulled only DC by mistake, so this is not national data.
HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_DC_ONLY.row: One mortgage application or loan in Washington DC: the applicant, the loan and what the lender did with it.

cols.AGENCY_NAME: The government agency's name, like Department of Housing and Urban Development. Empty in the grants table.
cols.SEQUENCE_NUMBER: The loan's row number inside the lender's yearly mortgage report, as 7-digit text. The New York City donation tables have this column but leave it empty.
cols.LOAN_TYPE: The kind of mortgage: 1 regular, 2 FHA, 3 VA, 4 USDA rural.
cols.PROPERTY_TYPE: What kind of property the loan is on. HMDA historic uses codes 1, 2, 3 that need a lookup; the FHA table spells it out, like Single Family or Condo.
cols.LOAN_PURPOSE: What the mortgage was for. HMDA tables use number codes like 1 for buying a home that need a lookup; the HUD table says it in words like Purchase.
cols.PREAPPROVAL: Whether the borrower asked for preapproval: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.ACTION_TAKEN: What the lender did with the mortgage application, as a number code: 1 means the loan was made; others like denied or withdrawn need a lookup.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_ABBR: The state, as two letters like TX. Territories like PR and GU show up, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state, as two letters like TX in some tables and as a number code like 48 or 06 in others, which needs a lookup and sometimes drops its leading zero. One table writes it like US_TX, and one leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some tables add County, Parish or the state, like Garza County, TX, so clean it before matching. One table uses Undetermined as a filler, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.COUNTY_CODE: The county's number code, written different ways: three digits like 001, sometimes without leading zeros like 3, five digits with the state like 11001, or state letters plus digits like FL095. One table uses name codes like US_SD_CLARK, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_1: The borrower's first listed race, as a number code like 5 for White or 3 for Black. Two-digit codes are subgroups; needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_2: The borrower's second listed race, as a number code like 5 for White. Blank for almost everyone.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_3: The borrower's third listed race, as a number code. Blank for almost everyone.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_4: The borrower's fourth listed race, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_5: The borrower's fifth listed race, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_1: The co-applicant's race as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup, like 5 for White or 3 for Black. 8 means there is no co-applicant.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_2: A second race the co-applicant picked, as a number code like 22 or 5. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_3: A third race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_4: A fourth race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_5: A fifth race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Nearly always blank, and empty in two of the four tables.
cols.APPLICANT_SEX: The applicant's sex as a number code: 1 male, 2 female, 3 not provided, 4 not applicable. The newer file also uses 6 for picked both.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_SEX: The co-applicant's sex as a number code: 1 male, 2 female, 3 not provided, 4 not applicable, 5 no co-applicant. The newer files also use 6 for picked both.
cols.PURCHASER_TYPE: Who bought the mortgage from the lender, as a number code. 0 means it was not sold; others like Fannie Mae need a lookup.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_1: The main reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. 10 means not applicable and 1111 means the lender is exempt; the older file is blank unless denied.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_2: A second reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_3: A third reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. Almost always blank.
cols.RATE_SPREAD: How many percentage points the loan's rate sits above the typical rate for a prime borrower. Can be negative, mostly blank, some rows say Exempt, and stored as text in some tables.
cols.HOEPA_STATUS: Whether it was a high-cost loan under federal rules: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.LIEN_STATUS: Where the loan stands in line to be paid back if the home is sold: 1 first, 2 second. The historic table adds 3 and 4, which need a lookup.
cols.POPULATION: How many people live in the area or group the row covers, like a county or census tract; the CDC WONDER table holds national figures around 160 million.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.LAR_RECORD_ID: A long scrambled code with a number after a dash, like -1 or -11, naming one mortgage application record. One per row.
cols.AS_OF_YEAR: The year the lender reported the application: 2015, 2016 or 2017.
cols.SOURCE_YEAR: The year of the source file, same as the reporting year.
cols.RESPONDENT_ID: The lender's HMDA ID. Pair it with the agency code to name the lender.
cols.AGENCY_ABBR: The agency that oversees the lender, like HUD, CFPB or FDIC.
cols.AGENCY_CODE: The same agency as a number, like 7 for HUD or 9 for CFPB.
cols.LOAN_TYPE_NAME: The loan type: Conventional, FHA-insured, VA-guaranteed or FSA/RHS-guaranteed.
cols.PROPERTY_TYPE_NAME: The home type: a one-to-four family house, manufactured housing, or multifamily.
cols.LOAN_PURPOSE_NAME: What the loan was for: Home purchase, Refinancing or Home improvement.
cols.OWNER_OCCUPANCY_NAME: Whether the borrower will live in the home as their main home.
cols.OWNER_OCCUPANCY: The same answer as a code: 1 owner-occupied, 2 not, 3 not applicable.
cols.LOAN_AMOUNT_000S: The loan amount in thousands of dollars, so 200 means $200,000.
cols.PREAPPROVAL_NAME: Whether the borrower asked for preapproval. Mostly Not applicable.
cols.ACTION_TAKEN_NAME: What happened to the application, like Loan originated or Application denied. Filter on this before counting loans.
cols.MSAMD_NAME: The metro area name, like Atlanta, Sandy Springs, Roswell - GA. Blank for rural homes.
cols.MSAMD: The metro area as a five-digit code, like 12060. Blank for rural homes.
cols.CENSUS_TRACT_NUMBER: The census tract, like 9501.00. Only unique inside a state and county.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_NAME: The main applicant's ethnicity: Hispanic or Latino, Not Hispanic or Latino, not provided, or not applicable.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY: The same ethnicity as a code 1 to 4. The name column says what each means.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_NAME: The co-applicant's ethnicity, or No co-applicant, which is about half the rows.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY: The same co-applicant ethnicity as a code 1 to 5. The name column says what each means.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_NAME_1: The main applicant's first listed race, like White or Asian.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_NAME_2: The main applicant's race number 2, when they listed more than one. Blank on almost every row.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_NAME_3: The main applicant's race number 3, when they listed more than one. Blank on almost every row.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_NAME_4: The main applicant's race number 4, when they listed more than one. Blank on almost every row.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_NAME_5: The main applicant's race number 5, when they listed more than one. Blank on almost every row.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_NAME_1: The co-applicant's first listed race, or No co-applicant.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_NAME_2: The co-applicant's race number 2, when they listed more than one. Blank on almost every row.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_NAME_3: The co-applicant's race number 3, when they listed more than one. Blank on almost every row.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_NAME_4: The co-applicant's race number 4, when they listed more than one. Blank on almost every row.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_NAME_5: The co-applicant's race number 5, when they listed more than one. Blank on almost every row.
cols.APPLICANT_SEX_NAME: The main applicant's sex: Male, Female, not provided, or not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_SEX_NAME: The co-applicant's sex, or No co-applicant.
cols.APPLICANT_INCOME_000S: The applicant's yearly income in thousands of dollars, so 60 means $60,000. Blank on some rows.
cols.PURCHASER_TYPE_NAME: Who bought the loan after it was made, like Fannie Mae or Ginnie Mae, or not sold.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_NAME_1: The main reason the loan was denied, like Credit history. Blank unless denied.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_NAME_2: A second denial reason. Blank on almost every row.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_NAME_3: A third denial reason. Blank on almost every row.
cols.HOEPA_STATUS_NAME: Whether it is a high-cost HOEPA loan. Almost never.
cols.LIEN_STATUS_NAME: Whether the loan is a first lien, a second lien, or has no lien.
cols.EDIT_STATUS_NAME: Quality edit failure only on flagged rows; blank on most rows.
cols.EDIT_STATUS: 6 on rows flagged with a quality edit failure; blank on most rows.
cols.MINORITY_POPULATION: The percent of people in the census tract who are minorities.
cols.HUD_MEDIAN_FAMILY_INCOME: The metro area's median family income in dollars, from HUD.
cols.TRACT_TO_MSAMD_INCOME: The tract's median income as a percent of the metro area's, so 100 means equal.
cols.NUMBER_OF_OWNER_OCCUPIED_UNITS: How many owner-occupied homes are in the census tract.
cols.NUMBER_OF_1_TO_4_FAMILY_UNITS: How many one-to-four family homes are in the census tract.
cols.APPLICATION_DATE_INDICATOR: A code 0, 1 or 2 about when the application was taken. Needs a lookup; blank on about a third of rows.

HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_HISTORIC.summary: Every home loan application US lenders reported under HMDA for 2015, 2016 and 2017, whether the loan was made, denied, withdrawn or bought from another lender.
HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_HISTORIC.row: One home loan application: the lender, the borrower, the home, the loan, and what happened to it.

cols.LAR_RECORD_ID: A long scrambled code with a number after a dash, like -1 or -11, naming one mortgage application record. One per row.
cols.ACTIVITY_YEAR: The year of the mortgage data, like 2022.
cols.LEI: The company's Legal Entity Identifier, a 20-character global ID. The FDIC table's values are only 16 characters, so they look cut short.
cols.DERIVED_MSA_MD: The metro area code for the property, 5 digits like 47894 for the Washington DC area. 99999 means not in a metro area.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state, as two letters like TX in some tables and as a number code like 48 or 06 in others, which needs a lookup and sometimes drops its leading zero. One table writes it like US_TX, and one leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY_CODE: The county's number code, written different ways: three digits like 001, sometimes without leading zeros like 3, five digits with the state like 11001, or state letters plus digits like FL095. One table uses name codes like US_SD_CLARK, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.CENSUS_TRACT: The census tract, a neighborhood-sized area. Mortgage tables give the full 11-digit code with state and county first; the HUD table gives only the 6-digit tract part.
cols.CONFORMING_LOAN_LIMIT: C if the loan is under the size limit for standard government-backed mortgages, NC if it is over.
cols.DERIVED_LOAN_PRODUCT_TYPE: The loan type and lien position together, like FHA:First Lien.
cols.DERIVED_DWELLING_CATEGORY: The kind of home, like Single Family 1-4 Units:Site-Built or Multifamily.
cols.DERIVED_ETHNICITY: The borrowers' ethnicity as summed up by the CFPB: Hispanic or Latino, Not Hispanic or Latino, Joint, Ethnicity Not Available, or rarely Free Form Text Only.
cols.DERIVED_RACE: The borrowers' race as summed up by the CFPB, like White, Asian, Joint or Race Not Available.
cols.DERIVED_SEX: The borrowers' sex as summed up by the CFPB: Male, Female, Joint or Sex Not Available.
cols.ACTION_TAKEN: What the lender did with the mortgage application, as a number code: 1 means the loan was made; others like denied or withdrawn need a lookup.
cols.PURCHASER_TYPE: Who bought the mortgage from the lender, as a number code. 0 means it was not sold; others like Fannie Mae need a lookup.
cols.PREAPPROVAL: Whether the borrower asked for preapproval: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.LOAN_TYPE: The kind of mortgage: 1 regular, 2 FHA, 3 VA, 4 USDA rural.
cols.LOAN_PURPOSE: What the mortgage was for. HMDA tables use number codes like 1 for buying a home that need a lookup; the HUD table says it in words like Purchase.
cols.LIEN_STATUS: Where the loan stands in line to be paid back if the home is sold: 1 first, 2 second. The historic table adds 3 and 4, which need a lookup.
cols.REVERSE_MORTGAGE: 1 if it is a reverse mortgage, 2 if not, 1111 if the lender is exempt from reporting it.
cols.OPEN_END_LINE_OF_CREDIT: 1 if it is an open-ended credit line like a home equity line, 2 if not, 1111 if the lender is exempt.
cols.BUSINESS_OR_COMMERCIAL_PURPOSE: 1 if the loan is mainly for business, 2 if not, 1111 if the lender is exempt.
cols.LOAN_AMOUNT: The loan amount in dollars, rounded to the middle of a $10,000 band, so 515000 covers 510,000 to 519,999.
cols.LOAN_TO_VALUE_RATIO: The loan as a percent of the property's value, like 80.0 or 95.0. About a third of rows are blank.
cols.INTEREST_RATE: The mortgage interest rate, as a percent like 6.125. Blank for loans not made, and stored as text in some tables.
cols.RATE_SPREAD: How many percentage points the loan's rate sits above the typical rate for a prime borrower. Can be negative, mostly blank, some rows say Exempt, and stored as text in some tables.
cols.HOEPA_STATUS: Whether it was a high-cost loan under federal rules: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.TOTAL_LOAN_COSTS: Total closing costs the borrower paid, in dollars. Often blank, and some rows say Exempt instead of a number.
cols.TOTAL_POINTS_AND_FEES: Total points and fees on the loan, in dollars. Almost always blank; some rows say Exempt instead of a number.
cols.ORIGINATION_CHARGES: The lender's fees for making the loan, in dollars. Often blank, and some rows say Exempt instead of a number.
cols.DISCOUNT_POINTS: Dollars the borrower paid up front to get a lower interest rate. Mostly blank, and some rows say Exempt instead of a number.
cols.LENDER_CREDITS: Dollars the lender paid toward the borrower's closing costs. Mostly blank; stored as text in some tables, where it can read Exempt.
cols.PREPAYMENT_PENALTY_TERM: How many months the loan charges a penalty for paying it off early, like 36. Mostly blank; can read Exempt in the text versions.
cols.INTRO_RATE_PERIOD: How many months the loan's starting teaser rate lasts before it can change, like 60 or 84. Blank for fixed-rate loans; can read Exempt.
cols.NEGATIVE_AMORTIZATION: Whether the loan balance can grow even when you pay: 1 yes, 2 no, 1111 exempt from reporting.
cols.INTEREST_ONLY_PAYMENT: Whether the loan lets you pay only interest for a while: 1 yes, 2 no, 1111 exempt from reporting.
cols.BALLOON_PAYMENT: Whether the loan ends with one big lump payment: 1 yes, 2 no, 1111 exempt from reporting.
cols.OTHER_NONAMORTIZING_FEATURES: Whether the loan has some other feature that keeps the balance from paying down normally: 1 yes, 2 no, 1111 exempt.
cols.PROPERTY_VALUE: The home's value in dollars, rounded to the middle of a 10,000 band, so values end in 5000. Stored as text in some tables.
cols.CONSTRUCTION_METHOD: How the home was built, as a code: 1 site-built, 2 manufactured home.
cols.OCCUPANCY_TYPE: How the borrower will use the home, as a code: 1 main home, 2 second home, 3 rental or investment.
cols.MANUFACTURED_HOME_SECURED_PROPERTY_TYPE: For manufactured homes, whether the loan covers the home and land or just the home, as a code. 3 means not a manufactured home; 1111 means exempt.
cols.MANUFACTURED_HOME_LAND_PROPERTY_INTEREST: For manufactured homes, whether the borrower owns or leases the land underneath, as a code. 5 means not a manufactured home; 1111 means exempt.
cols.TOTAL_UNITS: How many homes or apartments are in the property. The mortgage tables store it as text with ranges like 5-24.
cols.MULTIFAMILY_AFFORDABLE_UNITS: For apartment buildings, how many units are income-restricted affordable housing. Almost always blank; can read Exempt in the text versions.
cols.DEBT_TO_INCOME_RATIO: The borrower's monthly debt as a share of income. Mixes bands like 30%-<36% with exact numbers like 41, plus Exempt, so it is text, not a number.
cols.APPLICANT_CREDIT_SCORE_TYPE: Which credit scoring model the lender used for the borrower, as a number code like 1 or 3; 9 not applicable, 1111 exempt. Needs a lookup.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_CREDIT_SCORE_TYPE: Which credit scoring model the lender used for the co-borrower, as a number code; 10 means no co-borrower, 9 not applicable, 1111 exempt. Needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_1: The borrower's first listed ethnicity, as a number code like 1 Hispanic or 2 not Hispanic, with subgroups like 11 to 14. Needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_2: The borrower's second listed ethnicity, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_3: The borrower's third listed ethnicity, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_4: The borrower's fourth listed ethnicity, as a number code. Filled on just one row per table.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_5: The borrower's fifth listed ethnicity, as a number code. Filled on just one row per table.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_1: The co-borrower's first listed ethnicity, as a number code; 5 means no co-borrower. Needs a lookup.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_2: The co-borrower's second listed ethnicity, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_3: The co-borrower's third listed ethnicity, as a number code. Nearly always blank, and empty in the 2023 loan table.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_4: The co-borrower's fourth listed ethnicity, as a number code. Empty in every table.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_5: The co-borrower's fifth listed ethnicity, as a number code. Empty in every table.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's ethnicity by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the co-borrower's ethnicity by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 4 no co-borrower.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_1: The borrower's first listed race, as a number code like 5 for White or 3 for Black. Two-digit codes are subgroups; needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_2: The borrower's second listed race, as a number code like 5 for White. Blank for almost everyone.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_3: The borrower's third listed race, as a number code. Blank for almost everyone.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_4: The borrower's fourth listed race, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_5: The borrower's fifth listed race, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_1: The co-applicant's race as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup, like 5 for White or 3 for Black. 8 means there is no co-applicant.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_2: A second race the co-applicant picked, as a number code like 22 or 5. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_3: A third race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_4: A fourth race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_5: A fifth race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Nearly always blank, and empty in two of the four tables.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's race by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the co-borrower's race by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 4 no co-borrower.
cols.APPLICANT_SEX: The applicant's sex as a number code: 1 male, 2 female, 3 not provided, 4 not applicable. The newer file also uses 6 for picked both.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_SEX: The co-applicant's sex as a number code: 1 male, 2 female, 3 not provided, 4 not applicable, 5 no co-applicant. The newer files also use 6 for picked both.
cols.APPLICANT_SEX_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's sex by looks or name: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_SEX_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the co-borrower's sex by looks or name: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 4 no co-borrower.

cols.CO_APPLICANT_AGE: The co-borrower's age band, like 25-34 or >74. 9999 means no co-borrower and 8888 means not applicable.

cols.CO_APPLICANT_AGE_ABOVE_62: Whether the co-borrower is over 62, as Yes or No. Mostly blank, since most loans have no co-borrower.
cols.SUBMISSION_OF_APPLICATION: Whether the borrower applied straight to this lender, as a code: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 1111 exempt.
cols.INITIALLY_PAYABLE_TO_INSTITUTION: Whether the loan was first owed to this lender, as a code: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 1111 exempt.
cols.AUS_1: The first automated underwriting system the lender ran the loan through, as a number code like 1 or 2; 6 not applicable, 1111 exempt. Needs a lookup.
cols.AUS_2: A second automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Mostly blank.
cols.AUS_3: A third automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.AUS_4: A fourth automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.AUS_5: A fifth automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_1: The main reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. 10 means not applicable and 1111 means the lender is exempt; the older file is blank unless denied.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_2: A second reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_3: A third reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. Almost always blank.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_4: A fourth reason the loan was turned down, as a number code like 4 or 9. Nearly always blank. Needs a lookup.
cols.TRACT_POPULATION: How many people live in the home's census tract, the neighborhood-sized area the Census counts. A few rows hold 0, likely meaning missing.
cols.TRACT_MINORITY_POPULATION_PERCENT: The share of the home's census tract that is minority, as a percent from 0 to 100. A few rows hold 0, likely meaning missing.
cols.FFIEC_MSA_MD_MEDIAN_FAMILY_INCOME: The median family income in dollars for the home's metro area, the same for every loan in that area. 0 shows up where there is no metro area.
cols.TRACT_TO_MSA_INCOME_PERCENTAGE: The census tract's median family income as a percent of its metro area's, so 100 is average and 50 is half. 0 means missing.
cols.TRACT_OWNER_OCCUPIED_UNITS: How many homes in the census tract are lived in by their owners. A few rows hold 0, likely meaning missing.
cols.TRACT_ONE_TO_FOUR_FAMILY_HOMES: How many houses in the census tract hold one to four families. Some rows hold 0, likely meaning missing.
cols.TRACT_MEDIAN_AGE_OF_HOUSING_UNITS: The typical age in years of homes in the census tract. 0 likely means missing.
