cols.REGISTRATION_ID: FEMA's number for one household's aid application. Nearly every row has its own.
cols.DISASTER_NUMBER: FEMA's number for the declared disaster, like 4337. Links to FEMA's list of declared disasters.
cols.APPLIED_DATE: The day the household applied for aid.
cols.DECLARATION_DATE: The day the disaster was declared.
cols.INCIDENT_TYPE_CODE: The kind of disaster, as a one-letter code like H, W, F or B; H covers about three in four rows. The codes need a lookup.
cols.REGISTRATION_METHOD: How the household applied, as one letter: I, C, M or D. The codes need a lookup.
cols.DAMAGED_STATE_ABBREVIATION: State of the damaged home, as two letters.
cols.DAMAGED_ZIP_CODE: ZIP code of the damaged home.
cols.CENSUS_GEOID: The damaged home's 12-digit census block group code; the first 11 digits are the census tract. About a quarter of rows are blank, and some say NO_INTERSECT.
cols.CENSUS_YEAR: Which census the geography code comes from: 2000, 2010 or 2020. Mostly blank, and some read 2020.0 or nan.
cols.CURRENT_LOCATION: Where the household is staying now, as a letter code like D, F, O or H. The codes need a lookup.
cols.HIGH_WATER_LOCATION: How far flood water reached in the home, as a code like 1, B or N. Mostly blank; the codes need a lookup.
cols.HOUSEHOLD_COMPOSITION: How many people live in the household. A number stored as text.
cols.OCCUPANTS_UNDER_TWO: How many people in the household are under 2.
cols.OCCUPANTS_2_TO_5: How many people in the household are 2 to 5.
cols.OCCUPANTS_6_TO_18: How many people in the household are 6 to 18.
cols.OCCUPANTS_19_TO_64: How many people in the household are 19 to 64.
cols.OCCUPANTS_65_AND_OVER: How many people in the household are 65 or older.
cols.GROSS_INCOME: Meant to be household income, but every filled value is 0 and most rows are blank. Tells you nothing.
cols.ACCESS_FUNCTIONAL_NEEDS: True if someone in the household has a disability or access need. Stored as True or False text.
cols.OWN_RENT: Whether the household owns or rents: O or R.
cols.PRIMARY_RESIDENCE: True if the damaged home is where the household lives full time.
cols.RESIDENCE_TYPE: The kind of home, as a short code like H, A, M or TH. The codes need a lookup.
cols.EMERGENCY_NEEDS: True if the household said it had urgent needs.
cols.FOOD_NEED: True if the household said it needed food. Blank on about half of rows.
cols.SHELTER_NEED: True if the household said it needed shelter. Mostly blank.
cols.UTILITIES_OUT: True if the home's power, water or other utilities were out.
cols.HOME_DAMAGE: True if the household reported damage to the home.
cols.AUTO_DAMAGE: True if the household reported damage to a car.
cols.DESTROYED: True if the home was destroyed. True on under 1% of rows.
cols.REPORTED_DAMAGE: True if the household reported any damage.
cols.FLOOD_DAMAGE: True if the home had flood damage.
cols.FLOOD_DAMAGE_AMOUNT: Dollars of flood damage found. 0 on most rows.
cols.FOUNDATION_DAMAGE: True if the home's foundation was damaged.
cols.FOUNDATION_DAMAGE_AMOUNT: Dollars of foundation damage found. 0 on most rows.
cols.ROOF_DAMAGE: True if the roof was damaged.
cols.ROOF_DAMAGE_AMOUNT: Dollars of roof damage found. 0 on most rows.
cols.WATER_LEVEL: How high water rose in the home; 0 on most rows. The unit is not stated in the data.
cols.RENTER_DAMAGE_LEVEL: Damage level for renters, as a four-digit code like 5530. Filled on about 3% of rows; the codes need a lookup.
cols.HABITABILITY_REPAIRS_REQUIRED: True if repairs are needed to make the home livable. Blank on about 60% of rows.
cols.INSUFFICIENT_DAMAGE: True if FEMA found too little damage to qualify for aid.
cols.SELF_ASSESSMENT_INFORMATION: A code from the household's own damage report, a number from 1 to 6. Mostly blank; the codes need a lookup.
cols.INSPN_ISSUED: True if FEMA sent an inspector.
cols.INSPN_RETURNED: True if the inspection came back done. Its counts match INSPN_ISSUED exactly.
cols.VERIFIED_OCCUPANCY: True if FEMA confirmed the household lived in the home.
cols.VERIFIED_OWNERSHIP: True if FEMA confirmed the household owns the home.
cols.PPFVL: Dollars of personal belongings loss FEMA verified. 0 on most rows.
cols.RPFVL: Dollars of loss to the home itself that FEMA verified. 0 on most rows.
cols.FLOOD_INSURANCE: True if the household has flood insurance.
cols.HOMEOWNERS_INSURANCE: True if the household has homeowners insurance.
cols.INELIGIBLE_INSURANCE: True if the household was turned down because insurance covers the loss.
cols.INELIGIBLE_REASON: Why the household was turned down, as a number code from 1 to 9. Mostly blank; the codes need a lookup.
cols.IHP_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for FEMA's main aid program for individuals and households.
cols.IHP_AMOUNT: Total dollars granted under FEMA's main household aid program. 0 when not eligible.
cols.IHP_MAX: Meant for the household aid cap. Empty in this table.
cols.IHP_REFERRAL: True if the household was referred to FEMA's main household aid program.
cols.HA_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for housing aid.
cols.HA_AMOUNT: Dollars of housing aid granted. 0 when not eligible.
cols.HA_MAX: Meant for the housing aid cap. Empty in this table.
cols.HA_REFERRAL: True if the household was referred for housing aid.
cols.HA_STATUS: The housing-aid decision, as a short code plus words, like 'INS - Insured' or 'ER - Eligible - Rental Assistance'. Blank on about a quarter of rows.
cols.FIP_AMOUNT: A fixed payment in dollars; 0 on most rows, otherwise mostly 600 or 2,400.
cols.REPAIR_ASSISTANCE_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for home repair money.
cols.REPAIR_AMOUNT: Dollars granted for home repairs. 0 on most rows.
cols.REPLACEMENT_ASSISTANCE_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for money to replace a destroyed home. Rare.
cols.REPLACEMENT_AMOUNT: Dollars granted to replace the home. 0 on almost every row.
cols.RENTAL_ASSISTANCE_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for rent money.
cols.RENTAL_ASSISTANCE_AMOUNT: Dollars of rent aid granted. 0 on most rows.
cols.RENTAL_ASSISTANCE_END_DATE: The day rent aid ended. Filled on under 1% of rows.
cols.RENTAL_RESOURCE_CITY: City of the rental the household moved to. Filled on under 1% of rows.
cols.RENTAL_RESOURCE_STATE_ABBREV: State of the rental the household moved to, as two letters. Filled on under 1% of rows.
cols.RENTAL_RESOURCE_ZIP_CODE: ZIP code of the rental the household moved to. Filled on under 1% of rows.
cols.ONA_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for other-needs aid, which covers costs like belongings, funerals and medical bills.
cols.ONA_AMOUNT: Total dollars of other-needs aid granted. 0 when not eligible.
cols.ONA_MAX: Meant for the other-needs aid cap. Empty in this table.
cols.ONA_REFERRAL: True if the household was referred for other-needs aid.
cols.ONA_DENTAL_ASSIST_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for dental aid. Rare.
cols.ONA_DENTAL_ASSIST_AMOUNT: Dollars of dental aid granted. 0 on almost every row.
cols.ONA_FUNERAL_ASSIST_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for funeral aid.
cols.ONA_FUNERAL_ASSIST_AMOUNT: Dollars of funeral aid granted, often 9,000. 0 on most rows.
cols.ONA_MEDICAL_ASSIST_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for medical aid. Rare.
cols.ONA_MEDICAL_ASSIST_AMOUNT: Dollars of medical aid granted. 0 on almost every row.
cols.ONA_MOVING_ASSIST_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for moving and storage aid. Rare.
cols.ONA_MOVING_ASSIST_AMOUNT: Dollars of moving aid granted. 0 on almost every row.
cols.ONA_OTHER_ASSIST_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for other kinds of other-needs aid.
cols.ONA_OTHER_ASSIST_AMOUNT: Dollars of other kinds of other-needs aid granted. 0 on most rows.
cols.PERSONAL_PROPERTY_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for money to replace belongings.
cols.PERSONAL_PROPERTY_AMOUNT: Dollars granted to replace belongings. 0 on most rows.
cols.UNMET_NEED_PP: Dollars of belongings loss left uncovered after aid. 0 on most rows.
cols.UNMET_NEED_RP: Dollars of home damage left uncovered after aid. 0 on most rows.
cols.TRANSIENT_ACCOMMOD_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for money for a short hotel stay. Rare.
cols.TRANSIENT_ACCOMMOD_AMOUNT: Dollars granted for short hotel stays. 0 on almost every row.
cols.TSA_ELIGIBLE: True if the household qualified for FEMA-paid hotel rooms under transitional sheltering.
cols.TSA_CHECKED_IN: True if the household actually checked into a FEMA-paid hotel.
cols.SBA_APPROVED: True if the Small Business Administration approved a disaster loan for the household.
cols.LAST_REFRESH: When FEMA last updated the record, stored as text. 3,080,000 rows share one time in August 2026.

cols.NAME: The name of whatever the row is about: a person, company, bank, county, address or dataset, depending on the table. Spelling is not cleaned, fillers like UNNAMED or None show up, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.TOTAL_UNITS: How many homes or apartments are in the property. The mortgage tables store it as text with ranges like 5-24.
cols.TOTAL_OCCUPIED: How many subsidized units are occupied. Negative values like -4 are codes for missing or hidden data, not counts.
cols.PCT_OCCUPIED: Percent of subsidized units that are occupied. Negative values like -4 are codes for missing or hidden data, not percents.
cols.NUMBER_REPORTED: How many units sent in tenant reports to HUD. Negative values like -4 are codes for missing or hidden data, not counts.
cols.PCT_REPORTED: Percent of units that sent in tenant reports to HUD. Negative values like -4 are codes for missing or hidden data, not percents.
cols.SPENDING_PER_MONTH: Average HUD dollars spent per unit per month. Negative values like -4 and -5 are codes for missing or hidden data, not dollars.
cols.PCT_MINORITY: The percent of people nearby, or living in the housing project, who are minorities, like 33.7. The HUD table stores it as text and has bad values like -4.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.

cols.STD_CITY: The city of the address, cleaned up to a standard spelling.
cols.STD_ZIP5: The five-digit zip code of the address, stored as text so leading zeros stay.

cols.GSL: Always the word Projects: the level of detail for every row.
cols.ENTITIES: A label for the project that joins state, HUD code and project name, like XX Missing 800009346 05244019 WINDS. XX Missing means the state was not filled in.
cols.SUMLEVEL: Always 6: a HUD code for the project level of detail.
cols.PROGRAM_LABEL: The HUD program, like Project Based Section 8, Public Housing or 202/PRAC.
cols.PROGRAM: A number code for the HUD program; its matching name is in PROGRAM_LABEL.
cols.SUB_PROGRAM: The narrower HUD program, like NC/SR, LMSA or PH, non-MTW. These codes need a lookup.
cols.CODE: The project's HUD ID number or numbers, like 800009346 05244019.
cols.MONTHS_SINCE_REPORT: Months since the project last reported tenant data. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_MOVEIN: Percent of households that moved in during the past year, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PEOPLE_PER_UNIT: Average people per occupied unit. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PEOPLE_TOTAL: Total people living in the project. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.RENT_PER_MONTH: Average monthly rent the household pays, in dollars. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.

cols.PCT_5K_LT10K: Percent of households earning $5,000 to $10,000 a year, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_10K_LT15K: Percent of households earning $10,000 to $15,000 a year, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.

cols.PCT_20K_LT25K: Percent of households earning $20,000 to $25,000 a year, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.

cols.PCT_FEMALE_HEAD_CHILD: Percent of households headed by a woman with children, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_FEMALE_HEAD_CHILD0_5: Percent of households headed by a woman with children under 6, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.

cols.PCT_DISABLED_ALL: Percent of all people in the project who have a disability, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_LT62_HEAD: Percent of household heads under 62, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_LT24_HEAD: Percent of household heads 24 or younger, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_AGE25_50: Percent of household heads aged 25 to 50, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.

cols.PCT_BLACK_NONHSP: Percent of household heads who are Black and not Hispanic, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_NATIVE_AMERICAN_NONHSP: Percent of household heads who are Native American and not Hispanic, stored as text. It reads -1, a HUD code for suppressed or missing data, on about six in ten projects; -4 is another such code. Negative values are not real numbers.
cols.PCT_ASIAN_PACIFIC_NONHSP: Percent of household heads who are Asian or Pacific Islander and not Hispanic, stored as text. It reads -1, a HUD code for suppressed or missing data, on over half of projects; -4 is another such code. Negative values are not real numbers.
cols.PCT_WHITE_NOTHSP: Percent of household heads who are white and not Hispanic, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_BLACK_HSP: Percent of household heads who are Black and Hispanic, stored as text. It reads -1, a HUD code for suppressed or missing data, on about six in ten projects; -4 is another such code. Negative values are not real numbers.
cols.PCT_WHT_HSP: Percent of household heads who are white and Hispanic, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_OTH_HSP: Percent of household heads who are Hispanic of another race, stored as text. It reads -1, a HUD code for suppressed or missing data, on just over half of projects; -4 is another such code. Negative values are not real numbers.
cols.PCT_HISPANIC: Percent of household heads who are Hispanic, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_MULTI: Percent of household heads of more than one race, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.MONTHS_WAITING: Average months new tenants spent on the waiting list. It reads -1, a HUD code for suppressed or missing data, on about six in ten projects; -4 is another such code. Negative values are not real numbers.
cols.MONTHS_FROM_MOVEIN: Average months tenants have lived there since moving in. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_UTILITY_ALLOW: Percent of households that get a utility allowance, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.AVE_UTIL_ALLOW: Average monthly utility allowance in dollars, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_BED1: Percent of units with 0 or 1 bedroom, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_BED2: Percent of units with 2 bedrooms, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_BED3: Percent of units with 3 or more bedrooms, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.PCT_OVERHOUSED: Percent of households living in units bigger than they need, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.TPOVERTY: Percent of people in poverty in the project's census tract, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.TMINORITY: Percent of minority residents in the project's census tract, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.TPCT_OWNSFD: Percent of homes in the project's census tract that are owner-occupied single-family houses, stored as text. Negative values like -1 and -4 are HUD codes for suppressed or missing data, not real numbers.
cols.FEDHSE: The federal House district. Empty in this table.
cols.CBSA: The metro area code, five digits. 99999 is a placeholder for projects outside any metro area.
cols.PLACE: The Census code for the city or town, five digits. 99999 is a placeholder for no place.
cols.HA_SIZE: A size group code for the local housing authority, 1 to 9, that needs a lookup. Only filled for public housing projects.
cols.STD_ADDR: The project's street address, cleaned up.
cols.STCTYTRT: The project's census tract as an 11-digit code: state, county and tract.

HOUSING__FED_HUD_ASSISTED_HOUSING_PROJEC.summary: HUD's Picture of Subsidized Households at the project level: 35,601 public housing and subsidized apartment projects with unit counts, rents, incomes and who lives there. Negative numbers are HUD's codes for suppressed or not-available values, not real data.
HOUSING__FED_HUD_ASSISTED_HOUSING_PROJEC.row: One housing project: one subsidized property in one HUD program, with a profile of its tenants.

cols.DATASET_NAME: The name of the dataset. One table stores it web-encoded, like DataSet%201 for DataSet 1, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 06037. One table holds two-digit state codes instead, and nine tables leave it empty.
cols.ZIP: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Fillers like 00000, UNKNO or a lone dash show up, some codes lost a leading zero like 8721, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.EIN: The organization's 9-digit federal tax ID number, stored as text. Some rows hold 000000000 as a filler or only 8 digits because a leading zero was lost, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.DATASET_URL: The web link to the HUD dataset or page.
cols.DESCRIPTION: A short description of the dataset. Blank on most rows.
cols.VALUE: Holds another web link, not a number. Blank on most rows.

HOUSING__FED_HUD_DATA.summary: A list of 71 datasets and pages found on HUD's research website, with links and short descriptions. It holds no housing numbers itself.
HOUSING__FED_HUD_DATA.row: One dataset link: one HUD data page or file.

cols.LOAN_PURPOSE: What the mortgage was for. HMDA tables use number codes like 1 for buying a home that need a lookup; the HUD table says it in words like Purchase.
cols.PROPERTY_TYPE: What kind of property the loan is on. HMDA historic uses codes 1, 2, 3 that need a lookup; the FHA table spells it out, like Single Family or Condo.
cols.INTEREST_RATE: The mortgage interest rate, as a percent like 6.125. Blank for loans not made, and stored as text in some tables.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.LOAN_RECORD_ID: A made-up ID for one loan. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.ORIGINATING_MORTGAGEE_NUMBER: HUD's number for the lender that made the loan. Not Available fills about a quarter of rows.
cols.SPONSOR_NUMBER: HUD's number for the sponsoring lender. Not Available fills most rows.
cols.NON_PROFIT_NUMBER: The ID of a nonprofit involved in the loan. Not Avail fills almost every row.
cols.PROPERTY_STATE: The home's state, as two letters.
cols.PROPERTY_COUNTY: The home's county name, in capitals.
cols.ORIGINATING_MORTGAGEE_NAME: The lender that made the loan, like ROCKET MORTGAGE, LLC.
cols.SPONSOR_NAME: The sponsoring lender, like UNITED WHOLESALE MORTGAGE, LLC. Not Available fills most rows.
cols.DOWN_PAYMENT_SOURCE: Where the down payment came from: Borrower, Relative, Gov Asst, Employer or Non Profit.
cols.ENDORSEMENT_YEAR: The year FHA insured the loan. Always 2026 in this table.
cols.ENDORSEMENT_MONTH: The month FHA insured the loan. Always 6 in this table.

HOUSING__FED_HUD_FHA_SF_PORTFOLIO_SNAPSH.summary: Home loans FHA insured in June 2026, with lender, home location, rate and loan amount.
HOUSING__FED_HUD_FHA_SF_PORTFOLIO_SNAPSH.row: One FHA-insured home loan: the lender, the home's location, the loan type and amount.

cols.PROJECT_NAME: The name of the housing project, usually an apartment complex like Anamosa Villa I.
cols.PROJECT_STATE: The state where the loan's project or business is, as two letters.
cols.FACILITY_TYPE: What kind of facility it is, like Hospital, Nursing home, Health Center, or Apartment in the HUD housing table. One table leaves it empty.
cols.PROGRAM_TYPE: Which HUD loan program the apartment deal ran under, like Basic FHA or Risk Sharing. Empty in the PBGC table.
cols.LENDER_NAME: The name of the bank or company that made the loan. Almost always blank in the SBA loans table.
cols.TOTAL_UNITS: How many homes or apartments are in the property. The mortgage tables store it as text with ranges like 5-24.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.COMMITMENT_RECORD_ID: A made-up ID for the row. Each row has its own. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.FHA_NUMBER: HUD's number for the project's insured loan, like 27311024. Nearly every row has its own.
cols.PROGRAM_CATEGORY: The loan program in short form, like 223, f, Refi/Purchase Apts or FHA NC/SR Apts for new construction or major rehab.
cols.PROGRAM_SUBCATEGORY: The exact loan program section, like 221, d, 4, NC/SR or 223, a, 7, Refi of 223, f, Apts.
cols.ACTIVITY_DESCRIPTION: What the loan pays for, like Refinance, New Construction, Substantial Rehabilitation or Purchase.
cols.ACTIVITY_GROUP: The same in broad groups: refinance or purchase, new construction or rehab, improvements, or operating loss.
cols.FIRM_ACTIVITY: Whether the commitment was issued for the first time or reissued.
cols.MORTGAGE_AMOUNT: The size of the insured mortgage, in dollars.
cols.FIRM_ACTIVITY_DATE: The date the commitment was issued or reissued.
cols.FISCAL_YEAR_AT_FIRM_ACTIVITY: The federal fiscal year of that date, like 2013.
cols.MAP_OR_TAP: How the deal was processed: MAP or TAP. The codes need a lookup.
cols.LIHTC: Y if the project also uses low-income housing tax credits. Blank otherwise.
cols.TAX_EXEMPT_BONDS: Y if the project also uses tax-exempt bonds. Blank otherwise.
cols.HOME: Y if the project also uses HOME program money. Blank otherwise.
cols.CDBG: Y if the project also uses Community Development Block Grant money. Blank otherwise.
cols.REFI_202: Y if the loan refinances a Section 202 senior housing project. Blank otherwise.
cols.IRP_DECOUPLING: Y if the deal involves IRP decoupling. Blank otherwise; the term needs a lookup.
cols.HOPE_VI: Y if the project uses HOPE VI public housing money. Empty.
cols.CURRENT_STATUS: Where the loan stands now, like Finally Endorsed, Firm Commitment Withdrawn or Expired.

HOUSING__FED_HUD_MF_FIRM_COMMITMENTS.summary: Every federal loan-insurance promise HUD made for apartment building mortgages, fiscal 2001 through mid 2026, with the project, lender, loan size, units and subsidies.
HOUSING__FED_HUD_MF_FIRM_COMMITMENTS.row: One commitment: HUD's promise to insure one apartment project's mortgage, issued or reissued on one date.

cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CONTRACT_RECORD_ID: A made-up ID for each row, built from a hash, used because a contract number can show up twice. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CONTRACT_NUMBER: HUD's contract number, like CA39T861025. Almost every row has its own.
cols.PROPERTY_ID: HUD's nine-digit ID for the apartment property.
cols.TRACS_EFFECTIVE_DATE: Date the current contract terms took effect.
cols.TRACS_OVERALL_EXPIRATION_DATE: Date the contract finally runs out, counting all its terms.
cols.TRACS_OVERALL_EXP_FISCAL_YEAR: The federal fiscal year the contract finally runs out.
cols.TRACS_OVERALL_EXPIRE_QUARTER: The quarter of that fiscal year the contract runs out, Q1 to Q4.
cols.TRACS_CURRENT_EXPIRATION_DATE: Date the current contract term runs out, before any renewal.
cols.TRACS_STATUS_NAME: Contract status: almost all Active, with a few Expired, Pending, Suspended, Executed or Terminated.
cols.CONTRACT_TERM_MONTHS_QTY: Length of the contract in months. 240 months, 20 years, is the most common.
cols.IS_HUD_ADMINISTERED_IND: Whether HUD runs the contract itself, Y or N.
cols.IS_ACC_OLD_IND: A Y or N flag for an older ACC contract type. Almost all are N.
cols.IS_ACC_PERFORMANCE_BASED_IND: A Y or N flag for a performance-based ACC contract. Most are Y.
cols.CONTRACT_DOC_TYPE_CODE: The contract paperwork type: HAP, PRAC, RAC, PAC or COOP. The letters need a lookup.
cols.PROGRAM_TYPE_NAME: The specific HUD program, like Sec 8 NC, 202/8 NC or PRAC/811.
cols.PROGRAM_TYPE_GROUP_CODE: Short code for the program family, like PRAC, 202 or S8NC.
cols.PROGRAM_TYPE_GROUP_NAME: Name of the program family, like PRAC 202/811 or S8 Loan Mgmt.
cols.ASSISTED_UNITS_COUNT: How many apartments the contract pays rent help on.
cols.RENT_TO_FMR_RATIO: Contract rent as a percent of the local fair market rent. 0 means unknown.
cols.RENT_TO_FMR_DESCRIPTION: That rent ratio in bands, like Below 80% FMR or Over 160% FMR; Unknown when the ratio is 0.
cols.UNITS_0BR_COUNT: Assisted studio apartments, with no separate bedroom.
cols.UNITS_5PLUSBR_COUNT: Assisted apartments with five or more bedrooms. Almost all 0.
cols.FMR_0BR: The local fair market rent for a studio, in dollars a month. 0 when the contract has no studios.
cols.FMR_1BR: The local fair market rent for a one-bedroom apartment, in dollars a month. 0 when the contract has no such units.
cols.FMR_2BR: The local fair market rent for a two-bedroom apartment, in dollars a month. 0 when the contract has no such units.
cols.FMR_3BR: The local fair market rent for a three-bedroom apartment, in dollars a month. 0 when the contract has no such units.
cols.FMR_4BR: The local fair market rent for a four-bedroom apartment, in dollars a month. 0 when the contract has no such units.

HOUSING__FED_HUD_MF_SECTION8_CONTRACTS.summary: HUD rental-help contracts on privately owned apartment buildings: dates, status, program, assisted units by bedroom size, and how contract rents compare to local fair market rent.
HOUSING__FED_HUD_MF_SECTION8_CONTRACTS.row: One Section 8 contract: one rental-help deal on one property, with its dates, program and assisted units.

cols.OBJECTID: A row number from the map file the data came from. Not a real ID; do not join on it.
cols.TOTAL_UNITS: How many homes or apartments are in the property. The mortgage tables store it as text with ranges like 5-24.
cols.TOTAL_OCCUPIED: How many subsidized units are occupied. Negative values like -4 are codes for missing or hidden data, not counts.
cols.PCT_OCCUPIED: Percent of subsidized units that are occupied. Negative values like -4 are codes for missing or hidden data, not percents.
cols.PHA_TOTAL_UNITS: Total housing units run by the local public housing authority. Stored as text and often blank in the projects table.
cols.NUMBER_REPORTED: How many units sent in tenant reports to HUD. Negative values like -4 are codes for missing or hidden data, not counts.
cols.PCT_REPORTED: Percent of units that sent in tenant reports to HUD. Negative values like -4 are codes for missing or hidden data, not percents.
cols.SPENDING_PER_MONTH: Average HUD dollars spent per unit per month. Negative values like -4 and -5 are codes for missing or hidden data, not dollars.
cols.STATE_FIPS: The state's number code, like 48 or 06, which needs a lookup. Several tables drop the leading zero so 6 means 06, some rows hold other codes like C1, TX, 00 or N/A, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some tables add County, Parish or the state, like Garza County, TX, so clean it before matching. One table uses Undetermined as a filler, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.COUNTY_FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 01001, stored as text. One table holds only the three-digit county part like 017, one holds N/A, and two leave it empty.
cols.CENSUS_TRACT: The census tract, a neighborhood-sized area. Mortgage tables give the full 11-digit code with state and county first; the HUD table gives only the 6-digit tract part.
cols.PLACE_NAME: The name of the place the row covers, like a state, the whole United States, or a town like Buffalo city.
cols.CBSA_NAME: The name of the metro area, like Birmingham-Hoover, AL. Some tables add Metropolitan Statistical Area to the end.
cols.STD_CITY: The city of the address, cleaned up to a standard spelling.
cols.STD_ZIP5: The five-digit zip code of the address, stored as text so leading zeros stay.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.PARTICIPANT_CODE: HUD's code for the housing authority, two state letters plus a number, like WY015. Each authority has its own.
cols.FORMAL_PARTICIPANT_NAME: The housing authority's official name, like Evanston Housing Authority.
cols.HA_PHONE_NUMBER: The housing authority's main phone number, as ten digits.
cols.HA_FAX_NUMBER: The housing authority's fax number, as ten digits.
cols.HA_EMAIL_ADDRESS: The housing authority's main email address. Some management companies share one address across several authorities.
cols.EXEC_DIR_PHONE: The executive director's phone number, as ten digits.
cols.EXEC_DIR_FAX: The executive director's fax number. Blank for about a third of authorities.
cols.PHAS_DESIGNATION: HUD's grade for how well the authority runs its public housing: High Performer, Standard Performer, Troubled Performer and so on. Blank for about one in five.
cols.HA_LOW_RENT_SIZE_CATEGORY: Size band for the authority's public housing, from VERY SMALL, under 50 units, to EXTRA LARGE, 5,000 or more. Blank when it runs no public housing.
cols.HA_SECTION_8_SIZE_CATEGORY: Size band for the authority's Section 8 voucher program, from VERY SMALL, under 50 units, to EXTRA LARGE, 5,000 or more.
cols.HA_COMBINED_SIZE_CATEGORY: Size band for public housing and Section 8 together, from VERY SMALL, under 50 units, to EXTRA LARGE, 5,000 or more.
cols.HA_FISCAL_YEAR_END: The month and day the authority's budget year ends: 6/30, 12/31, 9/30 or 3/31.
cols.HA_PROGRAM_TYPE: Which programs the authority runs: Low-Rent public housing, Section 8 vouchers, or Combined for both.
cols.SECTION8_UNITS_COUNT: How many Section 8 voucher units the authority runs. Zero for authorities that only do public housing.
cols.TOTAL_DWELLING_UNITS: How many public housing apartments the authority owns. Zero for voucher-only authorities.
cols.ACC_UNITS: How many public housing units HUD has agreed to fund for the authority.
cols.PUBLIC_HOUSING_OCCUPIED: How many of the authority's public housing units have tenants.
cols.SECTION8_OCCUPIED: How many of the authority's Section 8 vouchers are in use.
cols.REGULAR_VACANT: How many public housing units sit empty.
cols.OPERATING_FUND_AMOUNT: Dollars HUD gave the authority this year to run its public housing.
cols.OPERATING_FUND_AMOUNT_PREV_YR: Dollars HUD gave the authority last year to run its public housing.
cols.CAPITAL_FUND_AMOUNT: Dollars HUD gave the authority this year for repairs and building upgrades.
cols.CAPITAL_FUND_AMOUNT_PREV_YR: Dollars HUD gave the authority last year for repairs and building upgrades. Zero for about half.
cols.ROSS_AMOUNT: Meant to hold resident self-sufficiency grant dollars. Zero on every row, so it tells you nothing.
cols.FSS_AMOUNT: Meant to hold family self-sufficiency grant dollars. Zero on every row, so it tells you nothing.
cols.SPENDING_PER_MONTH_PREV_YR: Average dollars spent per assisted unit per month last year. A -4 means no data.
cols.ANNUAL_EXPENSE_AMOUNT: Total dollars the authority spent on housing assistance this year. A -4 means no data.
cols.ANNUAL_EXPENSE_AMOUNT_PREV_YR: Total dollars the authority spent on housing assistance last year. A -4 means no data.
cols.CHILDREN_MEMBER_COUNT: How many children live in the authority's assisted homes. A -4 means no data.
cols.ELDERLY_PERCENT: Percent of the authority's tenants who are elderly. A -4 means no data.
cols.PCT_DISABLED_LT62_ALL: Percent of tenants under 62 who have a disability. A -4 means no data.
cols.PCT_BELOW_80PCT_MEDIAN_INCOME: Percent of tenant households earning under 80 percent of the local median income. Often 100. A -4 means no data.
cols.MEDIAN_INCOME_AMOUNT: The middle yearly household income among the authority's tenants, in dollars. A -4 means no data.
cols.BLOCK_GROUP: The census block group of the office address, a single digit. Only means something with the tract.
cols.CENSUS_BLOCK: The census block of the office address, four digits. Only means something with the tract.
cols.CURRENT_COUNTY_NAME: The county the authority's office is in.
cols.CURRENT_COUNTY_FIPS: The office's county as a three-digit federal code. Only means something with the state.
cols.CURRENT_COUNTY_SUBDIVISION: The census code for the town or township the office is in. Only means something with the state and county.
cols.CURRENT_COUNTY_SUBDIVISION_NAME: The name of the town, township or district the office is in.
cols.PLACE_FIPS: The census code for the city or town the office is in. 99999 means not inside any city.
cols.MSA_CODE: An old-style code for the metro area the office is in. 9999 means not in a metro area, which is most rows.
cols.MSA_NAME: The old-style metro area name, like Boston, MA-NH PMSA. Blank for most rows.
cols.CBSA_CODE: The census code for the metro or micro area the office is in. 99999 means neither.
cols.NECTA_CODE: New England town-based metro area code. 99999 for nearly every row, since it only covers New England.
cols.NECTA_NAME: New England town-based metro area name, like Boston-Cambridge-Newton. Blank outside New England, so almost always blank.
cols.METRO_FLAG: 1 when the office sits in a metro area, 0 when not.
cols.MICRO_FLAG: 1 when the office sits in a smaller micro area, 0 when not.
cols.FCD_FIPS91: A four-digit geography code from 1991. The codes need a lookup.
cols.HLC_CODE: A four-digit location code from the address geocoder. The codes need a lookup.
cols.DPV_CODE: A one-letter postal check on whether the address is deliverable: Y, D, N, S or M. The codes need a lookup.
cols.STD_ADDRESS: The office street address, cleaned up to postal format. Some are P.O. boxes.
cols.URBANIZATION: A Puerto Rico neighborhood name used in addresses. Filled on only two rows.
cols.STD_STATE: The office's state, as two letters.
cols.STD_ZIP9: The four-digit add-on to the ZIP code, despite the name. Some keep a leading zero, like 0117.
cols.ZIP_CLASS: A one-letter ZIP type, P or U. Blank on almost every row. The codes need a lookup.
cols.ZCTA: The five-digit ZIP code area of the office.
cols.DELIVERY_POINT_BARCODE: The two-digit postal delivery point from the barcode. Mostly useful to the post office.
cols.DELIVERY_POINT_BARCODE_CHECKSUM: The one-digit check number on the postal barcode. Mostly useful to the post office.
cols.STD_ZIP11: The full 11-digit postal delivery code for the office: ZIP, add-on and delivery point.
cols.ADDRESS_TYPE: A one-letter kind of address: S, H, P or R. The codes need a lookup.
cols.APT_NUMBER: The suite or unit number of the office. Mostly blank, and the code 1SUD fills most of what is there.
cols.APT_TYPE: The kind of unit, like Ste, Apt or Ofc. Blank for almost every row.
cols.GEOCODE_RETURN_CODE: A one-letter code for why the address match fell short: H, S or M. Blank for almost every row. The codes need a lookup.
cols.GEOCODE_PROBABILITY: A 0 to 5 score for how sure the address match is. The matching postal message column spells 0 out as 100% probable.
cols.GEOCODE_DRC: A one-letter geocoder flag: N, D or F. Blank for almost every row. The codes need a lookup.
cols.GEOCODE_SRC: A one-letter geocoder flag: N or S. Blank for almost every row. The codes need a lookup.
cols.GEOCODE_ARC: A one-letter geocoder flag: N or A. Blank for most rows. The codes need a lookup.
cols.GEOCODE_ZRC: A one-letter geocoder flag: H, S or M. Blank for almost every row. The codes need a lookup.
cols.USPS_MESSAGE: A plain-words note on how well the address matched postal records, like 100% Overall probable correctness or Street not found.
cols.LAT_GEOCODED: The latitude of the office address.
cols.LON_GEOCODED: The longitude of the office address.
cols.GEOCODE_RESULT_CODE: A one-character code for how the map point was found: S, 5 or 9. The codes need a lookup.
cols.GEOCODE_MATCH_TYPE: A one-letter match type: S, H or Z. Blank for most rows. The codes need a lookup.
cols.GEOCODE_LEVEL: A one-character code for how precise the map point is: R, T, B, 4 or 5. The geocode message column spells out the common ones.
cols.URBAN_RURAL_FLAG: U when the office is in an urban area, R when rural.
cols.GEOCODE_MESSAGE: How precise the map point is, in words: Street-Level Rooftop, Centroid, or no point made.
cols.COUNTY_LEVEL_KEY: The office's full five-digit county code, state plus county.
cols.PLACE_LEVEL_KEY: The office's full seven-digit city code, state plus place. Ending in 99999 means not inside a city.
cols.TRACT_LEVEL_KEY: The office's full 11-digit census tract code.
cols.BLOCK_GROUP_LEVEL_KEY: The office's full 12-digit census block group code.
cols.UGLG_KEY: A seven-digit code for the local government the office sits under, state plus place. The codes need a lookup.
cols.LAST_UPDATED_AT: When HUD last updated the list. Every row holds the same time, July 16, 2025.

HOUSING__FED_HUD_PUBLIC_HOUSING_AUTHORIT.summary: Every local public housing authority in HUD's list, with how many public housing and Section 8 units it runs, its federal funding, its tenants and its office location.
HOUSING__FED_HUD_PUBLIC_HOUSING_AUTHORIT.row: One public housing authority: its contacts, unit counts, funding, tenant makeup and mapped office address.

cols.FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 06037. One table holds two-digit state codes instead, and nine tables leave it empty.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.GEOMETRY: The shape of the area on a map, as GeoJSON map coordinates. Mostly blank in the NOAA weather table.
cols.LAT: Latitude in decimal degrees. In the redlining map table it is a long unrounded number.
cols.LON: Longitude in decimal degrees, negative in the U.S. In the redlining map table it is a long unrounded number.
cols.SOURCE_ID: A short name for the source feed the row came from, like fed_cfpb_complaints. In the ITIS other-sources table it is a plain number instead, which needs a lookup.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.HOLC_NEIGHBORHOOD_KEY: A made-up key built from the city, state, grade and a number, joined with | marks. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.HOLC_ID: Meant to be the map's own label for the area. Empty on every row.
cols.HOLC_GRADE: The redlining grade: A best, B, C, D hazardous, plus a few E and F. Blank on about one row in twelve.
cols.HOLC_COLOR: Meant to be the map color for the grade. Empty on every row.
cols.AREA_DESCRIPTION_DATA: Meant to hold the written notes about each area. Every row holds only {}, so the written reasons did not load.
cols.RESIDENTIAL_DESCRIPTION: Meant to be the written description of the housing. Empty on every row.
cols.YEAR_MAPPED: Meant to be the year the map was made. Empty on every row.
cols.HOLC_GRADE_RANK: The grade as a number: 1 for A through 4 for D.
cols.HOLC_GRADE_LABEL: The grade in words: Best, Still Desirable, Definitely Declining, Hazardous or Unknown.

HOUSING__FED_MAPPING_INEQUALITY.summary: 1930s federal redlining maps for about 200 U.S. cities: each neighborhood's A-to-D grade from the Home Owners' Loan Corporation.
HOUSING__FED_MAPPING_INEQUALITY.row: One graded neighborhood: one area on one city's redlining map.

cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.STATE_COUNTY_FIPS_CODE: The county's five-digit government code, where the first two digits are the state. Kept as text so leading zeros survive.
cols.PROJECT_NAME: The name of the housing project, usually an apartment complex like Anamosa Villa I.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_ABBREVIATION: The state as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam and AS for American Samoa appear too.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.BORROWER_ID: USDA's ID for the borrower that owns the project.
cols.PROJECT_ID: The project's number under its borrower, like 01 or 02. Pair it with the borrower ID to pin down one project.
cols.PROJECT_CHECK_DIGIT: A single check digit on the project number, used to catch typos. It means nothing on its own.
cols.MAIN_ADDRESS_LINE2: A second address line that sometimes holds stray words or phone numbers. Almost always blank.
cols.MAIN_ADDRESS_LINE3: A third address line holding odd leftovers like phone numbers. Almost always blank.
cols.RENTAL_CODE: Who the project houses, as a code like FA, EL or MX that needs a lookup. ?? is a placeholder.
cols.LABOR_HOUSING_TYPE: Farm labor housing type, code 0, 1 or 2 that needs a lookup. Almost all are 0.
cols.REVITALIZATION_INDICATOR: Marks projects in a revitalization program with 1. Blank for the rest, most rows.
cols.TAX_STATUS_INDICATOR: Whether the project uses tax credits, Y or N; Y rows are the ones with a tax credit end date.
cols.DATE_TAX_CREDIT_EXPIRES: Date the project's tax credit runs out. Filled only when tax status is Y, just under half the rows.
cols.PROFIT_TYPE_CODE: The owner's profit type, code 1, 2 or 3 that needs a lookup.
cols.MANAGEMENT_NAME: The company that manages the property.
cols.DATE_RESTRICTIVE_CLAUSE_EXPIRES: Date the rule that keeps the project as affordable housing runs out.
cols.TOTAL_4_BEDROOM_UNITS: Four-bedroom apartments in the project. Almost always 0.
cols.TOTAL_5_BEDROOM_UNITS: Five-bedroom apartments in the project. Almost always 0.
cols.TOTAL_HANDICAPPED_UNITS: Apartments built for residents with disabilities.
cols.VACANT_UNITS: Apartments sitting empty at the time of the report.
cols.RENTAL_ASSISTANCE_UNITS: Apartments whose tenants get USDA rent help.

HOUSING__FED_USDA_RD_MFH_ACTIVE_PROJECTS.summary: Active USDA Rural Development apartment projects for rural renters, with location, manager, unit counts, vacancies, rental help and key expiration dates.
HOUSING__FED_USDA_RD_MFH_ACTIVE_PROJECTS.row: One rural housing project: one borrower's project, with its units, manager and key dates.

cols.SOURCE_URL: The web address the data was taken from. Mostly blank in the place-names table, where it is often just a site name like www.census.gov.
cols.MONTHLY_TOTALS: The line's label, like At Entry, At Large or Nationwide Total Apprehensions.
cols.OCT_25: The count for October 2025. Stored as text.
cols.NOV_25: The count for November 2025. Stored as text.
cols.DEC_25: The count for December 2025. Stored as text.
cols.JAN_26: The count for January 2026. Stored as text.
cols.FEB_26: The count for February 2026. Stored as text.
cols.MAR_26: The count for March 2026. Stored as text.
cols.APR_26: The count for April 2026. Stored as text.
cols.MAY_26: The count for May 2026. Stored as text.
cols.JUN_26: The count for June 2026. Every row is -, so no numbers yet.
cols.JUL_26: The count for July 2026. Every row is -, so no numbers yet.
cols.AUG_26: The count for August 2026. Every row is -, so no numbers yet.
cols.SEP_26: The count for September 2026. Every row is -, so no numbers yet.
cols.DATA_AS_OF_DATE: The date the numbers were current as of. Empty in this table.

IMMIGRATION__FED_CBP_ENCOUNTERS.summary: A tiny nine-line summary table of Border Patrol apprehensions by month for fiscal 2026, October 2025 through May 2026, with later months still blank.
IMMIGRATION__FED_CBP_ENCOUNTERS.row: One line of the summary table, like At Entry or Nationwide Total Apprehensions, with one column per month.

cols.ENROLLMENT_ID: Medicare's ID for one enrollment record: the letter O, a date, then a number, like O20090204000452.
cols.ENROLLMENT_STATE: The state where the provider is enrolled in Medicare, as two letters.
cols.PROVIDER_TYPE_CODE: Medicare's code for the kind of provider, like 00-09 for a hospital. Each table mostly holds one value.
cols.PROVIDER_TYPE_TEXT: The kind of provider in words, like PART A PROVIDER - HOSPITAL.
cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit National Provider Identifier, stored as text. Some tables leave it mostly blank or empty, and the SAM exclusions table uses 0000000000 as a filler.
cols.MULTIPLE_NPI_FLAG: Y if this enrollment covers more than one provider number, N if not.
cols.CCN: The facility's 6-character Medicare certification number, stored as text; some hold letters, like 38T061. It is almost always blank in the three Open Payments tables.
cols.ASSOCIATE_ID: Medicare's 10-digit ID for the enrolled organization, used to link its enrollments and owners. Stored as text; a few look short, like lost leading zeros.
cols.ORGANIZATION_NAME: The name of the organization, like a charity, clinic, home health agency or government office. Some rows hold loose labels like Private Practice or Trust #1, and the judge positions table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.DOING_BUSINESS_AS_NAME: The name the facility operates under, when it differs from its legal name. Often empty.
cols.INCORPORATION_DATE: The date the company or organization was legally formed. The Irish registry uses 1901-01-01 as a stand-in date on hundreds of rows, and one small offshore-leaks table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.INCORPORATION_STATE: The state where the organization is legally formed, as two letters. Often empty.
cols.ORGANIZATION_TYPE_STRUCTURE: The organization's legal form: CORPORATION, LLC, PARTNERSHIP, SOLE PROPRIETOR, or OTHER.
cols.ORGANIZATION_OTHER_TYPE_TEXT: A free-text description of the legal form when it is OTHER, like COUNTY OWNED or 501C3. Empty for most rows.
cols.PROPRIETARY_NONPROFIT: Whether the facility is for-profit or non-profit: P for for-profit, N for non-profit. Some tables also have D.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_1: The first line of the street address, like 13 STATION ROAD.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_2: The second address line, often a suite or floor but sometimes a street or area name. Blank for many rows, one table leaves it empty, and two fill it with a lone dash.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.

IMMIGRATION__FED_CMS_HOSPICE_ENROLLMENTS.summary: Every hospice enrolled with Medicare, about 6,100, with its provider numbers, legal name, owner type and address.
IMMIGRATION__FED_CMS_HOSPICE_ENROLLMENTS.row: One hospice enrollment: one hospice's Medicare enrollment in one state.

cols.REPORT_MONTH: The month the numbers are for, stored as the first day of that month. Empty in the DHS table.
cols.TABLE_NAME: The name of the source table or report page the row came from, like S-52 or tri.tri_facility. Empty in the two DHS immigration tables.
cols.FISCAL_YEAR: The government fiscal year the row covers, like 2023, sometimes written as FY2026 or 2024 YTD. One ICE table holds small numbers that are not years, a DHS table leaves it mostly blank, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.MONTH: The month, in many formats: January, 01, 1998-11, 10-2011, a mid-month date like 2026-03-15, or Total. One table leaves it empty.
cols._SOURCE_ROW_HASH: A fingerprint of the row's contents, made to spot duplicate lines. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.ENCOUNTER_TYPE: Meant to hold the kind of encounter, but empty on every row.
cols.REGION_OR_SECTOR: Meant to hold the border region or sector, but empty on every row.
cols.CITIZENSHIP: Meant to hold people's citizenship, but empty on every row.
cols.FAMILY_STATUS: Meant to hold family status, but empty on every row.
cols.CRIMINALITY: Meant to hold criminal history, but empty on every row.
cols.INITIAL_ARRESTING_AGENCY: Meant to hold the agency that made the arrest, but empty on every row.
cols.BOOK_OUT_OUTCOME: Meant to hold what happened at release from custody, but empty on every row.
cols.REPATRIATION_TYPE: Meant to hold the kind of removal, but empty on every row.
cols.CREDIBLE_FEAR_RESULT: Meant to hold the credible fear interview result, but empty on every row.
cols.CHNV_PROCESS_TYPE: Meant to hold the parole program type, but empty on every row.
cols.CALENDAR_YEAR: Meant to hold the calendar year, but empty on every row.
cols.EVENT_COUNT: Meant to hold the event count, but empty on every row.
cols.ENCOUNTERS: A label for the kind of event on the line, like Encounters, Detentions or DHS Repatriations. Nearly always blank.
cols.SOURCE_FILE_NAME: The DHS spreadsheet release the row came from; there are 13.
cols.SOURCE_SHEET_NAME: The tab inside the spreadsheet, like SWB Encounters by Citizenship or ERO Arrests by Criminality. It tells you what the numbers on the row measure.
cols.TOTAL: The total count on the line, stored as text. Mostly blank.
cols.VENEZUELA: The count for people from Venezuela, stored as text. Mostly blank; X shows up as a placeholder, not a number.
cols.CUBA: The count for people from Cuba, stored as text. Mostly blank; X shows up as a placeholder, not a number.
cols.MEXICO: The count for people from Mexico, stored as text. Mostly blank; X shows up as a placeholder, not a number.
cols.HAITI: The count for people from Haiti, stored as text. Mostly blank; X shows up as a placeholder, not a number.
cols.HONDURAS: The count for people from Honduras, stored as text. Mostly blank; X shows up as a placeholder, not a number.
cols.COLOMBIA: The count for people from Colombia, stored as text. Mostly blank; X shows up as a placeholder, not a number.
cols.GUATEMALA: The count for people from Guatemala, stored as text. Mostly blank; X shows up as a placeholder, not a number.
cols.EL_SALVADOR: The count for people from El Salvador, stored as text. Mostly blank; X shows up as a placeholder, not a number.
cols.ECUADOR: The count for people from Ecuador, stored as text. Mostly blank; X shows up as a placeholder, not a number.
cols.RUSSIA: The count for people from Russia, stored as text. Mostly blank; X shows up as a placeholder, not a number.
cols.OTHER: The count for people from all other countries, stored as text. Nearly always blank; X shows up as a placeholder, not a number.
cols.NICARAGUA: The count for people from Nicaragua, stored as text. Mostly blank; X shows up as a placeholder, not a number.
cols.BORDER: The count at the border, stored as text. Nearly always blank.
cols.INTERIOR: The count inside the country, away from the border, stored as text. Nearly always blank.

IMMIGRATION__FED_DHS_OHSS.summary: DHS immigration enforcement statistics, border encounters, arrests, detentions, repatriations and credible fear results, copied line by line from 13 monthly spreadsheet releases; most label columns are empty.
IMMIGRATION__FED_DHS_OHSS.row: One line of one sheet in one monthly DHS spreadsheet release; the same figure can show up again in later releases.

cols.FISCAL_YEAR: The government fiscal year the row covers, like 2023, sometimes written as FY2026 or 2024 YTD. One ICE table holds small numbers that are not years, a DHS table leaves it mostly blank, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTRY_OF_BIRTH: The country a person was born in, spelled out, like Afghanistan or Russia. Mostly blank in the UK sanctions lists and empty in the DHS yearbook table.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.COUNT: A count of whatever the row describes. Filled on just one row in the ICE statistics table and empty in the DHS yearbook table.
cols.TABLE_NAME: The name of the source table or report page the row came from, like S-52 or tri.tri_facility. Empty in the two DHS immigration tables.
cols.VISA_CLASS: The visa type, like H-1B or E-3 Australian. Empty in the DHS yearbook table.
cols.COUNTRY_OF_LAST_RESIDENCE: The country where the people counted last lived. Empty in this table.
cols.CATEGORY: The immigration category counted. Empty in this table.
cols.YEARBOOK_EDITION: The year of the yearbook edition, like 2012. Each row has its own value.
cols.ENFORCEMENT_ACTION_TYPE: The kind of enforcement action counted. Empty in this table.
cols.SOURCE_PDF_URL: The web address of the yearbook PDF on the Homeland Security statistics site.

IMMIGRATION__FED_DHS_YEARBOOK.summary: Entries from the Homeland Security Yearbook of Immigration Statistics, one per yearbook edition, 27 in all, each with a link to its PDF. Every data column, COUNT included, is empty, so the table holds no statistics.
IMMIGRATION__FED_DHS_YEARBOOK.row: One yearbook edition: one year's edition of the yearbook and its source PDF.

cols.CASE_NUMBER: The agency's ID number for one case, in a format that depends on the agency, like 05-2014-5064 or I-200-19058-315794. In the OSHA injury tables it is a small running number like 1, 2 or 3 that repeats across work sites, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.DECISION_DATE: The date the decision came down on the application or case. One table stores it as text with a time, and the AustLII table is empty.
cols.VISA_CLASS: The visa type, like H-1B or E-3 Australian. Empty in the DHS yearbook table.
cols.JOB_TITLE: The job or position title, like SOFTWARE DEVELOPER or Judge. Mostly blank in the CourtListener positions table.
cols.SOC_CODE: The job's standard occupation code, like 29-1141 for registered nurses. OSHA rows often hold filler codes like 9999 or 00-9900.
cols.EMPLOYER_NAME: The employer's name. In lobbying tables it is the client that hired the lobbyist; in donation tables it is the donor's employer, often Self-Employed, Retired or Not Employed; in the labor certification table it is the hiring company.
cols.EMPLOYER_CITY: The city of the employer. Casing and naming vary, like Bronx versus The Bronx.
cols.EMPLOYER_STATE: The state of the employer, as two letters.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The industry code, usually six digits like 722110, which needs a lookup to read. Some tables hold shorter codes like 5416, the OSHA inspections table fills most rows with 000000, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.CASE_STATUS: Where the application ended up: certified, certified then withdrawn, withdrawn, or denied.
cols.CASE_SUBMITTED: When the employer submitted the application. A date and time stored as text.
cols.ORIGINAL_CERT_DATE: The date the application was first certified, filled only for cases later withdrawn after certification. Stored as text.
cols.SOC_TITLE: The job's occupation title from the federal job-code list, like software developers or computer systems analysts. Spelling varies slightly for the same job.
cols.FULL_TIME_POSITION: Y if the job is full time, N if part time.
cols.PERIOD_OF_EMPLOYMENT_START_DATE: The first day the foreign worker may start the job. Stored as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_EMPLOYMENT_END_DATE: The last day of the approved work period, often about three years after the start. Stored as text.
cols.TOTAL_WORKER_POSITIONS: How many foreign workers the application covers. Almost always 1. A number stored as text.
cols.NEW_EMPLOYMENT: How many of the workers are brand-new hires. A number stored as text.
cols.CONTINUED_EMPLOYMENT: How many workers are extending a job they already hold with this employer. A number stored as text.
cols.CHANGE_PREVIOUS_EMPLOYMENT: How many workers are staying with this employer but changing the terms of the job. A number stored as text.
cols.NEW_CONCURRENT_EMPLOYMENT: How many workers will hold this job on top of a job with another employer. A number stored as text.
cols.CHANGE_EMPLOYER: How many workers are moving over from a different employer. A number stored as text.
cols.AMENDED_PETITION: How many workers are covered by an amended version of an earlier petition. A number stored as text.
cols.EMPLOYER_BUSINESS_DBA: The trade name the employer does business under, if different from its legal name. Mostly blank.
cols.EMPLOYER_ADDRESS2: The second line of the employer's address, like a suite or floor. Mostly blank.
cols.EMPLOYER_POSTAL_CODE: The employer's ZIP code. Leading zeros are dropped, so 08817 shows as 8817.
cols.EMPLOYER_COUNTRY: The employer's country. Almost all are the United States.
cols.EMPLOYER_PROVINCE: The employer's province or county, used loosely; values mix counties, states and USA. Mostly blank.
cols.EMPLOYER_PHONE: The employer's phone number, digits only.
cols.EMPLOYER_PHONE_EXT: The employer's phone extension. Mostly blank.
cols.AGENT_REPRESENTING_EMPLOYER: Y if a lawyer or agent filed the application for the employer.
cols.AGENT_ATTORNEY_LAW_FIRM_BUSINESS_NAME: The law firm or agent business that filed for the employer, like Fragomen. The same firm can appear under slightly different spellings.
cols.AGENT_ATTORNEY_ADDRESS2: The second line of the law firm's address, like a suite or floor. Mostly blank.
cols.AGENT_ATTORNEY_STATE: The law firm's state, as two letters.
cols.AGENT_ATTORNEY_POSTAL_CODE: The law firm's ZIP or postal code. US ZIPs lose leading zeros, and Canadian postal codes appear too.
cols.AGENT_ATTORNEY_COUNTRY: The law firm's country, mostly the United States with some Canada.
cols.AGENT_ATTORNEY_PROVINCE: The law firm's province, filled mainly for Canadian firms in Ontario. Mostly blank.
cols.AGENT_ATTORNEY_PHONE: The law firm's phone number, digits only.
cols.AGENT_ATTORNEY_PHONE_EXT: The law firm's phone extension. Mostly blank.
cols.STATE_OF_HIGHEST_COURT: The name of the top court where the filing lawyer is licensed, like Supreme Court. Despite the column name, this holds the court, not the state.
cols.NAME_OF_HIGHEST_STATE_COURT: The state where the filing lawyer is licensed, like New York. Despite the column name, this holds the state, not the court.

cols.NATIONALITY: The person's nationality. Format differs by table: words like British, two-letter codes like EG in immigration court, or wrapped like {"VALUE": "Yemen"} in the UN list.
cols.LANGUAGE: The language, written differently by table: en, ENG, SP, a full name like French, or a bracketed list. Some rows say unspecified or hold an empty list [].

cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

cols.CASE_ID: The court's ID number for the case. Each case has its own.
cols.COURT_CODE: Three-letter code for the immigration court, like MIA or NYC; the codes need a lookup.
cols.CUSTODY: Custody code: N, D or R, with a few stray values. The label column shows N is never detained, D detained and R released.
cols.CUSTODY_LABEL: Custody status in words: never detained, detained or released.
cols.CASE_TYPE: Code for the kind of case, like RMV or DEP; the codes need a lookup. RMV is on most rows.
cols.LATEST_HEARING_AT: Date of the case's latest hearing. Many are in the future because hearings are scheduled ahead.
cols.LATEST_HEARING_TIME: Time of the latest hearing as four-digit text, like 0830 or 1300.
cols.LATEST_HEARING_CALENDAR_TYPE: Code for the kind of hearing calendar, mostly M or I; the codes need a lookup. A few rows hold stray times.
cols.DATE_OF_ENTRY: Date the person entered the United States. Blank on over a third of rows.
cols.DATE_DETAINED: Date the person was detained. Mostly blank.
cols.DATE_RELEASED: Date the person was released from detention. Mostly blank.
cols.EARLIEST_POSSIBLE_RELEASE_DATE: Earliest date the person could be released from a criminal sentence. Almost always blank, and 2099-12-31 shows up as a placeholder.
cols.DETENTION_FACILITY_ENTERED_AT: Meant to hold when the person entered a detention facility, but it is empty in this table.
cols.ASYLUM_CLOCK_TYPE: Code for the asylum clock status, mostly E, I or J; the codes need a lookup. A few rows hold stray dates.
cols.BIRTH_MONTH_YEAR: The person's birth month and year as text, like 10/2000. Blank on about half the rows.
cols.IS_LPR: True or false: whether the person is a lawful permanent resident. Mostly blank.
cols.CORRECTIONAL_FACILITY_CODE: Code for the kind of jail or prison holding the person, like S, D or F; the codes need a lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.INMATE_HOUSING_CODE: Code for where the person is held, like FDC or HUN; the codes need a lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.DETENTION_LOCATION: Name of the detention place, like HUNTSVILLE or EDEN DETENTION CENTER. Almost always blank.
cols.DETENTION_LOCATION_ADDRESS: Address or town of the detention place, typed freely, like Eloy Arizona. Almost always blank.
cols.DETENTION_FACILITY_TYPE: Detention facility type code. Filled on just one row.
cols.CASE_PRIORITY_CODE: Code for the case's priority group, like UC or AWC/ATD; the codes need a lookup. N/A on nearly every row.
cols.ALIEN_CITY: City of the person's address on file.
cols.ALIEN_STATE: State of the person's address on file, as two letters.
cols.ALIEN_ZIPCODE: ZIP code of the person's address on file. 00000 is used as a filler on many rows.
cols.UPDATED_CITY: City from an updated address. Almost always blank.
cols.UPDATED_STATE: State from an updated address, as two letters. Almost always blank.
cols.UPDATED_ZIPCODE: ZIP code from an updated address; 00000 shows up as a filler. Almost always blank.
cols.ADDRESS_CHANGED_AT: Date and time the person's address was last changed. Blank on over half the rows.
cols.HEARING_NOTICE_TYPE: Code for the kind of hearing notice, mostly M or I; the codes need a lookup. Blank on about half the rows.
cols.ATTORNEY_COUNT_LEGACY: Count of attorneys from an older system, stored as text with mixed padding, so 0 and 00 both appear.
cols.FIELD_COUNT: How many fields the raw file line split into; 39 on nearly every row, and other counts flag lines that parsed oddly. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

cols.SUBMISSIONYEARQUARTER: Which quarterly EPA data release this row came from, like 2026Q2.
cols.PWSID: The public water system's ID, usually two state letters then seven characters, like OK2006367, though a few use longer prefixes like UTAH18050.
cols.FIRST_REPORTED_DATE: The date this record was first reported into the EPA's drinking-water system.
cols.LAST_REPORTED_DATE: The date this record was last reported into the EPA's drinking-water system.
cols.SERVICE_AREA_TYPE_CODE: A two-letter code for the kind of place served, like RS, OT or SC. The codes need a lookup.
cols.IS_PRIMARY_SERVICE_AREA_CODE: Y if this is the system's main kind of place served, N if not. Blank for about a quarter.

cols.PERSON_HASH: A 40-character scrambled code standing in for one person, so you can follow them across rows without a name.
cols.DETENTION_FACILITY: The jail or ICE site where the person was held, like KROME NORTH SPC or GRAYSON COUNTY JAIL.
cols.DETENTION_FACILITY_CODE: ICE's short code for a detention facility, like GRAYSTX or POOHOLD. Join on it to get the facility's name.
cols.FACILITY_CITY: The city where the facility is.
cols.FACILITY_STATE: The facility's state. Two letters in the EPA table, full name like TEXAS in the ICE table.
cols.GENDER: The person's sex, written differently by table: Male or Female, M or F, m or f, or Male Owned for businesses. Some rows say Unknown or Unanswered, the clinical trials table mostly says ALL, and one table leaves it empty.

cols.BIRTH_COUNTRY: The country the person was born in, in capitals like MEXICO.
cols.CITIZENSHIP_COUNTRY: The country the person is a citizen of, in capitals like HONDURAS.
cols.ENTRY_STATUS: How the person came into the U.S., like Present Without Admission, shortened to PWA, or Border Crossing Card. Often blank or Not Applicable.
cols.ENTRY_DATE: The date the person entered the U.S. Filled on about six in ten detention rows but blank on most detainer rows.
cols.MSC_CHARGE_DATE: The date of the person's most serious criminal charge. Blank on most rows.
cols.MSC_CONVICTION_DATE: The date of the person's most serious criminal conviction. Blank on most rows.
cols.MSC_SENTENCE_DAYS: The days part of the sentence for the person's most serious conviction. Read with the months and years columns; mostly blank.
cols.MSC_SENTENCE_MONTHS: The months part of the sentence for the person's most serious conviction. Read with the days and years columns; mostly blank.
cols.MSC_SENTENCE_YEARS: The years part of the sentence for the person's most serious conviction. Read with the days and months columns; mostly blank.
cols.FELON: Whether ICE marks the person as an aggravated felon and for what, like Drugs or Other. Nearly every filled row says Not an Aggravated Felon, and about half the detention rows are blank.
cols.CASE_CATEGORY: Where the person's immigration case stands, as a bracketed code plus words, like [16] Reinstated Final Order.
cols.FINAL_ORDER_YES_NO: Whether the person has a final removal order, YES or NO.
cols.FINAL_ORDER_DATE: The date the final removal order was issued. Often blank.
cols.DEPARTED_DATE: The date the person left or was removed from the U.S. Blank if they have not left.
cols.DEPARTURE_COUNTRY: The country the person was sent or went to on leaving, in capitals like GUATEMALA.
cols.DUPLICATE_LIKELY: Whether this row looks like a repeat of another, the words True or False stored as text.
cols.FILE_ORIGINAL: The name of the spreadsheet file from the FOIA release that this row came from.
cols.SHEET_ORIGINAL: The tab of the source spreadsheet this row came from, a fiscal year like FY2025.
cols.ROW_ORIGINAL: The row number in the source spreadsheet, stored as text.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.DETAINER_PREPARE_DATE: The day ICE wrote up the detainer.
cols.DETAINER_TYPE: The ICE form used, like I247A Immigration Detainer or I247G Request for Advance Notification of release.
cols.FACILITY_AOR: The ICE field office region the jail sits in, like Miami Area of Responsibility. Blank for about one in five.
cols.DETAINER_PREPARED_CRIMINALITY: ICE's label for the person when the detainer was written: 1 Convicted Criminal, 2 Pending Criminal Charges, or 3 Other Immigration Violator.
cols.DETAINER_PREP_THREAT_LEVEL: ICE's threat level for the person, 1, 2 or 3. Some rows say NA. The levels need a lookup.
cols.MOST_SERIOUS_CONVICTION_CHARGE: The person's most serious criminal conviction, like Driving Under Influence Liquor or Assault. Blank when there is no conviction, which is most rows.
cols.MSC_CHARGE_CODE: The code for the most serious conviction, like 5404. The plain words are in the conviction charge column. Blank for most rows.
cols.PRIOR_FELONY_YES_NO: YES when the person has an earlier felony conviction. Blank for most rows.
cols.MULTIPLE_PRIOR_MISD_YES_NO: YES when the person has several earlier misdemeanor convictions. Blank for most rows.
cols.VIOLENT_MISDEMEANOR_YES_NO: YES when the person has a violent misdemeanor conviction. Blank for most rows.
cols.AGGRAVATED_FELONY_YES_NO: YES when the person has an aggravated felony conviction under immigration law. Blank for most rows.
cols.CRIMINAL_STREET_GANG_YES_NO: YES when ICE flagged the person as a street gang member. Rare, and blank for most rows.
cols.ILLEGAL_ENTRY_YES_NO: Meant to flag illegal entry. Filled on only 29 rows, all NO, so it tells you almost nothing.
cols.ILLEGAL_REENTRY_YES_NO: YES when the person came back into the country illegally after removal. Blank for most rows.
cols.IMMIGRATION_FRAUD_YES_NO: Meant to flag immigration fraud. Filled on only 29 rows, all NO, so it tells you almost nothing.
cols.SIGNIFICANT_RISK_YES_NO: YES when ICE judged the person a significant risk. Blank for most rows.
cols.OTHER_REMOVAL_REASON_YES_NO: Meant to flag some other reason for removal. Filled on only 29 rows, all NO.
cols.DEPORTATION_ORDERED_YES_NO: YES when the person already had a deportation order.
cols.ORDER_SHOW_CAUSE_SERVED_YES_NO: YES when the person had been served papers starting immigration court proceedings.
cols.BIOMETRIC_MATCH_YES_NO: YES when fingerprints matched the person to immigration records.
cols.STATEMENTS_MADE_YES_NO: YES when the person's own statements helped show they could be removed.
cols.UNLAWFUL_ATTEMPT_YES_NO: Filled on only 4 rows, all NO. Tells you nothing.
cols.UNLAWFUL_ENTRY_YES_NO: Filled on only 4 rows. Tells you almost nothing.
cols.VISA_YES_NO: Filled on only 4 rows, all NO. Tells you nothing.
cols.FEDERAL_INTEREST_YES_NO: YES on a bit over half of rows. The rest are blank, never NO, so blank may not mean no.
cols.RESUME_CUSTODY_YES_NO: YES when ICE asked to take the person back into its custody.
cols.ACTIVE_INVESTIGATION_YES_NO: Filled on one row only. Tells you nothing.
cols.NOTIFY_RELEASE_REQUEST_YES_NO: Filled on only 30 rows. Tells you almost nothing.
cols.PROCESSING_DISPOSITION: How ICE processed the case, like Detainer, Warrant of Arrest/Notice to Appear, or Reinstatement of Deport Order.
cols.CASE_STATUS: Where the person's immigration case stands, like ACTIVE or a code plus words such as 8-Excluded/Removed. Blank for about half.
cols.ARREST_TIME_CASE_CATEGORY: ICE's category for the case at arrest, a bracketed code plus words, like [16] Reinstated Final Order. Blank for most rows.
cols.ARREST_TIME_CURRENT_PROGRAM: The ICE program that made the arrest, like ERO Criminal Alien Program or 287G Program. Blank for most rows.
cols.APPREHENSION_METHOD: How the person was picked up, like CAP Local Incarceration or Custodial Arrest. Blank for most rows.
cols.APPREHENSION_AT: The date and time ICE arrested the person. Blank for most rows.
cols.PORT_OF_DEPARTURE: Where the person left the country when removed, like a border crossing or an airport. Blank for most rows.
cols.DETAINER_LIFT_REASON: Why the detainer ended, like Booked into Detention or Detainer Declined by LEA. Blank while it is still open.
cols.DETAINER_LIFT_REASON_CODE: A one-letter code for why the detainer ended. The plain words are in the lift reason column.
cols.TOD_CURRENT_DUTY_SITE: The ICE office that handled the detainer, like ERO Westminster, CA Sub Office.
