cols.DUPLICATE_DROP_ROW: A drop-this-row flag; False on every row because flagged rows were removed.

IMMIGRATION__FED_ICE_DETENTION_STINTS.summary: Every ICE detention stint from 2004 to 2026, with anonymized person IDs, facility, criminal history, bond and how each stint ended; rows the publisher marked as duplicates are left out.
IMMIGRATION__FED_ICE_DETENTION_STINTS.row: One detention stint: one person held at one facility, from book-in to book-out.

cols.FISCAL_YEAR: The government fiscal year the row covers, like 2023, sometimes written as FY2026 or 2024 YTD. One ICE table holds small numbers that are not years, a DHS table leaves it mostly blank, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.AOR: The ICE field office region that covers a facility, named by city like Chicago, sometimes with AOR on the end. Empty in the ICE statistics table.
cols.COUNT: A count of whatever the row describes. Filled on just one row in the ICE statistics table and empty in the DHS yearbook table.
cols.SNAPSHOT_DATE: The date the data was captured. Stored as text in the committee table.
cols.FISCAL_QUARTER: The quarter of the fiscal year the count covers. Empty in this table.
cols.METRIC_TYPE: What is being counted. All but one row say removals; one says unknown.
cols.COUNTRY_OF_CITIZENSHIP: The citizenship of the people counted. Blank for a few rows.
cols.CRIMINAL_HISTORY_CATEGORY: The criminal record group counted, like Criminal Convictions or Pending Criminal Charges. Filled for only 4 rows.
cols.REMOVAL_AUTHORITY: The legal authority used for the removals. Empty in this table.
cols.ATD_MONITORING_TYPE: The kind of monitoring used in ICE's alternatives to detention program. Empty in this table.

IMMIGRATION__FED_ICE_STATISTICS.summary: ICE removal counts from ICE's published statistics, mostly broken down by country of citizenship; only 204 rows.
IMMIGRATION__FED_ICE_STATISTICS.row: One count: one ICE figure for one fiscal year and one breakdown, like removals of one country's citizens.

cols.FISCAL_YEAR: The government fiscal year the row covers, like 2023, sometimes written as FY2026 or 2024 YTD. One ICE table holds small numbers that are not years, a DHS table leaves it mostly blank, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.QUARTER: The quarter the numbers cover, like Q1. The HUD table holds a quarter-end date like 31DEC2025, and the BLS table is empty.
cols.COUNTRY: The country, written different ways by table: a full name, a two- or three-letter code, or a number code that needs a lookup. Some rows hold a region like World or a UK nation like England, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.REPORT_TITLE: The title of a published report or filing, like Periodic Transaction Report for 12/24/2021 or EU-SOCTA 2025 - Executive Summary.
cols.PUBLICATION_DATE: The date the item was published. Three tables leave it empty.
cols.FORM_NUMBER: Meant to hold the USCIS form number, but it holds leftover spreadsheet text like Notes:, years and headings. Blank on about a quarter of rows.
cols.FORM_TITLE: Meant to hold the form's title, but it is empty in this table.
cols.CATEGORY: Meant to hold the case category, but it is empty in this table.
cols.USCIS_OFFICE: Meant to hold the USCIS office, but it is empty in this table.
cols.RECEIPTS: Meant to hold how many cases came in, but it is empty in this table.
cols.APPROVALS: Meant to count approvals, but its 24 filled rows hold footnote text and country names, not numbers.
cols.DENIALS: Meant to hold how many were denied, but it is empty in this table.
cols.PENDING: Meant to hold how many are waiting, but it is empty in this table.
cols.AVG_PROCESSING_TIME_DAYS: Meant to hold the average processing time, but it is empty in this table.
cols.RFE_COUNT: Meant to hold how many requests for more evidence were sent, but it is empty in this table.
cols.SOURCE_FILE_URL: The link to the USCIS spreadsheet the row came from.

IMMIGRATION__FED_USCIS_DATA.summary: Rows scraped from USCIS immigration statistics spreadsheets. The load went wrong: the count columns are empty or hold note text, so this table has no usable numbers.
IMMIGRATION__FED_USCIS_DATA.row: One line from a USCIS spreadsheet, mostly headings and footnotes rather than data.

cols.ENTITY: The country or region name, like Albania or World.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.WORLD_REGION_ACCORDING_TO_OWID: The continent the country belongs to, as Our World in Data groups them, like Europe or Africa.
cols.CODE: The country's three-letter code, like AGO. Blank for regions and groups of countries.
cols.REFUGEES_BY_COUNTRY_OF_ORIGIN: How many refugees came from this country that year. Stored as text, so convert it to a number first.

IMMIGRATION__XC_OWID_REFUGEES.summary: How many refugees fled from each country, year by year, from Our World in Data.
IMMIGRATION__XC_OWID_REFUGEES.row: One country-year: the refugee count from one country or region in one year.

cols.NOTE: A free-text note about the record, blank for most rows. One housing table fills many rows with a bare tab character instead of text.
cols.INCIDENTYEAR: The year the incident happened, 2022 to 2025.
cols.INCIDENTMONTH: The month the incident happened, spelled out, like January.
cols.INCIDENTDATERANGE: Yes when the incident ran over a stretch of time rather than one day.
cols.INCIDENTDATESTART: When a long-running incident started. DNA, does not apply, on most rows; some hold just a month name. Stored as text.
cols.INCIDENTDATEEND: When a long-running incident ended. DNA, does not apply, on most rows; some hold just a month name. Stored as text.
cols.WHAT: A short description of what happened, like GPS jamming over the Baltic or Operation Doppelganger.
cols.C_WHERE: The country where it happened, like Germany, Poland or France.
cols.EVENTCATEGORY: The kind of incident, like Influence operation, Sabotage, Arson or Reconnaissance.
cols.EVENTCATEGORY2: A second kind, when there is one. Almost always Does not apply.
cols.APPARENTGOAL1: What the operation seemed to be after, like Disrupt daily life or Disrupt military aid to Ukraine.
cols.APPARENTGOAL2: A second apparent goal. Mostly Does not apply.
cols.TARGETTYPE: What was targeted, like shopping centres, social media, military sites or energy lines.
cols.TARGETTYPE2: A second target. Almost always Does not apply.
cols.DISPOSABLEAGENTSINVOLVED: Yes when hired one-off helpers carried it out, No or Unknown otherwise. Blank for most incidents.
cols.FOR_DISCUSSION: Yes when the researchers flagged the incident as open to debate.

INVESTIGATIONS__INTL_LEIDEN_RUSSIAN_OPS_.summary: 150 suspected Russian sabotage, spying and influence incidents in Europe from 2022 to 2025, as logged by researchers at Leiden University.
INVESTIGATIONS__INTL_LEIDEN_RUSSIAN_OPS_.row: One incident: one suspected Russian operation in Europe, with when, where, what kind and what it seemed to aim at.

cols.PAGE_URL: The web address of the page this row came from.
cols.PAGE_DIGEST: A 32-character fingerprint of a web page's content. The same code means the same page content.
cols.CAPTURE_TIMESTAMP_RAW: When the Wayback Machine saved the web page, as 14 digits: year, month, day, hour, minute, second, like 20260215143121. Stored as text.
cols.CAPTURED_AT: When the web page snapshot was taken, date and time.
cols.HREF: The link address exactly as written on the DOJ Epstein web page, often a short path like /epstein/search, plus social share links.
cols.RESOLVED_URL: The full web address the link points to, with justice.gov filled in for short paths. Includes Facebook, X and LinkedIn share links.
cols.LINK_TEXT: The words shown on the clickable link, like DOJ Disclosures or Facebook.
cols.FETCHED_AT_UTC: When the scraper downloaded the page, in UTC time. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

INVESTIGATIONS__XC_WAYBACK_REPLAY_DOJ_DE.summary: Links found on archived copies of Justice Department web pages, pulled from the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine.
INVESTIGATIONS__XC_WAYBACK_REPLAY_DOJ_DE.row: One link: one hyperlink found on one archived capture of a DOJ page.

cols.PAGE_URL: The web address of the page this row came from.
cols.PAGE_DIGEST: A 32-character fingerprint of a web page's content. The same code means the same page content.
cols.CAPTURE_TIMESTAMP_RAW: When the Wayback Machine saved the web page, as 14 digits: year, month, day, hour, minute, second, like 20260215143121. Stored as text.
cols.CAPTURED_AT: When the web page snapshot was taken, date and time.
cols.HREF: The link address exactly as written on the DOJ Epstein web page, often a short path like /epstein/search, plus social share links.
cols.RESOLVED_URL: The full web address the link points to, with justice.gov filled in for short paths. Includes Facebook, X and LinkedIn share links.
cols.LINK_TEXT: The words shown on the clickable link, like DOJ Disclosures or Facebook.
cols.FETCHED_AT_UTC: When the scraper downloaded the page, in UTC time. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

INVESTIGATIONS__XC_WAYBACK_REPLAY_DOJ_LI.summary: Links scraped from archived copies of Justice Department listing pages saved in the Wayback Machine.
INVESTIGATIONS__XC_WAYBACK_REPLAY_DOJ_LI.row: One link: one link found on one archived capture of a DOJ page.

cols.PERSON_NAME: The name of the person tied to the record. Some tables mix in company names or court case names, some leave it mostly blank, and four leave it empty.
cols.CASE_NAME: The name of the court case, like Chong v. Holder. Some are just the party's name.
cols.DECISION_DATE: The date the decision came down on the application or case. One table stores it as text with a time, and the AustLII table is empty.
cols.DISPOSITION: How the case ended. Federal court statistics tables use number codes, including -8, that need a lookup; the opinion table uses words like Affirmed but is mostly blank, and the Oyez table is empty.
cols.SUMMARY:
A text summary of the investigation or court case. Court tables keep web tags like

; most CourtListener rows are blank, and the Oyez table mostly holds the word None.
cols.SCRAPED_AT: When the page was scraped. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CASE_ID: Oyez's ID number for the case. Each row has its own.
cols.DOCKET: The Supreme Court docket number, like 70-5055.
cols.DATE: A key date for the case, mostly in 1972.
cols.TERM: The court term the case belongs to, mostly 1971.
cols.PETITIONER: The side that brought the case to the Supreme Court.
cols.RESPONDENT: The side answering the case, like United States or Florida.
cols.LOWER_COURT: The court that ruled before the Supreme Court took the case. Blank for most rows.
cols.ARGUMENT_DATE: The date the case was argued before the court. Blank for some rows.
cols.DECISION: The ruling. Empty in this table.
cols.MAJORITY_AUTHOR: The justice who wrote the majority opinion. Empty in this table.
cols.CITATION: The case's official citation. Empty in this table.
cols.ADVOCATE_NAMES: The lawyers who argued, in one comma-separated list.
cols.JUSTICE_VOTES: How each justice voted, packed into one block of structured text that needs unpacking.
cols.AUDIO_URL: A link to the audio of the oral argument. Blank for some rows.
cols.TRANSCRIPT_URL: A link to the case record on Oyez.
cols.HAS_AUDIO: Whether the case has audio. True on every row, so it tells you nothing.
cols.HAS_TRANSCRIPT: Whether the case has a transcript. True on every row, so it tells you nothing.

JUDICIARY__FED_OYEZ.summary: A 25-case sample of U.S. Supreme Court cases from Oyez, mostly from the 1971 term: the parties, the lawyers who argued, how each justice voted, and links to audio and transcripts.
JUDICIARY__FED_OYEZ.row: One case: one Supreme Court case.

cols.FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 06037. One table holds two-digit state codes instead, and nine tables leave it empty.
cols.STATE_ABBR: The state, as two letters like TX. Territories like PR and GU show up, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some tables add County, Parish or the state, like Garza County, TX, so clean it before matching. One table uses Undetermined as a filler, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.BLACK_JAIL_RATE: Black residents in jail relative to the Black population; values like 4545.45 point to a per-100,000 rate.
cols.WHITE_JAIL_RATE: White residents in jail relative to the white population; values like 132.99 point to a per-100,000 rate.
cols.OVERDOSE_METRIC: Band number that goes with the overdose rate range.
cols.OVERDOSE_PCTILE: The county's percentile rank on overdose, 0 to 1.
cols.JAIL_RATE: Jail incarceration rate; a few counties run above 30,000, so check the base before comparing.
cols.JAIL_RATE_YEAR: Year the jail rate comes from, mostly 2019 to 2024 but some as old as 1978.
cols.JAIL_POPULATION: Number of people in the county jail.
cols.JAIL_PCTILE: The county's percentile rank on jail rate, 0 to 1.
cols.IS_OVERDOSE_TOP_DECILE: true if the county is in the worst tenth for overdose.
cols.IS_JAIL_TOP_DECILE: true if the county is in the worst tenth for jail rate.
cols.DOUBLE_BURDEN: true if the county is in the worst tenth for both; 54 counties.

JUSTICE__COUNTY_DOUBLE_BURDEN.summary: Every US county, 3,029 of them, scored on two crises at once: drug overdose death rates and jail incarceration, with a flag for counties in the worst tenth on both.
JUSTICE__COUNTY_DOUBLE_BURDEN.row: One county: its overdose band, jail rate and whether it ranks worst on both.

cols.BUSINESS_NAME: The name of the business, when the row is a business. Mostly blank in the exclusion list, where most rows are people, and the firearms-license table often holds the word None instead.
cols.MAIL_STREET: The mailing street address, in capitals, often a P.O. box.
cols.MAIL_CITY: The city of the mailing address.
cols.MAIL_STATE: The state of the mailing address, as two letters.
cols.MAIL_ZIP_CODE: The mailing zip code, stored as text. ATF's feed drops leading zeros; that table zero-fills them back to 5 digits, or 9 for a zip+4.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.FFL_NUMBER: The full license number, built from the region, district, county, type, expiration and serial parts. Nearly every row has its own.
cols.LIC_REGION: The ATF region number, the first part of the license number.
cols.LIC_DISTRICT: The ATF district number from the license number.
cols.LIC_COUNTY: The county number from the license number; it needs the state to point at one county.
cols.LIC_TYPE: The license type number, like 1 or 7. The types need a lookup.
cols.LIC_EXPIRATION_CODE: A code for when the license expires, like 9C or 8E. The code needs a lookup.
cols.LIC_SEQUENCE: The license's serial number, the last part of the license number.
cols.LICENSE_NAME: The name on the license, often a company like WAL-MART STORES EAST LP; one company can hold many licenses.
cols.PREMISE_STREET: The street address of the licensed business.
cols.PREMISE_CITY: The city of the licensed business.
cols.PREMISE_STATE: The business's state, as two letters.
cols.PREMISE_ZIP_CODE: The business's zip code, zero-filled so 602 reads 00602.
cols.VOICE_PHONE: The business phone number, stored as text with a stray .0 on the end.

JUSTICE__FED_ATF_FFL.summary: Every federally licensed gun dealer, maker and importer: 77,514 licenses from the ATF.
JUSTICE__FED_ATF_FFL.row: One gun license at one business address.

cols.REPORT_DATE: The date the report was issued. One CMS table stores it as text like Q2, 2026.
cols.METRIC_NAME: The label for the number in METRIC_VALUE, pulled out of a spreadsheet. Messy: states, years, percent bands, even column headers like Name.
cols.METRIC_VALUE: The number that goes with METRIC_NAME. Mixes counts, dollars and fractions, so check the label before adding them up; almost always blank in the prison statistics table.
cols.FACILITY_TYPE: What kind of facility it is, like Hospital, Nursing home, Health Center, or Apartment in the HUD housing table. One table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_FIPS: The state's number code, like 48 or 06, which needs a lookup. Several tables drop the leading zero so 6 means 06, some rows hold other codes like C1, TX, 00 or N/A, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.SOURCE_URL: The web address the data was taken from. Mostly blank in the place-names table, where it is often just a site name like www.census.gov.
cols.CATEGORY: Who the number is about; Federal Bureau of Prisons on every row.
cols.METRIC_UNIT: Unit of the number; count on every row.

JUSTICE__FED_BOP_STATISTICS.summary: A broken scrape of Federal Bureau of Prisons web pages, 50 rows dated July 1, 2026. Only 2 rows hold a number, and the metric names are just 0, 1, 2 and so on.
JUSTICE__FED_BOP_STATISTICS.row: One scraped item: one line pulled from a Bureau of Prisons web page. Most rows carry no number.

cols.DATE_ADDED: The date the record was added to the source's list or database. In NIH RePORTER about four in ten rows share the one date 2011-03-09.
cols.NOTES: Free-text notes from the source, often caveats or web links.
cols.CVE_ID: The hole's standard ID, like CVE-2020-1054. Each row has its own value.
cols.VENDOR_PROJECT: The company or project that makes the software, like Microsoft or Cisco.
cols.PRODUCT: The affected product, like Windows. Some say Multiple Products.
cols.VULNERABILITY_NAME: A short name for the hole, like Microsoft Win32k Privilege Escalation Vulnerability.
cols.SHORT_DESCRIPTION: A sentence or two on what the hole lets an attacker do.
cols.REQUIRED_ACTION: What agencies must do, like Apply updates per vendor instructions.
cols.DUE_DATE: The deadline for federal agencies to fix the hole.
cols.KNOWN_RANSOMWARE_CAMPAIGN_USE: Known if ransomware gangs are known to use the hole, Unknown if not.
cols.CWES: The kind of software weakness, as codes like CWE-78. The codes need a lookup. Blank for about 10%.

JUSTICE__FED_CISA_KEV.summary: CISA's list of software security holes that hackers are known to be using, with the maker, product, the deadline for federal agencies to fix them and whether ransomware gangs use them.
JUSTICE__FED_CISA_KEV.row: One security hole: one known exploited vulnerability, by its CVE number.

cols.NAME: The name of whatever the row is about: a person, company, bank, county, address or dataset, depending on the table. Spelling is not cleaned, fillers like UNNAMED or None show up, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.ADDRESSES: One or more addresses tied to a sanctioned or screened person or company, as free text that is often just a city or country, like Moscow RU. Mostly blank in the two OpenSanctions tables.
cols.START_DATE: The date it began, like an award, trial, listing or court. Mostly blank in several tables, and 1969-12-31 shows up in the offshore-leaks table as a stand-in date.
cols.END_DATE: The date it ended or is set to end, like an award or a listing. Some are in the future.
cols.CALL_SIGN: The radio call sign of a ship or radio station, like WDB2084. Blank for most sanctions rows.
cols.VESSEL_TYPE: For a sanctioned ship, what kind it is, like Crude Oil Tanker. Blank for everything that is not a ship.
cols.VESSEL_FLAG: For a sanctioned ship, the country whose flag it flies, like Iran or Panama. Blank for everything that is not a ship.
cols.VESSEL_OWNER: For a sanctioned ship, who owns it, like NITC. Almost always blank.
cols.REMARKS: Free-text remarks added to the record, like exhibit notes on insider filings or extra sanctions details. Mostly blank in the insider and screening-list tables.
cols.NATIONALITIES: The country or countries the sanctioned person is a national of, spelled out like Russia in the UK list and as two-letter codes like RU in the screening list. Mostly blank.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.ENTRY_ID: The list's ID for the entry. Nearly every row has its own.
cols.SOURCE_LIST: Which list the entry is on, like Specially Designated Nationals or the Entity List.
cols.ENTITY_NUMBER: An entry number from the source list. Blank for entries from some lists.
cols.ENTITY_TYPE: Whether the entry is an Entity, Individual, Vessel or Aircraft. Blank for entries from some lists.
cols.PROGRAMS: The sanctions program codes the entry falls under, like RUSSIA-EO14024 or SDGT. The codes need a lookup.
cols.TITLE: A person's job or role, like Member of the State Duma. Nearly always blank.
cols.FEDERAL_REGISTER_NOTICE: The Federal Register notice that added the entry, like 83 FR 18112. Mostly blank.
cols.STANDARD_ORDER: A Y or N flag, with one lowercase y. Nearly always blank; what it marks needs a lookup.
cols.LICENSE_REQUIREMENT: Which exports to this party need a license, as written text. Mostly blank.
cols.LICENSE_POLICY: How license requests will be treated, like Presumption of denial, in several spellings. Mostly blank.
cols.SOURCE_LIST_URL: The web link for the list the entry came from.
cols.ALT_NAMES: Other names the entry goes by, separated by semicolons. Blank on about half the rows.
cols.CITIZENSHIPS: Citizenship countries, as two-letter codes like MX or RU. Nearly always blank.
cols.DATES_OF_BIRTH: Birth dates for listed people. Mostly blank.
cols.PLACES_OF_BIRTH: Birthplaces for listed people, like Moscow, Russia. Mostly blank.
cols.IDENTIFIER_DOCUMENTS: ID papers and extra notes run together as text, like passport numbers, gender, or secondary sanctions warnings.

JUSTICE__FED_CONSOLIDATED_SCREENING_LIST.summary: The U.S. government's merged list of people, companies, ships and planes barred from exports or under sanctions, pulled together from the federal screening lists.
JUSTICE__FED_CONSOLIDATED_SCREENING_LIST.row: One listed entry: one person, company, ship or plane on one list.

cols.DATE_CREATED: When the source created this record in its own database, not when the event happened.
cols.DATE_MODIFIED: When the source last changed this record in its own database.
cols.ID: CourtListener's number for this citation.
cols.VOLUME: The volume number of the law reporter, stored as a decimal number.
cols.REPORTER: The reporter's short name, like F.2d, So. 2d or WL.
cols.PAGE: The page number. Stored as text.
cols.TYPE: Citation type, as a number from 1 to 9. The codes need a lookup.
cols.CLUSTER_ID: The opinion group the citation points to. Links to CourtListener's opinion clusters.

JUSTICE__FED_COURTLISTENER_CITATIONS.summary: Every citation CourtListener has for a court opinion, like a volume, reporter and page, 18.1 million of them.
JUSTICE__FED_COURTLISTENER_CITATIONS.row: One citation: one volume, reporter and page that points to one opinion.

cols.ADDRESS1: The first line of the street address. Almost always blank in the courthouses table.
cols.ADDRESS2: The second address line, like a suite number. Mostly blank in the research awards table and empty in the other two.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY: The county, usually as a name like Harris, though some tables add the word County and the federal court tables use five-digit number codes, including 88888, which needs a lookup. The UK company table holds UK counties, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTRY_CODE: The country as a code, usually two letters like US, but some tables use three letters like AGO. The World Bank debt table also holds group codes like MIC and LMC that need a lookup.
cols.COURT_ID: CourtListener's short code for a court, like scotus, ca9 for the Ninth Circuit, or flmb for a bankruptcy court. Mostly blank in the judge positions table.
cols.ID: CourtListener's number for this courthouse. Each row has its own value.
cols.COURT_SEAT: t if this building is the court's main seat, f if not. Almost all say f.
cols.BUILDING_NAME: The building's name. Filled for only 3 rows, all the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.

JUSTICE__FED_COURTLISTENER_COURTHOUSES.summary: CourtListener's courthouse list, one row per court, but the street address is filled on only 4 rows; state and country are filled on nearly all.
JUSTICE__FED_COURTLISTENER_COURTHOUSES.row: One courthouse row tied to one court, usually holding only its state and country, not a street address.

cols.DATE_MODIFIED: When the source last changed this record in its own database.
cols.FULL_NAME: The full name of the person, like Nancy Pelosi. In the court table it is the court's full name.
cols.URL: A web link to the record's own page at the source.
cols.START_DATE: The date it began, like an award, trial, listing or court. Mostly blank in several tables, and 1969-12-31 shows up in the offshore-leaks table as a stand-in date.
cols.END_DATE: The date it ended or is set to end, like an award or a listing. Some are in the future.
cols.NOTES: Free-text notes from the source, often caveats or web links.
cols.ID: CourtListener's short ID for the court, like judcoun9; each row has its own value.
cols.PACER_COURT_ID: The court's ID in PACER, the federal court filing system. Blank on almost every row.
cols.PACER_HAS_RSS_FEED: t if the court's PACER site has a news feed, f if not. Blank on almost every row.
cols.PACER_RSS_ENTRY_TYPES: What the PACER feed covers, like all or order,motion. Blank on almost every row.
cols.DATE_LAST_PACER_CONTACT: When CourtListener last checked PACER. Empty in this table.
cols.FJC_COURT_ID: The court's code from the Federal Judicial Center. Blank on almost every row.
cols.IN_USE: t if CourtListener actively uses this court, f if not.
cols.HAS_OPINION_SCRAPER: t if CourtListener automatically collects this court's opinions, f if not.
cols.HAS_ORAL_ARGUMENT_SCRAPER: t if CourtListener automatically collects this court's oral argument audio, f if not.
cols.POSITION: A number used to sort courts in order.
cols.CITATION_STRING: The short form used in legal citations, like Wythe Cir. Ct.

cols.VERSION: For criminal cases, a version number for the record, mostly 0 to 3. Blank on civil cases.

cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.COMPANY: The company the record is about, like the one a consumer complained about or the one that won a research award. Blank in most rows of the FHFA tables.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.EFFECTIVE_DATE: The date something took effect, like a merger, a drug price, or a suspension.
cols.SUSPENSION_END_DATE: The date the company's suspension from doing business with the housing finance agencies ends. Blank on most rows.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.SUSPENSION_ORDER: The web path to the suspension order file on the regulator's site, like /sites/default/files/ plus a name. Each ban has its own.

JUSTICE__FED_FJC_ARTICLE_III_JUDGES.row: One federal judge: their background and each court appointment, spread across numbered columns.

cols.CIRCUIT: The federal appeals court region, numbered 1 to 11. Some tables add a leading zero, like 05.
cols.TAPE_YEAR: The year of the court data release the row came from, like 2020. 2099 shows up and is not a real year.
cols.AGENCY: The government agency tied to the record, written differently by table: EPA or State, a full department name, a bracketed list in the Federal Register, or number codes in the federal appeals table, where most rows hold -9.
cols.TRANSFER_DATE: The date the case was transferred to another court. Nearly always blank in the civil table, mostly blank in the appeals table.
cols.DISPOSITION: How the case ended. Federal court statistics tables use number codes, including -8, that need a lookup; the opinion table uses words like Affirmed but is mostly blank, and the Oyez table is empty.
cols.HEARING_DATE: The date of the hearing: the court's hearing in appeals cases, the Senate hearing in judge records. Often blank.
cols.JUDGMENT_DATE: The date the court issued its judgment. Empty in the European human rights court table.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.APPEAL_RECORD_ID: A made-up ID for the appeal record, built from the court, docket, reopen number, snapshot year and docket date. Each record has its own. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.DOCKET: The appeals court's docket number for the case. Pair it with the circuit to find one case; the same case can repeat across yearly snapshots.
cols.REOPEN: How many times the appeal was reopened, like 1 or 2, or a letter code like M or S. A -8 means missing.
cols.DOCKET_DATE: The day the appeal was put on the appeals court docket.
cols.US_APPELLANT: 1 when the United States is the side appealing, 0 when not.
cols.APPELLANT: The name of the side appealing, usually the first party's last name, like WILLIAMS. Blank for about a quarter of rows.
cols.US_APPELLEE: 1 when the United States is the side answering the appeal, 0 when not.
cols.APPELLEE: The name of the side answering the appeal, often UNITED STATES OF AME or an attorney general like HOLDER or GARLAND. Some rows hold -8 for missing.
cols.APPEAL_TYPE: A number code for the kind of appeal, like criminal, civil or immigration. The codes need a lookup.
cols.ORIGINATING_PROCEEDING: A number code for the kind of trial court proceeding the appeal came from. A -8 means missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.JURISDICTION: A number code for why the case is in federal court. A -9 means missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NATURE_OF_SUIT: A three-digit code for what the civil case was about, like 530 or 440. A -9 means missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.OFFENSE: A four-digit code for the crime in criminal appeals. Mostly -9, meaning not a criminal case or missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.DISTRICT_CIRCUIT: The circuit number of the trial court the appeal came from. A -8 means missing.
cols.DISTRICT_COURT: A two-character code for the federal trial court the appeal came from, like 73 or 3A. A -8 means missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.DISTRICT_OFFICE: The trial court's office number within its district. A -8 means missing.
cols.DISTRICT_DOCKET: The trial court's docket number for the original case. A -8 means missing.
cols.DISTRICT_DEFENDANT_NUMBER: Which defendant in the trial case this appeal is for, like 1 or 2. Mostly -8, meaning missing.
cols.FEDERAL_CAPACITY: Y on only a handful of rows; every other row is -8, missing. Tells you almost nothing.
cols.DISTRICT_DOCKET_DATE: The day the original case was filed in the trial court. Blank for about a quarter of rows.
cols.APPEAL_DATE: The day the notice of appeal was filed. Blank for about a quarter of rows.
cols.TRANSFER_CODE: A one-letter code for the kind of record: J, E or R. The codes need a lookup.
cols.FILING_FEE_STATUS: FP when the appeal was filed without paying the fee because the person is poor. Otherwise -8.
cols.OUTCOME: A number code for how the appeal came out, like affirmed or reversed. Close to half are -8, missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.PROCEDURAL_TERMINATION: A number code for how an appeal ended without a ruling on the merits. Mostly -8, missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.METHOD: A number code for how the appeal was decided, like after oral argument or on the briefs. Mostly -8, missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.PUBLICATION_STATUS: A number code for whether the decision was published. A -8 means missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.OPINION_DISPOSITION: A number code for the kind of opinion issued. Mostly -8, missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.JOINT_APPEAL: A number code for whether this appeal was joined with others. Mostly 0. A -8 means missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.CONSOLIDATED_DOCKET: The docket number of the lead case this appeal was merged into. Mostly -8, missing.
cols.BRIEFS_FILED: The day the last brief was filed, written as month/day/year text. Blank for most rows.
cols.SUBMISSION_DATE: The day the appeal was handed to the judges to decide. Blank for about half of rows.
cols.OPINION: A number code for the kind of opinion. Almost all -8, missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.JUDGE_1_INVOLVEMENT: A letter code for the first judge's role, like A or P. A -8 means missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.JUDGE_2_INVOLVEMENT: A letter code for the second judge's role, like P or F. A -8 means missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.JUDGE_3_INVOLVEMENT: A letter code for the third judge's role, like P or A. A -8 means missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.PRO_SE_FILED: A number code for whether a side had no lawyer when the appeal was filed, 0 to 3. The codes need a lookup.
cols.PRO_SE_TERMINATED: A number code for whether a side had no lawyer when the appeal ended, 0 to 3. A -8 means missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.STATUS_CODE: A one-letter record status, L or S. The codes need a lookup.
cols.EN_BANC: Y when the full appeals court heard the case, N when a panel did. A -8 means missing.
cols.TERMINATION_TYPE: A number code for the kind of appeal at the time it ended. The codes need a lookup.
cols.TERMINATION_OR_PROCEDURAL_SUBMISSION: A number code for the trial court proceeding type, recorded at the end of the appeal. Mostly -8, missing. The codes need a lookup.
cols.TERMINATION_FEE_STATUS: FP when the appeal ended with the fee waived for a poor filer, N when not. A -8 means missing.

JUSTICE__FED_FJC_IDB_APPELLATE.summary: Federal appeals court cases from the Federal Judicial Center's case database, about 988,000 records covering who appealed, the trial case it came from, the judges' roles and how it ended.
JUSTICE__FED_FJC_IDB_APPELLATE.row: One appeal record: one appeals court docket as it stood in one yearly snapshot of the database.

cols.CIRCUIT: The federal appeals court region, numbered 1 to 11. Some tables add a leading zero, like 05.
cols.FILE_DATE: The date the case was filed in federal court.
cols.TOTAL_ASSETS: Total assets in dollars, whether of a credit union, hospital, bankruptcy filer, or labor union.
cols.TOTAL_LIABILITIES: Total debts owed, in dollars, by the hospital, bankrupt debtor or union. Most union rows read 0.
cols.CLOSE_DATE: The date the investigation, court case or grant opportunity closed. For grants it is the application deadline.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CASE_SNAPSHOT_ID: A made-up ID for one case in one snapshot. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CASE_KEY: The ID for one bankruptcy case, built from court and docket. The same case shows up once in each snapshot it was in.
cols.SNAPSHOT: The date of the Federal Judicial Center file this row came from. There are six, from 2021-09-30 to 2026-03-31.
cols.SNAPSHOT_FILED_FLAG: 1 if the case was filed during this snapshot's year, 0 if not.
cols.SNAPSHOT_PENDING_FLAG: 1 if the case was still open at the snapshot date, 0 if not.
cols.SNAPSHOT_CLOSED_FLAG: 1 if the case closed during this snapshot's year, 0 if not.
cols.DISTRICT: The federal court district, as a code like 52 or 3E. Needs a lookup.
cols.OFFICE: The court's office within the district, as a number. Needs a lookup.
cols.DOCKET: The court's case number within the office. Pair it with district and office to find one case.
cols.DOCKET_GENERATION: Usually 0; r on a small share of rows. The codes need a lookup.
cols.DOCKET_SEQUENCE: Usually 0; 1 to 7 on a small share of rows, marking related docket numbers.
cols.ORIGIN: How the case came to this court, as a code i, s or t. Needs a lookup and is blank on almost every row.
cols.ORIGINAL_FILING_DATE: The date the bankruptcy was first filed.
cols.FILING_CALENDAR_YEAR: The calendar year the case was filed.
cols.FILING_FISCAL_YEAR: The federal court fiscal year the case was filed.
cols.ORIGINAL_FILING_CHAPTER: The bankruptcy chapter at filing, like 7, 13 or 11. Chapter 15 shows as 15m or 15a.
cols.ORIGINAL_FILING_SUBCHAPTER: V when the case was filed as a small-business Subchapter V case. Blank otherwise.
cols.CURRENT_CHAPTER: The bankruptcy chapter now, like 7, 13 or 11. Differs from the filing chapter when a case converted.
cols.CURRENT_SUBCHAPTER: V when the case is now a small-business Subchapter V case. Blank otherwise.
cols.ORIGINAL_NATURE_OF_DEBT: What kind of debt it was at filing, as a code c, b or o. Needs a lookup.
cols.NATURE_OF_DEBT: What kind of debt it is now, as a code c, b or o. Needs a lookup.
cols.JOINT_FILING: y if a married couple filed together, n if not.
cols.DEBTOR1_ZIP: The first debtor's ZIP code, as nine digits, usually ending in 0000.
cols.DEBTOR1_COUNTY: The first debtor's county, as a five-digit county number code. Needs a lookup.
cols.ORIGINAL_DEBTOR1_FILING_PRO_SE: y if the first debtor filed without a lawyer, n if not.
cols.DEBTOR1_FILING_PRO_SE: y if the first debtor is recorded as filing without a lawyer, n if not.
cols.DEBTOR1_CHANGE_DATE: The date the first debtor's details changed. Blank on almost every row.
cols.DEBTOR2_ZIP: The second debtor's ZIP code, as nine digits. Only filled on joint filings.
cols.DEBTOR2_COUNTY: The second debtor's county, as a five-digit county number code. Only filled on joint filings.
cols.ORIGINAL_DEBTOR2_FILING_PRO_SE: y if the second debtor filed without a lawyer, n if not. Only filled on joint filings.
cols.DEBTOR2_FILING_PRO_SE: y if the second debtor is recorded as filing without a lawyer, n if not. Only filled on joint filings.
cols.DEBTOR2_CHANGE_DATE: The date the second debtor's details changed. Blank on almost every row.
cols.ORIGINAL_FEE_STATUS: How the filing fee was handled at filing, as a letter like p, i, u, w or c. Needs a lookup.
cols.FEE_STATUS: How the filing fee was handled later, as a letter like p or c. Needs a lookup and is blank on more than half the rows.
cols.CASE_TYPE: The kind of case, as a code v, i or 0. Almost always v. Needs a lookup.
cols.ORIGINAL_DEBTOR_TYPE: Who filed at filing, as a letter like i, u, n or p. Needs a lookup; a few rows hold junk like X, ? or 6.
cols.DEBTOR_TYPE: Who filed, as a letter like i, u, n or p. Needs a lookup; a few rows hold junk like ? or !.
cols.NATURE_OF_BUSINESS: The business type for business debtors, as a letter like n, h or r. Needs a lookup and is blank on most rows.
cols.PRIOR_FILING: Y if the debtor had filed for bankruptcy before, N if not.
cols.ORIGINAL_ESTIMATED_ASSETS: The debtor's estimated assets at filing, as a size bracket letter like A, B or C. The brackets need a lookup.
cols.ESTIMATED_ASSETS: The debtor's estimated assets, as a size bracket letter like A, B or C. The brackets need a lookup.
cols.ORIGINAL_ESTIMATED_LIABILITIES: The debtor's estimated debts at filing, as a size bracket letter like A, B or C. The brackets need a lookup.
cols.ESTIMATED_LIABILITIES: The debtor's estimated debts, as a size bracket letter like A, B or C. The brackets need a lookup.
cols.ORIGINAL_ESTIMATED_CREDITORS: How many creditors the debtor owed at filing, as a size bracket letter, almost always A. Needs a lookup.
cols.ESTIMATED_CREDITORS: How many creditors the debtor owed, as a size bracket letter, almost always A. Needs a lookup.
cols.ORIGINAL_ASSET_CASE: y if the case had assets to pay creditors at filing, n if not, u for unknown.
cols.ASSET_CASE: y if the case has assets to pay creditors, n if not, u for unknown.
cols.SMALL_BUSINESS: y if the debtor is a small business, n if not. Blank on almost every row.
cols.PREPACKAGED: Marks a prepackaged Chapter 11 plan, with codes B, Y, P or N. Needs a lookup and is blank on almost every row.
cols.REAL_PROPERTY: Dollar value of land and buildings the debtor listed. Zero on about half the rows.
cols.PERSONAL_PROPERTY: Dollar value of other property the debtor listed, like cars and bank accounts.
cols.SECURED_CLAIMS: Dollars owed on debts backed by property, like mortgages and car loans.
cols.UNSECURED_PRIORITY_CLAIMS: Dollars owed on unsecured debts that get paid first, like taxes and child support. Zero on most rows.
cols.UNSECURED_NONPRIORITY_CLAIMS: Dollars owed on ordinary unsecured debts, like credit cards and medical bills.
cols.DEBT_DISCHARGED: Dollars of debt wiped out by the bankruptcy.
cols.DEBT_NOT_DISCHARGED: Dollars of debt the bankruptcy did not wipe out. Zero on about half the rows.
cols.TOTAL_DEBT: Total dollars of debt in the case.
cols.COUNT_MONTHLY_INCOME: The debtor's monthly income as the court counts it, in dollars, stored as text. Zero on a small share of rows.
cols.AVG_MONTHLY_INCOME: The debtor's average monthly income, in dollars.
cols.AVG_MONTHLY_EXPENSES: The debtor's average monthly expenses, in dollars.
cols.SOURCE_CASE: The case number this case came from, when it was moved or split. Blank on almost every row.
cols.DESTINATION_CASE: The case number this case was sent to. Blank on almost every row.
cols.CONSOLIDATION_LEAD: The lead case this one was merged into. Blank on almost every row.
cols.JOINT_ADMINISTRATION_LEAD: The lead case when several related cases are run together, common in big company bankruptcies. Blank on almost every row.
cols.FILING_CMECF_VERSION: The version of the court's filing software when the case was filed, like 10.7.1.1. Rarely useful.
cols.CLOSING_CALENDAR_YEAR: The calendar year the case closed. Blank on open cases.
cols.CLOSING_FISCAL_YEAR: The federal court fiscal year the case closed. Blank on open cases.
cols.CLOSING_CHAPTER: The bankruptcy chapter when the case closed, like 7 or 13. Blank on open cases.
cols.CLOSING_SUBCHAPTER: V when the case closed as a Subchapter V case. Blank otherwise.
cols.DEBTOR1_CLOSING_PRO_SE: y if the first debtor had no lawyer at closing, n if not. Blank on open cases.
cols.DEBTOR1_FINAL_DISPOSITION: How the case ended for the first debtor, as a letter like A, T, K or I. Needs a lookup; blank on open cases.
cols.DEBTOR1_FINAL_DISPOSITION_DATE: The date the case ended for the first debtor. Blank on open cases.
cols.DEBTOR1_FINAL_DISPOSITION_CALENDAR_YEAR: The calendar year the case ended for the first debtor.
cols.DEBTOR1_FINAL_DISPOSITION_FISCAL_YEAR: The court fiscal year the case ended for the first debtor.
cols.DEBTOR2_CLOSING_PRO_SE: y if the second debtor had no lawyer at closing, n if not. Blank on most rows.
cols.DEBTOR2_FINAL_DISPOSITION: How the case ended for the second debtor, as a letter like A or T. Needs a lookup; blank on most rows.
cols.DEBTOR2_FINAL_DISPOSITION_DATE: The date the case ended for the second debtor. Blank on most rows.
cols.DEBTOR2_FINAL_DISPOSITION_CALENDAR_YEAR: The calendar year the case ended for the second debtor.
cols.DEBTOR2_FINAL_DISPOSITION_FISCAL_YEAR: The court fiscal year the case ended for the second debtor.
cols.CHAPTER11_DIVIDEND: The percent of debts paid back to creditors in a Chapter 11 case, like 100 or 10. Blank on almost every row.
cols.CHAPTER11_FUTURE_PAYMENTS: y if a Chapter 11 plan promises future payments, n if not. Blank on almost every row.
cols.CLOSING_CMECF_VERSION: The version of the court's filing software when the case closed. Rarely useful.
cols.TAX_EXEMPT: Y if the debtor is a tax-exempt group, N if not. Almost always N.

JUSTICE__FED_FJC_IDB_BANKRUPTCY.summary: Federal bankruptcy cases from the Federal Judicial Center's records, seen in six snapshots: each September from 2021 to 2025, plus March 2026. Covers chapter, debts, assets and how each case ended.
JUSTICE__FED_FJC_IDB_BANKRUPTCY.row: One bankruptcy case as it stood in one snapshot: the same case can appear once per snapshot.

cols.CIRCUIT: The federal appeals court region, numbered 1 to 11. Some tables add a leading zero, like 05.
cols.TAPE_YEAR: The year of the court data release the row came from, like 2020. 2099 shows up and is not a real year.
cols.FILE_DATE: The date the case was filed in federal court.
cols.JURY_DEMAND: Who asked for a jury. CourtListener spells it out like Plaintiff, Both or None and is almost always blank; the FJC table uses letter codes like P, N, B, D, Y and J that need a lookup, with -8 for missing.
cols.CLASS_ACTION: Whether the case was a class action. The linked table says t; the FJC table says 1, with -8 for missing.
cols.FILING_JUDGE: Meant to name the judge assigned when the case was filed, but it is empty in both tables.
cols.COUNTY: The county, usually as a name like Harris, though some tables add the word County and the federal court tables use five-digit number codes, including 88888, which needs a lookup. The UK company table holds UK counties, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.PLAINTIFF: The name of the side that sued, often just a surname like JOHNSON or the government written many ways like USA, US or U S A.
cols.DEFENDANT: The name of the side being sued, often cut short with ET AL. In the federal court case table, -8 stands in for a missing name.
cols.TRANSFER_DATE: The date the case was transferred to another court. Nearly always blank in the civil table, mostly blank in the appeals table.
cols.TRANSFER_OFFICE: A court office code tied to a transferred case, as a number that needs a lookup. Almost always -8 or blank, meaning missing.
cols.TRANSFER_DOCKET: The case number at the court the case was transferred from or to. -8 means none or missing.
cols.TRANSFER_ORIGIN: A number code for where a transferred case came from; needs the FJC codebook, and -8 means missing. Almost always blank in the linked table.
cols.TERM_DATE: The date the case was closed out in court. Blank in most criminal rows.
cols.TERM_JUDGE: Meant to name the judge on the case when it closed, but it is empty in both tables.
cols.PROCEDURAL_PROGRESS: A number code for how far the case got before it ended; needs the FJC codebook, and -8 means missing.
cols.DISPOSITION: How the case ended. Federal court statistics tables use number codes, including -8, that need a lookup; the opinion table uses words like Affirmed but is mostly blank, and the Oyez table is empty.
cols.AMOUNT_RECEIVED: Money awarded in the case, in thousands of dollars. 9999 is the top code and -8 means missing.
cols.JUDGMENT: A number code for who won the judgment; needs the FJC codebook, and -8 means missing.
cols.PRO_SE: A number code, 0 to 3, for which side had no lawyer, if any; needs the FJC codebook, and -8 means missing.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CASE_RECORD_ID: A made-up ID for one case record in one yearly file. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.DISTRICT: The federal court district, as a code like 13 or 3C. Needs a lookup.
cols.OFFICE: The court's office within the district, as a number. Needs a lookup.
cols.DOCKET: The court's case number within the office. Pair it with district and office to find a case.
cols.ORIGIN: How the case got to this court, as a number code like 1, 2 or 13. Needs a lookup.
cols.FILE_DATE_USE: The month the case was filed, as a text date like 07/01/2020. Always the first of the month.
cols.JURISDICTION: Why the case is in federal court, as a code 1 to 5, plus one stray -8. Needs a lookup.
cols.NATURE_OF_SUIT: What the case is about, as a three-digit code like 365 or 550. Needs a lookup.
cols.STATUTE_TITLE: The US Code title the case is brought under, like 28 or 42. Blank on most rows.
cols.STATUTE_SECTION: The US Code section, like 1332 or 1983. -8 fills some rows and looks like a missing-value placeholder.
cols.STATUTE_SUBSECTION: A short code like PL or PR. -8 fills most rows and looks like a missing-value placeholder; codes need a lookup.
cols.RESIDENCE: Where the parties live, as a number code. -8 fills most rows and looks like a missing-value placeholder.
cols.AMOUNT_DEMANDED: Money the plaintiff asked for, as a number that needs a lookup for its units. Mostly 0; -8 and 9999 look like placeholders.
cols.FILING_MAGISTRATE: Meant to hold the magistrate judge at filing, but it is empty.
cols.ARBITRATION: An arbitration code like E, M or V. -8 fills almost every row; codes need a lookup.
cols.MDL_DOCKET: The multi-district litigation number, like 2885, when the case is part of one. -8 fills most rows.
cols.TERM_DATE_USE: The month the case ended, as a text date like 12/01/2024. Blank on open cases.
cols.TERM_CLASS_ACTION: Class action code at the end, 2 or 3. -8 fills almost every row; codes need a lookup.
cols.TERM_MAGISTRATE: Meant to hold the magistrate judge at the end, but it is empty.
cols.NATURE_OF_JUDGMENT: What kind of judgment, as a code 0 to 6. -8 fills many rows; codes need a lookup.
cols.ISSUE_JOINED_DATE: The date both sides had filed their first papers. Blank on most rows.
cols.PRETRIAL_DATE: The date of the pretrial conference. Blank on almost every row.
cols.TRIAL_BEGAN_DATE: The date the trial began. Blank on almost every row, since few cases go to trial.
cols.TRIAL_END_DATE: The date the trial ended. Blank on almost every row.
cols.TERM_ARBITRATION: Arbitration code at the end, like E, M or V. -8 fills almost every row; codes need a lookup.
cols.IN_FORMA_PAUPERIS: FP if the plaintiff was allowed to sue without paying fees. -8 fills most filled rows.
cols.STATUS_CODE: L or S. S rows match the count of the pending-cases file; codes need a lookup.

JUSTICE__FED_FJC_IDB_CIVIL.summary: Federal civil court cases from the Federal Judicial Center's yearly files, with case type, dates and how they ended. Open cases sit in a pending file marked with year 2099.
JUSTICE__FED_FJC_IDB_CIVIL.row: One civil case as recorded in one yearly file: the court, the case type, the dates and the outcome.

cols.FISCAL_YEAR: The government fiscal year the row covers, like 2023, sometimes written as FY2026 or 2024 YTD. One ICE table holds small numbers that are not years, a DHS table leaves it mostly blank, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.TAPE_YEAR: The year of the court data release the row came from, like 2020. 2099 shows up and is not a real year.
cols.CIRCUIT: The federal appeals court region, numbered 1 to 11. Some tables add a leading zero, like 05.
cols.FILE_DATE: The date the case was filed in federal court.
cols.FILING_JUDGE: Meant to name the judge assigned when the case was filed, but it is empty in both tables.
cols.COUNTY: The county, usually as a name like Harris, though some tables add the word County and the federal court tables use five-digit number codes, including 88888, which needs a lookup. The UK company table holds UK counties, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.TRANSFER_OFFICE: A court office code tied to a transferred case, as a number that needs a lookup. Almost always -8 or blank, meaning missing.
cols.TRANSFER_DOCKET: The case number at the court the case was transferred from or to. -8 means none or missing.
cols.TERM_DATE: The date the case was closed out in court. Blank in most criminal rows.
cols.TERM_JUDGE: Meant to name the judge on the case when it closed, but it is empty in both tables.
cols.LOAD_DATE: When the record was loaded, as the table itself reports it: a date or a date and time.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.DEFENDANT_RECORD_ID: Generated ID for each defendant record. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.DEFENDANT_LINK_KEY: Code that ties together rows for the same defendant in the same case.
cols.CASE_LINK_KEY: Code that ties together rows for the same case, across all its defendants.
cols.REOPEN_SEQUENCE: How many times the case was reopened: 0 for the original filing, then 1, 2 or 3.
cols.DISTRICT: Federal court district, as a two-character code like 41 or 3C that needs a lookup.
cols.OFFICE: Court office within the district where the case was filed, as a one-digit code.
cols.DOCKET: Docket number of the case within its court office.
cols.DEFENDANT_NUMBER: The defendant's number within the case: 001 for the first defendant, 002 for the second, and so on.
cols.CT_DEFENDANTS: A defendant count field from the court file, stored as text. -8 is a placeholder for blank on over half of rows.
cols.DEFENDANT_NAME: The defendant's name. Empty in this table: filled 0.
cols.TYPE_REG: Case type on the main docket, CR or MJ.
cols.TYPE_TRN: Case type on the docket of a transferred case, CR or MJ. -8 is a placeholder for blank on almost all rows.
cols.TYPE_MAG: Case type on the magistrate judge's docket, MJ or CR. -8 is a placeholder for blank on most rows.
cols.MAGISTRATE_DOCKET: Docket number of the earlier magistrate judge case, if any. -8 is a placeholder for blank on most rows.
cols.MAGISTRATE_DEFENDANT_NUMBER: The defendant's number in the earlier magistrate judge case. -8 is a placeholder for blank on most rows.
cols.STATUS_CODE: Record status, E or J; the codes need a lookup. The E count matches the pending flag in CT_PN.
cols.FUGITIVE_STATUS: Whether the defendant was a fugitive: N, Y or Z; Z needs a lookup.
cols.FUGITIVE_START_DATE: Date the defendant became a fugitive. Mostly blank.
cols.FUGITIVE_END_DATE: Date the defendant stopped being a fugitive. Mostly blank.
cols.PROCEEDING_DATE: Date of the court proceeding named in PROCEEDING_CODE.
cols.PROCEEDING_CODE: Type of court proceeding, as a number code that needs a lookup.
cols.APP_DATE: Date that goes with the event in APP_CODE. Blank on about 30% of rows.
cols.APP_CODE: Code for an appearance or appointment event, digits and letters that need a lookup. -8 is a placeholder for blank.
cols.FILING_COUNSEL: Type of defense lawyer when the case was filed, as a number code that needs a lookup.

JUSTICE__FED_FJC_IDB_CRIMINAL.summary: Every federal criminal defendant in the Federal Judicial Center's Integrated Database, 6.3 million records, with the charges at filing, how each charge ended and the sentence, captured in yearly snapshots.

cols.DATE_FILED: The date the case, opinion, or document was filed. One settlements table stores messy text like 7/26/2019 or N/A.
cols.TOPIC: A text description of what the dataset covers. Filled only in the FAO table; the FTC and Densho tables are empty.
cols.DOCUMENT_URL: A web link to the original document, like the SEC filing or the enforcement order.
cols.EIN: The organization's 9-digit federal tax ID number, stored as text. Some rows hold 000000000 as a filler or only 8 digits because a leading zero was lost, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.ACTION_NAME: The case or document name, like HomeAdvisor, In the Matter of.
cols.RESPONDENT: Meant to hold who the FTC acted against, but it is empty.
cols.CASE_TYPE: Meant to hold the case type, but it is empty.
cols.STATUS: Meant to hold the case status, but it is empty.

JUSTICE__FED_FTC_DATASETS.summary: FTC cases and statements from the agency's website, with names, dates and links. The topic, EIN, respondent, type and status columns are empty.
JUSTICE__FED_FTC_DATASETS.row: One FTC case or document: its name, date and link.

cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.DISTRICT: Federal district where the MDL sits, a short code like CAN or NYS.
cols.MDL_NO: MDL number. Each row has its own value.
cols.LITIGATION: Name of the litigation, like IN RE: ... Antitrust Litigation.
cols.PENDING_CASES: Cases still pending in the MDL. Blank on some rows.
cols.TOTAL_CASES: Total cases ever in the MDL. Blank on about a quarter of rows.

JUSTICE__FED_JPML_PENDING_MDLS.row: One MDL: one group of related federal lawsuits handled by one judge.

cols.CALL_SIGN: The radio call sign of a ship or radio station, like WDB2084. Blank for most sanctions rows.
cols.VESSEL_TYPE: For a sanctioned ship, what kind it is, like Crude Oil Tanker. Blank for everything that is not a ship.
cols.TONNAGE: The ship's size in tons. Mostly blank.
cols.VESSEL_FLAG: For a sanctioned ship, the country whose flag it flies, like Iran or Panama. Blank for everything that is not a ship.
cols.VESSEL_OWNER: For a sanctioned ship, who owns it, like NITC. Almost always blank.
cols.IMO_NUMBER: The ship's 7-digit IMO number, a permanent international hull ID. The AIS table puts IMO in front and often holds the filler IMO0000000; the sanctions tables leave it off and are mostly blank.
cols.REMARKS: Free-text remarks added to the record, like exhibit notes on insider filings or extra sanctions details. Mostly blank in the insider and screening-list tables.
cols.IS_INDIVIDUAL: True if the listed party is a person, False if it is a company or group.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.ENT_NUM: Treasury's entry number for the listing. Nearly every row has its own.
cols.SDN_NAME: The listed name; people are written LAST, First.
cols.SDN_TYPE: individual, vessel or aircraft. Blank for companies and groups.
cols.ENTITY_KIND: The kind of listing: organization, individual, vessel or aircraft. It fills in organization where SDN_TYPE is blank.
cols.PROGRAM: The sanctions program codes, like RUSSIA-EO14024 or SDGT; several can be packed in with brackets. The codes need a lookup.
cols.TITLE: A person's job or role, like Member of the State Duma. Nearly always blank.
cols.GROSS_REGISTERED_TONNAGE: A ship's size in gross registered tons. Nearly always blank.
