cols.AGE: The person's age in years, or an age group like 15-24 years in the CDC table. Stored as text in some tables.
cols.GENDER: The person's sex, written differently by table: Male or Female, M or F, m or f, or Male Owned for businesses. Some rows say Unknown or Unanswered, the clinical trials table mostly says ALL, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.RACE: The person's race as the source recorded it: spelled out like White or Asian, or as short codes like W, B or mena that need a lookup. Many rows say Unknown or Unanswered.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY: The county, usually as a name like Harris, though some tables add the word County and the federal court tables use five-digit number codes, including 88888, which needs a lookup. The UK company table holds UK counties, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.ID: The Washington Post's ID for the shooting.
cols.VICTIM_NAME: The name of the person killed. Blank on a few rows where the name is unknown.
cols.THREAT_TYPE: What the person was doing, like shoot, threat, point or attack.
cols.FLEE_STATUS: Whether the person was fleeing: not, car, foot or other. Blank on some rows.
cols.ARMED_WITH: What the person had, like gun, knife, unarmed or vehicle.
cols.MENTAL_ILLNESS_RELATED: Always false in this table, which looks like a load problem, not a real answer. Do not use it.
cols.BODY_CAMERA_PRESENT: Always false in this table, which looks like a load problem, not a real answer. Do not use it.
cols.RACE_SOURCE: How the person's race was found, like photo or public_record. Mostly not_available.

JUSTICE__XC_WAPO_FATAL_FORCE.summary: People shot and killed by US police, as tracked by The Washington Post.
JUSTICE__XC_WAPO_FATAL_FORCE.row: One person shot and killed by police: who, when, where, and what they were doing.

cols.ACK_ID: The Labor Department's receipt number for one Form 5500 pension plan filing, starting with the date and time filed. Joins the main form to its schedules.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.SB_PLAN_YEAR_BEGIN_DATE: First day of the plan year this filing covers; almost all start in 2024.
cols.SB_TAX_PRD: Last day of the plan's tax year for this filing.
cols.SB_PN: Plan number the employer gives this plan, like 001 or 002.
cols.SB_EIN: The employer's federal tax ID number.
cols.SB_PLAN_TYPE_CODE: Plan type, a code 1, 2 or 3 that needs a lookup; nearly all are 1.
cols.SB_CNT_PARTCP_PR_YR_CD: Code 1, 2 or 3 for how the participant count was taken; codes need a lookup.
cols.SB_VALUE_DATE: Date the plan's assets and pension debts were valued.
cols.SB_CURR_VALUE_AST_01_AMT: Market value of the plan's assets on the valuation date, in dollars.
cols.SB_ACTRL_VALUE_AST_AMT: Actuarial value of the plan's assets, a smoothed figure used for funding rules, in dollars.
cols.SB_RTD_PARTCP_CNT: Number of retirees and survivors already getting a pension. 0 on most filings.
cols.SB_RTD_FNDNG_TGT_AMT: Value of pensions owed to retirees and survivors already being paid, in dollars. 0 on most filings.
cols.SB_TERM_PARTCP_CNT: Number of former workers who left with a pension due later.
cols.SB_TERM_FNDNG_TGT_AMT: Value of pensions owed to those former workers, in dollars.
cols.SB_ACT_NONVSTD_FNDNG_TGT_AMT: Value of not-yet-vested pensions for current workers. Empty in this table: filled 0.
cols.SB_ACT_VSTD_FNDNG_TGT_AMT: Value of vested pensions earned so far by current workers, in dollars.
cols.SB_ACT_PARTCP_CNT: Number of current workers in the plan.
cols.SB_LIAB_ACT_TOT_FNDNG_TGT_AMT: Total value of pensions earned so far by current workers, in dollars.
cols.SB_TOT_PARTCP_CNT: Total people in the plan: current workers, former workers and retirees.
cols.SB_TOT_FNDNG_TGT_AMT: Total value of all pensions earned so far, the plan's funding target, in dollars.
cols.SB_PLAN_AT_RISK_IND: 1 if the plan is flagged at-risk for low funding, 0 if not. Mostly blank, and almost always 0.
cols.SB_TGT_DISREGARD_ASSUMP_AMT: Funding target of an at-risk plan figured without the at-risk assumptions, in dollars. Filled on only 21 filings.
cols.SB_TGT_REFLECT_ASSUMP_AMT: Funding target of an at-risk plan figured with the at-risk assumptions, in dollars. Filled on only 21 filings.
cols.SB_EFF_INT_RATE_PRCNT: Effective interest rate used to value the pensions, as a percent.
cols.SB_TGT_NRML_COST_01_AMT: Target normal cost: the value of pensions workers earn this year, plus expenses, in dollars.
cols.SB_SIGNATURE_DATE: Date the actuary signed the filing.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_NAME_LINE: Name of the actuary who signed, sometimes with credentials after it.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_US_ADDRESS1: The actuary's street address, sometimes a P.O. box.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_US_ADDRESS2: Second address line for the actuary, like a suite. Mostly blank.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_US_STATE: The actuary's state, as two letters.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_US_ZIP: The actuary's ZIP code, five or nine digits.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_FOREIGN_ADDRESS1: Foreign street address for the actuary. Filled on only one filing, and that one is a US address.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_FOREIGN_ADDRESS2: Foreign second address line. Filled on only one filing.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_FOREIGN_CITY: Foreign city for the actuary. Filled on only one filing, and it is a US city.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_FOREIGN_PROV_STATE: Foreign province or state. Filled on only one filing, with CA.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_FOREIGN_CNTRY: Foreign country. Filled on only one filing, with US.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_FOREIGN_POSTAL_CD: Foreign postal code. Filled on only one filing, with a US ZIP.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_PHONE_NUM: The actuary's phone number, digits only.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_NOT_REFLECT_IND: 1 if the actuary flagged that something is not reflected in the figures, 0 if not. Only 2 filings say 1.
cols.SB_CARRYOVER_PR_YR_AMT: Carryover balance from the prior year, a credit built from past extra payments, in dollars. 0 on most filings.
cols.SB_PRE_FNDNG_PR_YR_AMT: Prefunding balance from the prior year, a credit built from past extra payments, in dollars. 0 on most filings.
cols.SB_CARRYOVER_USED_PR_YR_AMT: Carryover balance used toward the prior year's required payment, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_PRE_FNDNG_USED_PR_YR_AMT: Prefunding balance used toward the prior year's required payment, in dollars. Mostly 0.
cols.SB_CARRYOVER_PR_YR_TOT_AMT: Carryover balance left from the prior year after use, in dollars. Mostly 0.
cols.SB_PRE_FNDNG_PR_YR_TOT_AMT: Prefunding balance left from the prior year after use, in dollars. Mostly 0.
cols.SB_INT_PR_YR_PRCNT: Investment return on plan assets for the prior year, as a percent.
cols.SB_INT_PR_YR_CARRYOVER_AMT: Investment gain or loss credited to the carryover balance, in dollars. Mostly 0.
cols.SB_INT_PR_YR_PRE_FNDNG_AMT: Investment gain or loss credited to the prefunding balance, in dollars; can be negative. Mostly 0.
cols.SB_EXCESS_CONTRIB_AMT: Prior-year contributions above the minimum required, in dollars.
cols.SB_EXCESS_CONTRIB_INT_PRCNT: Interest rate applied to those extra contributions, as a percent.
cols.SB_EXCESS_CONTRIB_INT_AMT: Interest on those extra contributions, in dollars. Mostly 0.
cols.SB_EXCESS_CONTRIB_AVAIL_AMT: Extra contributions available to add to the prefunding balance, in dollars.
cols.SB_EXCESS_CONTRIB_ADDED_AMT: Part of the extra contributions actually added to the prefunding balance, in dollars. Mostly 0.
cols.SB_CARRYOVER_REDUCTION_AMT: Carryover balance the employer chose to give up, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_PRE_FNDNG_REDUCTION_AMT: Prefunding balance the employer chose to give up, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_CARRYOVER_BOY_TOT_AMT: Carryover balance at the start of this plan year, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_PRE_FNDNG_BOY_TOT_AMT: Prefunding balance at the start of this plan year, in dollars. Mostly 0.
cols.SB_FNDNG_TGT_PRCNT: Funding percentage: plan assets as a percent of the funding target.
cols.SB_ADJ_FNDNG_TGT_PRCNT: Adjusted funding percentage, the ratio used to decide whether benefit limits kick in.
cols.SB_PR_YR_FNDNG_PRCNT: Funding percentage for the prior year.
cols.SB_AST_LESS_70_PRCNT: A funding percentage that is reported only when the plan falls under 70%. Filled on only 881 filings.
cols.SB_TOT_EMPLR_CONTRIB_AMT: Total employer contributions for the plan year, in dollars.
cols.SB_TOT_EMPLEE_CONTRIB_AMT: Total employee contributions, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_CONTRIB_ALLOC_PR_YR_01_AMT: Contributions counted toward earlier years' unpaid minimum, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_CONTRIB_AVOID_RESTRIC_AMT: Contributions made to avoid limits on benefits, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_CONTRIB_ALLOC_CURR_YR_AMT: Contributions counted toward this year's minimum required payment, in dollars.
cols.SB_FNDNG_SHORT_IND: Whether the plan had a funding shortfall, coded 1 or 2; codes need a lookup.
cols.SB_QRTLY_INSTALL_IND: Whether required quarterly payments were made on time, coded 1 or 2; codes need a lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.SB_1ST_LIQUIDITY_SHORT_AMT: Cash shortfall to pay benefits in the first quarter, in dollars. Mostly blank, and almost always 0.
cols.SB_2ND_LIQUIDITY_SHORT_AMT: Cash shortfall to pay benefits in the second quarter, in dollars. Mostly blank, and almost always 0.
cols.SB_3RD_LIQUIDITY_SHORT_AMT: Cash shortfall to pay benefits in the third quarter, in dollars. Mostly blank, and almost always 0.
cols.SB_4TH_LIQUIDITY_SHORT_AMT: Cash shortfall to pay benefits in the fourth quarter, in dollars. Mostly blank, and almost always 0.
cols.SB_1ST_SEG_RATE_PRCNT: First segment interest rate, used for pensions due soonest, as a percent.
cols.SB_2ND_SEG_RATE_PRCNT: Second segment interest rate, used for pensions due in the middle years, as a percent.
cols.SB_3RD_SEG_RATE_PRCNT: Third segment interest rate, used for pensions due furthest out, as a percent.
cols.SB_YIELD_CURVE_IND: 1 if a full yield curve was used for interest rates instead of the three segment rates, 0 if not.
cols.SB_APPLICABLE_MONTH_CD: Which month's interest rates were used, coded 0 to 8; codes need a lookup.
cols.SB_WEIGHTED_RTM_AGE: Average expected retirement age used in the math, like 62 or 65.
cols.SB_MORTALITY_TBL_CD: Which life-expectancy table the actuary used, coded 1, 2 or 3; codes need a lookup.
cols.SB_CHG_ACTRL_ASSUMP_CURR_IND: Whether the actuary's assumptions changed this year, coded 1 or 2; codes need a lookup.
cols.SB_CHG_METHOD_IND: Whether the funding method changed, coded 1 or 2; codes need a lookup.
cols.SB_SCH_ACTIVE_PARTCP_RQD_IND: Whether a schedule of current workers' data is required, coded 1 or 2; codes need a lookup.
cols.SB_ALT_FNDNG_RULES_CD: Code for alternative funding rules used, 1 or 9; codes need a lookup. Filled on only 41 filings.
cols.SB_UNPAID_PR_YR_CONTRIB_AMT: Unpaid minimum contributions from earlier years, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_CONTRIB_ALLOC_PR_YR_02_AMT: Contributions counted toward earlier years' unpaid minimum, a second line on the form, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_UNPAID_MIN_RQD_TOT_AMT: Total unpaid minimum contributions from earlier years, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_TGT_NRML_COST_02_AMT: Target normal cost, a second line on the form; values track SB_TGT_NRML_COST_01_AMT.
cols.SB_SHORT_AMORTZ_OUTSTD_AMT: Remaining balance of the funding shortfall being paid off over time, in dollars. Mostly 0.
cols.SB_SHORT_AMORTZ_INST: This year's installment toward paying off the funding shortfall, in dollars. Mostly 0.
cols.SB_WVRS_AMORTZ_OUTSTD_AMT: Remaining balance of waived payments being paid off, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_WVRS_AMORTZ_INST: This year's installment on waived payments, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_WVR_APPROVED_LTR_DATE: Date on the IRS letter approving a funding waiver. Filled on only 143 filings.
cols.SB_WAIVED_AMT: Minimum contribution waived, in dollars. Filled on only 152 filings, and nearly all are 0.
cols.SB_FNDNG_RQMT_TOT_AMT: Minimum required contribution for the year, in dollars.
cols.SB_OFFSET_CARRYOVER_AMT: Carryover balance used to cover this year's minimum, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_OFFSET_PRE_FNDNG_AMT: Prefunding balance used to cover this year's minimum, in dollars. Mostly 0.
cols.SB_OFFSET_BAL: Total credit balances used to cover this year's minimum, in dollars. Mostly 0.
cols.SB_ADDL_CASH_TOT_AMT: Cash the employer still had to pay toward this year's minimum after credits, in dollars.
cols.SB_CONTR_ALLOC_CURR_YR_02_AMT: Contributions counted toward this year's minimum, a second line on the form, in dollars.
cols.SB_EXCES_CONTR_CURR_YR_TOT_AMT: Extra contributions for the current year. Empty in this table: filled 0.
cols.SB_UNP_MIN_CONT_CUR_YR_TOT_AMT: Unpaid minimum contribution for this year, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_UNP_MIN_CONTRIB_ALL_YR_AMT: Unpaid minimum contributions for all years combined, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_ACCELERATION_ADJ_AMT: Adjustment for sped-up payments. Empty in this table: filled 0.
cols.SB_ACTUARY_PHONE_NUM_FOREIGN: The actuary's foreign phone number. Filled on only 3 filings.
cols.SB_ELIGIBLE_PLAN_YEAR_1_IND: Flag for an eligible plan year, first box. Empty in this table: filled 0.
cols.SB_ELIGIBLE_PLAN_YEAR_2_IND: Flag for an eligible plan year, second box. Empty in this table: filled 0.
cols.SB_ELIGIBLE_PLAN_YEAR_3_IND: Flag for an eligible plan year, third box. Empty in this table: filled 0.
cols.SB_ELIGIBLE_PLAN_YEAR_4_IND: Flag for an eligible plan year, fourth box. Empty in this table: filled 0.
cols.SB_EXCESS_INSTALL_ACCELER_AMT: Extra installment from sped-up payments. Empty in this table: filled 0.
cols.SB_MIN_REQ_CONT_EXCESS_AST_AMT: A minimum required contribution figure from the form, in dollars.
cols.SB_PORT_PREFNDNG_FNDNG_CAR_AMT: Part of the prefunding and carryover balances used, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_PRESENT_VAL_EXCES_CONT_AMT: Present value of this year's extra contributions, in dollars.
cols.SB_SHOR_AMOR_BASE_SCH_ELEC_IND: Flag for a shortfall payment schedule election. Empty in this table: filled 0.
cols.SB_RTD_VSTD_TGT_AMT: Vested value of pensions owed to retirees and survivors being paid, in dollars. 0 on most filings.
cols.SB_TERM_VSTD_FNDNG_TGT_AMT: Vested value of pensions owed to former workers, in dollars.
cols.SB_TOT_VSTD_FNDNG_TGT_AMT: Total vested value of all pensions earned so far, in dollars.
cols.SB_INT_PRIOR_YEAR_ACTUAL_AMT: Actual investment return credited from the prior year, in dollars. Almost always 0.
cols.SB_PRE_VAL_CUR_PLN_YR_ACR_AMT: Present value of pensions expected to be earned in this plan year, in dollars.
cols.SB_ANTIC_PLAN_RELATED_EXP_AMT: Expected plan expenses for the year, in dollars. 0 on most filings.
cols.SB_EXPECTED_BNFT_PAYMENTS_IND: Whether expected benefit payments are reported, coded 1 or 2; codes need a lookup.
cols.SB_AMORTZ_BASE_ELECT_IND: Code 1, 2 or 3 for an election about shortfall payment schedules; codes need a lookup. Mostly blank.

LABOR__FED_DOL_EBSA_FORM5500_SCHEDULE_SB.summary: Actuarial reports that single-employer traditional pension plans file with the Labor Department, 41,802 filings, showing how well each plan is funded, who it covers, what the employer paid in and which actuary signed.
LABOR__FED_DOL_EBSA_FORM5500_SCHEDULE_SB.row: One actuarial filing: one pension plan's Schedule SB for one plan year.

cols.FORM_TYPE: Which form was filed, like 8-K for the SEC or LM-2 for union reports; the codes depend on the agency. One IRS table just says EFILE.
cols.ESTABLISHED_DATE: The date the union or political group was set up. In the union table most rows say 1970-12-01, which looks like a stand-in date.
cols.TERMINATION_DATE: The date the thing ended, like a registration, recall or judge's service, and blank when it has not ended. Some rows hold far-future dates like 2101-01-04 or 2200-12-30.
cols.TOTAL_ASSETS: Total assets in dollars, whether of a credit union, hospital, bankruptcy filer, or labor union.
cols.TOTAL_LIABILITIES: Total debts owed, in dollars, by the hospital, bankrupt debtor or union. Most union rows read 0.
cols.TOTAL_RECEIPTS: All the money the union or PAC took in for the period, in dollars.
cols.TOTAL_DISBURSEMENTS: All the money the union or PAC paid out for the period, in dollars.
cols.MEMBERS: How many members the credit union or labor union has.
cols.AMENDED_FLAG: Whether this filing is a corrected version of an earlier one. The IRS table writes 1 or 0; the union table writes T or F.
cols.STREET_ADDRESS: The street address, like 4201 IVAR AVE. Some rows hold fillers or directions instead, like TBD, LAT/LONG_USED, PORTABLE SOURCE or 5 MI NE OF.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Fillers like 00000, UNKNO or a lone dash show up, some codes lost a leading zero like 8721, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.PHONE: A phone number, in mixed formats, sometimes with an extension like x1102. Empty in the labor union table, and the FCC table has one value, just I.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.FILING_RECORD_ID: A generated ID for each filing row, like a long code ending in -1. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.RPT_ID: The Labor Department's ID for the report. Each filing has its own.
cols.FILE_NUMBER: The union's file number with the Labor Department. It stays the same across years, so use it to follow one union over time.
cols.REPORT_YEAR_RAW: The year the report covers, as text.
cols.YEAR_COVERED: The year the report covers, as a number.
cols.UNION_NAME: The national union's name, like STEELWORKERS, AFL-CIO. Shared by all its locals.
cols.AFFILIATION_ABBR: Short name of the national union, like NALC or USW. UNAFF marks unions with no national affiliation.
cols.UNIT_NAME: Extra name for the local unit, like TRANSPORTATION DIVISION LOCAL or DOD. Mostly blank.
cols.DESIGNATION_PREFIX: Text that comes before the local's number, like 01 or 04. Mostly blank.
cols.DESIGNATION_NUMBER: The local's number, like 142 in Local 142. Stored as text.
cols.DESIGNATION_SUFFIX: Letter that comes after the local's number, like S or C. Mostly blank.
cols.DESIGNATION_NAME: Short code for the kind of unit, like LU, BR, LG or DIV; the codes need a lookup.
cols.SUBSIDIARY: T or F flag, F on nearly every filled row. A handful hold stray addresses instead. Blank on about half the rows.
cols.FISCAL_YEAR_END: Month the union's fiscal year ends, as a number; 12 on most rows.
cols.PERIOD_COVERED_FROM: First day of the period the report covers.
cols.PERIOD_COVERED_TO: Last day of the period the report covers.
cols.REGISTER_DATE: Date the report was entered into the Labor Department's system.
cols.RECEIVE_DATE: Date the Labor Department received the report.
cols.NEXT_ELECTION_DATE: Date of the union's next officer election, as reported.
cols.SHORTAGE_AMOUNT: Meant to hold a dollar shortage, but filled on only 78 rows and those values look like years, like 2005.
cols.MAXIMUM_BOND: Dollar amount of the bond covering union officers who handle money.
cols.NUM_ATTACHMENTS: Meant to count attachments on the report, but it is empty in this table.
cols.CONSTITUTION_BYLAW: T or F flag about the union's constitution and bylaws; F on most rows. 78 rows hold a stray 201.
cols.TERMINATE_FLAG: T or F: whether this is the union's final report because it is shutting down. A few rows hold stray first names.
cols.AMENDMENT: Amendment count for the report: 0 on most rows, 1 or more for amended reports. Stored as text.
cols.HARDSHIP_FLAG: T or F flag for a hardship filing; almost always F.
cols.HAS_TRUST: T or F: whether the union reported a trust or similar fund.
cols.PAC_FUNDS: T or F: whether the union reported political action fund money.
cols.OUTSIDE_AUDIT: T or F: whether the union's books had an outside audit.
cols.HAS_PROPERTY_CHANGE: T or F flag about property changes during the year; mostly F.
cols.ASSETS_PLEDGED: T or F: whether the union pledged assets as security. Mostly blank.
cols.CONTINGENT_LIABILITIES: T or F: whether the union reported possible future debts. Mostly blank.
cols.HAS_LIQUIDATED_LIABILITIES: T or F flag about written-off debts; almost always F. Mostly blank.
cols.HAS_EXTENDED_LOAN_CREDIT: T or F flag about loans or credit given, but it is F on every filled row. Mostly blank.
cols.HAS_LIQUIDATED_RECEIVABLES: T or F flag about written-off money owed to the union, but it is F on every filled row. Mostly blank.
cols.HAS_SUBSIDIARY: T or F: whether the union reported a subsidiary organization.
cols.RECORDS_KEPT_AT: T or F flag about where the union keeps its records.
cols.ADDRESS_ID: The Labor Department's ID for the union's mailing address record.
cols.ADDRESS_TYPE: Address type code; 201 on every filled row, so it tells you nothing.
cols.MAIL_FIRST_NAME: First name of the person the union's mail goes to.
cols.MAIL_LAST_NAME: Last name of the person the union's mail goes to.
cols.BUILDING_NUMBER: Extra address line, often a P.O. box, suite or care-of line rather than a building number. Mostly blank.
cols.MODIFIED_DATE: Date the record was last changed in the Labor Department's system.
cols.MODIFIED_BY_ID: Code for who last changed the record, like 10000 or 127; the codes need a lookup.

LABOR__FED_DOL_OLMS.summary: Yearly financial reports that US labor unions file with the Labor Department, 2000 to 2026, with each union's name, officers' mailing address and yes-or-no answers about its finances.
LABOR__FED_DOL_OLMS.row: One union filing: one financial report from one union for one year.

cols.MINE_ID: The 7-digit ID the mine safety agency gives each mine. Stored as text to keep leading zeros like 0100003.
cols.CONTROLLER_ID: The mine safety agency's ID for the person or company that controls the mine, like C00692. Stored as text.
cols.CONTROLLER_NAME: The person or company that controls the mine. Several names can be packed in, split by semicolons.
cols.OPERATOR_NAME: The company that runs the well, pipeline, or mine.
cols.FIPS_STATE_CD: The state as a two-digit federal code, like 48 for Texas. Stored as text.
cols.ACCIDENT_TYPE: What kind of accident it was, in words: things like "Struck by falling object" for mines, "Derailment" for trains.
cols.OCCUPATION: The person's job as they wrote it, like RETIRED or Attorney, not cleaned. The mine accident table uses NO VALUE FOUND as a filler, and one FEC table leaves it almost always blank.
cols.NARRATIVE: A free-text account of what happened, as the reporter wrote it, often in capitals with abbreviations. Mostly blank in several tables, and the rail equipment table fills many rows with junk like NoneNoneNone.
cols.COAL_METAL_IND: Whether it is a coal mine or a metal and nonmetal mine: C or M.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.DOCUMENT_NO: The mine safety agency's number for the accident report. Each row has its own.
cols.OPERATOR_ID: The mine safety agency's ID for the company running the mine, like P00812.
cols.SUBUNIT: The part of the mine where it happened, like UNDERGROUND, the open pit, or the mill.
cols.DEGREE_INJURY_CD: A two-digit code for how bad the injury was. The next column spells it out.
cols.DEGREE_INJURY: How bad the injury was, in short capitals, like DAYS AWAY FROM WORK ONLY or ACCIDENT ONLY for no injury.
cols.CLASSIFICATION: The kind of accident, like HANDLING OF MATERIALS, SLIP OR FALL OF PERSON or FALL OF ROOF OR BACK.
cols.NO_INJURIES: How many people were hurt. 0 for accidents with no injury.
cols.DAYS_LOST: How many work days the injured person missed.
cols.DAYS_RESTRICT: How many days the injured person worked on light duty.
cols.ACTIVITY: What the worker was doing, like Machine maintenance. Some rows hold the filler NO VALUE FOUND.
cols.INJURY_SOURCE: What caused the injury, like GROUND or broken rock. Some rows hold the filler NO VALUE FOUND.
cols.NATURE_INJURY: The kind of injury, like a sprain, cut or fracture. Some rows hold the filler NO VALUE FOUND.
cols.INJ_BODY_PART: The part of the body hurt, like fingers, back or knee. Some rows hold the filler NO VALUE FOUND.
cols.IS_FATALITY: True if someone died. About 1,200 rows are deaths. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

LABOR__FED_MSHA_ACCIDENTS.summary: Every accident, injury and illness reported at U.S. mines to the Mine Safety and Health Administration, with what happened, who was hurt and how badly.
LABOR__FED_MSHA_ACCIDENTS.row: One accident report: one incident at one mine on one day.

cols.MINE_ID: The 7-digit ID the mine safety agency gives each mine. Stored as text to keep leading zeros like 0100003.
cols.COAL_METAL_IND: Whether it is a coal mine or a metal and nonmetal mine: C or M.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.FIPS_CNTY_CD: The county as a three-digit federal code, kept as text with leading zeros. Only unique when paired with the state code.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.IS_ACTIVE: True if the company, facility or mine is active now, False if not.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CURRENT_MINE_NAME: The mine's current name. Generic names like No 1 Mine are common, so the name alone does not identify a mine.
cols.CURRENT_MINE_TYPE: Whether the mine is surface, underground, or a facility like a processing plant.
cols.CURRENT_MINE_STATUS: The mine's current status, like active, abandoned, or temporarily idled. Most are abandoned.
cols.CURRENT_STATUS_DT: The day the mine's current status took effect.
cols.CURRENT_CONTROLLER_ID: MSHA's code for the company that ultimately controls the mine. Use it to group mines by owner.
cols.CURRENT_CONTROLLER_NAME: The company that ultimately controls the mine, like Vulcan Materials or Martin Marietta.
cols.CURRENT_OPERATOR_ID: MSHA's code for the company that runs the mine day to day.
cols.CURRENT_OPERATOR_NAME: The company or agency that runs the mine day to day, like a county highway department or a sand and gravel firm.
cols.FIPS_CNTY_NM: The county where the mine is, by name only, like Pike or Buchanan. Pair it with the state to tell counties apart.
cols.PRIMARY_SIC_CD: The six-digit industry code for what the mine mainly produces; the next column spells it out.
cols.PRIMARY_SIC: What the mine mainly produces, like bituminous coal, sand and gravel, or crushed limestone.
cols.NO_EMPLOYEES: How many people work at the mine. Zero is the most common value.
cols.DAYS_PER_WEEK: How many days a week the mine works. Zero is the most common value.
cols.HOURS_PER_SHIFT: How many hours a work shift lasts. Zero is the most common value. Mostly blank.
cols.NEAREST_TOWN: The town nearest the mine. Placeholders like ? and None appear.

LABOR__FED_MSHA_MINES.summary: Every mine the Mine Safety and Health Administration has on file, active or long abandoned, with its owner, operator, type and what it digs.
LABOR__FED_MSHA_MINES.row: One mine: one mine or mine facility, with its current owner and status.

cols.MINE_ID: The 7-digit ID the mine safety agency gives each mine. Stored as text to keep leading zeros like 0100003.
cols.COAL_METAL_IND: Whether it is a coal mine or a metal and nonmetal mine: C or M.
cols.CONTROLLER_ID: The mine safety agency's ID for the person or company that controls the mine, like C00692. Stored as text.
cols.CONTROLLER_NAME: The person or company that controls the mine. Several names can be packed in, split by semicolons.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.EVENT_NO: The number of the inspection that found the violation. Many violations share one inspection.
cols.VIOLATION_NO: The citation number. Almost every row has its own; a contested citation can show up twice.
cols.DOCKET_NO: The case number when the company fought the citation, like WEVA 2008-82. Blank for most rows.
cols.MINE_NAME: The mine's name, like MARSHALL COUNTY MINE. Generic names like Mine #1 are shared by many mines.
cols.MINE_TYPE: Whether the mine is Surface, Underground, or a processing Facility.
cols.VIOLATOR_ID: The mine safety agency's ID for the company or person cited, like P00812.
cols.VIOLATOR_NAME: The name of the company or person cited, like Consolidation Coal Company.
cols.VIOLATION_ISSUE_DATE: The date the citation was written.
cols.SECTION_OF_ACT: The section of the mine safety law cited, written like 316, b, or 103, h. Blank for almost every row.
cols.SIG_SUB: Y if the inspector judged the violation significant and substantial, meaning likely to cause serious harm; N if not.
cols.LIKELIHOOD: How likely the hazard was to hurt someone: NoLikelihood, Unlikely, Reasonably, Highly, or Occurred.
cols.INJ_ILLNESS: How bad an injury the hazard could cause: NoLostDays, LostDays, Permanent, or Fatal.
cols.NO_AFFECTED: How many people the hazard could have hurt. Usually 1.
cols.NEGLIGENCE: How careless the inspector judged the company to be: NoNegligence, LowNegligence, ModNegligence, HighNegligence, or Reckless.
cols.PROPOSED_PENALTY: The fine first proposed for the violation, in dollars.
cols.AMOUNT_DUE: The fine owed after any changes, in dollars.
cols.AMOUNT_PAID: How much of the fine was actually paid, in dollars. Use this column to add up money collected; 0 is common.
cols.VIOLATOR_VIOLATION_CNT: How many violations the company racked up before this one, used in setting the fine. 0 is common.
cols.VIOLATOR_INSPECTION_DAY_CNT: How many inspection days the company had in the look-back period, used in setting the fine. 0 is common.
cols.IS_SIGNIFICANT_AND_SUBSTANTIAL: True if the violation was judged significant and substantial, the same answer as the Y or N column, as true or false.

LABOR__FED_MSHA_VIOLATIONS.summary: Every safety citation federal mine inspectors have written, about 3.1 million of them: which mine, which company, how serious, and what penalty was proposed and paid.
LABOR__FED_MSHA_VIOLATIONS.row: One violation per court case: one citation, with a second row when a contested citation opens another case.

cols.ESTABLISHMENT_NAME: The name of the business or work site, as the company wrote it. Some are just codes or branch numbers.
cols.ESTABLISHMENT_ID: OSHA's ID number for the work site. Use it to join the injury summary and case tables.
cols.EIN: The organization's 9-digit federal tax ID number, stored as text. Some rows hold 000000000 as a filler or only 8 digits because a leading zero was lost, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.COMPANY_NAME: The company's name as the source wrote it, so one company can show up several ways, like Wal-Mart Stores and Walmart Inc. One table leaves it empty.
cols.STREET_ADDRESS: The street address, like 4201 IVAR AVE. Some rows hold fillers or directions instead, like TBD, LAT/LONG_USED, PORTABLE SOURCE or 5 MI NE OF.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The industry code, usually six digits like 722110, which needs a lookup to read. Some tables hold shorter codes like 5416, the OSHA inspections table fills most rows with 000000, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.NAICS_YEAR: Which edition of the industry code list was used: 2012, 2017 or 2022. A few rows hold 0 instead.
cols.INDUSTRY_DESCRIPTION: The industry in words, as the employer wrote it. Not standardized, so the same industry is spelled several ways.
cols.SIZE: A code for how many people work at the site, like 1, 2, 3, 21, or 22. Needs OSHA's lookup to read.
cols.ANNUAL_AVERAGE_EMPLOYEES: The average number of employees at the site over the year.
cols.TOTAL_HOURS_WORKED: The total hours all employees worked at the site that year. Some rows hold 0.
cols.NO_INJURIES_ILLNESSES: Whether the workplace had any injuries or illnesses that year, as a 1 or 2 code that needs OSHA's lookup. A few rows in the 2025 table hold 0.
cols.TOTAL_DEATHS: How many workers died from work injuries or illnesses at this workplace that year.
cols.TOTAL_DAFW_CASES: How many injury or illness cases kept a worker home from work at this workplace that year.
cols.TOTAL_DJTR_CASES: How many cases moved a worker to another job or light duty instead of sending them home, that year.
cols.TOTAL_OTHER_CASES: How many recordable cases needed neither time off nor light duty, that year.
cols.TOTAL_DAFW_DAYS: Total days workers spent home from work because of injuries or illnesses at this workplace that year.
cols.TOTAL_DJTR_DAYS: Total days workers spent on light duty or moved to another job because of injuries or illnesses, that year.
cols.TOTAL_SKIN_DISORDERS: How many work-related skin illnesses, like rashes or burns from chemicals, this workplace recorded that year.
cols.TOTAL_RESPIRATORY_CONDITIONS: How many work-related breathing illnesses this workplace recorded that year.
cols.TOTAL_POISONINGS: How many work-related poisonings this workplace recorded that year. Almost always 0; a few 2025 rows hold 2025, a year typed into the count.
cols.TOTAL_HEARING_LOSS: How many cases of work-related hearing loss this workplace recorded that year.
cols.TOTAL_OTHER_ILLNESSES: How many other work-related illnesses, not skin, breathing, poisoning or hearing, this workplace recorded that year.
cols.CREATED_TIMESTAMP: When the report was sent to OSHA. Watch out: two tables show year 0024 or 0026 when they mean 2024 or 2026.
cols.CHANGE_REASON: The employer's own note on why they changed or resubmitted their yearly report, typed freely. Mostly blank; junk like 0 and NO shows up.
cols.YEAR_FILING_FOR: The year the OSHA injury report covers, like 2023. Each table holds one year.
cols.ID: OSHA's number for the filed summary. Nearly every summary has its own.
cols.ESTABLISHMENT_TYPE: A number code for the kind of employer, 0 to 3. Nearly all are 1. The codes need a lookup.

cols.ANNUAL_AVERAGE_EMPLOYEES: The average number of employees at the site over the year.
cols.TOTAL_HOURS_WORKED: The total hours all employees worked at the site that year. Some rows hold 0.
cols.CASE_NUMBER: The agency's ID number for one case, in a format that depends on the agency, like 05-2014-5064 or I-200-19058-315794. In the OSHA injury tables it is a small running number like 1, 2 or 3 that repeats across work sites, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.JOB_DESCRIPTION: The injured worker's job title as the employer typed it, like Warehouse Associate or RN.
cols.SOC_CODE: The job's standard occupation code, like 29-1141 for registered nurses. OSHA rows often hold filler codes like 9999 or 00-9900.
cols.SOC_DESCRIPTION: The injured worker's job sorted into the government's standard job category, like Registered Nurses. Uncoded or Insufficient Information - NIOSH means it could not be matched.
cols.SOC_REVIEWED: A 0, 1 or 2 flag about whether the worker's job code was reviewed. What each number means needs OSHA's lookup.
cols.SOC_PROBABILITY: How confident the automatic job-category match was, from 0 to 1. Stored as text; odd values like 5 show up.
cols.DATE_OF_INCIDENT: The date the worker was hurt or got sick.
cols.INCIDENT_OUTCOME: How bad the case got, as a code: 1 death, 2 days away from work, 3 light duty or job transfer, 4 other recordable case.
cols.DAFW_NUM_AWAY: How many days the injured worker was kept home from work.
cols.DJTR_NUM_TR: How many days the injured worker spent on light duty or in another job.
cols.TYPE_OF_INCIDENT: What kind of case it was, as a code: 1 injury, 2 skin illness, 3 breathing illness, 4 poisoning, 5 hearing loss, 6 other illness.
cols.TIME_STARTED_WORK: What time the worker started their shift that day, as text. 2023 writes 7:00:00.000; later years write 7:00. Sometimes blank.
cols.TIME_OF_INCIDENT: What time of day the worker got hurt, as text. 2023 writes 20:00:00.000; later years write 20:00. Sometimes blank.
cols.TIME_UNKNOWN: Whether the time of the incident is unknown: 1 yes, 0 no.
cols.DATE_OF_DEATH: The date the worker died, if the case was fatal. Almost always blank, and empty in the 2024 table.
cols.CREATED_TIMESTAMP: When the report was sent to OSHA. Watch out: two tables show year 0024 or 0026 when they mean 2024 or 2026.
cols.YEAR_FILING_FOR: The year the OSHA injury report covers, like 2023. Each table holds one year.
cols.NEW_NAR_WHAT_HAPPENED: The employer's own words on how the injury happened. Names are replaced with [REDACTED].
cols.NEW_NAR_BEFORE_INCIDENT: The employer's own words on what the worker was doing just before getting hurt. Names are replaced with [REDACTED]; Unknown and N A show up often.
cols.NEW_INCIDENT_LOCATION: Where at the workplace it happened, in the employer's words, like Emergency Room or Decant line 1 station 12.
cols.NEW_NAR_INJURY_ILLNESS: The employer's own words on the injury and the body part hurt, like Left knee sprain.
cols.NEW_NAR_OBJECT_SUBSTANCE: The object or substance that hurt the worker, in the employer's words, like Pallet or needle. Junk like blank and n a shows up.
cols.NEW_INCIDENT_DESCRIPTION: A short summary of the incident in the employer's words, like Tripped over a pallet. Names are replaced with [REDACTED].
cols.NATURE_CODE_PRED: A number code for the kind of injury, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. The words for it are in NATURE_TITLE_PRED.
cols.NATURE_TITLE_PRED: The injury type in words, as OSHA's auto-coder predicted it. Each year uses its own label list, so the same injury can be worded differently across years.
cols.PART_CODE_PRED: A number code for the body part hurt, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. The words for it are in PART_TITLE_PRED.
cols.PART_TITLE_PRED: The body part hurt in words, like hand or leg, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. The wording changed between 2023 and 2024.
cols.EVENT_CODE_PRED: A number code for how the injury happened, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. The words for it are in EVENT_TITLE_PRED.
cols.EVENT_TITLE_PRED: How the injury happened in words, like "Falls on same level", as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder.
cols.SOURCE_CODE_PRED: A number code for the object or thing that caused the injury, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. The words for it are in SOURCE_TITLE_PRED.
cols.SOURCE_TITLE_PRED: The object or thing that caused the injury in words, like "Containers" or "Ladders", as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder.
cols.SEC_SOURCE_CODE_PRED: A number code for a second thing that helped cause the injury, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. Mostly blank in 2023; in 2024 most rows are 99, which the title column calls other source.
cols.SEC_SOURCE_TITLE_PRED: A second thing that helped cause the injury, in words, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. Mostly blank in 2023; in 2024 most rows just say "Other source, secondary source".
cols.ID: OSHA's ID for the case record. Nearly every row has its own.
cols.ESTABLISHMENT_TYPE: A number from 0 to 3 for the kind of employer, 1 on almost all rows. The codes need a lookup.

cols.TOTAL_HOURS_WORKED: The total hours all employees worked at the site that year. Some rows hold 0.
cols.CASE_NUMBER: The agency's ID number for one case, in a format that depends on the agency, like 05-2014-5064 or I-200-19058-315794. In the OSHA injury tables it is a small running number like 1, 2 or 3 that repeats across work sites, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.JOB_DESCRIPTION: The injured worker's job title as the employer typed it, like Warehouse Associate or RN.
cols.SOC_CODE: The job's standard occupation code, like 29-1141 for registered nurses. OSHA rows often hold filler codes like 9999 or 00-9900.
cols.SOC_DESCRIPTION: The injured worker's job sorted into the government's standard job category, like Registered Nurses. Uncoded or Insufficient Information - NIOSH means it could not be matched.
cols.SOC_REVIEWED: A 0, 1 or 2 flag about whether the worker's job code was reviewed. What each number means needs OSHA's lookup.
cols.SOC_PROBABILITY: How confident the automatic job-category match was, from 0 to 1. Stored as text; odd values like 5 show up.
cols.DATE_OF_INCIDENT: The date the worker was hurt or got sick.
cols.INCIDENT_OUTCOME: How bad the case got, as a code: 1 death, 2 days away from work, 3 light duty or job transfer, 4 other recordable case.
cols.DAFW_NUM_AWAY: How many days the injured worker was kept home from work.
cols.DJTR_NUM_TR: How many days the injured worker spent on light duty or in another job.
cols.TYPE_OF_INCIDENT: What kind of case it was, as a code: 1 injury, 2 skin illness, 3 breathing illness, 4 poisoning, 5 hearing loss, 6 other illness.
cols.TIME_STARTED_WORK: What time the worker started their shift that day, as text. 2023 writes 7:00:00.000; later years write 7:00. Sometimes blank.
cols.TIME_OF_INCIDENT: What time of day the worker got hurt, as text. 2023 writes 20:00:00.000; later years write 20:00. Sometimes blank.
cols.TIME_UNKNOWN: Whether the time of the incident is unknown: 1 yes, 0 no.
cols.DATE_OF_DEATH: The date the worker died, if the case was fatal. Almost always blank, and empty in the 2024 table.
cols.CREATED_TIMESTAMP: When the report was sent to OSHA. Watch out: two tables show year 0024 or 0026 when they mean 2024 or 2026.
cols.YEAR_OF_FILING: The year the injury report was filed, like 2024. One value per table, stored as text.
cols.NEW_NAR_WHAT_HAPPENED: The employer's own words on how the injury happened. Names are replaced with [REDACTED].
cols.NEW_NAR_BEFORE_INCIDENT: The employer's own words on what the worker was doing just before getting hurt. Names are replaced with [REDACTED]; Unknown and N A show up often.
cols.NEW_INCIDENT_LOCATION: Where at the workplace it happened, in the employer's words, like Emergency Room or Decant line 1 station 12.
cols.NEW_NAR_INJURY_ILLNESS: The employer's own words on the injury and the body part hurt, like Left knee sprain.
cols.NEW_NAR_OBJECT_SUBSTANCE: The object or substance that hurt the worker, in the employer's words, like Pallet or needle. Junk like blank and n a shows up.
cols.NEW_INCIDENT_DESCRIPTION: A short summary of the incident in the employer's words, like Tripped over a pallet. Names are replaced with [REDACTED].
cols.NATURE_CODE_PRED: A number code for the kind of injury, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. The words for it are in NATURE_TITLE_PRED.
cols.NATURE_TITLE_PRED: The injury type in words, as OSHA's auto-coder predicted it. Each year uses its own label list, so the same injury can be worded differently across years.
cols.PART_CODE_PRED: A number code for the body part hurt, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. The words for it are in PART_TITLE_PRED.
cols.PART_TITLE_PRED: The body part hurt in words, like hand or leg, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. The wording changed between 2023 and 2024.
cols.EVENT_CODE_PRED: A number code for how the injury happened, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. The words for it are in EVENT_TITLE_PRED.
cols.EVENT_TITLE_PRED: How the injury happened in words, like "Falls on same level", as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder.
cols.SOURCE_CODE_PRED: A number code for the object or thing that caused the injury, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. The words for it are in SOURCE_TITLE_PRED.
cols.SOURCE_TITLE_PRED: The object or thing that caused the injury in words, like "Containers" or "Ladders", as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder.
cols.SEC_SOURCE_CODE_PRED: A number code for a second thing that helped cause the injury, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. Mostly blank in 2023; in 2024 most rows are 99, which the title column calls other source.
cols.SEC_SOURCE_TITLE_PRED: A second thing that helped cause the injury, in words, as predicted by OSHA's auto-coder. Mostly blank in 2023; in 2024 most rows just say "Other source, secondary source".
cols.ID: OSHA's ID for the case. Nearly every row has its own.
cols.ESTABLISHMENT_TYPE: A number code for the kind of employer, 1, 2 or 3. Almost all are 1; the codes need a lookup.

cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.DATE_FILED: The date the case, opinion, or document was filed. One settlements table stores messy text like 7/26/2019 or N/A.
cols.INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded, as microseconds since 1970, not a readable date. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.SOURCE_RUN_ID: A random code naming the load run that brought this row in. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot changed files. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.C_CASE: A running case number for the settlement.
cols.DATERESOLVED: The day the case was settled, written like 3/25/1983. A date stored as text.
cols.DEFENDANTS: The company or companies sued, like GlaxoSmithKline or Pfizer.
cols.ADDITIONALDEFENDANTS: Other companies named in the case beyond the main defendants. Mostly blank.
cols.TOTALSETTLEMENTAMOUNT: The total dollars paid in the settlement, written with a dollar sign and commas, like $6,000,000. $0 is common.
cols.TOTALSTATESHARE: The dollars that went to the states, written with a dollar sign and commas. $0 is common.
cols.TOTAL_FEDERAL_SHARE: The dollars that went to the federal government. N/A appears as a placeholder. Mostly blank.
cols.LEADAGS: The states whose attorneys general led the case, as two-letter codes. A dash means none listed.
cols.PARTICIPATINGAGS: Every state that joined the settlement, as a list of two-letter codes. A dash means none listed.
cols.DEMLEADSTATES: How many lead states had a Democratic attorney general. A dash means none listed.
cols.GOPLEADSTATES: How many lead states had a Republican attorney general. A dash means none listed.
cols.DEMPARTICIPATINGSTATE: How many joining states had a Democratic attorney general. A dash means none listed.
cols.GOPPARTICIPATINGSTATE: How many joining states had a Republican attorney general. A dash means none listed.
cols.INDUSTRYTYPE: The defendant's industry, like drug makers, finance and insurance, or retail.
cols.ISSUEAREAGENERAL: The broad area of law: consumer protection, Medicaid fraud, antitrust or environment.
cols.ISSUEAREASPECIFIC: The narrower issue, like marketing and advertising, hidden fees, or merger review.
cols.ENFORCEMENTCAMPAIGN: The named wave of cases this one belongs to, like tobacco sales to minors or sweepstakes marketing.
cols.PRODUCT_INVOLVED: The product at issue in the case. Empty in this table.
cols.DESCRIPTION: A paragraph describing what the company did and how the case unfolded.
cols.DATE_ENTRY_CREATED: When the record was added to the database. The same date, 2021-07-12, on every row.
cols.DATE_ENTRY_UPDATED: When the record was last changed. Empty in this table.
cols.OFAGS: How many attorneys general took part. 2 is the most common count, and 50 or 51 are common too.
cols.FEDERALINVOLVEMENT: Federal agencies that joined the case, like DOJ, FTC or EPA, separated by semicolons. N/A appears as a placeholder. Mostly blank.
cols.CONSUMER_RESTITUTION: Money paid back to consumers. N/A appears as a placeholder. Mostly blank.
cols.LOCATION_SETTLEMENT_FILED: Where the settlement was filed. Empty in this table.
cols.RELATED6DIGITNAICSCODE: The six-digit federal industry code for the defendant's business. The codes need a lookup.
cols.FILED_COMPLAINT: A web link to the filed complaint, stored as HTML link code. Mostly blank.
cols.SETTLEMENT_DOCUMENTS_OR_PRESS_RELEASE: A web link to the settlement papers or press release, stored as HTML link code. Mostly blank.
cols.PRESS_RELEASES: A web link to a press release, often an archived copy, stored as HTML link code. Mostly blank.
cols.OTHER_SINGLE_STATE_SETTLEMENTS: Related settlements won by a single state. Empty in this table.
cols.KEYSETTLEMENTTERMS: The main terms the company agreed to, in words. A dash means none listed.
cols.COURT_LEVEL: Whether the case was in federal or state court. Mostly blank.
cols.CITATION: The court case number, like 3:18-cv-00969. Mostly blank.
cols.TOTALDEMAGSINOFFICE: How many Democratic attorneys general were in office nationwide at the time.
cols.TOTALGOPAGSINOFFICE: How many Republican attorneys general were in office nationwide at the time.
cols.LEGAL_BASIS: The laws the case relied on, like state antitrust laws or false claims acts. Mostly blank.
cols.SETTLEMENT_PROVISION_TYPES: Special terms in the deal, like an independent monitor or a divestiture. Mostly blank.
cols.CORPORATE_MONITOR_PROVISION: Yes if the deal puts an outside monitor on the company. Mostly blank.
cols.RELATED4DIGITNAICSCODE: The four-digit federal industry code for the defendant's business. The codes need a lookup.
cols.CORPORATEHEADQUARTERS: The state where the company is based, as two letters, or Foreign.
cols.OTHERPARTIESINVOLVED: Other parties in the case. Empty in this table.
cols.FOCUS: Whether the case was national or regional.
cols.DATE_OF_FINAL_COURT_APPROVAL: When a court gave final approval. The one filled value is N/A. Mostly blank.
cols.PRESIDENTIALADMINISTRATION: Which president's term the case was settled in, like Barack Obama second term.
cols.QUI_TAM_REALTOR_SHARE: The share paid to the whistleblower who brought the case. N/A appears as a placeholder. Mostly blank.
cols.OTHER_SETTLEMENT_AMOUNT: Other money in the deal, written with a dollar sign, sometimes with notes like subordinated. Mostly blank.
cols.STATE_COSTS_FEES: Money paid to the states for their costs and legal fees, written with a dollar sign. Mostly blank.
cols.RELATED_CLASS_ACTION_SETTLEMENT_S: Yes if there was a related class action settlement. Mostly blank.
cols.SORT_ID: A running number used to sort the list.
cols.ID: The database's number for the settlement record.

LEGAL_ENFORCEMENT__FED_NAAG_MULTISTATE_S.row: One settlement: one multistate case against one or more companies, resolved on one date.

cols.IMO_NUMBER: The ship's 7-digit IMO number, a permanent international hull ID. The AIS table puts IMO in front and often holds the filler IMO0000000; the sanctions tables leave it off and are mostly blank.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.CALL_SIGN: The radio call sign of a ship or radio station, like WDB2084. Blank for most sanctions rows.
cols.SOURCE_FILE: The file or link the row was loaded from, like FARA_All_Registrants.csv or a quarter like 2024q2.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.SOURCE_ID: A short name for the source feed the row came from, like fed_cfpb_complaints. In the ITIS other-sources table it is a plain number instead, which needs a lookup.
cols.AIS_POSITION_SK: A made-up ID for the ping. Almost every ping has its own. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.MMSI: The ship's nine-digit radio ID. Use it to follow one ship across pings.
cols.IMO_NORMALIZED: The ship's permanent seven-digit IMO number, padded with zeros. Blank for more than half of pings, and fake values like 0000001 show up a lot.
cols.DATE: The day of the ping. Only eight days show up, January 1 to 8, 2024.
cols.BASE_DATETIME: The exact time of the ping, to the second.
cols.BASE_DATETIME_HOUR: The time of the ping rounded down to the hour.
cols.SPEED_OVER_GROUND: How fast the ship was moving, in knots. 0 on most pings, since most ships sit still.
cols.COURSE_OVER_GROUND: The direction the ship was moving, in degrees. 360 shows up a lot, often from ships standing still.
cols.HEADING: The way the ship's bow was pointing, in degrees. Blank for about half of pings.
cols.VESSEL_NAME: The ship's name, like PACIFIC CHALLENGER.
cols.VESSEL_TYPE_CODE: A two-digit code for the kind of ship, like 31, 37 or 52. The codes need a lookup.
cols.NAV_STATUS: A number code for what the ship said it was doing, 0 to 15, like underway or anchored. The codes need a lookup.
cols.DRAFT_METERS: How deep the ship sits in the water, in meters. Often 0, which likely means not reported.
cols.CARGO_TYPE_CODE: A number code for the ship type and cargo, like 52 or 57. The codes need a lookup.
cols.SPEED_CATEGORY: A plain label for the ship's speed: moored, slow, underway or fast.
cols.POSITION_GEOGRAPHY: The ship's position as a map point, for map queries.
cols.TRANSCEIVER_CLASS: The kind of radio the ship carries: A for big commercial ships, B for smaller boats.

MARITIME__FED_NOAA_AIS.row: One position ping: where one ship was at one moment, with its speed, heading and ship details.

cols.COUNTRY_CODE: The country as a code, usually two letters like US, but some tables use three letters like AGO. The World Bank debt table also holds group codes like MIC and LMC that need a lookup.
cols.COUNTRY_NAME: The country's full name, spelled different ways, like USA, US or UNITED STATES. The World Bank debt table also holds groups like Middle income.
cols.DATA_YEAR: The year the data covers, like 2024. One table runs into future years like 2032.
cols.COUNTRY_YEAR_ID: Country code and year joined, like PRY_2032. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.TOTAL_DEBT_SERVICE_USD: Total debt payments due that year, principal plus interest, in US dollars.
cols.PRINCIPAL_REPAYMENT_USD: Loan principal due that year, in US dollars.
cols.INTEREST_PAYMENT_USD: Interest due that year, in US dollars.
cols.TOTAL_DEBT_SERVICE_USD_BN: Total debt payments due that year, in billions of US dollars.
cols.PRINCIPAL_REPAYMENT_USD_BN: Principal due that year, in billions of US dollars.
cols.INTEREST_PAYMENT_USD_BN: Interest due that year, in billions of US dollars.
cols.PRINCIPAL_SHARE_OF_SERVICE: Share of the year's payments that is principal, from 0 to 1.
cols.PREV_YEAR_TOTAL_DEBT_SERVICE_USD: Total debt payments due the year before, in US dollars.
cols.YOY_CHANGE_USD: Change in total debt payments from the year before, in US dollars.
cols.YOY_CHANGE_PCT: Change from the year before as a fraction, so 0.18 means up 18%.

cols.IS_AGGREGATE: true when the row is a group of countries, not one country.

cols.DESCRIPTION: The dataset's description, in Spanish.
cols.SERIE_ID: The ID of a statistics series. Empty.
cols.PROVINCIA_ID: A two-digit code for the Argentine province, like 06. Almost always blank; the codes need a lookup.
cols.MUNICIPIO_ID: A six-digit code for the town, like 060364. Filled on only 100 rows; the codes need a lookup.
cols.DEPARTAMENTO_ID: A five-digit code for the department, a county-like area, like 14182. Filled on only 100 rows; the codes need a lookup.

cols.GOVTRACK: The member's ID number on GovTrack, a site that follows Congress. Stored as text.
cols.OPENSECRETS: The member's ID on OpenSecrets, the money-in-politics site, like N00007836. Mostly blank.
cols.VOTESMART: The member's ID number on Vote Smart. Mostly blank.
cols.CSPAN: The member's ID number on C-SPAN. Mostly blank.
cols.HOUSE_HISTORY: The member's ID number on the House history website. Blank for senators.
cols.BALLOTPEDIA: The member's page name on Ballotpedia, usually their full name. Mostly blank.
cols.MAPLIGHT: The member's ID number on MapLight, a money-in-politics site. Mostly blank.
cols.WIKIDATA: The member's Wikidata ID, like Q22250.
cols.WIKIPEDIA: The title of the member's Wikipedia article, usually their name.
cols.GOOGLE_ENTITY_ID: The member's Google knowledge-graph ID, like kg:/m/01x68t.
cols.LEGISLATOR_SET: Which list the person came from: current, historical or executive. Empty in the congress legislators table.
cols.FEC_IDS: Every campaign ID the member has had at the Federal Election Commission, as a list like ["S8WA00194", "H2WA01054"]. Most rows hold an empty list.
cols.NAME_FIRST: The person's first name, like John, for a judge or member of Congress.
cols.NAME_LAST: The person's last name, like a judge or member of Congress.
cols.BIRTHDAY: The member's date of birth. Stored as text.
cols.GENDER: The person's sex, written differently by table: Male or Female, M or F, m or f, or Male Owned for businesses. Some rows say Unknown or Unanswered, the clinical trials table mostly says ALL, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.SENATE_CLASS: For senators, which of the three election cycles their seat is in: 1, 2 or 3. Blank for House members.
cols.N_TERMS: How many terms the person has served in Congress or office. Stored as text in the legislators table.
cols.NAME_OFFICIAL_FULL: The member's full official name, like Eric Swalwell. Filled only for recent members.
cols.TERM_TYPE: Which chamber the member's latest term was in: rep for the House, sen for the Senate.
cols.PARTY: The member's party, like Democrat, Republican, Whig or Federalist.
cols.DISTRICT: The House district number. -1 means an at-large seat or an unknown district; blank for senators.
cols.TERM_START: The day the member's first term began, as text like 1875-12-06.
cols.TERM_END: The day the member's last term ends or ended, as text. 2027-01-03 marks members serving now.

POLITICS__FED_CONGRESS_LEGISLATORS.summary: Everyone who has served in the U.S. House or Senate, with their IDs across many political databases, party, state and first and last terms.
POLITICS__FED_CONGRESS_LEGISLATORS.row: One member: one person who served in Congress, with all their terms rolled up.

cols.PAGE_URL: The web address of the page this row came from.
cols.HREF: The link address exactly as written on the DOJ Epstein web page, often a short path like /epstein/search, plus social share links.
cols.RESOLVED_URL: The full web address the link points to, with justice.gov filled in for short paths. Includes Facebook, X and LinkedIn share links.
cols.LINK_TEXT: The words shown on the clickable link, like DOJ Disclosures or Facebook.
cols.FETCHED_AT_UTC: When the scraper downloaded the page, in UTC time. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

POLITICS__FED_EAC_EAVS.summary: The federal Election Administration and Voting Survey: how each local election office ran its election, from voter registration and military ballots to mail voting, poll workers, provisional ballots and voting machines.
POLITICS__FED_EAC_EAVS.row: One local election office's survey answers, usually a county, or a town in New England and Wisconsin.

cols.CALL_SIGN: The radio call sign of a ship or radio station, like WDB2084. Blank for most sanctions rows.
cols.ENTITY_NAME: The name of the company, person or group the record is about. The two exclusion tables leave it mostly blank.
cols.EIN: The organization's 9-digit federal tax ID number, stored as text. Some rows hold 000000000 as a filler or only 8 digits because a leading zero was lost, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE1: The first line of the street or mailing address. Can be a P.O. box, and in the water system table it sometimes holds a contact line like MANAGER or ATTN: WATER PLANT OPERATOR.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.PHONE: A phone number, in mixed formats, sometimes with an extension like x1102. Empty in the labor union table, and the FCC table has one value, just I.
cols.EMAIL: A contact email address. no@email shows up often as a fake value, and the FCC licensing table is empty.
cols.LAST_ACTION_DATE: The date of the most recent action on the license or aircraft registration.
cols.UNIQUE_SYSTEM_IDENTIFIER: The FCC's internal number for the license record. Use it to join to the FCC's other license files.
cols.ULS_FILE_NUMBER: The file number of the application behind the license.
cols.EBF_TRANSACTION_ID: A transaction number for batch filings. Empty in this table.
cols.LICENSE_STATUS: A one-letter code for the license's status, A, E, C or T. The codes need a lookup.
cols.RADIO_SERVICE_CODE: The kind of radio license, HA or HV. The codes need a lookup.
cols.GRANT_DATE: The day the license was granted.
cols.EXPIRED_DATE: The day the license expires or expired.
cols.CANCELLATION_DATE: A cancellation date for the license. Filled on about half of licenses, far more than the ones with status C, so it also shows up on expired licenses.
cols.ELIGIBILITY_RULE_NUM: The FCC rule that makes the holder eligible. Empty in this table.
cols.FRN: The holder's FCC Registration Number, the ID the FCC gives everyone who does business with it.
cols.PO_BOX: The holder's post office box number. Mostly blank.
cols.ATTENTION_LINE: The person to address mail to, usually a person's name. Mostly blank.
cols.FAX: The holder's fax number. Empty in this table.
cols.CONTACT_COMPANY: The company of the contact person. Empty in this table.
cols.APPLICANT_TYPE_CODE: A one-letter code for the kind of license holder, mostly I. The codes need a lookup.
cols.FCC_COUNTY_CODE: The FCC's county code for the holder. Empty in this table.

POLITICS__FED_FCC_LICENSING.summary: FCC radio licenses in the two services coded HA and HV, with the holder's FCC registration number and when each license was granted, expires or was canceled.
POLITICS__FED_FCC_LICENSING.row: One license: one FCC radio license held by one person or business.

cols.TRANSACTION_ID: The source's own number for a transaction, in a different format in each source, so never join across tables on it. In the drug-shipment table one number can repeat up to 5,356 times, so it does not pick out one row.
cols.COMMITTEE_ID: The ID of the campaign committee. The FEC table uses IDs like C00808311; the New York City tables use one letter that only means something together with the candidate ID.
cols.CANDIDATE_ID: The candidate's ID in that agency's own system: FEC IDs look like H4GA07275, NYC IDs are short codes like 369. Nearly always blank in the FEC API table.
cols.CONTRIBUTOR_NAME: The donor's name, usually last name first, not cleaned. Groups and fillers show up too, like UNAVAILABLE, NAME, or a summary line for contributions of $200 or less.
cols.CONTRIBUTOR_EMPLOYER: The donor's employer, as written. Often RETIRED or N/A.
cols.CONTRIBUTOR_OCCUPATION: The donor's job, as written, like RETIRED, NOT EMPLOYED or ATTORNEY. Placeholders like NA and N/A are common.
cols.CONTRIBUTOR_ZIP: The donor's zip code, stored as text. Can be 5 digits or 9 digits run together.
cols.CONTRIBUTOR_STATE: The donor's state, as two letters.
cols.ELECTION_YEAR: The election year, like 1976. Empty in the FEC API table.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.IS_INDIVIDUAL: True if the listed party is a person, False if it is a company or group.
cols.LOAD_DATE: When the record was loaded, as the table itself reports it: a date or a date and time.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_URL: The web address the data was downloaded from. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CONTRIBUTION_RECEIPT_AMOUNT: The contribution amount in dollars. Many are tiny, like 4.17.
cols.CONTRIBUTION_RECEIPT_DATE: The date the contribution was received. Most of this sample is one day, 2022-05-26.
cols.REPORT_TYPE: A short code for the report it came in on, like MY, YE or Q1. Codes need a lookup.
cols.FILING_FORM: The FEC form it was filed on: F3X or F3.
cols.ENTITY_TYPE: A code for the kind of giver, like IND or PAC; IND fills most rows. Codes need a lookup.
cols.PARTY: The candidate's party. Empty in this table.
cols.OFFICE: The office the candidate is running for. Empty in this table.
cols.DISTRICT: The candidate's district. Empty in this table.

POLITICS__FED_FEC_API.summary: A 500-row sample of itemized political contributions pulled from the FEC's web API, good for testing only. It is not the full data; the FEC bulk files are.
POLITICS__FED_FEC_API.row: One itemized contribution to a federal committee, from a small sample page.

cols.CMTE_ID: The Federal Election Commission's ID for the political committee, a C and eight digits like C00493783.
cols.TOTAL_RECEIPTS: All the money the union or PAC took in for the period, in dollars.
cols.TOTAL_DISBURSEMENTS: All the money the union or PAC paid out for the period, in dollars.
cols.DEBTS_OWED_BY: Debts the campaign or PAC owed at the end of the period, in dollars.
cols.COVERAGE_END_DATE: The last day the money summary covers. Text like 12/31/2024 in one table, a real date in the other.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.COMMITTEE_TYPE: The kind of committee, as a one-letter code like N, Q or O. The codes need a lookup.
cols.COMMITTEE_DESIGNATION: The committee's role, as a one-letter code like U, B or J. The codes need a lookup.
cols.FILING_FREQUENCY: How often the committee files reports, as a one-letter code like Q or M. The codes need a lookup.
cols.INDIVIDUAL_CONTRIBUTIONS: Dollars the committee raised from individual people. Blank for about 17% of rows.
cols.PAC_CONTRIBUTIONS: Dollars the committee got from other PACs. Mostly 0.
cols.TRANSFERS_FROM_AFFILIATES: Dollars moved in from related committees. 0 on nearly every filled row; blank for about 17% of rows.
cols.TRANSFERS_TO_AFFILIATES: Dollars moved out to related committees. 0 on most filled rows; blank for about 17% of rows.
cols.CONTRIBUTIONS_TO_OTHER_COMMITTEES: Dollars the committee gave to candidates and other committees. 0 on about half the filled rows; blank for about 17% of rows.
cols.INDEPENDENT_EXPENDITURES: Dollars spent on ads or other efforts for or against candidates without working with them. 0 on nearly every filled row; blank for about 17% of rows.
cols.CASH_BEGINNING_OF_PERIOD: Cash on hand at the start of the period, in dollars.
cols.CASH_CLOSE_OF_PERIOD: Cash on hand at the end of the period, in dollars.
cols.NONFEDERAL_TRANSFERS_RECEIVED: Dollars moved in from state or local party accounts that are not under federal limits. 0 on nearly every filled row; blank for about 17% of rows.
cols.PCT_FROM_INDIVIDUALS: The share of money raised that came from individual people, as a decimal where 1 means all of it. Blank for about a third.
cols.PCT_DISBURSED_TO_OTHERS: The share of spending that went to other committees and candidates, as a decimal where 1 means all of it. Blank for about 30%.

POLITICS__FED_FEC_PAC_SUMMARY.summary: Money in and out of political action committees, party committees and similar groups filing with the FEC, one line per committee per two-year election cycle.
POLITICS__FED_FEC_PAC_SUMMARY.row: One committee in one cycle: one committee's totals for one election cycle. A committee shows up once for each cycle it filed.

cols.NID: The Federal Judicial Center's ID number for a federal judge.
cols.JID: The Federal Judicial Center's ID number for a federal judge. Same number in all three judge tables, so it joins them.
cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.MIDDLE_NAME: The person's middle name, or just an initial.
cols.SUFFIX: The name suffix, like Jr., Sr., or III. Blank for most people.
cols.BIRTH_MONTH: The month the judge was born, as a number 1 to 12 stored as text.
cols.BIRTH_DAY: The day of the month the judge was born, stored as text.
cols.BIRTH_YEAR: The person's year of birth, like 1975. Stored as text in some tables.
cols.BIRTH_CITY: The city where the judge was born.
cols.BIRTH_STATE: The state where the judge was born, as two letters.
cols.DEATH_MONTH: The month the judge died, as a number 1 to 12 stored as text. Blank if living or unknown.
cols.DEATH_DAY: The day of the month the judge died, stored as text. Blank if living or unknown.
cols.DEATH_YEAR: The year the judge died, like 1971. Blank if still living or unknown.
cols.DEATH_CITY: The city where the judge died. Blank if living or unknown.
cols.DEATH_STATE: The state where the judge died, as two letters. Blank if living or unknown.
cols.GENDER: The person's sex, written differently by table: Male or Female, M or F, m or f, or Male Owned for businesses. Some rows say Unknown or Unanswered, the clinical trials table mostly says ALL, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.RACE_OR_ETHNICITY: The judge's race or ethnicity in words, like White, African American or Hispanic. Hispanic and Hispanic/Latino both appear.
cols.COURT_TYPE_1: The kind of court for the judge's first federal judgeship, like U.S. District Court.
cols.COURT_NAME_1: The full court name for the judge's first federal judgeship.
cols.APPOINTMENT_TITLE_1: The judge's title in their first federal judgeship, like Judge or Chief Justice.
cols.APPOINTING_PRESIDENT_1: The president who appointed the judge to their first federal judgeship. None means a reassignment or assignment.
cols.PARTY_OF_APPOINTING_PRESIDENT_1: The party of the president who made the judge's first appointment, like Democratic or Republican.
cols.REAPPOINTING_PRESIDENT_1: The president who reappointed the judge in their first judgeship. Filled for only 10 judges.
cols.PARTY_OF_REAPPOINTING_PRESIDENT_1: The party of the president who reappointed the judge in their first judgeship. Filled for only 10 judges, all Republican.

cols.STATUTE_AUTHORIZING_NEW_SEAT_1: The law that created the seat for the judge's first judgeship, as a Statutes at Large cite like 92 Stat. 1629. Blank if the seat already existed.
cols.RECESS_APPOINTMENT_DATE_1: The date of a recess appointment, made while the Senate was away, for the judge's first judgeship. Blank for most judges.
cols.NOMINATION_DATE_1: The date the judge was nominated for their first judgeship.
cols.COMMITTEE_REFERRAL_DATE_1: The date the Senate sent the judge's first nomination to the Judiciary Committee.
cols.HEARING_DATE_1: The date of the Senate committee hearing on the judge's first nomination.
cols.JUDICIARY_COMMITTEE_ACTION_1: What the Senate Judiciary Committee did with the judge's first nomination, like Reported favorably.
cols.COMMITTEE_ACTION_DATE_1: The date the Senate Judiciary Committee acted on the judge's first nomination.
cols.SENATE_VOTE_TYPE_1: How the Senate voted on the judge's first nomination: Roll Call, Voice, or Unknown.
cols.AYES_NAYS_1: The Senate vote count on the judge's first nomination, as text like 53/43 with yes votes first. Only roll call votes have one.
cols.CONFIRMATION_DATE_1: The date the Senate confirmed the judge for their first judgeship.
cols.COMMISSION_DATE_1: The date the judge was commissioned, formally starting their first judgeship.
cols.SERVICE_AS_CHIEF_JUDGE_BEGIN_1: The year the judge started as chief judge in their first judgeship, stored as text.
cols.SERVICE_AS_CHIEF_JUDGE_END_1: The year the judge stopped being chief judge in their first judgeship, stored as text.
cols.SENIOR_STATUS_DATE_1: The date the judge took senior status, a semi-retired role, in their first judgeship.
cols.TERMINATION_1: How the judge's first judgeship ended, like Death, Retirement, or Appointment to Another Judicial Position.
cols.TERMINATION_DATE_1: The date the judge's first judgeship ended.

cols.NID: The Federal Judicial Center's ID number for a federal judge.
cols.SEQUENCE: Which of the judge's appointments this is, counting 1, 2, 3.
cols.JUDGE_NAME: The judge's name, last name first, like "Abrams, Ronnie".
cols.COURT_TYPE: The kind of federal court, like U.S. District Court, U.S. Court of Appeals or Supreme Court.
cols.COURT_NAME: The full name of the court the judge served on, like U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.
cols.APPOINTMENT_TITLE: The judge's title in that seat, like Judge, Chief Judge or Associate Justice.
cols.APPOINTING_PRESIDENT: The president who appointed the judge. "None - assignment" style values mean the judge was moved, not appointed.
cols.PARTY_OF_APPOINTING_PRESIDENT: The appointing president's party, like Democratic or Republican. Starts with "None" for reassignments.
cols.NOMINATION_DATE: The date the president nominated the judge. Text in one table, a real date in the other.
cols.HEARING_DATE: The date of the hearing: the court's hearing in appeals cases, the Senate hearing in judge records. Often blank.
cols.AYES_NAYS: The Senate vote count on the judge, yes/no, like "53/43". Blank for voice votes; one table adds a leading space.
cols.CONFIRMATION_DATE: The date the Senate confirmed the judge. Text in one table, a real date in the other.
cols.COMMISSION_DATE: The date the judge was formally commissioned into the seat. Text in one table, a real date in the other.
cols.TERMINATION_DATE: The date the thing ended, like a registration, recall or judge's service, and blank when it has not ended. Some rows hold far-future dates like 2101-01-04 or 2200-12-30.
cols.REAPPOINTING_PRESIDENT: The president who reappointed the judge, when there was a reappointment. Filled for only 10 rows.
cols.PARTY_OF_REAPPOINTING_PRESIDENT: The reappointing president's party. All 10 filled rows say Republican.
cols.ABA_RATING: The American Bar Association's rating of the nominee, like Well Qualified or Qualified. Blank for about 40%.
cols.SEAT_ID: The FJC's code for the specific judge seat, like MAD0901.
cols.STATUTE_AUTHORIZING_NEW_SEAT: The law that created the seat, as a Statutes at Large citation like 92 Stat. 1629. Mostly blank.
cols.RECESS_APPOINTMENT_DATE: The date of a recess appointment made while the Senate was away. Almost always blank.
cols.COMMITTEE_REFERRAL_DATE: The date the nomination went to the Senate Judiciary Committee.
cols.JUDICIARY_COMMITTEE_ACTION: What the Judiciary Committee did, like Reported favorably or Not Referred to Committee.
cols.COMMITTEE_ACTION_DATE: The date the Judiciary Committee acted.
cols.SENATE_VOTE_TYPE: How the Senate confirmed the judge: Voice or Roll Call.
cols.SERVICE_AS_CHIEF_JUDGE_BEGIN: The year the judge became chief judge of the court. Mostly blank.
cols.SERVICE_AS_CHIEF_JUDGE_END: The year the judge stopped being chief judge. Mostly blank.
cols.C_2ND_SERVICE_AS_CHIEF_JUDGE_BEGIN: The year a second term as chief judge began. Filled for only 5 rows.
cols.C_2ND_SERVICE_AS_CHIEF_JUDGE_END: The year a second term as chief judge ended. Filled for only 4 rows.
cols.SENIOR_STATUS_DATE: The date the judge took senior status, a form of semi-retirement. Blank for more than half.
cols.TERMINATION: How the service ended, like Death, Retirement or Impeachment & Conviction. Blank for about 30%.
