cols.ELECTION_YEAR: The election year, like 1976. Empty in the FEC API table.

cols.VOTE_MODE: How the votes were cast. Always "total", meaning all modes combined, written in capitals in some Senate rows.
cols.CANDIDATE_VOTES: How many votes the candidate got in that race.
cols.VOTE_SHARE: The candidate's share of the vote as a decimal, so 0.55 means 55 percent.
cols.IS_SPECIAL_ELECTION: True if it was a special election to fill an open seat. Only 90 House rows are true; every Senate row is false.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.OFFICE: The office being elected. US House on every row.
cols.DISTRICT: The congressional district number within the state.
cols.PARTY: The candidate's party in lowercase, like democrat or republican. NA appears as a placeholder.
cols.TOTAL_VOTES: All votes cast in the district race, for every candidate combined.
cols.IS_RUNOFF: True if the race was a runoff. Only 8 rows are.

cols.REPORT_TITLE: The title of a published report or filing, like Periodic Transaction Report for 12/24/2021 or EU-SOCTA 2025 - Executive Summary.
cols.FILING_KIND: How the Senate stock-trade disclosure was filed: ptr for an online trade report, or paper.
cols.IS_AMENDMENT: True if the filing amends an earlier one, False if not. Stored as text.

cols.FILING_UUID: The Senate's long unique ID for one lobbying filing.
cols.FILING_YEAR: The year the filing covers, like 2021, stored as text.
cols.DT_POSTED: When the lobbying filing was posted, as a text date and time with a time zone.
cols.REGISTRANT_ID: The Senate's number for the lobbying firm or group that filed. Stored as text.
cols.REGISTRANT_NAME: The name of whoever registered, like a lobbying firm, fund, foreign agent, aircraft owner or offender, with people often last name first. The aircraft table also uses REGISTRATION PENDING as a filler.
cols.CLIENT_ID: The Senate's number for the client the lobbying was done for. Stored as text.
cols.CLIENT_NAME: The name of the client the lobbying was done for, like COMCAST CORPORATION.
cols.LOBBYIST_ID: An ID number for the lobbyist. California and the U.S. Senate each hand out their own, so the numbers do not match across them.
cols.LOBBYIST_FIRST_NAME: The lobbyist's first name in capitals, often with a middle initial like DAVID R.
cols.LOBBYIST_LAST_NAME: The lobbyist's last name, in capitals.

cols.LOBBYIST_MIDDLE_NAME: The lobbyist's middle name or initial. Mostly blank.
cols.LOBBYIST_SUFFIX: The name suffix, like JR or III. Nearly always blank.
cols.GENERAL_ISSUE: The broad issue area lobbied on, like Budget/Appropriations or Health Issues.
cols.COVERED_POSITION: The past government job the lobbyist had to disclose, as written. Mostly blank, and N/A or n/a shows up.
cols.HAS_COVERED_POSITION: True if the lobbyist listed a past government job, stored as the text True or False.

cols.CONGRESS: Which Congress, by number, like 118. Each Congress lasts two years.
cols.CHAMBER: Which chamber of Congress: House or Senate. Some tables write rep or sen, and one also has President.
cols.ICPSR: The member of Congress's ICPSR number, a standard ID used by the Voteview voting data. Use it to join member tables.
cols.BIONAME: The member's name, last name in capitals first, like "SCHUMER, Charles Ellis".
cols.NOMINATE_LOG_LIKELIHOOD: A fit score from the NOMINATE ideology model, a negative number; closer to zero fits better. Stored as text in one table, and about 11,900 roll-call rows sit at exactly 0.0.
cols.STATE_ICPSR: The state as a number code used by political scientists. The codes need a lookup.
cols.DISTRICT_CODE: The House district number, stored as text; 0 is the most common value.
cols.PARTY_CODE: The party as a number code, like 100 or 200. The codes need a lookup.
cols.OCCUPANCY: A code for whether the member held the seat the whole term or shared it; 0 is most common. The codes need a lookup.
cols.LAST_MEANS: A code for how the member got the seat, like an election or appointment; 1 is most common. The codes need a lookup.
cols.BIOGUIDE_ID: The member's Congress biography ID, like B001261.
cols.BORN: The member's birth year, stored as text.
cols.DIED: The member's death year, stored as text with a trailing .0. Blank if alive.
cols.NOMINATE_DIM1: The member's left-right score from their votes, from -1 to 1; negative is liberal. Stored as text.
cols.NOMINATE_DIM2: The member's second voting score, from -1 to 1, for issues that cut across left and right. Stored as text.
cols.NOMINATE_GEO_MEAN_PROBABILITY: How well the voting score predicts this member's votes, from 0 to 1. Stored as text.
cols.NOMINATE_NUMBER_OF_VOTES: How many votes the score is based on.
cols.NOMINATE_NUMBER_OF_ERRORS: How many of the member's votes the score got wrong.
cols.CONDITIONAL: A flag from the scoring method. Empty in this table.
cols.NOKKEN_POOLE_DIM1: A left-right score figured one Congress at a time, from -1 to 1. Stored as text.
cols.NOKKEN_POOLE_DIM2: A second voting score figured one Congress at a time, from -1 to 1. Stored as text.

cols.NOMINATE_SPREAD_1: How far apart yes and no voters sit on the main left-right line. 0.0 often means no score. A number stored as text.
cols.NOMINATE_SPREAD_2: How far apart yes and no voters sit on the second line. 0.0 often means no score. A number stored as text.

cols.CIRCUIT_MEDIAN9: Median ideology score of judges on the 9th Circuit appeals court. Stored as text; NA where missing.
cols.CIRCUIT_SD9: How spread out the judges' ideology scores are on the 9th Circuit appeals court. Stored as text; NA where missing.
cols.CIRCUIT_MEDIAN10: Median ideology score of judges on the 10th Circuit appeals court. Stored as text; NA where missing.
cols.CIRCUIT_SD10: How spread out the judges' ideology scores are on the 10th Circuit appeals court. Stored as text; NA where missing.
cols.CIRCUIT_MEDIAN11: Median ideology score of judges on the 11th Circuit appeals court. Stored as text; NA on over half the rows.
cols.CIRCUIT_SD11: How spread out the judges' ideology scores are on the 11th Circuit appeals court. Stored as text; NA on over half the rows.
cols.CIRCUIT_MEDIAN12: Median ideology score of judges on appeals circuit number 12. Stored as text; NA where missing.
cols.CIRCUIT_SD12: How spread out the judges' ideology scores are on appeals circuit number 12. Stored as text; NA where missing.
cols.CIRCUIT_MEDIAN13: Median ideology score of judges on appeals circuit number 13. Stored as text; NA on over half the rows.
cols.CIRCUIT_SD13: How spread out the judges' ideology scores are on appeals circuit number 13. Stored as text; NA on over half the rows.

cols.UNNAMED_0: A leftover row number from how the file was saved, counting 1, 2, 3. It means nothing about the data.
cols.JCS: The judge's ideology score on the Judicial Common Space scale, from about -1 liberal to +1 conservative. Stored as text in two tables.
cols.TERM: The Supreme Court term year, stored as text.
cols.JUSTICENAME: The justice, squashed into one word like WODouglas.

POLITICS__XC_JCS_SCOTUS.row: One justice in one term: their ideology score.

cols.ENTITY: The country or region name, like Albania or World.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.WORLD_REGION_ACCORDING_TO_OWID: The continent the country belongs to, as Our World in Data groups them, like Europe or Africa.
cols.CODE: The three-letter country code, like ZWE or VNM.
cols.CORRUPTION_PERCEPTIONS_INDEX: The country's score from 0 to 100. Higher means seen as less corrupt.

POLITICS__XC_OWID_CPI.summary: Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index for each country by year, from Our World in Data.
POLITICS__XC_OWID_CPI.row: One country-year: one country's corruption score for one year.

cols.SAM_NUMBER: The federal contracting system's own ID for an exclusion, a long random-looking code, one per row.
cols.UEI: The 12-character Unique Entity ID the federal government gives each business, which replaced DUNS. Often blank.
cols.CAGE_CODE: The contractor's five-character Defense Department vendor code, like 1L027. Blank for many rows in some tables.
cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit National Provider Identifier, stored as text. Some tables leave it mostly blank or empty, and the SAM exclusions table uses 0000000000 as a filler.
cols.ENTITY_NAME: The name of the company, person or group the record is about. The two exclusion tables leave it mostly blank.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.EXCLUSION_TYPE: Why the person or company is barred. HHS tables use the law section as a code like 1128a1; the SAM tables use words like Voluntary Exclusion. It is almost always blank in the health-center people table.
cols.EXCLUSION_PROGRAM: What the ban covers: Procurement, NonProcurement, or Reciprocal.
cols.EXCLUDING_AGENCY: The federal agency that barred the person or company, as a short abbreviation like HHS, DOJ, or EPA.
cols.ACTIVATION_DATE: The date the ban took effect.
cols.TERMINATION_DATE_RAW: The date the ban ends, or the word Indefinite. Stored as text, so it will not sort as a date.
cols.TERMINATION_DATE: The date the thing ended, like a registration, recall or judge's service, and blank when it has not ended. Some rows hold far-future dates like 2101-01-04 or 2200-12-30.
cols.RECORD_STATUS: Whether the record is live at the source. Always Published in the device table and Active in the exclusions table.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Fillers like 00000, UNKNO or a lone dash show up, some codes lost a leading zero like 8721, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTRY: The country, written different ways by table: a full name, a two- or three-letter code, or a number code that needs a lookup. Some rows hold a region like World or a UK nation like England, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.IS_CURRENTLY_EXCLUDED: True if the ban is still in force, False if it has ended.
cols.IS_ENTITY_NOT_INDIVIDUAL: True if the barred party is a business or group, False if it is a person.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.CLASSIFICATION: What kind of party was barred: Individual, Firm, Vessel, or Special Entity Designation.

PROCUREMENT__FED_SAM_EXCLUSIONS.summary: Everyone barred from federal contracts and grants, from SAM.gov's debarment and suspension list, as pulled in full on 2026-08-11.
PROCUREMENT__FED_SAM_EXCLUSIONS.row: One exclusion: one person, company, vessel or other party barred, in one record.

cols.CONTRACT_TRANSACTION_UNIQUE_KEY: USAspending's ID for one contract action, built from agency codes, the contract number and the change number joined by underscores. -NONE- fills empty parts.
cols.CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY: USAspending's own key for the whole contract, built from the contract number and agency code, like CONT_AWD_FA527023F0101_9700.
cols.AWARD_ID_PIID: The government's contract number, like FA527023F0101. Some rows hold only a short order number like 0001.
cols.MODIFICATION_NUMBER: Which change to the award this row is, with 0 for the original. Formats are messy: 0, 0000 and P00003 all appear.
cols.TRANSACTION_NUMBER: A number that tells apart contract actions that would otherwise look the same. Almost always 0.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_AGENCY_ID: The 4-character code of the agency that owns the umbrella contract this order falls under, like 3600 for Veterans Affairs. Blank when there is no umbrella contract.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_AGENCY_NAME: The name of the agency that owns the umbrella contract this order falls under. Spelling varies, like DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS versus VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_ID_PIID: The contract number of the umbrella contract this order falls under, like GS03FGA010. Blank when there is none.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_MODIFICATION_NUMBER: Which change to the umbrella contract this refers to, like P00006 or 0 for the original.
cols.FEDERAL_ACTION_OBLIGATION: The dollars the government committed or took back in this one transaction. Negative numbers are cuts or cancellations.
cols.TOTAL_DOLLARS_OBLIGATED: The total dollars the government has committed to the whole contract so far, across all its transactions. Blank in many rows of the older tables.
cols.TOTAL_OUTLAYED_AMOUNT_FOR_OVERALL_AWARD: Total dollars actually paid out on the whole award so far. Mostly blank, and 0 is common.
cols.BASE_AND_EXERCISED_OPTIONS_VALUE: The dollar value the government has committed to so far, the base deal plus any extra options it chose to use. Can be negative when a change cuts it.
cols.CURRENT_TOTAL_VALUE_OF_AWARD: What the whole contract is currently worth in dollars, counting options already used. Blank in many rows of the older tables.
cols.BASE_AND_ALL_OPTIONS_VALUE: The dollar value if the government used every option in the contract. Can be negative when a change cuts it.
cols.POTENTIAL_TOTAL_VALUE_OF_AWARD: The most the whole contract could be worth in dollars. Sometimes blank in the full contracts table.
cols.DISASTER_EMERGENCY_FUND_CODES_FOR_OVERAL: Which emergency spending law funded the award, as a code plus words, like Q: Not Designated or Z: Emergency P.L. 117-58. Some rows list several codes, and it is mostly blank.
cols.OUTLAYED_AMOUNT_FROM_COVID_19_SUPPLEMENT: Dollars paid out on the award from COVID-19 relief money. Nearly always blank.
cols.OBLIGATED_AMOUNT_FROM_COVID_19_SUPPLEMEN: Dollars promised to the award from COVID-19 relief money. Nearly always blank, and can be negative after a cut.
cols.OUTLAYED_AMOUNT_FROM_IIJA_SUPPLEMENTAL_F: Dollars paid out on the award from the 2021 infrastructure law money. Nearly always blank.
cols.OBLIGATED_AMOUNT_FROM_IIJA_SUPPLEMENTAL_: Dollars promised to the award from the 2021 infrastructure law money. Nearly always blank.
cols.ACTION_DATE: The date of the award action, like a new contract or a change to one. Two tables store it as text.
cols.ACTION_DATE_FISCAL_YEAR: The federal fiscal year of the transaction, like 2007. Federal fiscal years start October 1.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_START_DATE: The date the work or grant was set to begin. Some tables store it as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_CURRENT_END_DATE: The date the work or grant is currently set to end, which can be in the future. Some tables store it as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_POTENTIAL_END_DATE: The latest date the work could run to if every option is used.
cols.ORDERING_PERIOD_END_DATE: The last date agencies can place orders under this umbrella contract. Mostly blank.
cols.SOLICITATION_DATE: The date the government asked for bids. Mostly blank in the full contracts table.
cols.AWARDING_AGENCY_CODE: The three-digit code for the federal department that made the award, like 036. Stored as text to keep the leading zero.
cols.AWARDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency that made the award, like Department of Defense.
cols.AWARDING_SUB_AGENCY_CODE: The four-character code for the office inside the department that made the award, like 3600. Some contain letters, like 12K3.
cols.AWARDING_SUB_AGENCY_NAME: The office inside the agency that gave the award, like Department of the Navy or National Park Service.
cols.AWARDING_OFFICE_CODE: The code for the office that made the award, like 47QSSC or 12346T. Nearly a third of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.AWARDING_OFFICE_NAME: The name of the office that made the award, like DLA TROOP SUPPORT. Nearly a third of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_AGENCY_CODE: The three-digit code for the federal department paying for the award, like 047. About a quarter of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency whose money paid for the award. Can differ from the agency that made it.
cols.FUNDING_SUB_AGENCY_CODE: The four-character code for the office inside the department paying for the award, like 7300 or 97AS. About a quarter of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_SUB_AGENCY_NAME: The name of the office inside the department paying for the award, like Department of the Navy. About a quarter of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_OFFICE_CODE: The code for the office paying for the award, like 47QSSC or 12346T. Nearly a third of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.FUNDING_OFFICE_NAME: The name of the office paying for the award, like DLA TROOP SUPPORT. Nearly a third of grant and loan rows leave it blank.
cols.TREASURY_ACCOUNTS_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: The Treasury accounts that paid for the award, as codes like 012-X-4336-000, several split by semicolons. About half the grant and loan rows fill it, most bulk contract rows are blank, and the full contracts table is empty.
cols.FEDERAL_ACCOUNTS_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: The federal budget accounts that paid for the award, like 073-1154, several split by semicolons. About half the grant and loan rows fill it, most bulk contract rows are blank, and the full contracts table is empty.
cols.OBJECT_CLASSES_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: What kind of spending paid for the award, as a budget category code plus words, like 26.0: Supplies and materials; some rows list several. About half the grant and loan rows fill it, and most contract rows are blank.
cols.PROGRAM_ACTIVITIES_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: The budget programs that paid for the award, as a code plus words, like 0101: FEDERAL PELL GRANTS. Mostly blank, and filler like 0000: UNKNOWN/OTHER or OPTN: FIELD IS OPTIONAL PRIOR TO FY21 shows up.
cols.FOREIGN_FUNDING: Whether foreign money paid for the contract, as a letter: A foreign military sales, B other foreign funds, X not applicable.
cols.FOREIGN_FUNDING_DESCRIPTION: Whether foreign money paid for the contract, in words: NOT APPLICABLE, FOREIGN FUNDS FMS for foreign military sales, or FOREIGN FUNDS NON-FMS.
cols.SAM_EXCEPTION: A code for why the contractor did not have to register in the federal vendor system, SAM. Almost always blank.
cols.SAM_EXCEPTION_DESCRIPTION: Why the contractor did not have to register in SAM, the federal vendor system, in words like AWARDS TO FOREIGN ENTITIES. Almost always blank; the text NAN fills millions of rows and some hold stray letters like C or G.
cols.RECIPIENT_UEI: The recipient's 12-character federal ID, the Unique Entity ID that replaced the DUNS number. Mostly blank in the federal assistance table and empty in one small API table.
cols.RECIPIENT_DUNS: The recipient's old 9-digit DUNS business number. Mostly blank in the federal assistance table, empty in the three newer tables, and an obvious filler like 123456787 shows up.
cols.RECIPIENT_NAME: Who received the money, like a company, agency or candidate. In the federal assistance table many rows say REDACTED or MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS instead of a name.
cols.RECIPIENT_NAME_RAW: The award recipient's name exactly as the source wrote it, not cleaned up. Grant and loan rows often hold stand-ins like REDACTED DUE TO PII or MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS.
cols.RECIPIENT_DOING_BUSINESS_AS_NAME: The trade name the contractor goes by, if different from its legal name. Blank for most rows.
cols.CAGE_CODE: The contractor's five-character Defense Department vendor code, like 1L027. Blank for many rows in some tables.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_UEI: The 12-character federal ID of the recipient's parent company. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_DUNS: The 9-digit DUNS number, the old business ID, of the recipient's parent company. Mostly blank in the grants table, empty in the bulk table, and the fake-looking 123456787 shows up often in contracts.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_NAME: The name of the recipient's parent company or government, in capitals. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_NAME_RAW: The name of the recipient's parent company or government, exactly as the source wrote it. Mostly blank in the grants and loans table.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTRY_CODE: The recipient's country as a three-letter code, like USA or GBR.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTRY_NAME: The country where the recipient is based, in capitals. The US shows up as both UNITED STATES and UNITED STATES OF AMERICA.
cols.RECIPIENT_ADDRESS_LINE_1: The first line of the recipient's street address.
cols.RECIPIENT_ADDRESS_LINE_2: The second line of the recipient's address, like a suite number. Mostly blank, and N/A shows up as filler.
cols.RECIPIENT_CITY_NAME: The city where the recipient is based, in capitals.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_COUNTY: The recipient's 5-digit county code, like 06037. Keep it as text for the leading zero.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTY_NAME: The recipient's county name, in capitals.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_STATE_: The recipient's state as a 2-digit code, like 06 for California. Keep it as text for the leading zero.
cols.RECIPIENT_STATE_CODE: The recipient's state, as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam appear too.
cols.RECIPIENT_STATE_NAME: The recipient's state spelled out, like MARYLAND.
cols.RECIPIENT_ZIP_4_CODE: The contractor's full nine-digit zip code, with no dash, like 070043561.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_CD_ORI: The recipient's congressional district when the award was made, as state and number like MD-06.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_CD_CUR: The recipient's congressional district under today's district lines, as state and number like MD-06.
cols.RECIPIENT_PHONE_NUMBER: The contractor's phone number, 10 digits with no dashes, stored as text.
cols.RECIPIENT_FAX_NUMBER: The contractor's fax number, 10 digits with no dashes, stored as text.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_COUNTRY_COD: The country where the work is done, as a three-letter code like USA.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_COUNTRY_NAM: The country where the work is done, spelled out, like UNITED STATES.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_CITY_NAME: The city where the work was actually done, in capitals. Can differ from where the recipient is based.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_PLACE_OF_PERFORM: The 5-digit county code where the work is done, like 06037 for Los Angeles. Keep it as text for the leading zero.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_COUNTY_NAME: The county where the work is done, in capitals.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_PLACE_OF_PERFORM: The state where the work is done, as a 2-digit code like 06 for California.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_STATE_CODE: The state where the work was actually done, as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam appear too.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_STATE_NAME: The state where the work is done, spelled out.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_ZIP_4: The ZIP code where the work is done, often with the extra four digits, written like 600858337 or 48226-1906. Some grant rows say CITY-WIDE instead.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_PLACE_OF_PERFORM: The congressional district where the work is done, when the award was made, as state and number like IL-10.
The congressional district where the work is done, under today's district lines, like IL-10. Grant rows often show a 90 district like CA-90, which needs a lookup.
cols.AWARD_OR_IDV_FLAG: Whether the row is a regular contract, AWARD, or an umbrella deal other orders are placed under, IDV.
cols.AWARD_TYPE_CODE: What kind of contract it is, as a letter A to D, like a purchase order or delivery order. Needs a lookup.
cols.AWARD_TYPE: What kind of award: a contract type like PURCHASE ORDER or DELIVERY ORDER, or a grant type. Some rows use short forms like PO or DO, and the NIH table uses a one-digit code.
cols.IDV_TYPE_CODE: What kind of umbrella deal it is, as a letter A to E. Needs a lookup; blank for regular contracts.
cols.IDV_TYPE: What kind of umbrella deal it is, as a short name like IDC, BPA, FSS or GWAC. Blank for regular contracts.
cols.MULTIPLE_OR_SINGLE_AWARD_IDV_CODE: Whether the umbrella deal went to one company or several: S single, M multiple. Mostly blank.
cols.MULTIPLE_OR_SINGLE_AWARD_IDV: Whether the umbrella deal went to one company or several: SINGLE AWARD or MULTIPLE AWARD. Mostly blank.
cols.TYPE_OF_IDC_CODE: For open-ended delivery contracts, how the amount is set, as a letter A, B or C. Nearly always blank.
cols.TYPE_OF_IDC: For open-ended delivery contracts, how the amount is set, like INDEFINITE DELIVERY / INDEFINITE QUANTITY. Nearly always blank; the text NAN fills millions of rows.
cols.TYPE_OF_CONTRACT_PRICING_CODE: How the contract price is set, as a short code like J for firm fixed price. Needs a lookup.
cols.TYPE_OF_CONTRACT_PRICING: How the contract price is set, in words like FIRM FIXED PRICE, COST PLUS FIXED FEE or TIME AND MATERIALS.
cols.TRANSACTION_DESCRIPTION: A free-text note on what was bought or funded, often full of internal codes and abbreviations. Some rows just say DESCR N.A.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_BASE_TRANSACTION_DESCRIPTION: What the award is for, in the agency's own free-text words.
cols.ACTION_TYPE: What kind of change this contract action was, in words, like CHANGE ORDER, FUNDING ONLY ACTION or CLOSE OUT. Mostly blank.
cols.SOLICITATION_IDENTIFIER: The government's ID for the request for bids that led to this contract, like N0002406R5430. Mostly blank.
cols.NUMBER_OF_ACTIONS: How many contract actions this row stands for. Almost always 1.
cols.INHERENTLY_GOVERNMENTAL_FUNCTIONS: A code for whether the work is close to jobs only government should do: CL, CT, OT, or a combo like CL,CT. The words are in INHERENTLY_GOVERNMENTAL_FUNCTIONS_DESCRIPTION.
cols.INHERENTLY_GOVERNMENTAL_FUNCTIONS_DESCRI: Whether the work is close to jobs only government should do, in words, like CLOSELY ASSOCIATED, CRITICAL FUNCTIONS or OTHER FUNCTIONS.
cols.PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_CODE: A four-character code for what was bought, like 7110 or R499. All-number codes are goods, letter-first codes are services; needs a lookup.
cols.PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_CODE_DESCRIPTION: What kind of thing the government bought, in capitals, like OFFICE SUPPLIES or DRUGS AND BIOLOGICALS.
cols.CONTRACT_BUNDLING_CODE: A short code for whether several needs were bundled into one contract, like D, C or H. The words for it are in CONTRACT_BUNDLING.
cols.CONTRACT_BUNDLING: Whether several needs were bundled into one contract, in words, like NOT A BUNDLED REQUIREMENT or NOT BUNDLED.
cols.DOD_CLAIMANT_PROGRAM_CODE: A short code for the Defense Department spending category, like A3, C9E or S1. The words for it are in DOD_CLAIMANT_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION.
cols.DOD_CLAIMANT_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION: The Defense Department spending category in words, like SHIPS, SERVICES or COMBAT VEHICLES.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The industry code, usually six digits like 722110, which needs a lookup to read. Some tables hold shorter codes like 5416, the OSHA inspections table fills most rows with 000000, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.NAICS_DESCRIPTION: The industry in words, like Full-Service Restaurants, matching the NAICS code. One table leaves it empty.
cols.RECOVERED_MATERIALS_SUSTAINABILITY_CODE: A short code for which recycled-material or green-buying clauses the contract has, like A, B or C. The words for it are in RECOVERED_MATERIALS_SUSTAINABILITY.
cols.RECOVERED_MATERIALS_SUSTAINABILITY: Which recycled-material or green-buying clauses the contract has, in words, like FAR 52.223-4 INCLUDED or BIO-BASED. Some values are cut off mid-word.
cols.DOMESTIC_OR_FOREIGN_ENTITY_CODE: A short code for whether the contractor is U.S. or foreign owned, like A, C or D. The words for it are in DOMESTIC_OR_FOREIGN_ENTITY.
cols.DOMESTIC_OR_FOREIGN_ENTITY: Whether the contractor is U.S. or foreign owned, in words, like U.S. OWNED BUSINESS or FOREIGN-OWNED BUSINESS NOT INCORPORATED IN THE U.S.
cols.DOD_ACQUISITION_PROGRAM_CODE: A short code for the Defense weapons or buying program, like 234, DAL or 000. The words for it are in DOD_ACQUISITION_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION.
cols.DOD_ACQUISITION_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION: The Defense weapons or buying program in words, like TRIDENT II MISSILE or F-16. Mostly blank or NONE.
cols.INFORMATION_TECHNOLOGY_COMMERCIAL_ITEM_C: A short code for what kind of tech purchase this was, like Z, A or E. The words for it are in INFORMATION_TECHNOLOGY_COMMERCIAL_ITEM_CATEGORY.
What kind of tech purchase this was, in words, like NOT IT PRODUCTS OR SERVICES or COMMERCIAL SERVICE.
cols.EPA_DESIGNATED_PRODUCT_CODE: A short code for whether the goods had to meet EPA recycled-content rules, like A or E. The words for it are in EPA_DESIGNATED_PRODUCT.
cols.EPA_DESIGNATED_PRODUCT: Whether the goods had to meet EPA recycled-content rules, in words, like MEETS REQUIREMENTS or NOT REQUIRED.
cols.COUNTRY_OF_PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_ORIGIN_COD: The country the goods or services came from, as a three-letter code like USA, DEU or AFG. The text NAN shows up in place of a blank.
cols.COUNTRY_OF_PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_ORIGIN: The country the goods or services came from, spelled out, like UNITED STATES or IRAQ.
cols.PLACE_OF_MANUFACTURE_CODE: A short code for where the goods were made, like C, D or G. The words for it are in PLACE_OF_MANUFACTURE.
cols.PLACE_OF_MANUFACTURE: Where the goods were made, in words, like MFG IN U.S. or NOT A MANUFACTURED END PRODUCT. Some values are cut off.
cols.SUBCONTRACTING_PLAN_CODE: A short code for whether the contractor needed a plan to pass work to small businesses, like A, B or F. The words for it are in SUBCONTRACTING_PLAN.
cols.SUBCONTRACTING_PLAN: Whether the contractor needed a plan to pass work to small businesses, in words, like PLAN NOT REQUIRED.
cols.EXTENT_COMPETED_CODE: A short code for how much competition there was for the contract, like A, B, D or G. The words for it are in EXTENT_COMPETED.
cols.EXTENT_COMPETED: How much competition there was for the contract, in words, like FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION or NOT COMPETED.
cols.SOLICITATION_PROCEDURES_CODE: A short code for how bids were asked for, like SP1, NP or SSS. The words for it are in SOLICITATION_PROCEDURES.
cols.SOLICITATION_PROCEDURES: How bids were asked for, in words, like SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION, SEALED BID or ONLY ONE SOURCE.
cols.TYPE_OF_SET_ASIDE_CODE: A short code for which kind of business the contract was reserved for, like SBA, 8A or SDVOSBC; NONE means no set-aside, and it is the most common value in the big contracts table. The words for it are in TYPE_OF_SET_ASIDE.
cols.TYPE_OF_SET_ASIDE: Which kind of business the contract was reserved for, in words, like NO SET ASIDE USED. or HUBZONE SET-ASIDE.
cols.EVALUATED_PREFERENCE_CODE: A short code for a price edge given to certain small businesses, like HZE or SPS. Almost always NONE or blank.
cols.EVALUATED_PREFERENCE: Whether certain small businesses got a price edge when bids were judged, in words. Almost always NO PREFERENCE USED.
cols.RESEARCH_CODE: A short code for the small-business research program and phase, like SR1 or ST1. The words for it are in RESEARCH.
cols.RESEARCH: The small-business research program and phase in words, like SMALL BUSINESS INNOVATION RESEARCH PROGRAM PHASE II ACTION. Almost always blank or the text NAN.
cols.FAIR_OPPORTUNITY_LIMITED_SOURCES_CODE: A short code for why an order under an existing contract was or was not opened to other holders, like FAIR, ONE or FOO. The words for it are in FAIR_OPPORTUNITY_LIMITED_SOURCES.
cols.FAIR_OPPORTUNITY_LIMITED_SOURCES: Why an order under an existing contract was or was not opened to other holders, in words, like FAIR OPPORTUNITY GIVEN or URGENCY. The text NAN often stands in for blank.
cols.OTHER_THAN_FULL_AND_OPEN_COMPETITION_COD: A short code for the legal reason the contract skipped open bidding, like UNQ, OTH or ONE. The words for it are in OTHER_THAN_FULL_AND_OPEN_COMPETITION.
cols.OTHER_THAN_FULL_AND_OPEN_COMPETITION: The legal reason the contract skipped open bidding, in words, like UNIQUE SOURCE or AUTHORIZED BY STATUTE.
cols.NUMBER_OF_OFFERS_RECEIVED: How many bids came in. A 999 shows up and is likely filler, not a real count.

cols.NATIONAL_INTEREST_ACTION_CODE: A code for the national emergency the buy was tied to, like P20C or H05K. Almost always NONE or blank.

cols.CONSOLIDATED_CONTRACT: Whether several needs were merged into one contract, in words, like NO, YES or NOT CONSOLIDATED.

cols.PERFORMANCE_BASED_SERVICE_ACQUISITION: Whether the service contract pays for results rather than hours, in words, like YES - SERVICE WHERE PBA IS USED. or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.MULTI_YEAR_CONTRACT_CODE: Whether the contract covers several years of needs up front, as Y or N.
cols.MULTI_YEAR_CONTRACT: Whether the contract covers several years of needs up front, as YES or NO.

PROCUREMENT__FED_USASPENDING_BULK.summary: A 50,000-row sample of federal contract spending from USAspending, not the full data. Use it to see the columns, never for totals.
PROCUREMENT__FED_USASPENDING_BULK.row: One contract action: one new contract or change to a contract, on one day.

cols.RECIPIENT_NAME: Who received the money, like a company, agency or candidate. In the federal assistance table many rows say REDACTED or MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS instead of a name.
cols.AMOUNT: The dollar amount. In the Senate stock table it is a text range like $1,001 - $15,000 or the word Unknown, not an exact number.
cols.ACTION_DATE: The date of the award action, like a new contract or a change to one. Two tables store it as text.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.SUBAWARD_ID: USAspending's ID number for the subaward. Close to one per row.
cols.SUBAWARD_NUMBER: The subaward number the prime winner assigned, like ZJK85. Many rows can share one.
cols.DESCRIPTION: What the money is for, like LEGACY CORPS FOR HEALTH AND INDEPENDENCE.
cols.RECORD_JSON: The whole original record as one block of structured text, with dates, amounts and more inside. It needs unpacking.

PROCUREMENT__FED_USASPENDING_SUBAWARDS.summary: A 5,000-row sample, not the full data, of federal subawards from USAspending: money a prime grant or contract winner passed on to another organization. Use it to see the shape, not for totals.
PROCUREMENT__FED_USASPENDING_SUBAWARDS.row: One subaward: one payment a prime award winner passed down to another organization.

cols.SOURCE_ID: A short name for the source feed the row came from, like fed_cfpb_complaints. In the ITIS other-sources table it is a plain number instead, which needs a lookup.
cols.RECORD_DATE: The date the figure or record is as of, like the end of a month or day. Mostly Treasury tables plus one procurement table, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.LANGUAGE: The language, written differently by table: en, ENG, SP, a full name like French, or a bracketed list. Some rows say unspecified or hold an empty list [].
cols.BUYER_NAME: The name of whoever did the buying: a pharmacy or drug company in the drug-shipment table, a government office in the Ecuador contracts table.
cols.AWARD_ID: The award's ID in the source's own system, like NNG15CR64C. The format differs by agency and country.
cols.AWARD_DATE: The date the contract or grant was awarded. Mostly blank in the Ecuador table.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.OCDS_PREFIX: The publisher's prefix for all record IDs. Every row says ocds-5wno2w, so it tells you nothing.
cols.OCID: The worldwide ID for the buying process, like ocds-5wno2w-CE-20250002909455-2411. Nearly every row has its own.
cols.RECORD_ID: The ID of this record, built from the process ID. Nearly every row has its own.
cols.COMPANY_ID: The Ecuador tax ID of the government buyer, as EC-RUC plus 13 digits. Holds the same values as the buyer ID column.
cols.TAG: The record stage. Every row says compiled, so it tells you nothing.
cols.INITIATION_TYPE: How the process started. Every row says tender, so it tells you nothing.
cols.BUYER_ID: The Ecuador tax ID of the government agency doing the buying, as EC-RUC plus 13 digits.
cols.TENDER_ID: The government's number for the buying process, like CE-20260002994410-44481.
cols.TENDER_TITLE: The title of the purchase, in Spanish. Many just say Orden de compra, purchase order, plus the number.
cols.TENDER_STATUS: Whether the buying process is complete or still active.
cols.TENDER_PROCUREMENT_METHOD: How suppliers were picked: selective, direct, open or limited.
cols.TENDER_VALUE_AMOUNT: The estimated value of the purchase, in U.S. dollars.
cols.TENDER_VALUE_CURRENCY: The currency of the estimated value. Always USD.
cols.AWARD_STATUS: The award status. Says active when filled; blank otherwise.
cols.AWARD_VALUE_AMOUNT: How much the winning supplier was awarded, in U.S. dollars.
cols.AWARD_VALUE_CURRENCY: The currency of the award. Always USD.
cols.SUPPLIER_ID: The winning supplier's Ecuador tax ID, EC-RUC plus 13 digits, with an extra number tacked on the end.
cols.SUPPLIER_NAME: The winning supplier's name, a company or a person. Accented letters are garbled, like COMPA�IA.
cols.CONTRACT_ID: The ID of the signed contract, often the process number plus -contract.
cols.CONTRACT_DATE_SIGNED: The day the contract was signed. Blank for most rows.
cols.CONTRACT_VALUE_AMOUNT: The signed contract's value, in U.S. dollars. Blank for most rows.
cols.CONTRACT_VALUE_CURRENCY: The currency of the contract value. Always USD, and blank for most rows.
cols.PARTIES_ID: Tax IDs of everyone involved in the process, joined with | marks.
cols.PARTIES_NAME: Names of everyone involved in the process, joined with | marks, in the same order as the parties ID column.
cols.PARTIES_ROLES: The role of each party, like buyer,procuringEntity or supplier, joined with | marks in the same order as the names.
cols.PLANNING_BUDGET_AMOUNT: The budget set aside for the purchase, in U.S. dollars. Blank for most rows.

PROCUREMENT__INTL_EC_SERCOP.summary: Ecuador's government purchases, about 133,000 records of which public agency bought what, from which company, and for how much.
PROCUREMENT__INTL_EC_SERCOP.row: One purchase record: one government buying process in Ecuador, with its buyer, the winning supplier and the dollar amounts.

cols.DATE_DAY: One calendar day; each row is one date. The calendar table starts at 1700, the date table at 1950.
cols.DAY_OF_WEEK_ISO: The day of the week as a number, 1 Monday through 7 Sunday.
cols.DAY_NAME: The day of the week in words. The date table spells it out like Monday; the calendar table uses three letters like Mon.
cols.MONTH_NAME: The month spelled out, like January. One calendar table uses short forms like Jan.
cols.IS_WEEKEND: Whether the day is a Saturday or Sunday: True or False.
cols.ELECTION_CYCLE: The election year, like 2021. The calendar table runs far into the future, like 2124, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.DATE_TS: The day, as a date and time at midnight. Each row has its own.
cols.DAY_NUM: The day of the month, 1 to 31.
cols.WEEK_OF_YEAR: The week of the year, 1 to 53.
cols.ISO_YEAR: The year under the international week-numbering rule, which can differ from the calendar year in the first and last days of the year.
cols.ISO_WEEK: The week number under the international week-numbering rule, 1 to 53.
cols.WEEK_START: The first day of the week this day falls in.
cols.MONTH_START: The first day of the month.
cols.QUARTER_START: The first day of the quarter.
cols.YEAR_START: The first day of the year.
cols.MONTH_END: The last day of the month.
cols.QUARTER_END: The last day of the quarter.
cols.YEAR_END: The last day of the year.
cols.IS_MONTH_START: True on the first day of a month.
cols.IS_MONTH_END: True on the last day of a month.
cols.FEDERAL_FISCAL_YEAR: The federal budget year, which starts October 1, so October 2024 falls in fiscal 2025.
cols.FEDERAL_FISCAL_MONTH: The month of the federal budget year, 1 to 12, where October is 1.
cols.FEDERAL_FISCAL_QUARTER: The quarter of the federal budget year, 1 to 4.

cols.COUNTRY_NAME: The country's full name, spelled different ways, like USA, US or UNITED STATES. The World Bank debt table also holds groups like Middle income.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.ROR_ID: The organization's ROR ID, written as a web link like https://ror.org/02xhcf905. Each row has its own value.
cols.GRID_ID: The organization's ID in the older GRID registry, like grid.501528.b. Blank for about a quarter of rows.
cols.GRID_IDS_ALL: Every GRID ID on file for the organization. Blank for about a quarter of rows.
cols.ISNI_ID: The organization's main ISNI number, a 16-digit ID written in blocks of four. Blank for most rows.
cols.ISNI_IDS_ALL: Every ISNI number on file for the organization. Blank for over half the rows.
cols.WIKIDATA_ID: The organization's main Wikidata ID, like Q24949311. Blank for most rows.
cols.WIKIDATA_IDS_ALL: Every Wikidata ID on file for the organization. Blank for over half the rows.
cols.FUNDREF_ID: The organization's main Crossref Funder ID, for groups that give research money. Blank for most rows.
cols.FUNDREF_IDS_ALL: Every Crossref Funder ID on file, separated by semicolons. Blank for most rows.
cols.GEONAMES_ID: The GeoNames ID of the city the organization is in. Many organizations share a city.
cols.DISPLAY_NAME_LANG: The language of the main name, as a short code like en or fr. no_lang_code means none was given.
cols.NAME_LABELS: The organization's name in other languages, each tagged with a language code like de:.
cols.NAME_ALIASES: Other names the organization goes by, each tagged with a language code. Blank for most rows.
cols.NAME_ACRONYMS: Short forms of the name, like UPEI. Blank for over half the rows.
cols.STATUS: active, inactive or withdrawn.
cols.ORG_TYPES: What kind of organization it is, like company, education, healthcare, nonprofit or facility.
cols.ESTABLISHED_YEAR: The year the organization was founded. Blank for about one in five rows.
cols.WEB_DOMAINS: The organization's web domain, like gumrf.ru or iuvsta.org. Blank for most rows.
cols.WIKIPEDIA_URL: Link to the organization's Wikipedia page. Blank for most rows.
cols.RELATIONSHIPS: Links to related organizations, like its parent, each written as a type and a ROR link. Blank for most rows.
cols.LOCATION_NAME: The city the organization is in, like Tokyo or London.
cols.SUBDIVISION_CODE: Short code for the state or province, like CA or ENG. Some countries use numbers like 13.
cols.SUBDIVISION_NAME: The state or province name, like California or England.
cols.CONTINENT_CODE: Two-letter continent code, like EU or AS. Blank on exactly the North America rows, likely because its code NA was read as empty.
cols.CONTINENT_NAME: The continent, like Europe, North America or Asia.
cols.RECORD_CREATED_DATE: The date the record was added to ROR. About two in three were added on 2018-11-14, likely the first bulk load.
cols.RECORD_LAST_MODIFIED_DATE: The date the record was last changed in ROR.
cols.CREATED_SCHEMA_VERSION: The version of ROR's format the record was first written in: 1.0, 2.0 or 2.1.
cols.LAST_MODIFIED_SCHEMA_VERSION: The version of ROR's format the record was last written in. Always 2.1.

REFERENCE__XC_ROR_RESEARCH_ORGANIZATIONS.summary: The Research Organization Registry: universities, companies, hospitals, labs and other research bodies worldwide, with their other ID numbers so you can link them across datasets.
REFERENCE__XC_ROR_RESEARCH_ORGANIZATIONS.row: One research organization: its name, type, location and IDs in other registries.

cols.FIPS_CODE: The county's five-digit number code, like 06037, stored as text. One table mixes in state-letter codes like TX155, and one leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_FIPS: The state's number code, like 48 or 06, which needs a lookup. Several tables drop the leading zero so 6 means 06, some rows hold other codes like C1, TX, 00 or N/A, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some tables add County, Parish or the state, like Garza County, TX, so clean it before matching. One table uses Undetermined as a filler, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.STATE_ABBR: The state, as two letters like TX. Territories like PR and GU show up, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.EPA_REGION: The EPA region number, 01 to 10, stored as two-digit text.
cols.COUNTY_FIPS_SUFFIX: The last three digits of the county's FIPS code, like 001, stored as text to keep the zeros.
cols.CENTROID_LATITUDE: The latitude of the county's center point.
cols.CENTROID_LONGITUDE: The longitude of the county's center point; negative for the western half of the world.
cols.FACILITY_COUNT: How many facilities sit in the county.

REF__DIM_GEOGRAPHY.summary: A county lookup list: FIPS codes, county and state names, EPA region, a center point and a count of facilities.
REF__DIM_GEOGRAPHY.row: One county: its codes, names, center point and facility count.

cols.STATE_FIPS: The state's number code, like 48 or 06, which needs a lookup. Several tables drop the leading zero so 6 means 06, some rows hold other codes like C1, TX, 00 or N/A, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.STATE_ABBR: The state, as two letters like TX. Territories like PR and GU show up, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.CENSUS_REGION: Census region: South, West, Midwest or Northeast; Territory for the territories.
cols.CENSUS_DIVISION: Census division, like South Atlantic or Pacific.

REF__DIM_STATE.summary: A lookup of 56 states, DC and territories with their codes, Census region and division.
REF__DIM_STATE.row: One state: one state or territory.

cols.AGENCY: The government agency tied to the record, written differently by table: EPA or State, a full department name, a bracketed list in the Federal Register, or number codes in the federal appeals table, where most rows hold -9.
cols.ABSTRACT: A short summary paragraph of the document, grant or paper. Often blank.
cols.PUBLICATION_DATE: The date the item was published. Three tables leave it empty.
cols.HTML_URL: The web link to the document's page.
cols.PDF_URL: The web address of the PDF of the official notice, on govinfo.gov or Spain's BOE site.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.DOCUMENT_NUMBER: Federal Register document number, like 2017-16997. Each row has its own value.
cols.CITATION: Page citation, like 82 FR 37517: volume, then first page.
cols.DOCKET_IDS: Agency docket numbers as a bracketed list; [] means none.
cols.REGULATION_ID_NUMBERS: Regulation ID numbers as a bracketed list, like 2120-AA64; [] on most rows.
cols.CFR_REFERENCES: Parts of the Code of Federal Regulations touched, as a JSON list; [] on most rows.
cols.TITLE: Document title.
cols.TYPE: Notice, Rule, Proposed Rule, Presidential Document or Uncategorized Document.
cols.SUBTYPE: Kind of presidential document, like Proclamation or Executive Order. Blank for everything else.
cols.ACTION: Short action line, like Final rule. or Notice.
cols.EXCERPTS: Opening text snippet of the document.
cols.PRESIDENT: President in office when it was published, as a small JSON record with the name.
cols.EXECUTIVE_ORDER_NOTES: Notes on an executive order, like which later order revoked it. Filled on only 649 rows.
cols.AGENCIES: Issuing agencies as a JSON list with names, IDs and links.
cols.AGENCY_NAMES: Issuing agency names as a bracketed list.
cols.EFFECTIVE_ON: Date a rule takes effect. Mostly blank.
cols.COMMENTS_CLOSE_ON: Last day to send public comments. Mostly blank.
cols.PUBLICATION_MONTH: Month the document was published, 1 to 12.
cols.PUBLICATION_QUARTER: First day of the quarter the document was published.
cols.START_PAGE: First page in the Federal Register.
cols.END_PAGE: Last page in the Federal Register.
cols.DERIVED_PAGE_COUNT: Page count worked out from the start and end pages; matches PAGE_LENGTH.
cols.IS_SIGNIFICANT: true if the rule is flagged significant, false if not. Mostly blank.
cols.COMMENT_WINDOW_DAYS: Days from publication to the comment deadline, often 30 or 60. Mostly blank.
cols.DAYS_UNTIL_EFFECTIVE: Days from publication to the effective date. Mostly blank.
cols.FULL_TEXT_XML_URL: Link to the full text as XML.
cols.BODY_HTML_URL: Link to the full text as a web page.
cols.JSON_URL: Link to the document's record in the Federal Register API.
cols.RAW_TEXT_URL: Link to the full text as plain text.
cols.IMAGES: Images in the document as JSON links; {} means none, on almost all rows.

REGULATORY__FED_FEDERAL_REGISTER_DOCUMEN.summary: Federal Register documents over about 17 years, 485,585 of them: rules, proposed rules, notices and presidential documents, with agencies, dates, page citations and links.
REGULATORY__FED_FEDERAL_REGISTER_DOCUMEN.row: One document: one rule, notice or presidential document as published in the Federal Register.

cols.URL: A web link to the record's own page at the source.
cols.API_NAME: Which NASA service the item came from: NeoWs Near Earth Objects or NASA Image and Video Library.
cols.REQUEST_URL: The web address that was called to get the item. Only two addresses appear.
cols.RESPONSE_DATE: The date tied to the item, written two ways: plain dates like 2026-06-26 and full timestamps. Stored as text.
cols.TITLE: The item's title: an asteroid's name like 2018 NV, in brackets, or an image title.
cols.DESCRIPTION: A short description: for asteroids, whether it is hazardous and how far it missed Earth; for images, a caption.
cols.MEDIA_TYPE: The kind of item: data for asteroids, image for pictures.
cols.RAW_JSON: The full reply from NASA's service, as raw JSON text.

SCIENCE__FED_NASA_OPEN_DATA.summary: A small test pull of 54 items from two NASA web services: near-Earth asteroids and the NASA image library.
SCIENCE__FED_NASA_OPEN_DATA.row: One item returned by a NASA web service: one asteroid pass or one image.

cols.AWARD_ID: The award's ID in the source's own system, like NNG15CR64C. The format differs by agency and country.
cols.PI_NAME: The name of the lead researcher on the grant.
cols.AWARD_AMOUNT: The dollar amount of the award or grant. Some rows hold stand-in amounts of 0 or 1.
cols.AWARD_DATE: The date the contract or grant was awarded. Mostly blank in the Ecuador table.
cols.START_DATE: The date it began, like an award, trial, listing or court. Mostly blank in several tables, and 1969-12-31 shows up in the offshore-leaks table as a stand-in date.
cols.END_DATE: The date it ended or is set to end, like an award or a listing. Some are in the future.
cols.ABSTRACT: A short summary paragraph of the document, grant or paper. Often blank.
cols.EIN: The organization's 9-digit federal tax ID number, stored as text. Some rows hold 000000000 as a filler or only 8 digits because a leading zero was lost, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.ZIP: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Fillers like 00000, UNKNO or a lone dash show up, some codes lost a leading zero like 8721, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.COUNTRY: The country, written different ways by table: a full name, a two- or three-letter code, or a number code that needs a lookup. Some rows hold a region like World or a UK nation like England, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.CFDA_NUMBER: The federal assistance program number, like 93.778. Some rows list several, split by commas.
cols.TITLE: The grant's title, like Collaborative Research: SaTC 2.0.
cols.AWARDEE_NAME: The university or group that got the grant, like University of Iowa.
cols.INSTITUTION: The university or group that got the grant; same values as AWARDEE_NAME.
cols.CO_PI_NAMES: Names of the other lead researchers. Empty in this table.
cols.PROGRAM_OFFICER: Despite the name, this holds the grant's lead researcher, the same person as PI_NAME, not an NSF staff member.
cols.STATUS: Whether the grant is active. Empty in this table.
cols.PROGRAM_NAME: The NSF program that paid for it, like RSCH EXPER FOR UNDERGRAD SITES.

SCIENCE__FED_NSF_AWARDS.summary: A small pull of 115 National Science Foundation research grants, with titles, universities and program names.
SCIENCE__FED_NSF_AWARDS.row: One grant: one NSF research award to one institution.

cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.TIME: When the quake happened, to the thousandth of a second.
cols.DEPTH: How deep the quake started, in kilometers. 10 and 35 show up far more than nearby depths, a sign of set default values.
cols.MAGTYPE: How the magnitude was measured, as a code like mb, ml or mww. Some codes show up in two cases, like md and Md; the codes need a lookup.
cols.NST: How many seismic stations were used to locate the quake. Blank on almost half the rows.
cols.GAP: The widest angle, in degrees, with no station around the quake; bigger means a shakier location.
cols.DMIN: Distance from the quake to the nearest station, in degrees.
cols.RMS: How well the recorded arrival times fit the computed location, in seconds; lower is a better fit.
cols.NET: The network that reported the quake, as a short code like us, ak or pr.
cols.ID: The USGS ID for the event, a network code plus a number. Nearly every row has its own.
cols.UPDATED: When the record was last changed.
cols.PLACE: A written location, like 6 km SW of Volcano, Hawaii, or a region name.
cols.TYPE: What kind of event: earthquake on almost all rows, plus mining explosion, explosion, ice quake and others.
cols.HORIZONTALERROR: How far off the quake's map position might be, in kilometers.
cols.DEPTHERROR: How far off the depth might be, in kilometers.
cols.MAGERROR: How far off the magnitude might be.
cols.MAGNST: How many stations were used to measure the magnitude.
cols.STATUS: Whether a person checked the event: reviewed on almost all rows, else automatic or manual.
cols.LOCATIONSOURCE: The network that located the quake, as a short code like us or ak.
cols.MAGSOURCE: The network that measured the magnitude, as a short code like us or ak.

SCIENCE__FED_USGS_EARTHQUAKES.summary: Earthquakes of magnitude 2.5 and up from the USGS catalog, 443,274 events with time, place, depth, size and how well each was measured.
SCIENCE__FED_USGS_EARTHQUAKES.row: One earthquake, or another shaking event like a mine blast.

cols.SOURCE_NAME: The name of the source the record came from: a scientific reference in the species catalog, an annotation team like havana in the gene table.
cols.ID: The Ensembl ID, like ENST00000618119; each row has its own value.
cols.SPECIES: Always homo_sapiens: every row is human.
cols.ASSEMBLY: Always GRCh38, the version of the human genome map used.
cols.REGION: Where the feature sits, written chromosome:start-end, like 17:39699740-39728714.
cols.FEATURE_TYPE: Whether the row is a Gene or a Transcript. Almost all are transcripts.
cols.SYMBOL: The gene or transcript name, like ALK-208.
cols.BIOTYPE: What the transcript does, like protein_coding or retained_intron.
cols.STRAND: Which strand of DNA it sits on: 1 or -1.
cols.C_START: The start position on the chromosome, stored as text.
cols.END: The end position on the chromosome, stored as text.
cols.SEQ_REGION_NAME: The chromosome number, stored as text.
cols.VERSION: The version number of the Ensembl ID, stored as text.
cols.DB_TYPE: Always core, the main Ensembl database.
cols.TAXON_ID: The species ID number. Empty in this table.
cols.CONSEQUENCE_TYPE: What a genetic variant does. Empty in this table.
cols.ALLELE_STRING: The DNA letters of a variant. Empty in this table.
cols.POPULATION_NAME: A population group for variant data. Empty in this table.
cols.ONTOLOGY_TERM: A standard term describing the feature. Empty in this table.
cols.PRIMARY_ACCESSION: The main Ensembl ID again; matches the ID column.

SCIENCE__INTL_EMBL_ENSEMBL.summary: A small pull of 643 human genes and gene transcripts from the Ensembl genome database, with where each sits on the chromosome.
SCIENCE__INTL_EMBL_ENSEMBL.row: One gene feature: one human gene or transcript, with its chromosome position.

cols.ENTITY: The country or region name, like Albania or World.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.CODE: The Our World in Data code for the place. OWID_WRL, the whole world, on every row.
cols.ANNUAL_REPORTED_ARTIFICIAL_INTELLIGENCE_: How many AI incidents and controversies were reported that year. A number stored as text.

SCIENCE__XC_OWID_AI_INCIDENTS_ANNUAL.summary: How many artificial intelligence incidents and controversies were reported worldwide each year, a 14-row series from Our World in Data.
SCIENCE__XC_OWID_AI_INCIDENTS_ANNUAL.row: One year: the world's count of reported AI incidents and controversies for that year.

cols.FISCAL_YEAR: The government fiscal year the row covers, like 2023, sometimes written as FY2026 or 2024 YTD. One ICE table holds small numbers that are not years, a DHS table leaves it mostly blank, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.ORG_NAME: The name of the organization, like a charity, campaign committee, university or pharmacy chain. In the drinking-water table it often holds a person's name instead, and two tables leave it mostly blank.
cols.DATE_ADDED: The date the record was added to the source's list or database. In NIH RePORTER about four in ten rows share the one date 2011-03-09.
cols.AWARD_AMOUNT: The dollar amount of the award or grant. Some rows hold stand-in amounts of 0 or 1.
cols.AWARD_TYPE: What kind of award: a contract type like PURCHASE ORDER or DELIVERY ORDER, or a grant type. Some rows use short forms like PO or DO, and the NIH table uses a one-digit code.
cols.OPPORTUNITY_NUMBER: The code for the grant announcement the money was offered under, like RFA-ES-28-001 or PA-13-302.
cols.CONG_DIST: The congressional district. Just the number in the credit union table; state plus number like WI-02 in the NIH table.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.APPL_ID: NIH's ID for one grant application. Each row has its own.
cols.SUBPROJECT_ID: The part number inside a big multi-part grant, like 0001. Blank on most rows.
cols.PROJECT_NUM: The full grant number for this year, like 5R01NS030839-14.
cols.CORE_PROJECT_NUM: The grant number without the year parts, like P30CA006516. Use it to follow one grant across years.
cols.ORG_CITY: Meant to hold the institution's city, but it is empty in this table.
cols.ORG_STATE: Meant to hold the institution's state, but it is empty in this table.
cols.ORG_STATE_NAME: Meant to hold the institution's state name, but it is empty in this table.
cols.ORG_COUNTRY: Meant to hold the institution's country, but it is empty in this table.
cols.ORG_UEI: The institution's federal UEI number. Some rows hold two, separated by a comma.
cols.ORG_IPF_CODE: Meant to hold NIH's institution code, but it is empty in this table.
cols.ORG_ZIP: Meant to hold the institution's ZIP code, but it is empty in this table.
cols.ORG_FIPS: Meant to hold the institution's area code, but it is empty in this table.
cols.DEPT_TYPE: The kind of department, like INTERNAL MEDICINE/MEDICINE. Blank on about 40 percent of rows; some say NONE.
cols.ORG_DEPT: Meant to hold the department's name, but it is empty in this table.
cols.PI_NAMES: The lead scientists on the grant, separated by semicolons.
cols.PI_PROFILE_IDS: NIH's IDs for the lead scientists, separated by commas. Use these rather than names to follow a person.
cols.PO_NAMES: The NIH program officer who manages the grant. Blank on about a quarter of rows.
cols.ABSTRACT_TEXT: The grant's summary as written by the applicant. Long free text.
cols.PROJECT_START_DATE: The date the whole project started.
cols.PROJECT_END_DATE: The date the whole project is set to end.
cols.BUDGET_START_DATE: The start of this year's budget period.
cols.BUDGET_END_DATE: The end of this year's budget period.
cols.AWARD_NOTICE_DATE: The date NIH sent the award notice.
cols.DIRECT_COST_AMT: Dollars for the research itself this year. Blank on some rows.
cols.INDIRECT_COST_AMT: Dollars for the institution's overhead this year. Blank on some rows.
cols.AGENCY_CODE: The agency that funded it: NIH for almost all, else ALLCDC, VA, SAMSHA, AHRQ or FDA.
cols.ACTIVITY_CODE: The grant type, like R01 or P30. Needs a lookup.
cols.FUNDING_MECHANISM: The broad kind of funding, like Research Centers or Training, Individual.
cols.CFDA_CODE: The federal assistance program number, like 93.859.
cols.ARRA_FUNDED: Y if paid for by the 2009 stimulus, N if not.
cols.COVID_RESPONSE: Marks COVID money with codes like Reg-CV or C6. Needs a lookup; blank on almost every row.
cols.SPENDING_CATEGORIES: NIH spending category numbers in brackets, like [108, 276]. Needs a lookup; blank on about 40 percent of rows.
cols.STUDY_SECTION: Meant to hold the review panel code, but it is empty in this table.
cols.STUDY_SECTION_NAME: Meant to hold the review panel name, but it is empty in this table.
cols.SRG_CODE: Meant to hold the scientific review group code, but it is empty in this table.
cols.REPORTER_PROJECT_URL: The link to this grant on the NIH RePORTER website.
cols.TERMS: Science keywords for the grant, each wrapped in angle brackets.

SCIENCE_RESEARCH__FED_NIH_REPORTER.summary: Grant records from NIH RePORTER, mostly NIH with some CDC, VA and other agency grants, reaching back to the late 1990s: who got the money, the scientists, the title, the dates and the dollars.
SCIENCE_RESEARCH__FED_NIH_REPORTER.row: One grant application for one year: the institution, lead scientists, title, dates and money.

cols.SUBJECTS: Subject tags for the item, several in one field split by | or ;.
cols.INSTITUTIONS: The universities or organizations the paper's authors work at, in full text. Some rows say Unknown or Unavailable instead.
cols.JOURNAL: The journal or conference where the paper was published.
cols.PUBLISHER: Who published the item, like a government office or journal publisher. Some tables store it as a web address or code-style text, and the species publications table mostly says None.
cols.COUNTRIES: The country or countries tied to the record, with several joined by semicolons. The two sanctions tables use lowercase two-letter codes like us, some rows say Not identified, and one small offshore-leaks table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.AUTHORS: The paper's authors in one text field. Retraction Watch separates names with ; and bioRxiv writes Last, F.; style.
cols.URLS: Links to Retraction Watch blog posts about the paper. Often blank.
cols.RETRACTION_DATE: The date the retraction or correction notice came out.
cols.RETRACTION_DOI: The DOI of the retraction notice, the permanent ID that points to a paper online, like 10.1109/ETCS.2010.393. A few thousand rows say Unavailable instead.
cols.RETRACTION_PUBMED_ID: The PubMed number of the retraction notice. 0 means none; stored as text.
cols.ORIGINAL_PAPER_DATE: The date the original paper was published.
cols.ORIGINAL_PAPER_DOI: The DOI of the original paper, the permanent ID that points to it online. A few thousand rows say Unavailable instead.
cols.ORIGINAL_PAPER_PUBMED_ID: The PubMed number of the original paper. 0 means none; stored as text.
cols.RETRACTION_NATURE: What kind of notice it is: Retraction, Correction, Expression of concern or Reinstatement.
cols.REASONS: Why the paper was pulled, as a list split by semicolons, like "False/Forged Authorship;".
cols.PAYWALLED: Whether the notice sits behind a paywall: Yes, No or Unknown.
cols.NOTES: Free-text notes from the source, often caveats or web links.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.RECORD_ID: Retraction Watch's ID for the record; each row has its own value.
cols.TITLE: The paper's title. Some are book parts like Frontmatter or Inhalt.
cols.ARTICLE_TYPE: The kind of paper, like Research Article; or Review Article;, with a trailing semicolon. Can list more than one.

SCIENCE_RESEARCH__FED_RETRACTION_WATCH.summary: Retraction Watch's database of retracted and corrected research papers, with journal, authors, institutions and the stated reasons.
SCIENCE_RESEARCH__FED_RETRACTION_WATCH.row: One retraction notice: one paper that was retracted, corrected or flagged, with the notice details.

cols.AGENCY: The government agency tied to the record, written differently by table: EPA or State, a full department name, a bracketed list in the Federal Register, or number codes in the federal appeals table, where most rows hold -9.
cols.UEI: The 12-character Unique Entity ID the federal government gives each business, which replaced DUNS. Often blank.
cols.AWARD_AMOUNT: The dollar amount of the award or grant. Some rows hold stand-in amounts of 0 or 1.
cols.COMPANY: The company the record is about, like the one a consumer complained about or the one that won a research award. Blank in most rows of the FHFA tables.
cols.ADDRESS1: The first line of the street address. Almost always blank in the courthouses table.
cols.ADDRESS2: The second address line, like a suite number. Mostly blank in the research awards table and empty in the other two.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Fillers like 00000, UNKNO or a lone dash show up, some codes lost a leading zero like 8721, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.CONTACT_NAME: The name of the contact person listed on the filing or award. Mostly blank in the SBIR awards table, where some name an office instead of a person.
cols.PI_NAME: The name of the lead researcher on the grant.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.AWARD_RECORD_ID: A made-up ID for the award row. Each row has its own. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.BRANCH: The part of the agency that gave the award, like National Institutes of Health or Air Force. Blank for about a third of rows.
cols.PHASE: The award's stage: Phase I for a small first test, Phase II for the bigger follow-on.
cols.PROGRAM: Which program: SBIR, or STTR, which requires a research-institution partner.
cols.AGENCY_TRACKING_NUMBER: The agency's own tracking number for the award, like R44HL141928. Formats differ by agency.
cols.CONTRACT: The contract or grant number, like FA8649-20-P-0989. Formats differ by agency; blank for about a quarter of rows.
cols.DUNS: The company's old 9-digit DUNS number, the ID used before the UEI. Blank for some rows.
cols.AWARD_TITLE: The title of the research project. Some rows hold Not Available.
cols.AWARD_YEAR: The year of the award, like 2004.
cols.PROPOSAL_AWARD_DATE: The date the award was made. Blank for about half of rows.
cols.CONTRACT_END_DATE: The date the contract or grant ends. Blank for about half of rows.
cols.SOLICITATION_NUMBER: The ID of the call for proposals the company answered, like 2004.1 or PHS2004-2. Blank for about half of rows.
cols.SOLICITATION_YEAR: The year of the call for proposals. Blank for about four in ten rows.
cols.SOLICITATION_CLOSE_DATE: The deadline for proposals. Mostly blank.
cols.PROPOSAL_RECEIPT_DATE: The date the agency got the proposal. Mostly blank.
cols.DATE_OF_NOTIFICATION: The date the company was told it won. Mostly blank.
cols.TOPIC_CODE: The research topic the award falls under, like NIAID or 102. Formats differ by agency, so it needs a lookup.
cols.HUBZONE_OWNED: Y if the company is in a HUBZone, a federally named low-income business area; N if not, U if unknown.
cols.SOCIALLY_AND_ECONOMICALLY_DISADVANTAGED: Y if the company is owned by socially and economically disadvantaged people, N if not, U if unknown.
cols.WOMAN_OWNED: Y if the company is woman-owned, N if not, U if unknown.
cols.NUMBER_EMPLOYEES: How many people the company employs.
cols.COMPANY_WEBSITE: The company's website. Blank for about four in ten rows.
cols.CONTACT_TITLE: The job title of the agency contact, like Program Director. Mostly blank.
cols.CONTACT_PHONE: The agency contact's phone number. Mostly blank, with filler values like an empty phone mask or 9999999999.
cols.CONTACT_EMAIL: The agency contact's email. Mostly blank.
cols.PI_TITLE: The lead researcher's job title, like Principal Investigator or President.
cols.PI_PHONE: The lead researcher's phone number. Many rows hold an empty phone mask instead of a number.
cols.RI_NAME: The university or lab partnered on the award, mainly for STTR. Mostly blank; many rows hold the filler Stub.
cols.RI_POC_NAME: The contact person at the partner university or lab. Mostly blank.
cols.RI_POC_PHONE: The phone number of the partner's contact. Mostly blank, and some filled rows hold an empty phone mask instead of a number.

SCIENCE_RESEARCH__FED_SBIR_STTR_AWARDS.summary: Federal research grants and contracts to small businesses under the SBIR and STTR programs, with the agency, the amount and the company that won.
SCIENCE_RESEARCH__FED_SBIR_STTR_AWARDS.row: One award: one research grant or contract to one small business, in one phase.

cols.DOI: The DOI, a permanent web ID for a paper or dataset, like 10.2813/0758057.
cols.PERSON_NAME: The name of the person tied to the record. Some tables mix in company names or court case names, some leave it mostly blank, and four leave it empty.
cols.AUTHORS: The paper's authors in one text field. Retraction Watch separates names with ; and bioRxiv writes Last, F.; style.
cols.LICENSE: The license the dataset is published under, like Creative Commons Attribution, written as text or a web link. Many rows are blank or say no license was specified, and two small tables leave it empty.
cols.ABSTRACT: A short summary paragraph of the document, grant or paper. Often blank.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.BIORXIV_DOI: The preprint's DOI on bioRxiv. Empty in this table.
cols.PUBLISHED_DOI: The DOI of the journal article the preprint became, like 10.1038/s41556-026-01964-2.
cols.FUNDER_ROR_ID: The funder's ID in the ROR registry. Empty in this table.
cols.TITLE: The paper's title.
cols.AUTHOR_CORRESPONDING_INSTITUTION: The lead contact author's university or institute. Mostly blank.
cols.PREPRINT_POSTED_DATE: When the preprint was posted. Mostly blank, and every filled row says 2026-05-18.
cols.VERSION: Which version of the preprint this is, 1 to 4. Mostly blank.
cols.SUBMISSION_TYPE: The kind of preprint: new results, confirmatory results, or a PUBLISHAHEADOFPRINT tag on about half the filled rows. Mostly blank.
cols.CATEGORY: The subject area, like cell biology or neuroscience. Mostly blank.
cols.SERVER: Which preprint site: bioRxiv or medRxiv, in mixed capitals.
cols.JATS_XML_PATH: Link to the paper's full text file. Empty in this table.
cols.FUNDING_NAME: The funder's name. Empty in this table.
cols.FUNDING_ID_TYPE: What kind of funder ID is used. Empty in this table.
cols.FUNDING_AWARD: The grant number. Empty in this table.
cols.PUBLISHED_JOURNAL_DOI_RAW: Meant to hold the journal article's DOI, but every filled row just says NA. Mostly blank.
cols.PUBLISHED_JOURNAL: The journal that later published the paper, like Nature Communications or PLOS One.
cols.PREPRINT_PLATFORM: Which preprint site the paper first appeared on: bioRxiv or medRxiv.
cols.PREPRINT_TITLE: The title of the paper as a preprint.
cols.PREPRINT_AUTHORS: The preprint's authors, last name first, separated by semicolons.
cols.PREPRINT_CATEGORY: The preprint's subject area, like neuroscience or epidemiology.
cols.PUBLISHED_DATE: When the journal article came out. All in May 2026.
cols.PREPRINT_AUTHOR_CORRESPONDING: The name of the preprint's lead contact author.
cols.PREPRINT_AUTHOR_CORRESPONDING_INSTITUTIO: The lead contact author's university or institute.
cols.IS_PUBLISHED: Always true: every preprint here was later published in a journal.
cols.DAYS_PREPRINT_TO_PUBLICATION: Days between the preprint going up and the journal article coming out.
cols.STAT_MONTH: The month for site-wide usage numbers. Empty in this table.
cols.NEW_PAPERS: New papers posted that month. Empty in this table.
cols.NEW_PAPERS_CUMULATIVE: Running total of new papers. Empty in this table.
cols.REVISED_PAPERS: Revised papers posted that month. Empty in this table.
cols.REVISED_PAPERS_CUMULATIVE: Running total of revised papers. Empty in this table.
cols.ABSTRACT_VIEWS: How many times summaries were viewed. Empty in this table.
cols.FULL_TEXT_VIEWS: How many times full texts were viewed. Empty in this table.
cols.PDF_DOWNLOADS: How many PDFs were downloaded. Empty in this table.
cols.ABSTRACT_CUMULATIVE: Running total of summary views. Empty in this table.
cols.FULL_TEXT_CUMULATIVE: Running total of full-text views. Empty in this table.
cols.PDF_CUMULATIVE: Running total of PDF downloads. Empty in this table.

SCIENCE_RESEARCH__XC_BIORXIV_MEDRXIV.summary: A small pull of 432 bioRxiv and medRxiv preprints, mostly linking each preprint to the journal article it later became. The funding and download-count columns are empty.
SCIENCE_RESEARCH__XC_BIORXIV_MEDRXIV.row: One preprint: an early biology or medical paper, either its own details or the journal article it was published as.

cols.RECORD_TYPE: What kind of record this is: INDIVIDUAL or ENTITY on the UN sanctions list, always "registrations" in the study registrations table.
cols.TAGS: Keywords attached to the record, usually joined with commas. Some rows hold an empty list [].
cols.DATE_CREATED: When the source created this record in its own database, not when the event happened.
cols.DATE_MODIFIED: When the source last changed this record in its own database.
cols.IS_WITHDRAWN: True if it was pulled: a cosponsor who took their name off, or a study registration that was withdrawn.
cols.LICENSE_ID: The license the dataset is published under, as a short code like cc-by or a web link; some say notspecified. Mostly blank in the German and Greek tables, and one table holds internal ID codes instead.
cols.HTML_URL: The web link to the document's page.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
