cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.OSF_ID: The short code that identifies the registration on the Open Science Framework. Each row has its own.
cols.TITLE: The title of the registered study.
cols.DESCRIPTION: The researchers' summary of the study.
cols.CATEGORY: The kind of registration, which is project on every filled row.
cols.REGISTRATION_SUPPLEMENT: Which registration form the researchers used, like OSF Preregistration or Secondary Data Preregistration.
cols.REGISTRATION_RESPONSES_SUMMARY: A summary answer from the registration form. Mostly blank.
cols.REGISTRATION_RESPONSES_UPLOADER: Files uploaded with the form answers. The one filled value is an empty list. Mostly blank.
cols.DATE_REGISTERED: When the study plan was registered.
cols.DATE_WITHDRAWN_RAW: When the registration was withdrawn, if ever. Empty in this table.
cols.EMBARGO_END_DATE: When a hidden registration becomes public. Mostly blank.
cols.IS_REGISTRATION: True if this is a registration. True on every row.
cols.IS_PUBLIC: True if anyone can see the registration. True on every row.
cols.IS_FORK: True if the registration is a copy of another project. False on every row.
cols.IS_PENDING_WITHDRAWAL: True if a withdrawal is waiting for approval. False on every row.
cols.IS_PENDING_REGISTRATION_APPROVAL: True if the registration is waiting for approval. False on every row.
cols.IS_EMBARGOED: True if the registration is hidden until a set date. False on every row.
cols.IS_PENDING_EMBARGO_APPROVAL: True if a request to hide the registration is waiting for approval. False on every row.
cols.IS_PENDING_EMBARGO_TERMINATION_APPROVAL: True if a request to end the hiding early is waiting for approval. False on every row.
cols.IS_ARCHIVING: True if the files are still being archived. False on every row.
cols.REVIEWS_STATE: Where the registration stands in review. Accepted on every row.
cols.REVISION_STATE: Where the latest edit stands. Approved on every row.
cols.WITHDRAWAL_JUSTIFICATION_RAW: Why the registration was withdrawn, if ever. Empty in this table.
cols.ROOT_ID: The code of the top-level project this registration belongs to. Here it matches the registration's own code.
cols.REGISTERED_FROM_ID: The code of the project the registration was made from.
cols.REGISTERED_BY_ID: The code of the user who made the registration.
cols.REGISTRATION_SCHEMA_ID: The code of the registration form used; the supplement column names the form.
cols.PROVIDER_ID: Which service hosts the registration. Always osf.
cols.REGION_ID: Where the files are stored, like us or au-1.
cols.CITATION_ID: The code used to cite the registration. Matches the registration's own code.
cols.STORAGE_ID: The code for the registration's file storage. Matches the registration's own code.
cols.ORIGINAL_RESPONSE_ID: The code of the first set of form answers.
cols.LATEST_RESPONSE_ID: The code of the latest set of form answers. Matches the first set on every row.
cols.API_URL: The web address to fetch this registration's data from the Open Science Framework.
cols.IRI: The public web page for the registration, like https://osf.io/p7qvx.

SCIENCE_RESEARCH__XC_OSF_REGISTRATIONS.summary: A 10-row sample, not the full set, of study plans researchers publicly registered on the Open Science Framework before running their studies.
SCIENCE_RESEARCH__XC_OSF_REGISTRATIONS.row: One registration: one study plan frozen and time-stamped on the Open Science Framework.

cols.ORIGINAL_PAPER_DOI: The DOI of the original paper, the permanent ID that points to it online. A few thousand rows say Unavailable instead.
cols.ORIGINAL_PAPER_PUBMED_ID: The PubMed number of the original paper. 0 means none; stored as text.
cols.RETRACTION_DOI: The DOI of the retraction notice, the permanent ID that points to a paper online, like 10.1109/ETCS.2010.393. A few thousand rows say Unavailable instead.
cols.RETRACTION_PUBMED_ID: The PubMed number of the retraction notice. 0 means none; stored as text.
cols.SUBJECTS: Subject tags for the item, several in one field split by | or ;.
cols.INSTITUTIONS: The universities or organizations the paper's authors work at, in full text. Some rows say Unknown or Unavailable instead.
cols.JOURNAL: The journal or conference where the paper was published.
cols.PUBLISHER: Who published the item, like a government office or journal publisher. Some tables store it as a web address or code-style text, and the species publications table mostly says None.
cols.COUNTRIES: The country or countries tied to the record, with several joined by semicolons. The two sanctions tables use lowercase two-letter codes like us, some rows say Not identified, and one small offshore-leaks table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.AUTHORS: The paper's authors in one text field. Retraction Watch separates names with ; and bioRxiv writes Last, F.; style.
cols.URLS: Links to Retraction Watch blog posts about the paper. Often blank.
cols.RETRACTION_NATURE: What kind of notice it is: Retraction, Correction, Expression of concern or Reinstatement.
cols.REASONS: Why the paper was pulled, as a list split by semicolons, like "False/Forged Authorship;".
cols.RETRACTION_DATE: The date the retraction or correction notice came out.
cols.ORIGINAL_PAPER_DATE: The date the original paper was published.
cols.PAYWALLED: Whether the notice sits behind a paywall: Yes, No or Unknown.
cols.NOTES: Free-text notes from the source, often caveats or web links.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot a changed file. Some tables hold the placeholder "streamed-see-source-zip" or leave it empty. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.RETRACTION_RECORD_ID: A key made from the source record number plus a counter, like 33362-1. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.RECORD_ID: Retraction Watch's own number for the record. Nearly every row has its own value.
cols.TITLE: The title of the retracted paper.
cols.ARTICLE_TYPES: What kind of paper it was, like Research Article or Conference Abstract/Paper, each ending in a semicolon.

SCIENCE_RESEARCH__XC_RETRACTION_WATCH_DA.summary: The Retraction Watch database: scientific papers that were retracted, corrected or flagged, with the journal, the institutions and the reasons.
SCIENCE_RESEARCH__XC_RETRACTION_WATCH_DA.row: One retraction notice: one paper and the retraction or correction issued for it.

cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.MONTH: The month, in many formats: January, 01, 1998-11, 10-2011, a mid-month date like 2026-03-15, or Total. One table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_FIPS: The state's number code, like 48 or 06, which needs a lookup. Several tables drop the leading zero so 6 means 06, some rows hold other codes like C1, TX, 00 or N/A, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY_FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 01001, stored as text. One table holds only the three-digit county part like 017, one holds N/A, and two leave it empty.
cols.DATABASE_NAME: The name of a BTS database, like Aviation Accident Statistics.
cols.DESCRIPTION: What the database holds, in a sentence or two.
cols.PROFILE_URL: Link to the database's page on the BTS site.
cols.MODE: Meant for the transport mode. Empty in this table.
cols.SUBJECT: Meant for the subject. Empty in this table.
cols.CARRIER_CODE: Meant for an airline or carrier code. Empty in this table.
cols.ORIGIN: Meant for a trip origin. Empty in this table.
cols.DEST: Meant for a trip destination. Empty in this table.

TRANSPORT__FED_DOT_BTS.summary: A 21-row list of Bureau of Transportation Statistics databases with names, descriptions and links; the transport data columns are empty.

cols.REGISTRANT_NAME: The name of whoever registered, like a lobbying firm, fund, foreign agent, aircraft owner or offender, with people often last name first. The aircraft table also uses REGISTRATION PENDING as a filler.
cols.STREET: The street address line, like 925 DAYNA ST or PO BOX 505. Some rows hold UNKNOWN instead.
cols.CITY: The city or town name, in capitals or mixed case, with spellings not cleaned. Some rows hold fillers like UNKNOWN or TBD, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.STATE: The state, usually as two letters like TX, but some tables spell out the name like Texas or United States. A few hold junk like active or a region name, and some leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text, as 5 digits or 9 with or without a dash. Some rows hold junk like XXXXX or 00000 or a 4-digit code that lost its leading zero, and two tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY_CODE: The county's number code, written different ways: three digits like 001, sometimes without leading zeros like 3, five digits with the state like 11001, or state letters plus digits like FL095. One table uses name codes like US_SD_CLARK, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.COUNTRY_CODE: The country as a code, usually two letters like US, but some tables use three letters like AGO. The World Bank debt table also holds group codes like MIC and LMC that need a lookup.
cols.LAST_ACTION_DATE: The date of the most recent action on the license or aircraft registration.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.N_NUMBER: The aircraft's tail number, without the leading N. Nearly every row has its own value.
cols.SERIAL_NUMBER: The maker's serial number for the aircraft. Not unique across makers; 1 is a common value.
cols.MFR_MDL_CODE: A code for the aircraft's maker and model; the code needs a lookup in the FAA's aircraft reference file.
cols.ENG_MFR_MDL: A code for the engine's maker and model; the code needs a lookup in the FAA's engine reference file. Blank on about one in eight rows.
cols.YEAR_MFR: The year the aircraft was built. Blank on about one in five rows.
cols.TYPE_REGISTRANT: A number code for the kind of owner, like 1, 3, 4, 5 or 7; the codes need a lookup.
cols.STREET2: Second line of the owner's street address. Blank on almost every row.
cols.REGION: A code for the FAA region of the owner's address, letters or numbers like 2, C or S; the codes need a lookup.
cols.CERT_ISSUE_DATE: The date the current registration certificate was issued.
cols.CERTIFICATION_CODES: Codes for the aircraft's airworthiness class and approved uses, like 1N, 1 or 1NU; the codes need a lookup.
cols.TYPE_AIRCRAFT: A number code for the kind of aircraft, like 4, 5 or 6; the codes need a lookup.
cols.TYPE_ENGINE: A number code for the kind of engine, like 1, 5 or 8; the codes need a lookup.
cols.STATUS_CODE: A code for the registration's status, mostly V; the codes need a lookup.
cols.MODE_S_CODE: The aircraft's transponder code as an eight-digit number. Nearly every row has its own value.
cols.FRACTIONAL_OWNER: Y when the aircraft is under fractional ownership. Filled on only about 1,100 rows; blank means no.
cols.AIRWORTHINESS_DATE: The date the aircraft's airworthiness certificate was issued. Blank on about one in seven rows.
cols.OTHER_NAME_1: An extra owner or co-owner name on the registration. Blank on about nine in ten rows.
cols.OTHER_NAME_2: A second extra owner or co-owner name. Blank on almost every row.
cols.OTHER_NAME_3: A third extra owner or co-owner name. Blank on almost every row.
cols.OTHER_NAME_4: A fourth extra owner or co-owner name. Blank on almost every row.
cols.OTHER_NAME_5: A fifth extra owner or co-owner name. Blank on almost every row.
cols.EXPIRATION_DATE: The date the registration runs out.
cols.UNIQUE_ID: The FAA's own ID number for this registration record. Each row has its own value.
cols.KIT_MFR: Who made the kit, for home-built aircraft, like VANS AIRCRAFT INC. Blank on about 95% of rows.
cols.KIT_MODEL: The kit model, for home-built aircraft, like RV-8. Blank on about 95% of rows.
cols.MODE_S_CODE_HEX: The aircraft's transponder code in hexadecimal, like A5E7C5. This is the code flight trackers show.

TRANSPORT__FED_FAA_AIRCRAFT_REGISTRY.summary: Every civil aircraft registered in the U.S. with the FAA, as of August 2026: tail number, maker and model, owner name and address, and certificate dates.
TRANSPORT__FED_FAA_AIRCRAFT_REGISTRY.row: One registered aircraft: one tail number with its owner and details.

cols.RAILROAD_CODE: The short code for a railroad, like UP for Union Pacific or CSX.
cols.RAILROAD_NAME: The railroad company's full name, like CSX Transportation. The FRA safety table holds only N/A.
cols.INCIDENT_NUMBER: The railroad's own number for the incident, like GT0634. Only unique together with the railroad and date.
cols.INCIDENT_YEAR: The year the incident happened, like 2005. The rail crossing table holds two-digit values like 13 instead.
cols.INCIDENT_MONTH: The month of the incident as two digits, like 08. Stored as text.
cols.COUNTY_CODE: The county's number code, written different ways: three digits like 001, sometimes without leading zeros like 3, five digits with the state like 11001, or state letters plus digits like FL095. One table uses name codes like US_SD_CLARK, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some tables add County, Parish or the state, like Garza County, TX, so clean it before matching. One table uses Undetermined as a filler, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state, as two letters like TX in some tables and as a number code like 48 or 06 in others, which needs a lookup and sometimes drops its leading zero. One table writes it like US_TX, and one leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.TYPE_OF_PERSON: Who was hurt or killed, like Trespassers, Passengers on Trains or Worker on Duty.
cols.POSITIVE_ALCOHOL_TESTS: How many people tested positive for alcohol after the incident. Mostly blank; text in one table.
cols.POSITIVE_DRUG_TESTS: How many people tested positive for drugs after the incident. Mostly blank; text in one table.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.NARRATIVE: A free-text account of what happened, as the reporter wrote it, often in capitals with abbreviations. Mostly blank in several tables, and the rail equipment table fills many rows with junk like NoneNoneNone.
cols.FORM_54_FILED: Whether the railroad also filed a Form 54 report on the incident: Yes or No.
cols.REPORT_KEY: A row ID for the rail incident report, built by gluing the railroad code, its own report number and the year and month together.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_SMT_GROUPING: Which federal rail safety team the reporting railroad falls under, like SMT-5 - BNSF. Not Assigned shows up.
cols.REPORTING_PARENT_RAILROAD_CODE: The short code for the parent railroad of the company that filed the report, like BNSF or CSX.
cols.REPORTING_PARENT_RAILROAD_NAME: The full name of the parent railroad of the company that filed the report, like BNSF Railway Company.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_HOLDING_COMPANY: The company that owns the railroad that filed the report, like Genesee & Wyoming or BNSF Railway Company. Not Assigned shows up.
cols.GEOCODE: The map point as text, like POINT with longitude then latitude. POINT 0 0 means no location. Often blank.
cols.INCIDENT_KEY: A key built from the railroad code, its incident number, year and month run together, like BNGT0634199011.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_INDIVIDUAL_CLASS: The size class of the railroad that filed the report: Class I is the big national lines, Class III the small ones. Not Assigned and Unassigned both show up.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_PASSENGER: Whether the railroad that filed the report carries passengers: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_COMMUTER: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a commuter line: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_SWITCHING_TERMINAL: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a switching or terminal line that moves cars around yards: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_TOURIST: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a tourist or excursion line: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_FREIGHT: Whether the railroad that filed the report hauls freight: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_SHORT_LINE: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a small short-line railroad: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.PDF_REPORT: A web link to the government's PDF report for this casualty.
cols.INCIDENT_DAY: The day of the month the casualty happened, as two digits. Most rows hold the placeholder 00, meaning the day was not given.
cols.DATE: The day the casualty happened. Blank on most rows.
cols.TIME: The time the casualty happened, like 10:00 AM. Most rows hold the placeholder 00:00, meaning no time was given.
cols.TYPE_OF_PERSON_CODE: A letter code for who was hurt. The codes need a lookup.
cols.EMPLOYEE_JOB_CODE: A number code for the hurt worker's railroad job; the next column spells it out.
cols.EMPLOYEE_JOB_DESCRIPTION: The hurt worker's railroad job, like section laborer, yard brakeman or machinist.
cols.AGE_OF_PERSON: The age of the person hurt.
cols.INJURY_ILLNESS_CODE: A code for the kind of injury and body part; the injury column spells it out.
cols.NATURE_OF_INJURY: A two-digit code for the kind of injury. The codes need a lookup.
cols.LOCATION_OF_INJURY_ON_BODY: A one-digit code for the general body area hurt. The codes need a lookup.
cols.SPECIFIC_LOCATION: A letter code for the exact body part hurt. The codes need a lookup.
cols.INJURY_ILLNESS: The injury in words, like sprain or strain of the lower back, or a cut on the thumb.
cols.PHYSICAL_ACT_CIRCUMSTANCES_CODE: A number code for what the person was doing; the next column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.PHYSICAL_ACT_CIRCUMSTANCES: What the person was doing when hurt, like walking, driving, riding or getting off. Mostly blank.
cols.GENERAL_LOCATION_OF_PERSON_CODE: A letter code for the general place the person was; the next column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.GENERAL_LOCATION_OF_PERSON: The general place the person was, like the main line, a rail yard, a passenger station or a repair shop. Mostly blank.
cols.ON_TRACK_EQUIPMENT_CODE: A number code for the rail equipment involved; the next column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.ON_TRACK_EQUIPMENT: The rail equipment involved, like a moving freight train, or none at all. Mostly blank.
cols.SPECIFIC_LOCATION_OF_PERSON_CODE: A code for exactly where the person was; the next column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.SPECIFIC_LOCATION_OF_PERSON: Exactly where the person was, like beside the track, on a road crossing or inside a rail car. Mostly blank.
cols.EVENT_CODE: A number code for what happened; the next column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.EVENT: What happened, like a road crossing crash, a slip or fall, overexertion, or being hit by a train. Mostly blank.
cols.TOOLS_CODE: A code for the object or surface involved; the next column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.TOOLS: The object or surface involved in the injury, like the ground, a road, a locomotive or a stair step. Mostly blank.
cols.INJURY_CAUSE_CODE: A number code for the cause; the next column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.INJURY_CAUSE: What caused the casualty, like human factor, trespassing, equipment, or undetermined. Mostly blank.
cols.DAYS_AWAY_FROM_WORK: How many days a hurt worker missed work.
cols.DAYS_RESTRICTED_ACTIVITY: How many days a hurt worker could only do limited duty.
cols.HAZMAT_EXPOSURE: Whether the person was exposed to hazardous materials. Mostly blank.
cols.COVERED_DATA_CODE: A letter code for why a borderline case was reported; the next column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.COVERED_DATA_REASON: Why a borderline case counts, like a doctor prescribing over-the-counter medicine or time off. Mostly blank.
cols.EMPLOYEE_SUSPENSION: Whether the hurt worker was suspended. Mostly blank.
cols.DISTRICT: The number of the federal rail safety region, 1 through 8, where it happened.
cols.FATALITY: Yes if the person died. Use this column to count deaths.
cols.FORM_57_FILED: Yes if this casualty also has a road-crossing crash report.
cols.CLASS_CODE: A code for the kind of railroad, like 1L or 3S; the codes need a lookup.
cols.CLASS: The railroad's size class: Class I, Class II, Class III, or not assigned.
cols.CASUALTY_OCCURRENCE_CODE: A three-digit code for how the casualty happened. The codes need a lookup.
cols.EQUIPMENT_MOVEMENT_CODE: A one-letter code for how the rail equipment was moving. The codes need a lookup. Mostly blank.

TRANSPORT__FED_FRA_CASUALTIES.summary: Every injury, illness and death railroads reported to the Federal Railroad Administration from 1975 on, covering workers, passengers, trespassers and others, with who was hurt and how.
TRANSPORT__FED_FRA_CASUALTIES.row: One casualty: one person injured, made ill or killed in one railroad incident.

cols.RAILROAD_CODE: The short code for a railroad, like UP for Union Pacific or CSX.
cols.RAILROAD_NAME: The railroad company's full name, like CSX Transportation. The FRA safety table holds only N/A.
cols.REPORT_YEAR: The year the report covers, like 2010. One table stores it as a January 1 date like 2014-01-01.
cols.INCIDENT_NUMBER: The railroad's own number for the incident, like GT0634. Only unique together with the railroad and date.
cols.INCIDENT_YEAR: The year the incident happened, like 2005. The rail crossing table holds two-digit values like 13 instead.
cols.INCIDENT_MONTH: The month of the incident as two digits, like 08. Stored as text.
cols.OTHER_RAILROAD_CODE: The short code of a second railroad involved, like CSX. Almost always blank.
cols.OTHER_RAILROAD_NAME: The name of a second railroad involved. Almost always blank.
cols.MAINTENANCE_RAILROAD_CODE: The short code of the railroad that maintains the track, like NS or CSX.
cols.MAINTENANCE_RAILROAD_NAME: The name of the railroad that maintains the track, like Norfolk Southern Railway Company.
cols.GRADE_CROSSING_ID: The national ID of the road-rail crossing, six digits and a letter, like 630474Y. Mostly blank in the equipment accidents table, and some crossing rows say NOTASGN instead.
cols.MONTH: The month, in many formats: January, 01, 1998-11, 10-2011, a mid-month date like 2026-03-15, or Total. One table leaves it empty.
cols.DAY: The day of the month as two digits, like 09. Stored as text.
cols.SUBDIVISION: The railroad's name for its stretch of line, like PIEDMONT. Mostly blank.
cols.COUNTY_CODE: The county's number code, written different ways: three digits like 001, sometimes without leading zeros like 3, five digits with the state like 11001, or state letters plus digits like FL095. One table uses name codes like US_SD_CLARK, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some tables add County, Parish or the state, like Garza County, TX, so clean it before matching. One table uses Undetermined as a filler, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state, as two letters like TX in some tables and as a number code like 48 or 06 in others, which needs a lookup and sometimes drops its leading zero. One table writes it like US_TX, and one leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.CITY_NAME: The city name. Casing varies, and some rows hold fillers like Not in a City, UNKNOWN or N/A.
cols.TEMPERATURE: The air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit when the rail incident happened. Empty in the weather table.
cols.VISIBILITY_CODE: A code 1 to 4 for light conditions. The words for it are in VISIBILITY.
cols.VISIBILITY: The light conditions: Dawn, Day, Dusk or Dark.
cols.WEATHER_CONDITION_CODE: A code 1 to 6 for the weather. The words for it are in WEATHER_CONDITION.
cols.WEATHER_CONDITION: The weather at the time, like Clear, Rain, Fog or Snow.
cols.EQUIPMENT_TYPE_CODE: A code for the kind of train or equipment involved, a number or letter. Needs the rail agency's lookup.
cols.EQUIPMENT_TYPE: What kind of rail equipment was involved, like Freight Train, Yard/switching or Cut of cars. The safety table holds only N/A.
cols.TRACK_TYPE_CODE: A code 1 to 4 for the kind of track. The words for it are in TRACK_TYPE.
cols.TRACK_TYPE: The kind of track: Main, Yard, Siding or Industry.
cols.TRACK_NAME: The railroad's own name for the track, like SINGLE MAIN TRACK. Free text, spelled many ways.
cols.TRACK_CLASS: The track's safety class, mostly a number from 1 to 6 that sets its speed limit; X means excepted track, and a few rows hold 0 or 7.
cols.TRAIN_SPEED: How fast the train was going, in miles per hour.
cols.TRAIN_DIRECTION_CODE: A code 1 to 4 for which way the train was heading. The words for it are in TRAIN_DIRECTION.
cols.TRAIN_DIRECTION: Which way the train was heading: North, South, East or West.
cols.FORM_54_FILED: Whether the railroad also filed a Form 54 report on the incident: Yes or No.
cols.PASSENGERS_KILLED: How many train passengers were killed. Almost always 0.
cols.PASSENGERS_INJURED: How many train passengers were hurt.
cols.SPECIAL_STUDY_1: A tag the rail agency uses to mark incidents for a special study, like CWR or OTH, whose meanings need a lookup. Almost always blank, with junk like N/A, 0 and NO NO mixed in.
cols.SPECIAL_STUDY_2: A second special-study tag, free text like "VIDEO USED - NO" or number strings like 000-000-000. Almost always blank.
cols.NARRATIVE: A free-text account of what happened, as the reporter wrote it, often in capitals with abbreviations. Mostly blank in several tables, and the rail equipment table fills many rows with junk like NoneNoneNone.
cols.REPORT_KEY: A row ID for the rail incident report, built by gluing the railroad code, its own report number and the year and month together.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_CLASS: The size class of the railroad that filed the report: Class I is the big ones, Class III the small ones. Some rows say Not Assigned or Unassigned.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_SMT_GROUPING: Which federal rail safety team the reporting railroad falls under, like SMT-5 - BNSF. Not Assigned shows up.
cols.REPORTING_PARENT_RAILROAD_CODE: The short code for the parent railroad of the company that filed the report, like BNSF or CSX.
cols.REPORTING_PARENT_RAILROAD_NAME: The full name of the parent railroad of the company that filed the report, like BNSF Railway Company.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_HOLDING_COMPANY: The company that owns the railroad that filed the report, like Genesee & Wyoming or BNSF Railway Company. Not Assigned shows up.
cols.URL: A web link to the record's own page at the source.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_INDIVIDUAL_CLASS: The size class of the railroad that filed the report: Class I is the big national lines, Class III the small ones. Not Assigned and Unassigned both show up.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_PASSENGER: Whether the railroad that filed the report carries passengers: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_COMMUTER: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a commuter line: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_SWITCHING_TERMINAL: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a switching or terminal line that moves cars around yards: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_TOURIST: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a tourist or excursion line: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_FREIGHT: Whether the railroad that filed the report hauls freight: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_SHORT_LINE: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a small short-line railroad: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.OTHER_INCIDENT_NUMBER: The incident number the second railroad gave this crash, when two railroads were involved. Placeholders like XXX and ZZZ appear. Mostly blank.
cols.OTHER_INCIDENT_YEAR: The two-digit year of the second railroad's incident number, like 77 for 1977. Mostly blank.
cols.OTHER_INCIDENT_MONTH: The two-digit month of the second railroad's incident number. Mostly blank.
cols.MAINTAINANCE_INCIDENT_NUMBER: The incident number of the railroad that maintains the crossing. The placeholder XXX shows up often.
cols.MAINTENANCE_INCIDENT_YEAR: The two-digit year of the maintaining railroad's incident number, like 78 for 1978.
cols.MAINTENANCE_INCIDENT_MONTH: The two-digit month of the maintaining railroad's incident number.
cols.HOUR: The hour of the crash on a 12-hour clock; read it with the AM or PM column.
cols.AM_PM: Whether the crash hour is AM or PM.
cols.TIME: The time of the crash as text, like 02:40 PM.
cols.NEAREST_STATION: The nearest railroad station or town to the crossing.
cols.DIVISION: The railroad's own operating division where the crash happened, like Chicago or Gulf. Mostly blank.
cols.HIGHWAY_NAME: The name of the road that crosses the tracks. Private crossings are often just labeled PRIVATE.
cols.PUBLIC_PRIVATE_CODE: Y for a public road crossing, N for a private one.
cols.PUBLIC_PRIVATE: Whether the crossing is on a public or private road.
cols.HIGHWAY_USER_CODE: A letter code for what the train hit; the next column spells it out, like A for auto and B for truck.
cols.HIGHWAY_USER: What the train hit or was hit by, like an auto, truck, truck-trailer or pedestrian.
cols.ESTIMATED_VEHICLE_SPEED: The road vehicle's estimated speed in miles per hour. Zero is common because many vehicles were stopped.
cols.VEHICLE_DIRECTION_CODE: A number code for which way the road vehicle was heading; the next column spells it out.
cols.VEHICLE_DIRECTION: Which way the road vehicle was heading: north, south, east or west.
cols.HIGHWAY_USER_POSITION_CODE: A number code for where the road user was; the next column spells it out.
cols.HIGHWAY_USER_POSITION: Where the road user was when hit, like moving over the crossing, stopped on it, or stalled on it.
cols.EQUIPMENT_INVOLVED_CODE: A number code for the kind of rail equipment involved; the next column spells it out.
cols.EQUIPMENT_INVOLVED: What rail equipment was involved, like a train with engines pulling or pushing, or a lone locomotive.
cols.RAILROAD_CAR_UNIT_POSITION: Which car or engine in the train made contact, counting from the front. Usually 1, the lead unit.
cols.EQUIPMENT_STRUCK_CODE: A number code for who hit whom; the next column spells it out.
cols.EQUIPMENT_STRUCK: Whether the train struck the road user, or the road user struck the train.
cols.HAZMAT_INVOLVEMENT_CODE: A number code for whether hazardous materials were involved; the next column spells it out.
cols.HAZMAT_INVOLVEMENT: Whether hazardous materials were on the train, the road vehicle, both, or neither.
cols.HAZMAT_RELEASED_BY_CODE: A number code for who released hazardous materials; the next column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.HAZMAT_RELEASED_BY: Who spilled hazardous materials, if anyone: the road user, the train, both, or neither. Mostly blank.
cols.HAZMAT_RELEASED_NAME: The hazardous material that spilled, like diesel fuel. Placeholders like 0 and NULL appear. Mostly blank.
cols.HAZMAT_RELEASED_QUANTITY: How much hazardous material spilled, as free text with placeholders like 000 and units mixed in. Mostly blank.
cols.HAZMAT_RELEASED_MEASURE: The unit for the spilled amount, like gallons or tons, spelled many ways. Mostly blank, and most filled rows hold the placeholder 0.
cols.NUMBER_OF_LOCOMOTIVE_UNITS: How many locomotives were in the train. A number stored as text.
cols.NUMBER_OF_CARS: How many rail cars were in the train. A number stored as text.
cols.ESTIMATED_RECORDED_SPEED: Whether the train's speed was estimated, E, or recorded by equipment, R.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_CODE_1: A number code for warning device 1 at the crossing; the matching expanded column spells it out.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_CODE_2: A number code for warning device 2 at the crossing; the matching expanded column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_CODE_3: A number code for warning device 3 at the crossing; the matching expanded column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_CODE_4: A number code for warning device 4 at the crossing; the matching expanded column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_CODE_5: A number code for warning device 5 at the crossing; the matching expanded column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_CODE_6: A number code for warning device 6 at the crossing; the matching expanded column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_CODE_7: A number code for warning device 7 at the crossing; the matching expanded column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_CODE_8: A number code for warning device 8 at the crossing; the matching expanded column spells it out. Filled on 1 row only.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_CODE_9: A number code for warning device 9 at the crossing; the matching expanded column spells it out. Empty in this table.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_CODE_10: A number code for warning device 10 at the crossing; the matching expanded column spells it out. Empty in this table.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_CODE_11: A number code for warning device 11 at the crossing; the matching expanded column spells it out. Empty in this table.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_CODE_12: A number code for warning device 12 at the crossing; the matching expanded column spells it out. Empty in this table.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_1: The first kind of warning at the crossing, like crossbucks, gates or standard flashing lights, written Standard FLS.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_2: Warning device 2 at the crossing, like crossbucks, gates, stop signs or bells marked Audible. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_3: Warning device 3 at the crossing, like crossbucks, gates, stop signs or bells marked Audible. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_4: Warning device 4 at the crossing, like crossbucks, gates, stop signs or bells marked Audible. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_5: Warning device 5 at the crossing, like crossbucks, gates, stop signs or bells marked Audible. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_6: Warning device 6 at the crossing, like crossbucks, gates, stop signs or bells marked Audible. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_7: Warning device 7 at the crossing, like crossbucks, gates, stop signs or bells marked Audible. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_8: Warning device 8 at the crossing, like crossbucks, gates, stop signs or bells marked Audible. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_9: Warning device 9 at the crossing, like crossbucks, gates, stop signs or bells marked Audible. Empty in this table.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_10: Warning device 10 at the crossing, like crossbucks, gates, stop signs or bells marked Audible. Empty in this table.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_11: Warning device 11 at the crossing, like crossbucks, gates, stop signs or bells marked Audible. Empty in this table.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPANDED_12: Warning device 12 at the crossing, like crossbucks, gates, stop signs or bells marked Audible. Empty in this table.
cols.SIGNALED_CROSSING_WARNING_CODE: A number code for whether the crossing signals gave proper warning; the next column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.SIGNALED_CROSSING_WARNING: Whether the crossing signals worked, like provided the minimum 20-second warning, or alleged no warning. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPLANATION_CODE: A letter code explaining a signal problem; the next column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_EXPLANATION: Why the signals did not work as they should, like devices out of service. Mostly blank.
cols.ROADWAY_CONDITION_CODE: A letter code for the road surface; the next column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.ROADWAY_CONDITION: The road surface at the time, like dry, wet, snow or ice. Mostly blank.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_LOCATION_CODE: A number code for where the warning devices stand; the next column spells it out. Includes a 0 not explained there.
cols.CROSSING_WARNING_LOCATION: Which side of the crossing the warning devices are on: both sides, or only one side.
cols.WARNING_CONNECTED_TO_SIGNAL: Whether the crossing warning is wired to a nearby road traffic signal: yes, no or unknown.
cols.CROSSING_ILLUMINATED: Whether the crossing had street lighting: yes, no or unknown.
cols.USER_AGE: The age of the road user. Zero appears often and likely means unknown. Mostly blank.
cols.USER_SEX: The road user's sex, male or female. Mostly blank.
cols.USER_STRUCK_BY_SECOND_TRAIN: Whether the road user was then hit by a second train: yes, no or unknown.
cols.HIGHWAY_USER_ACTION_CODE: A number code for what the road user did; the next column spells it out.
cols.HIGHWAY_USER_ACTION: What the road user did, like did not stop, stopped on the crossing, or went around the gate.
cols.DRIVER_PASSED_VEHICLE: Whether the driver passed another vehicle to get onto the crossing: yes, no or unknown.
cols.VIEW_OBSTRUCTION_CODE: A number code for what blocked the view of the track; the next column spells it out.
cols.VIEW_OBSTRUCTION: What blocked the driver's view of the train, like vegetation or a building. Mostly not obstructed.
cols.DRIVER_CONDITION_CODE: A number code for how the driver came out; the next column spells it out.
cols.DRIVER_CONDITION: How the driver came out: uninjured, injured or killed.
cols.DRIVER_IN_VEHICLE: Whether the driver was still in the vehicle when it was hit.
cols.CROSSING_USERS_KILLED: How many road users were killed.
cols.CROSSING_USERS_INJURED: How many road users were hurt.
cols.VEHICLE_DAMAGE_COST: The estimated damage to the road vehicle, in dollars.
cols.NUMBER_VEHICLE_OCCUPANTS: How many people were in the road vehicle, counting the driver.
cols.EMPLOYEES_KILLED: How many railroad workers were killed.
cols.EMPLOYEES_INJURED: How many railroad workers were hurt.
cols.NUMBER_PEOPLE_ON_TRAIN: How many people were on the train. Mostly blank.
cols.VIDEO_TAKEN: Whether a camera recorded the crash. Mostly blank.
cols.VIDEO_USED: Whether that video was used in the report. Mostly blank.
cols.TOTAL_KILLED_FORM_57: Everyone killed in the crash, as counted on the crossing crash form. Use this column to count deaths.
cols.TOTAL_INJURED_FORM_57: Everyone hurt in the crash, as counted on the crossing crash form. Use this column to count injuries.
cols.RAILROAD_TYPE: A code for the kind of railroad, like 1L or 3S; the codes need a lookup.
cols.JOINT_CODE: A code, 1 or 2, for whether the crash was reported jointly by more than one railroad. Almost all are 1; the codes need a lookup.
cols.TOTAL_KILLED_FORM_55A: Deaths as counted on the railroad's monthly casualty summary form. Can differ slightly from the crash form count.
cols.TOTAL_INJURED_FORM_55A: Injuries as counted on the railroad's monthly casualty summary form. Can differ slightly from the crash form count.
cols.DISTRICT: The number of the federal rail safety region, 1 through 8, where the crash happened.
cols.WHISTLE_BAN_CODE: A code for whether a local ban on train horns applies; the next column spells it out. Mostly blank.
cols.WHISTLE_BAN: Whether a local ban on sounding train horns was in effect at the crossing: yes, no or not provided. Mostly blank.

TRANSPORT__FED_FRA_CROSSING_INCIDENTS.summary: Every collision between a train and a car, truck or person at a road-rail crossing reported to the Federal Railroad Administration, from the late 1970s on, with where it happened, who was hit and how bad it was; 24 incident numbers appear twice because of amended or joint filings.
TRANSPORT__FED_FRA_CROSSING_INCIDENTS.row: One crossing crash: one train hitting, or being hit by, a road user at one crossing on one day, as reported by one railroad.

cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. A few tables use a range like 2020-2022, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.OTHER_RAILROAD_CODE: The short code of a second railroad involved, like CSX. Almost always blank.
cols.OTHER_RAILROAD_NAME: The name of a second railroad involved. Almost always blank.
cols.MAINTENANCE_RAILROAD_CODE: The short code of the railroad that maintains the track, like NS or CSX.
cols.MAINTENANCE_RAILROAD_NAME: The name of the railroad that maintains the track, like Norfolk Southern Railway Company.
cols.GRADE_CROSSING_ID: The national ID of the road-rail crossing, six digits and a letter, like 630474Y. Mostly blank in the equipment accidents table, and some crossing rows say NOTASGN instead.
cols.DAY: The day of the month as two digits, like 09. Stored as text.
cols.ACCIDENT_TYPE: What kind of accident it was, in words: things like "Struck by falling object" for mines, "Derailment" for trains.
cols.SUBDIVISION: The railroad's name for its stretch of line, like PIEDMONT. Mostly blank.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state, as two letters like TX in some tables and as a number code like 48 or 06 in others, which needs a lookup and sometimes drops its leading zero. One table writes it like US_TX, and one leaves it empty.
cols.STATE_ABBREVIATION: The state as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam and AS for American Samoa appear too.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas, in capitals in some tables. Territories like Guam show up, one table lists New York City as its own entry, and one table leaves it empty.
cols.COUNTY_CODE: The county's number code, written different ways: three digits like 001, sometimes without leading zeros like 3, five digits with the state like 11001, or state letters plus digits like FL095. One table uses name codes like US_SD_CLARK, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some tables add County, Parish or the state, like Garza County, TX, so clean it before matching. One table uses Undetermined as a filler, and the rail casualty table leaves it mostly blank.
cols.TEMPERATURE: The air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit when the rail incident happened. Empty in the weather table.
cols.VISIBILITY_CODE: A code 1 to 4 for light conditions. The words for it are in VISIBILITY.
cols.VISIBILITY: The light conditions: Dawn, Day, Dusk or Dark.
cols.WEATHER_CONDITION_CODE: A code 1 to 6 for the weather. The words for it are in WEATHER_CONDITION.
cols.WEATHER_CONDITION: The weather at the time, like Clear, Rain, Fog or Snow.
cols.TRACK_TYPE_CODE: A code 1 to 4 for the kind of track. The words for it are in TRACK_TYPE.
cols.TRACK_TYPE: The kind of track: Main, Yard, Siding or Industry.
cols.TRACK_NAME: The railroad's own name for the track, like SINGLE MAIN TRACK. Free text, spelled many ways.
cols.TRACK_CLASS: The track's safety class, mostly a number from 1 to 6 that sets its speed limit; X means excepted track, and a few rows hold 0 or 7.
cols.TRAIN_DIRECTION_CODE: A code 1 to 4 for which way the train was heading. The words for it are in TRAIN_DIRECTION.
cols.TRAIN_DIRECTION: Which way the train was heading: North, South, East or West.
cols.EQUIPMENT_TYPE_CODE: A code for the kind of train or equipment involved, a number or letter. Needs the rail agency's lookup.
cols.EQUIPMENT_TYPE: What kind of rail equipment was involved, like Freight Train, Yard/switching or Cut of cars. The safety table holds only N/A.
cols.TRAIN_SPEED: How fast the train was going, in miles per hour.
cols.POSITIVE_ALCOHOL_TESTS: How many people tested positive for alcohol after the incident. Mostly blank; text in one table.
cols.POSITIVE_DRUG_TESTS: How many people tested positive for drugs after the incident. Mostly blank; text in one table.
cols.PASSENGERS_KILLED: How many train passengers were killed. Almost always 0.
cols.PASSENGERS_INJURED: How many train passengers were hurt.
cols.SPECIAL_STUDY_1: A tag the rail agency uses to mark incidents for a special study, like CWR or OTH, whose meanings need a lookup. Almost always blank, with junk like N/A, 0 and NO NO mixed in.
cols.SPECIAL_STUDY_2: A second special-study tag, free text like "VIDEO USED - NO" or number strings like 000-000-000. Almost always blank.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.NARRATIVE: A free-text account of what happened, as the reporter wrote it, often in capitals with abbreviations. Mostly blank in several tables, and the rail equipment table fills many rows with junk like NoneNoneNone.
cols.INCIDENT_KEY: A key built from the railroad code, its incident number, year and month run together, like BNGT0634199011.
cols.REPORT_KEY: A row ID for the rail incident report, built by gluing the railroad code, its own report number and the year and month together.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_CLASS: The size class of the railroad that filed the report: Class I is the big ones, Class III the small ones. Some rows say Not Assigned or Unassigned.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_SMT_GROUPING: Which federal rail safety team the reporting railroad falls under, like SMT-5 - BNSF. Not Assigned shows up.
cols.REPORTING_PARENT_RAILROAD_CODE: The short code for the parent railroad of the company that filed the report, like BNSF or CSX.
cols.REPORTING_PARENT_RAILROAD_NAME: The full name of the parent railroad of the company that filed the report, like BNSF Railway Company.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_HOLDING_COMPANY: The company that owns the railroad that filed the report, like Genesee & Wyoming or BNSF Railway Company. Not Assigned shows up.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_INDIVIDUAL_CLASS: The size class of the railroad that filed the report: Class I is the big national lines, Class III the small ones. Not Assigned and Unassigned both show up.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_PASSENGER: Whether the railroad that filed the report carries passengers: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_COMMUTER: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a commuter line: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_SWITCHING_TERMINAL: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a switching or terminal line that moves cars around yards: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_TOURIST: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a tourist or excursion line: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_FREIGHT: Whether the railroad that filed the report hauls freight: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_SHORT_LINE: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a small short-line railroad: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_CODE: The short code of the railroad that filed this report, like UP or BNSF.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_NAME: The name of the railroad that filed this report, like Union Pacific Railroad Company.
cols.ACCIDENT_NUMBER: The railroad's own number for the accident. Read it together with the railroad, year and month to pin down one accident.
cols.PDF_LINK: A web link to the accident report on the rail agency's safety data site.
cols.ACCIDENT_YEAR: The year of the accident as two digits, like 78 for 1978. Stored as text.
cols.ACCIDENT_MONTH: The month of the accident as two digits, like 03. Stored as text.
cols.OTHER_ACCIDENT_NUMBER: The accident number used by a second railroad involved. Mostly blank; placeholders like INDUSTRY and ZZZZZZZZZZ show up.
cols.OTHER_ACCIDENT_YEAR: The year on the second railroad's report, as two digits. Mostly blank.
cols.OTHER_ACCIDENT_MONTH: The month on the second railroad's report, as two digits. Mostly blank.
cols.MAINTENANCE_ACCIDENT_NUMBER: The accident number used by the railroad that maintains the track. INDUSTRY appears as a placeholder.
cols.MAINTENANCE_ACCIDENT_YEAR: The year on the track-maintaining railroad's report, as two digits.
cols.MAINTENANCE_ACCIDENT_MONTH: The month on the track-maintaining railroad's report, as two digits.
cols.TIME: The time of the accident, like 5:00 PM. Stored as text.
cols.ACCIDENT_TYPE_CODE: A two-digit code for the kind of accident, like 01. The words for it are in ACCIDENT_TYPE.
cols.HAZMAT_CARS: How many cars in the train carried hazardous materials. Mostly 0.
cols.HAZMAT_CARS_DAMAGED: How many hazardous-material cars were damaged or derailed. Mostly 0.
cols.HAZMAT_RELEASED_CARS: How many cars leaked hazardous material. Almost always 0.
cols.PERSONS_EVACUATED: How many people were evacuated. Almost always 0.
cols.DIVISION_CODE: A short code for the railroad's operating division, like SYSTEM. ?????? is a common placeholder for unknown.
cols.DIVISION: The railroad's operating division, like CHICAGO or SYSTEM.
cols.STATION: The nearest station or yard, like KANSAS CITY.
cols.MILEPOST: The milepost where it happened, as text. Values like 0.0, 0000.0 and YARD are common fillers.
cols.DISTRICT: The rail agency's region number, 1 to 8.
cols.TRACK_DENSITY: How much traffic the track carries, as text. Mostly blank, and zeros written many ways are common.
cols.EQUIPMENT_ATTENDED: Whether a crew was on the equipment: Yes or No, with a few stray codes.
cols.TRAIN_NUMBER: The railroad's name or number for the train, like 1 or CUTO.
cols.RECORDED_ESTIMATED_SPEED: Whether the speed was Recorded by equipment or Estimated, with a few stray letter codes.
cols.MAXIMUM_SPEED: The highest speed allowed on that track, in miles per hour.
cols.GROSS_TONNAGE: The train's total weight in tons, not counting locomotives. 0 is common, often meaning not given.
cols.SIGNALIZATION_CODE: A code 1 or 2 for whether the track has signals. The words are in SIGNALIZATION. Mostly blank.
cols.SIGNALIZATION: Whether the track has signals: Signaled or Not Signaled. Mostly blank.
cols.METHOD_OF_OPERATION_CODE: A letter code for how trains on that track are controlled, like N or E. Codes need a lookup.
cols.METHOD_OF_OPERATION: How trains on that track are controlled, like Signal Indication or Other Than Main Track. Mostly blank.
cols.ADJUNCT_CODE_1: A letter code for an extra train-control system in use, like K. The words are in ADJUNCT_NAME_1. Mostly blank.
cols.ADJUNCT_NAME_1: An extra train-control system in use, like Restricted Speed or Positive Train Control. Mostly blank.
cols.ADJUNCT_CODE_2: A second extra train-control system code. Mostly blank.
cols.ADJUNCT_NAME_2: A second extra train-control system, like Special Instructions. Mostly blank.
cols.ADJUNCT_CODE_3: A third extra train-control system code. Mostly blank.
cols.ADJUNCT_NAME_3: A third extra train-control system, like Traffic Control System. Mostly blank.
cols.REMOTE_CONTROL_LOCOMOTIVE_CODE: A code 0 to 3 for whether the locomotive was run by remote control. The words are in REMOTE_CONTROL_LOCOMOTIVE. Mostly blank.
cols.REMOTE_CONTROL_LOCOMOTIVE: Whether the locomotive was run by remote control, and how, like from a portable transmitter or a tower. Mostly blank.
cols.FIRST_CAR_INITIALS: The owner letters painted on the first car involved, like UP or GATX.
cols.FIRST_CAR_NUMBER: The number painted on the first car involved.
cols.FIRST_CAR_POSITION: Where the first car involved sat in the train, counting from the front.
cols.FIRST_CAR_LOADED: Whether the first car involved was loaded: Yes or No, with a few stray letters.
cols.CAUSING_CAR_INITIALS: The owner letters on the car that caused the accident. Mostly blank.
cols.CAUSING_CAR_NUMBER: The number on the car that caused the accident. Mostly blank.
cols.CAUSING_CAR_POSITION: Where the car that caused the accident sat in the train. Mostly blank, and 0 is the most common value.
cols.CAUSING_CAR_LOADED: Whether the car that caused the accident was loaded: Yes or No. Mostly blank.
cols.PASSENGERS_TRANSPORTED: Whether the train was carrying passengers: Yes or No.
cols.HEAD_END_LOCOMOTIVES: How many locomotives were at the front of the train. Stored as text.
cols.MID_TRAIN_MANUAL_LOCOMOTIVES: How many crewed locomotives were in the middle of the train. Almost always 0. Stored as text.
cols.MID_TRAIN_REMOTE_LOCOMOTIVES: How many remote-controlled locomotives were in the middle of the train. Almost always 0. Stored as text.
cols.REAR_END_MANUAL_LOCOMOTIVES: How many crewed locomotives were at the back of the train. Almost always 0. Stored as text.
cols.REAR_END_REMOTE_LOCOMOTIVES: How many remote-controlled locomotives were at the back of the train. Almost always 0. Stored as text.
cols.DERAILED_HEAD_END_LOCOMOTIVES: How many front locomotives came off the rails. Mostly 0. Stored as text.
cols.DERAILED_MID_TRAIN_MANUAL_LOCOMOTIVES: How many crewed middle locomotives came off the rails. Almost always 0.
cols.DERAILED_MID_TRAIN_REMOTE_LOCOMOTIVES: How many remote-controlled middle locomotives came off the rails. Almost always 0.
cols.DERAILED_REAR_END_MANUAL_LOCOMOTIVES: How many crewed rear locomotives came off the rails. Almost always 0.
cols.DERAILED_REAR_END_REMOTE_LOCOMOTIVES: How many remote-controlled rear locomotives came off the rails. Almost always 0.
cols.LOADED_FREIGHT_CARS: How many loaded freight cars were in the train. Stored as text.
cols.LOADED_PASSENGER_CARS: How many passenger cars with people aboard were in the train. Mostly 0. Stored as text.
cols.EMPTY_FREIGHT_CARS: How many empty freight cars were in the train. Stored as text.
cols.EMPTY_PASSENGER_CARS: How many empty passenger cars were in the train. Mostly 0. Stored as text.
cols.CABOOSES: How many cabooses were in the train, usually 0 or 1. Stored as text.
cols.DERAILED_LOADED_FREIGHT_CARS: How many loaded freight cars came off the rails. Stored as text.
cols.DERAILED_LOADED_PASSENGER_CARS: How many passenger cars with people aboard came off the rails. Almost always 0.
cols.DERAILED_EMPTY_FREIGHT_CARS: How many empty freight cars came off the rails. Stored as text.
cols.DERAILED_EMPTY_PASSENGER_CARS: How many empty passenger cars came off the rails. Almost always 0.
cols.DERAILED_CABOOSES: How many cabooses came off the rails. A few odd values like 100 and 350 look like typos.
cols.EQUIPMENT_DAMAGE_COST: Dollar damage to locomotives and cars, as the railroad reported it.
cols.TRACK_DAMAGE_COST: Dollar damage to track and signals. 0 is common.
cols.TOTAL_DAMAGE_COST: Total dollar damage, equipment plus track. Use this column to size an accident.
cols.PRIMARY_ACCIDENT_CAUSE_CODE: A code for the main cause, like T110 or H702. The words are in PRIMARY_ACCIDENT_CAUSE.
cols.PRIMARY_ACCIDENT_CAUSE: The main cause in words, like Switch improperly lined or Wide gage.
cols.CONTRIBUTING_ACCIDENT_CAUSE_CODE: A code for a second, contributing cause. Mostly blank.
cols.CONTRIBUTING_ACCIDENT_CAUSE: A second, contributing cause in words. Mostly blank.
cols.ACCIDENT_CAUSE_CODE: A cause code, like T110. Nearly the same as PRIMARY_ACCIDENT_CAUSE_CODE but differs on some rows.
cols.ACCIDENT_CAUSE: The cause in words. Nearly the same as PRIMARY_ACCIDENT_CAUSE but differs on some rows.
cols.ENGINEERS_ON_DUTY: How many engineers were on duty on the train, usually 1. Stored as text.
cols.FIREMEN_ON_DUTY: How many firemen were on duty on the train, usually 0. Stored as text.
cols.CONDUCTORS_ON_DUTY: How many conductors were on duty on the train, usually 1. Stored as text.
cols.BRAKEMEN_ON_DUTY: How many brakemen were on duty on the train. Stored as text.
cols.HOURS_ENGINEERS_ON_DUTY: How many hours the engineer had been on duty. Add MINUTES_ENGINEERS_ON_DUTY for the full time.
cols.MINUTES_ENGINEERS_ON_DUTY: The minutes part of the engineer's time on duty.
cols.HOURS_CONDUCTORS_ON_DUTY: How many hours the conductor had been on duty. Add MINUTES_CONDUCTORS_ON_DUTY for the full time.
cols.MINUTES_CONDUCTORS_ON_DUTY: The minutes part of the conductor's time on duty.
cols.RAILROAD_EMPLOYEES_KILLED: How many railroad workers were killed. Almost always 0.
cols.RAILROAD_EMPLOYEES_INJURED: How many railroad workers were hurt. Mostly 0.
cols.OTHERS_KILLED: How many other people, not railroad workers, were killed. Almost always 0.
cols.OTHERS_INJURED: How many other people, not railroad workers, were hurt. Almost always 0.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_FATALITIES_FOR_55A: Deaths the reporting railroad counted on its monthly summary form. Mostly 0. Stored as text.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_INJURIES_FOR_55A: Injuries the reporting railroad counted on its monthly summary form. Mostly 0. Stored as text.
cols.TOTAL_PERSONS_KILLED: Everyone killed in the accident. Mostly 0.
cols.TOTAL_PERSONS_INJURED: Everyone hurt in the accident. Mostly 0.
cols.TOTAL_KILLED_FORM_54: Deaths counted on the accident report form itself. Mostly 0. Stored as text.
cols.TOTAL_INJURED_FORM_54: Injuries counted on the accident report form itself. Mostly 0. Stored as text.
cols.JOINT_TRACK_TYPE: The kind of track where it happened: Yard, Main, Industry or Siding.
cols.JOINT_TRACK_CLASS: The safety class of the track, mostly a number 1 to 6; X and 0 also show up.
cols.CLASS_CODE: The size class of the reporting railroad, like 1L, 3L or CL, with mixed casing. Codes need a lookup.
cols.CLASS: Same values as CLASS_CODE: the railroad size class code, like 1L.
cols.JOINT_CD: A code 1, 2 or 3 for how many railroads were involved in the accident. Codes need a lookup.
cols.LOCATION: The map point of the accident as POINT with longitude then latitude. Mostly blank, and the point at 0, 0 is a placeholder for no location.

TRANSPORT__FED_FRA_EQUIPMENT_ACCIDENTS.summary: Train derailments, collisions and other rail equipment accidents reported to the Federal Railroad Administration since the 1970s, with damage costs, causes and deaths. The same accident repeats once for each railroad involved, so count accidents with care.
TRANSPORT__FED_FRA_EQUIPMENT_ACCIDENTS.row: One accident as reported by one railroad: if two railroads were involved, the accident shows up twice.

cols.RAILROAD_CODE: The short code for a railroad, like UP for Union Pacific or CSX.
cols.RAILROAD_NAME: The railroad company's full name, like CSX Transportation. The FRA safety table holds only N/A.
cols.INCIDENT_YEAR: The year the incident happened, like 2005. The rail crossing table holds two-digit values like 13 instead.
cols.TYPE_OF_PERSON: Who was hurt or killed, like Trespassers, Passengers on Trains or Worker on Duty.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.PARENT_RAILROAD_CODE: Short code of the parent railroad, like UP, CN or CSX.
cols.PARENT_RAILROAD_NAME: Name of the parent railroad, like Union Pacific Railroad Company.
cols.HOLDING_COMPANY: The holding company over the railroad. Not Assigned on over a third of rows.

TRANSPORT__FED_FRA_RAIL_DEATHS_BY_RAILRO.summary: Deaths on U.S. railroads from 1975 on, counted by railroad, year and kind of person killed, like worker, passenger or trespasser, from Federal Railroad Administration reports.
TRANSPORT__FED_FRA_RAIL_DEATHS_BY_RAILRO.row: One railroad-year count: deaths of one kind of person reported by one railroad in one year.

cols.REPORT_ID: The ID of one report or filing. One table holds N/A instead.
cols.RAILROAD_NAME: The railroad company's full name, like CSX Transportation. The FRA safety table holds only N/A.
cols.STATE_FIPS: The state's number code, like 48 or 06, which needs a lookup. Several tables drop the leading zero so 6 means 06, some rows hold other codes like C1, TX, 00 or N/A, and three tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY_FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 01001, stored as text. One table holds only the three-digit county part like 017, one holds N/A, and two leave it empty.
cols.EQUIPMENT_TYPE: What kind of rail equipment was involved, like Freight Train, Yard/switching or Cut of cars. The safety table holds only N/A.
cols.NARRATIVE: A free-text account of what happened, as the reporter wrote it, often in capitals with abbreviations. Mostly blank in several tables, and the rail equipment table fills many rows with junk like NoneNoneNone.
cols.EVENT_DATE: Meant to hold the event's date. The one row says N/A.
cols.EVENT_TYPE: Meant to hold the kind of event. The one row says API_DOCUMENTATION_PAGE, showing a documentation page was loaded instead of data.
cols.CASUALTIES: Meant to hold casualty counts. The one row says N/A.
cols.CAUSE_CODE: Meant to hold the cause code. The one row says N/A.

TRANSPORT__FED_FRA_SAFETY.summary: A failed load: the table's one row holds placeholder text from a data documentation page, not any railroad safety records.
TRANSPORT__FED_FRA_SAFETY.row: One placeholder row: filler from a documentation page, not a real railroad event.

cols.EV_ID: The NTSB's ID for one aviation accident, starting with a date, like 20260625203249. Same ID across the aircraft, event and injury tables, so it joins them.
cols.AIRCRAFT_KEY: Which aircraft in the accident this row is about: almost always 1, then 2 when two planes were involved, and rarely 3 or 5.
cols.NTSB_NO: The accident safety board's case number, like DFW08LA055. The aircraft table adds A or B for each plane in a two-plane crash.
cols.OWNER_CITY: The city where the owner lives or is based. Capitals are mixed, and in the aviation table the text None often stands in for blank.
cols.OWNER_STATE: The owner's state, as two letters. In the aviation table the text None often stands in for blank.
cols.OWNER_ZIP: The owner's zip code, stored as text. Some are 9 digits, some lost a leading zero like 8540, a few are typo'd like 73`120, and in the aviation table the text None often stands in for blank.
cols.LCHG_DATE: The date the NTSB last changed this record.
cols.LCHG_USERID: The short login name of the NTSB staffer who last changed this record, like coln or dobn. Most rows hold the word None instead of a name.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.REGIS_NO: The aircraft's registration number, the tail number like N4535A or a foreign one like G-BCGJ.
cols.ACFT_MISSING: Y if the aircraft is missing, N if not. Almost all say N.
cols.FAR_PART: The federal flight rules the flight was flying under, as a code like 091 or 121 that needs a lookup. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.FLT_PLAN_FILED: What kind of flight plan was filed, like NONE, IFR or VFR. Codes need a lookup; UNK means unknown. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.FLIGHT_PLAN_ACTIVATED: Whether the flight plan was activated: Y, N, or U for unknown. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.DAMAGE: How badly the aircraft was damaged, as a code: SUBS, DEST, MINR or UNK. The codes need a lookup. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.ACFT_FIRE: Whether the aircraft caught fire and where, as a code like NONE, GRD, IFLT or BOTH that needs a lookup. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.ACFT_EXPL: Whether the aircraft exploded and where, as a code like NONE, GRD, IFLT or BOTH that needs a lookup. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.ACFT_MAKE: The aircraft maker, like CESSNA, PIPER or BOEING. Spelling and capitals vary, so Cessna and CESSNA both appear.
cols.ACFT_MODEL: The aircraft model, like 172, 737 or PA28.
cols.ACFT_SERIES: The model series letter or name, like A or B. Mostly the word None or NO SERIES.
cols.ACFT_SERIAL_NO: The maker's serial number for the airframe. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.CERT_MAX_GR_WT: The most the aircraft is certified to weigh at takeoff, in pounds, stored as text. Blanks are stored as the text nan.
cols.ACFT_CATEGORY: What kind of aircraft it is, as a code like AIR, HELI, GLI or BALL that needs a lookup. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.ACFT_REG_CLS: The aircraft's registration class. Every row says None, so it holds nothing.
cols.HOMEBUILT: Y if the aircraft was built by an amateur, N if factory-built.
cols.FC_SEATS: How many flight crew seats the aircraft has, stored as text. Mostly the text nan, meaning blank.
cols.CC_SEATS: How many cabin crew seats the aircraft has, stored as text. Almost always the text nan, meaning blank.
cols.PAX_SEATS: How many passenger seats the aircraft has, stored as text. Mostly the text nan, meaning blank.
cols.TOTAL_SEATS: How many seats the aircraft has in all, stored as text. Blanks are stored as the text nan.
cols.NUM_ENG: How many engines the aircraft has, stored as text like 1.0. Blanks are stored as the text nan.
cols.FIXED_RETRACTABLE: Whether the landing gear is fixed or folds up: FIXD or RETR.
cols.TYPE_LAST_INSP: The kind of inspection the aircraft last had, as a code like ANNL or 100H that needs a lookup. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.DATE_LAST_INSP: The date of the aircraft's last inspection. Blank for about a third of aircraft.
cols.AFM_HRS_LAST_INSP: Hours the airframe had flown since its last inspection, stored as text. Mostly the text nan, meaning blank.
cols.AFM_HRS: Total hours the airframe had flown, stored as text. Blanks are stored as the text nan.
cols.ELT_INSTALL: Whether an emergency locator beacon was installed: Y or N. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.ELT_OPER: Whether the emergency locator beacon went off: Y or N. Nearly half are the word None, meaning blank.
cols.ELT_AIDED_LOC_EV: Whether the emergency locator beacon helped find the wreck: Y or N. Mostly the word None.
cols.ELT_TYPE: The model standard of the emergency locator beacon, as a code like C126 or C91A that needs a lookup. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.OWNER_ACFT: The name of the aircraft's owner, a person or a company like DELTA AIR LINES INC. About half are the word None.
cols.OWNER_STREET: The owner's street address. Mostly the word None, and some say On File.
cols.OWNER_COUNTRY: The owner's country, like USA or a two-letter code like BR. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.OPER_INDIVIDUAL_NAME: Y if the operator is a person, N if it is a company.
cols.OPER_NAME: The name of whoever was operating the aircraft, like an airline, or just Pilot. About half are the word None.
cols.OPER_SAME: Whether the operator is the same as the owner. Every row says None, so it holds nothing.
cols.OPER_DBA: The trade name the operator does business as, like American Eagle. Almost always the word None.
cols.OPER_ADDR_SAME: Whether the operator's address matches the owner's. Every row says None, so it holds nothing.
cols.OPER_STREET: The operator's street address. Mostly the word None, and some say On File.
cols.OPER_CITY: The operator's city. Capitals vary, so ANCHORAGE and Anchorage both appear. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.OPER_STATE: The operator's state, as two letters. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.OPER_COUNTRY: The operator's country, like USA or a two-letter code like BR. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.OPER_ZIP: The operator's ZIP code. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.OPER_CODE: The operator's four-letter airline code, like DALA. Almost always the word None.
cols.CERTS_HELD: Y if the operator holds an FAA operating certificate. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.OPRTNG_CERT: The operator's certificate type. Every row says None, so it holds nothing.
cols.OPER_CERT: The operator's certificate. Every row says None, so it holds nothing.
cols.OPER_CERT_NUM: The operator's FAA certificate number, like SWAA304A. Almost always the word None.
cols.OPER_SCHED: Whether the flight was a scheduled service: SCHD or NSCH. Mostly the word None.
cols.OPER_DOM_INT: Whether the flight was domestic or international: DOM or INT. Mostly the word None.
cols.OPER_PAX_CARGO: Whether the flight carried passengers, cargo or mail: PAX, CARG or MAIL. Mostly the word None.
cols.TYPE_FLY: What the flight was for, as a code like PERS, INST or BUS that needs a lookup. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.SECOND_PILOT: Y if a second pilot was aboard, N if not. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.DPRT_PT_SAME_EV: Whether the flight took off from the accident site, as a code S, L, Y or U that needs a lookup. Mostly the word None.
cols.DPRT_APT_ID: The code of the airport the flight left from, like FAI. PVT, NONE and N/A also appear for private strips or none. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.DPRT_CITY: The city the flight left from. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.DPRT_STATE: The state the flight left from, as two letters. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.DPRT_COUNTRY: The country the flight left from, like USA or a two-letter code. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.DPRT_TIME: The local time the flight left, as a 24-hour number stored as text like 1700.0. Blanks are stored as the text nan.
cols.DPRT_TIMEZN: The time zone of the departure time. Every row says None, so it holds nothing.
cols.DEST_SAME_LOCAL: Whether the flight was meant to land where it took off. Every row says None, so it holds nothing.
cols.DEST_APT_ID: The code of the airport the flight was headed to. PVT and NONE also appear. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.DEST_CITY: The city the flight was headed to. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.DEST_STATE: The state the flight was headed to, as two letters. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.DEST_COUNTRY: The country the flight was headed to, like USA or a two-letter code. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.PHASE_FLT_SPEC: The phase of flight when things went wrong. Every row says None, so it holds nothing.
cols.REPORT_TO_ICAO: Whether the accident was reported to the world aviation body. Every row says None, so it holds nothing.
cols.EVACUATION: Whether the aircraft was evacuated. Every row says None, so it holds nothing.
cols.AFM_HRS_SINCE: Y or N flag tied to the airframe hours figure; its exact meaning needs the codebook.
cols.RWY_NUM: The runway number used, like 18 or 36. Mostly the word None.
cols.RWY_LEN: The runway length in feet, stored as text like 5000.0. Mostly the text nan, meaning blank.
cols.RWY_WIDTH: The runway width in feet, stored as text like 100.0. Mostly the text nan, meaning blank.
cols.SITE_SEEING: Y if the flight was a sightseeing flight, N if not. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.AIR_MEDICAL: Y if the flight was an air ambulance flight, N if not. Blanks are stored as the word None.
cols.MED_TYPE_FLIGHT: The kind of air ambulance flight, as a code like MEDE, DISC or ORGT that needs a lookup. Almost always the word None.
cols.ACFT_YEAR: The year the aircraft was built, stored as text like 1979.0. About half are the text nan, meaning blank.
cols.FUEL_ON_BOARD: How much fuel was aboard, stored as text; the unit is not stated. Mostly the word None.
cols.COMMERCIAL_SPACE_FLIGHT: True if this was a commercial space flight. Only one row says True.
cols.UNMANNED: True if the aircraft was a drone with no one aboard.
cols.IFR_EQUIPPED_CERT: True if the aircraft was equipped and certified to fly by instruments alone.
cols.ELT_MOUNTED_AIRCRAFT: True if the emergency locator beacon was mounted in the aircraft.
cols.ELT_CONNECTED_ANTENNA: True if the emergency locator beacon was connected to its antenna.
cols.ELT_MANUFACTURER: The maker of the emergency locator beacon, like Artex. Names vary, so ACK and ACK Technologies both appear. Mostly the word None.
cols.ELT_MODEL: The model of the emergency locator beacon, like AK-450. Mostly the word None.
cols.ELT_REASON_OTHER: Other reason the beacon failed. Every row says None, so it holds nothing.

TRANSPORT__FED_NTSB_AVIATION_AIRCRAFT.summary: Every aircraft involved in an accident or incident investigated by the NTSB, with its registration, make and model, damage, owner, operator and flight details.
TRANSPORT__FED_NTSB_AVIATION_AIRCRAFT.row: One aircraft in one accident: a crash with two planes gets two rows.

cols.EV_ID: The NTSB's ID for one aviation accident, starting with a date, like 20260625203249. Same ID across the aircraft, event and injury tables, so it joins them.
cols.NTSB_NO: The accident safety board's case number, like DFW08LA055. The aircraft table adds A or B for each plane in a two-plane crash.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, usually in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 481243N, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, usually in decimal degrees; U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0 or the word None instead of a real spot, the aviation table writes it like 0955859W, and several tables leave it empty.
cols.LCHG_DATE: The date the NTSB last changed this record.
cols.LCHG_USERID: The short login name of the NTSB staffer who last changed this record, like coln or dobn. Most rows hold the word None instead of a name.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.EV_TYPE: ACC for an accident, INC for a lesser incident.
cols.EV_DOW: The day of the week, as two letters like Sa or Mo.
cols.EV_TIME: The time of day, as a number like 1800.0 for 6 pm, stored as text.
cols.EV_TMZN: The time zone of the time, UTC on most rows. The rest hold the word None.
cols.EV_CITY: The city or place nearest the accident. Includes places abroad.
cols.EV_STATE: The US state, as two letters. Foreign accidents hold the word None or OF.
cols.EV_COUNTRY: The country, USA for most rows, else a two-letter code like BR or GB.
cols.EV_SITE_ZIPCODE: The ZIP code of the crash site. The word None fills about a fifth of rows.
cols.EV_YEAR: The year of the accident, stored as text.
cols.EV_MONTH: The month of the accident, as a number 1 to 12, stored as text.
cols.MID_AIR: Y or N for a mid-air collision. The word None fills almost every row.
cols.ON_GROUND_COLLISION: Y or N for a collision on the ground. The word None fills almost every row.
cols.LATLONG_ACQ: How the location was found: MEAS for measured, EST for estimated. The word None fills many rows.
cols.APT_NAME: The nearest airport's name. The word None fills more than a third of rows, and some say Private or N/A.
cols.EV_NR_APT_ID: The nearest airport's code, like GGW. Many rows hold None, PVT, NONE, N/A or NA instead.
cols.EV_NR_APT_LOC: ONAP if the accident was on an airport, OFAP if off it. Some rows hold the word None.
cols.APT_DIST: Distance from the nearest airport, stored as text. Mostly 0.0; some rows say nan.
cols.APT_DIR: Compass direction from the nearest airport, in degrees, stored as text. The word nan fills most rows.
cols.APT_ELEV: The nearest airport's elevation in feet, stored as text. The word nan fills almost half the rows.
cols.WX_BRIEF_COMP: Always the word None, so it is empty in practice.
cols.WX_SRC_IIC: Where the weather report came from, as a code like WFAC or PILO. Needs a lookup; some rows hold None.
cols.WX_OBS_TIME: The time of the weather reading, like 1753.0, stored as text. Some rows say nan.
cols.WX_OBS_DIR: Compass direction from the weather station to the site, in degrees, stored as text. 0.0 on about 4 in 10 rows.
cols.WX_OBS_FAC_ID: The code of the weather station used, like KGGW. Some rows hold the word None.
cols.WX_OBS_ELEV: The weather station's elevation in feet, stored as text. Some rows say nan.
