cols.WX_OBS_DIST: Distance from the weather station to the site, stored as text. 0.0 on about half the rows.
cols.WX_OBS_TMZN: The time zone of the weather reading, UTC or the word None.
cols.LIGHT_COND: The light at the time, as a code like DAYL, NITE or DUSK. Some rows hold the word None.
cols.SKY_COND_NONCEIL: Clouds below the ceiling, as a code like CLER, FEW or SCAT. Many rows hold the word None.
cols.SKY_NONCEIL_HT: Height of those lower clouds in feet, stored as text. Mostly 0.0.
cols.SKY_CEIL_HT: Height of the cloud ceiling in feet, stored as text. Mostly 0.0.
cols.SKY_COND_CEIL: The cloud ceiling type, as a code like BKN or OVC, or NONE. Many rows hold the word None.
cols.VIS_RVR: Runway visual range in feet, stored as text. The word nan fills almost every row.
cols.VIS_RVV: Always the word None, so it is empty in practice.
cols.VIS_SM: Visibility in statute miles, stored as text. Mostly 10.0; some rows say nan.
cols.WX_TEMP: Air temperature, stored as text. 0.0 fills about a fifth of rows and likely means not recorded.
cols.WX_DEW_PT: Dew point temperature, stored as text. 0.0 fills about a quarter of rows and likely means not recorded.
cols.WIND_DIR_DEG: Wind direction in degrees, stored as text. 0.0 on about 4 in 10 rows.
cols.WIND_DIR_IND: A wind direction flag, mostly U, sometimes Y. Needs a lookup.
cols.WIND_VEL_KTS: Wind speed in knots, stored as text. The word nan fills about a third of rows.
cols.WIND_VEL_IND: A wind speed flag, F or T. Needs a lookup.
cols.GUST_IND: A gust flag, T or F.
cols.GUST_KTS: Wind gust speed in knots, stored as text. Mostly 0.0.
cols.ALTIMETER: The altimeter pressure setting, like 30.04, stored as text with long decimals. 0.0 fills about a quarter of rows.
cols.WX_DENS_ALT: Always the word None, so it is empty in practice.
cols.WX_INT_PRECIP: Always the word None, so it is empty in practice.
cols.METAR: The raw airport weather report text, like KGGW 241453Z AUTO. The word None fills most rows.
cols.EV_HIGHEST_INJURY: The worst injury in the accident: NONE, MINR, SERS or FATL. Some rows hold the word None.
cols.INJ_F_GRND: People killed on the ground. Blank on most rows.
cols.INJ_M_GRND: People with minor injuries on the ground. Blank on most rows.
cols.INJ_S_GRND: People seriously hurt on the ground. Blank on most rows.
cols.INJ_TOT_F: Total people killed. Use this to count deaths.
cols.INJ_TOT_T: Total people on board or involved.
cols.INVEST_AGY: Who investigated, as a code N or O. Needs a lookup; a few rows hold the word None.
cols.NTSB_DOCKET: Always the word None, so it is empty in practice.
cols.NTSB_NOTF_FROM: Always the word None, so it is empty in practice.
cols.NTSB_NOTF_DATE: Meant to hold the date the NTSB was told, but it is empty.
cols.NTSB_NOTF_TM: Always the word None, so it is empty in practice.
cols.FICHE_NUMBER: Always the word None, so it is empty in practice.
cols.WX_COND_BASIC: Basic weather: VMC for clear enough to fly by sight, IMC for flying by instruments. Some rows hold None or Unk.
cols.FAA_DIST_OFFICE: Always the word None, so it is empty in practice.
cols.DEC_LATITUDE: The crash site's latitude, as a decimal.
cols.DEC_LONGITUDE: The crash site's longitude, as a decimal.

TRANSPORT__FED_NTSB_AVIATION_EVENTS.summary: Aviation accidents and incidents investigated by the NTSB, with place, weather, light and injury counts.
TRANSPORT__FED_NTSB_AVIATION_EVENTS.row: One aviation accident or incident: where and when it happened, the weather, and how many people were hurt.

cols.EV_ID: The NTSB's ID for one aviation accident, starting with a date, like 20260625203249. Same ID across the aircraft, event and injury tables, so it joins them.
cols.AIRCRAFT_KEY: Which aircraft in the accident this row is about: almost always 1, then 2 when two planes were involved, and rarely 3 or 5.
cols.LCHG_DATE: The date the NTSB last changed this record.
cols.LCHG_USERID: The short login name of the NTSB staffer who last changed this record, like coln or dobn. Most rows hold the word None instead of a name.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store a long number counting microseconds since 1970, and a few hold broken dates with impossible years like 56645445. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A label for the load run that brought this row in, usually a random ID but sometimes a name like manual-1785965790 or a file name. One table can hold many run IDs. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.INJURY_RECORD_ID: A made-up ID for the row. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols.INJ_PERSON_CATEGORY: Who the count is about, shortened to four letters: Flig, Pass, Cabi or LapC.
cols.INJURY_LEVEL: Injury level, as a code: FATL, SERS, MINR, NONE or TOTL.
cols.INJ_PERSON_COUNT: How many people fall in this group and injury level. Blank on about 13% of rows.

TRANSPORT__FED_NTSB_AVIATION_INJURY.summary: Injury counts from NTSB aviation accident records, by aircraft, type of person on board and injury level.
TRANSPORT__FED_NTSB_AVIATION_INJURY.row: One injury count: one aircraft in one event, one kind of person, one injury level.

cols.OLDCREATIVEID: The ad's old ID, starting CR.
cols.NEWCREATIVEID: The ad's new ID, starting CR. Blank on a few rows.

EDUCATION__FED_GOOGLE_POLADS_CREATIVE_ID.summary: A lookup matching Google political ad IDs in the old format to the new format.
EDUCATION__FED_GOOGLE_POLADS_CREATIVE_ID.row: One ad: its old ID and its new ID.

cols.BUSINESSYEAR: The plan year. Every row is 2026.
cols.STATECODE: The state where the plan is sold, as two letters. Only 30 states appear, the ones that use the federal marketplace.
cols.ISSUERID: The insurance company's five-digit federal ID number, stored as text.
cols.ISSUERMARKETPLACEMARKETINGNAME: The insurance company's brand name as shoppers see it, like Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Texas or Oscar.
cols.SOURCENAME: Which federal filing system the plan data came from: HIOS or SERFF.
cols.IMPORTDATE: The date CMS loaded this plan's data, stored as text like 10/15/2025.
cols.MARKETCOVERAGE: Who can buy the plan: Individual for people buying on their own, or SHOP for small employers.
cols.DENTALONLYPLAN: Yes if this is a stand-alone dental plan, No for a health plan.
cols.STANDARDCOMPONENTID: The plan's ID without the variant suffix, starting with the insurer's ID and state. Several variants of one plan share it.
cols.PLANMARKETINGNAME: The plan's name as sold to shoppers, like Blue Advantage Plus Silver Standard.
cols.HIOSPRODUCTID: The ID of the product line the plan belongs to, built from the insurer ID, state and a number.
cols.NETWORKID: The ID of the doctor and hospital network the plan uses, like TXN009. It only means something within one insurer and state.
cols.SERVICEAREAID: The ID of the geographic area where the plan is sold, like FLS001. It needs the service area file to turn into counties.
cols.FORMULARYID: The ID of the plan's list of covered drugs, like TXF001. Blank for dental plans.
cols.ISNEWPLAN: New if the plan is new this year, Existing if it was sold before.
cols.PLANTYPE: The kind of network the plan uses: HMO, EPO, PPO, POS or Indemnity.
cols.METALLEVEL: The plan's metal tier, like Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum or Catastrophic. Dental plans use High or Low instead.
cols.DESIGNTYPE: Which federal standard plan design the plan follows, like Design 1, or Not Applicable for most plans.
cols.UNIQUEPLANDESIGN: Yes if the insurer used its own custom plan design instead of the standard federal calculator.
cols.QHPNONQHPTYPEID: Whether the plan is sold on the marketplace, off it, or both. Almost all say Both.
cols.ISNOTICEREQUIREDFORPREGNANCY: Yes if a member must notify the plan when pregnant.
cols.ISREFERRALREQUIREDFORSPECIALIST: Yes if members need a referral to see a specialist.
cols.SPECIALISTREQUIRINGREFERRAL: Free text naming which specialists need a referral. Mostly blank, filled only where referrals are required.
cols.PLANLEVELEXCLUSIONS: Free text listing services the plan does not cover, like abortion. Mostly blank.
cols.INDIANPLANVARIATIONESTIMATEDADVANCEDPAYM: The estimated federal payment per member for the American Indian plan variant. Every filled value is $0.00, stored as text.
cols.COMPOSITERATINGOFFERED: Yes if the plan offers one flat premium per employee instead of pricing by age. Almost all say No.
cols.CHILDONLYOFFERING: Whether the plan sells to adults and children or only to children. Almost all say Allows Adult and Child-Only; 211 say Allows Child-Only.
cols.WELLNESSPROGRAMOFFERED: Yes if the plan offers a wellness program.
cols.DISEASEMANAGEMENTPROGRAMSOFFERED: A text list of the illnesses the plan runs care programs for, like asthma, diabetes and heart disease.
cols.EHBPERCENTTOTALPREMIUM: The share of the premium that pays for the federally required basic benefits, as a decimal where 1 means all of it.
cols.EHBPEDIATRICDENTALAPPORTIONMENTQUANTITY: For dental plans, the share of the premium that pays for required children's dental care, as a decimal. Mostly blank.
cols.ISGUARANTEEDRATE: For dental plans, says Guaranteed Rate when the premium is locked. Blank for all health plans.
cols.PLANEFFECTIVEDATE: The date coverage starts, stored as text. Almost every plan starts 1/1/2026.
cols.PLANEXPIRATIONDATE: The date coverage ends. Every filled value is 2026-12-31; about a quarter of rows are blank.
cols.OUTOFCOUNTRYCOVERAGE: Yes if the plan covers any care outside the United States.
cols.OUTOFCOUNTRYCOVERAGEDESCRIPTION: Free text on what care abroad is covered, often emergencies only.
cols.OUTOFSERVICEAREACOVERAGE: Yes if the plan covers any care outside its home area.
cols.OUTOFSERVICEAREACOVERAGEDESCRIPTION: Free text on what care outside the home area is covered, often emergency and urgent care only.
cols.NATIONALNETWORK: Yes if the plan's network is nationwide.
cols.URLFORENROLLMENTPAYMENT: The web address where members pay for or enroll in the plan.
cols.FORMULARYURL: The web address of the plan's list of covered drugs. Blank for dental plans.
cols.PLANID: The full plan variant ID: the plan's ID plus a two-digit variant suffix like -01. Each row has its own value.
cols.PLANVARIANTMARKETINGNAME: The name of this specific plan variant as sold to shoppers.
cols.CSRVARIATIONTYPE: Which version of the plan this is, like the standard silver plan, a 94% or 87% AV level silver plan, or a zero cost sharing version.
cols.ISSUERACTUARIALVALUE: The insurer's own figure for the share of average medical costs the plan pays, as a percent stored as text. Mostly blank.
cols.AVCALCULATOROUTPUTNUMBER: The share of average medical costs the plan pays according to the federal calculator, as a decimal stored as text.
cols.MEDICALDRUGDEDUCTIBLESINTEGRATED: Yes if medical care and drugs share one deductible.
cols.MEDICALDRUGMAXIMUMOUTOFPOCKETINTEGRATED: Yes if medical care and drugs share one out-of-pocket maximum. Every filled row says Yes.
cols.MULTIPLEINNETWORKTIERS: Yes if the plan splits its network into tiers with different costs.
cols.FIRSTTIERUTILIZATION: The expected share of care that goes to tier 1 network providers, as a percent stored as text. 100% for plans with one tier.
cols.SECONDTIERUTILIZATION: The expected share of care that goes to tier 2 network providers, as a percent stored as text. Mostly blank, filled only for tiered plans.
cols.SBCHAVINGABABYDEDUCTIBLE: In the plan's standard example of having a baby, how much the patient pays toward the deductible. Dollar amount stored as text, like $6,000.
cols.SBCHAVINGABABYCOPAYMENT: In the plan's standard example of having a baby, how much the patient pays in copays. Dollar amount stored as text.
cols.SBCHAVINGABABYCOINSURANCE: In the plan's standard example of having a baby, how much the patient pays in coinsurance. Dollar amount stored as text.
cols.SBCHAVINGABABYLIMIT: In the plan's standard example of having a baby, the cost of services the plan does not cover. Dollar amount stored as text, mostly $60.
cols.SBCHAVINGDIABETESDEDUCTIBLE: In the plan's standard example of managing diabetes, how much the patient pays toward the deductible. Dollar amount stored as text.
cols.SBCHAVINGDIABETESCOPAYMENT: In the plan's standard example of managing diabetes, how much the patient pays in copays. Dollar amount stored as text.
cols.SBCHAVINGDIABETESCOINSURANCE: In the plan's standard example of managing diabetes, how much the patient pays in coinsurance. Dollar amount stored as text.
cols.SBCHAVINGDIABETESLIMIT: In the plan's standard example of managing diabetes, the cost of services the plan does not cover. Dollar amount stored as text.
cols.SBCHAVINGSIMPLEFRACTUREDEDUCTIBLE: In the plan's standard example of a simple broken bone, how much the patient pays toward the deductible. Dollar amount stored as text.
cols.SBCHAVINGSIMPLEFRACTURECOPAYMENT: In the plan's standard example of a simple broken bone, how much the patient pays in copays. Dollar amount stored as text.
cols.SBCHAVINGSIMPLEFRACTURECOINSURANCE: In the plan's standard example of a simple broken bone, how much the patient pays in coinsurance. Dollar amount stored as text.
cols.SBCHAVINGSIMPLEFRACTURELIMIT: In the plan's standard example of a simple broken bone, the cost of services the plan does not cover. Almost always $0, stored as text.
cols.SPECIALTYDRUGMAXIMUMCOINSURANCE: The most a member pays per prescription for a specialty drug, stored as text like $650. Filled for only 294 plans.
cols.INPATIENTCOPAYMENTMAXIMUMDAYS: The most hospital days a member pays a daily copay for. 0 for almost every plan, stored as text.
cols.BEGINPRIMARYCARECOSTSHARINGAFTERNUMBEROF: How many primary care visits are free before the member starts paying. 0 for most plans.
cols.BEGINPRIMARYCAREDEDUCTIBLECOINSURANCEAFT: How many primary care copays a member pays before the deductible and coinsurance kick in. 0 for almost every plan, stored as text.
cols.ISHSAELIGIBLE: Yes if the plan can be paired with a health savings account.
cols.HSAORHRAEMPLOYERCONTRIBUTION: Whether an employer puts money into a health savings account for small-group plans. Every filled row says No, and most rows are blank.
cols.URLFORSUMMARYOFBENEFITSCOVERAGE: The web address of the plan's official summary of benefits and coverage.
cols.PLANBROCHURE: The web address of the plan's sales brochure.
cols.CHILDONLYPLANID: The ID of a matching child-only plan. Empty in this table.
cols.HSAORHRAEMPLOYERCONTRIBUTIONAMOUNT: How much an employer puts into a health savings account. Empty in this table.
cols.MEHBINNTIER1_INDIVIDUALMOOP: The out-of-pocket maximum for one person, at tier 1 in-network providers, as dollar text. Filled only for the 1,389 stand-alone dental plans, most often $450; blank for every health plan.
cols.MEHBINNTIER1_FAMILYPERPERSONMOOP: The out-of-pocket maximum for each person on a family plan, at tier 1 in-network providers, as dollar text. Filled only for the 1,389 stand-alone dental plans, most often $450 per person; blank for every health plan.
cols.MEHBINNTIER1_FAMILYPERGROUPMOOP: The out-of-pocket maximum for a whole family, at tier 1 in-network providers, as dollar text. Filled only for the 1,389 stand-alone dental plans, most often $900 per group; blank for every health plan.
cols.MEHBINNTIER2_INDIVIDUALMOOP: The out-of-pocket maximum for one person, at tier 2 in-network providers, as dollar text. Filled on only 100 plans, most often $450; blank everywhere else.
cols.MEHBINNTIER2_FAMILYPERPERSONMOOP: The out-of-pocket maximum for each person on a family plan, at tier 2 in-network providers, as dollar text. Filled on only 100 plans, most often $450 per person; blank everywhere else.
cols.MEHBINNTIER2_FAMILYPERGROUPMOOP: The out-of-pocket maximum for a whole family, at tier 2 in-network providers, as dollar text. Filled on only 100 plans, most often $900 per group; blank everywhere else.
cols.MEHBOUTOFNETINDIVIDUALMOOP: The out-of-pocket maximum for one person, for out-of-network care, as dollar text. Filled only for the 1,389 stand-alone dental plans, and mostly Not Applicable there; blank for every health plan.
cols.MEHBOUTOFNETFAMILYPERPERSONMOOP: The out-of-pocket maximum for each person on a family plan, for out-of-network care, as dollar text. Filled only for the 1,389 stand-alone dental plans, and mostly Not Applicable there; blank for every health plan.
cols.MEHBOUTOFNETFAMILYPERGROUPMOOP: The out-of-pocket maximum for a whole family, for out-of-network care, as dollar text. Filled only for the 1,389 stand-alone dental plans, and mostly Not Applicable there; blank for every health plan.
cols.MEHBCOMBINNOONINDIVIDUALMOOP: The out-of-pocket maximum for one person, for in-network and out-of-network care combined, as dollar text. Filled only for the 1,389 stand-alone dental plans, and mostly Not Applicable there; blank for every health plan.
cols.MEHBCOMBINNOONFAMILYPERPERSONMOOP: The out-of-pocket maximum for each person on a family plan, for in-network and out-of-network care combined, as dollar text. Filled only for the 1,389 stand-alone dental plans, and mostly Not Applicable there; blank for every health plan.
cols.MEHBCOMBINNOONFAMILYPERGROUPMOOP: The out-of-pocket maximum for a whole family, for in-network and out-of-network care combined, as dollar text. Filled only for the 1,389 stand-alone dental plans, and mostly Not Applicable there; blank for every health plan.
cols.DEHBINNTIER1_INDIVIDUALMOOP: The plan's drug out-of-pocket maximum for one person, for tier 1 in-network providers. Empty in this table.
cols.DEHBINNTIER1_FAMILYPERPERSONMOOP: The plan's drug out-of-pocket maximum for each person on a family plan, for tier 1 in-network providers. Empty in this table.
cols.DEHBINNTIER1_FAMILYPERGROUPMOOP: The plan's drug out-of-pocket maximum for a whole family, for tier 1 in-network providers. Empty in this table.
cols.DEHBINNTIER2_INDIVIDUALMOOP: The plan's drug out-of-pocket maximum for one person, for tier 2 in-network providers. Empty in this table.
cols.DEHBINNTIER2_FAMILYPERPERSONMOOP: The plan's drug out-of-pocket maximum for each person on a family plan, for tier 2 in-network providers. Empty in this table.
cols.DEHBINNTIER2_FAMILYPERGROUPMOOP: The plan's drug out-of-pocket maximum for a whole family, for tier 2 in-network providers. Empty in this table.
cols.DEHBOUTOFNETINDIVIDUALMOOP: The plan's drug out-of-pocket maximum for one person, for out-of-network care. Empty in this table.
cols.DEHBOUTOFNETFAMILYPERPERSONMOOP: The plan's drug out-of-pocket maximum for each person on a family plan, for out-of-network care. Empty in this table.
cols.DEHBOUTOFNETFAMILYPERGROUPMOOP: The plan's drug out-of-pocket maximum for a whole family, for out-of-network care. Empty in this table.
cols.DEHBCOMBINNOONINDIVIDUALMOOP: The plan's drug out-of-pocket maximum for one person, for in-network and out-of-network care combined. Empty in this table.
cols.DEHBCOMBINNOONFAMILYPERPERSONMOOP: The plan's drug out-of-pocket maximum for each person on a family plan, for in-network and out-of-network care combined. Empty in this table.
cols.DEHBCOMBINNOONFAMILYPERGROUPMOOP: The plan's drug out-of-pocket maximum for a whole family, for in-network and out-of-network care combined. Empty in this table.
cols.TEHBINNTIER1_INDIVIDUALMOOP: The plan's combined medical and drug out-of-pocket maximum for one person, for tier 1 in-network providers. A dollar amount stored as text.
cols.TEHBINNTIER1_FAMILYPERPERSONMOOP: The plan's combined medical and drug out-of-pocket maximum for each person on a family plan, for tier 1 in-network providers. A dollar amount stored as text.
cols.TEHBINNTIER1_FAMILYPERGROUPMOOP: The plan's combined medical and drug out-of-pocket maximum for a whole family, for tier 1 in-network providers. A dollar amount stored as text.
cols.TEHBINNTIER2_INDIVIDUALMOOP: The plan's combined medical and drug out-of-pocket maximum for one person, for tier 2 in-network providers. A dollar amount stored as text. Mostly blank.
cols.TEHBINNTIER2_FAMILYPERPERSONMOOP: The plan's combined medical and drug out-of-pocket maximum for each person on a family plan, for tier 2 in-network providers. A dollar amount stored as text. Mostly blank.
cols.TEHBINNTIER2_FAMILYPERGROUPMOOP: The plan's combined medical and drug out-of-pocket maximum for a whole family, for tier 2 in-network providers. A dollar amount stored as text. Mostly blank.
cols.TEHBOUTOFNETINDIVIDUALMOOP: The plan's combined medical and drug out-of-pocket maximum for one person, for out-of-network care. A dollar amount stored as text, with Not Applicable for many plans.
cols.TEHBOUTOFNETFAMILYPERPERSONMOOP: The plan's combined medical and drug out-of-pocket maximum for each person on a family plan, for out-of-network care. A dollar amount stored as text, with Not Applicable for many plans.

cols.C_1_YEAR: The reporting year. Always 2023 in this table.
cols.C_2_TRIFD: The EPA's ID for the facility in the Toxics Release Inventory. One site files one row per chemical.
cols.C_3_FRS_ID: The EPA's cross-program ID for the facility, used to link it to other EPA records.
cols.C_4_FACILITY_NAME: The name of the plant or site that filed the report.
cols.C_5_STREET_ADDRESS: The facility's street address. A few are directions instead, like miles from a town.
cols.C_7_COUNTY: The facility's county name, in capitals.
cols.C_8_ST: The facility's state, as two letters.
cols.C_10_BIA: The Bureau of Indian Affairs code for the tribe whose land the site sits on. Needs a lookup and is blank on almost every row.
cols.C_11_TRIBE: The tribe whose land the site sits on, like The Chickasaw Nation. Blank on almost every row.
cols.C_14_HORIZONTAL_DATUM: Meant to name the map system behind the coordinates, but it is empty.
cols.C_15_PARENT_CO_NAME: The parent company as the facility wrote it, like MARATHON PETROLEUM CORP. Blank on about a fifth of rows.
cols.C_16_PARENT_CO_DB_NUM: The parent company's Dun and Bradstreet number. Blank on about a third of rows.
cols.C_17_STANDARD_PARENT_CO_NAME: The parent company name as cleaned up by the EPA. Better for grouping than the raw parent name.
cols.C_18_FOREIGN_PARENT_CO_NAME: The foreign parent company, like BASF SE or SHELL PLC. Blank on most rows.
cols.C_19_FOREIGN_PARENT_CO_DB_NUM: The foreign parent's Dun and Bradstreet number. Blank on most rows.
cols.C_20_STANDARD_FOREIGN_PARENT_CO_NAME: The foreign parent name as cleaned up by the EPA. Blank on most rows.
cols.C_21_FEDERAL_FACILITY: YES if the site is run by the federal government, NO if not.
cols.C_22_INDUSTRY_SECTOR_CODE: A short industry code, like 325 for chemicals. The matching name is in the next column.
cols.C_23_INDUSTRY_SECTOR: The industry in plain words, like Chemicals, Petroleum or Food.
cols.C_24_PRIMARY_SIC: Meant to hold an older SIC industry code, but it is empty. Use the NAICS columns instead.
cols.C_25_SIC_2: Meant to hold an older SIC industry code, but it is empty. Use the NAICS columns instead.
cols.C_26_SIC_3: Meant to hold an older SIC industry code, but it is empty. Use the NAICS columns instead.
cols.C_27_SIC_4: Meant to hold an older SIC industry code, but it is empty. Use the NAICS columns instead.
cols.C_28_SIC_5: Meant to hold an older SIC industry code, but it is empty. Use the NAICS columns instead.
cols.C_29_SIC_6: Meant to hold an older SIC industry code, but it is empty. Use the NAICS columns instead.
cols.C_30_PRIMARY_NAICS: The site's main six-digit NAICS industry code. Needs a lookup.
cols.C_31_NAICS_2: Extra NAICS industry code number 2 for the site. Needs a lookup and is blank on most rows.
cols.C_32_NAICS_3: Extra NAICS industry code number 3 for the site. Needs a lookup and is blank on most rows.
cols.C_33_NAICS_4: Extra NAICS industry code number 4 for the site. Needs a lookup and is blank on most rows.
cols.C_34_NAICS_5: Extra NAICS industry code number 5 for the site. Needs a lookup and is blank on most rows.
cols.C_35_NAICS_6: Extra NAICS industry code number 6 for the site. Needs a lookup and is blank on most rows.
cols.C_36_DOC_CTRL_NUM: The ID of the filed report form. Each row has its own.
cols.C_37_CHEMICAL: The chemical reported, like Lead or Methanol.
cols.C_38_ELEMENTAL_METAL_INCLUDED: YES if the amount includes the pure metal along with its compounds.
cols.C_39_TRI_CHEMICAL_COMPOUND_ID: The EPA's chemical ID. Mostly a zero-padded CAS number, but chemical groups get codes like N420 that need a lookup.
cols.C_40_CAS: The chemical's CAS registry number, like 7439-92-1. Chemical groups get codes like N420 instead.
cols.C_41_SRS_ID: The EPA's substance registry number for the chemical.
cols.C_42_CLEAN_AIR_ACT_CHEMICAL: YES if the chemical is regulated under the Clean Air Act.
cols.C_43_CLASSIFICATION: The chemical's reporting class: TRI, PBT or Dioxin. PBT means persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic.
cols.C_44_METAL: YES if the chemical is a metal or metal compound.
cols.C_45_METAL_CATEGORY: What kind of metal chemical it is, like Elemental metals or Non_Metal.
cols.C_46_CARCINOGEN: YES if the chemical is a known or suspected cause of cancer.
cols.C_47_PBT: YES if the chemical is persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic.
cols.C_48_PFAS: YES if the chemical is a PFAS forever chemical. Only a few hundred rows say YES.
cols.C_49_FORM_TYPE: Which EPA form was filed, R or A. Form A is the short form with fewer details.
cols.C_50_UNIT_OF_MEASURE: Pounds for almost everything; Grams for dioxins. Check this before adding amounts.
cols.C_51_5_1_FUGITIVE_AIR: Chemical that leaked into the air from equipment, not a smokestack, in pounds, stored as text. Zero on about half the rows.

cols.C_53_5_3_WATER: Chemical released into rivers, lakes or other water, in pounds, stored as text. Zero on most rows.
cols.C_54_5_4_UNDERGROUND: Always 0.000 in this table, so it tells you nothing.

cols.DATE_FILE: Date of the EU list file, 05/06/2026 on every row, stored as text.
cols.ENTITY_LOGICAL_ID: The EU's ID for the sanctioned person or company; it ties together all of its detail lines.
cols.SUBJECT_TYPE: P for a person or E for an entity such as a company.
cols.LEBA_NUMTITLE: The EU regulation that listed this person or company, by number and Official Journal reference.
cols.LEBA_PUBLICATION_DATE: Date that regulation was published, stored as text.
cols.LEBA_URL: Link to that regulation on EUR-Lex.
cols.PROGRAMME: Sanctions program, as a code like UKR, IRN or SYR that needs a lookup.
cols.ENTITY_REMARK: Free-text remarks, often the date the UN designated them.
cols.NAAL_LOGICAL_ID: ID of this name or alias entry. Filled only on name lines.
cols.ENTITY_LOGICAL_ID_1: The person or company ID again, filled only on name lines.
cols.NAAL_LEBA_NUMTITLE: The EU regulation that added this name, by number and Official Journal reference. Filled only on name lines.
cols.NAAL_LEBA_PUBLICATION_DATE: Date the regulation that added this name was published, stored as text.
cols.NAAL_LEBA_URL: Link to the regulation that added this name.
cols.NAAL_PROGRAMME: Sanctions program code for this name line, like UKR or IRN; codes need a lookup.
cols.NAAL_LASTNAME: Last name, in Latin or Cyrillic letters. Mostly blank; NAAL_WHOLENAME is fuller.
cols.NAAL_FIRSTNAME: First name, in Latin or Cyrillic letters. Mostly blank.
cols.NAAL_MIDDLENAME: Middle name or patronymic, like Vladimirovich. Mostly blank.
cols.NAAL_WHOLENAME: Full name or alias as listed, in many languages and scripts.
cols.NAAL_TITLE: Title or rank, like Major General, or a company form like Joint Stock Company. Mostly blank.
cols.NAAL_FUNCTION: Job or role, like Member of the State Duma. Mostly blank.
cols.NAAL_LANGUAGE: Language of this spelling of the name, as a two-letter code like EN or RU.
cols.ADDR_LOGICAL_ID: ID of this address entry. Filled only on address lines.
cols.ENTITY_LOGICAL_ID_2: The person or company ID again, filled only on address lines.
cols.ADDR_LEBA_NUMTITLE: The EU regulation that added this address. Filled only on address lines.
cols.ADDR_LEBA_PUBLICATION_DATE: Date the regulation that added this address was published, stored as text. Mostly blank.
cols.ADDR_LEBA_URL: Link to the regulation that added this address. Mostly blank.
cols.ADDR_PROGRAMME: Sanctions program code for this address line; codes need a lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.ADDR_NUMBER: House number. Empty in this table: filled 0.
cols.ADDR_STREET: Street address, sometimes a P.O. box. Mostly blank.
cols.ADDR_ZIPCODE: Postal code of the address. Filled on few rows.
cols.ADDR_CITY: City of the address, like Tehran or Moscow. Mostly blank.
cols.ADDR_COUNTRY: Country of the address, as a three-letter code like RUS. Mostly blank.
cols.ADDR_OTHER: Notes on the address, like previous address or place of registration. Mostly blank.
cols.BIRT_LOGICAL_ID: ID of this birth entry. Filled only on birth lines.
cols.ENTITY_LOGICAL_ID_3: The person or company ID again, filled only on birth lines.
cols.BIRT_LEBA_NUMTITLE: The EU regulation that added this birth record. Filled only on birth lines.
cols.BIRT_LEBA_PUBLICATION_DATE: Date the regulation that added this birth record was published. Mostly blank.
cols.BIRT_LEBA_URL: Link to the regulation that added this birth record. Mostly blank.
cols.BIRT_PROGRAMME: Sanctions program code for this birth line; codes need a lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.BIRT_PLACE: Place of birth, like Moscow or Damascus. Mostly blank.
cols.BIRT_COUNTRY: Country of birth, as a three-letter code like RUS. Mostly blank.
cols.IDEN_LOGICAL_ID: ID of this identity document entry. Filled only on ID lines.
cols.ENTITY_LOGICAL_ID_4: The person or company ID again, filled only on ID lines.
cols.IDEN_LEBA_NUMTITLE: The EU regulation that added this ID document. Filled only on ID lines.
cols.IDEN_LEBA_PUBLICATION_DATE: Date the regulation that added this ID document was published. Mostly blank.
cols.IDEN_LEBA_URL: Link to the regulation that added this ID document. Mostly blank.
cols.IDEN_PROGRAMME: Sanctions program code for this ID line; codes need a lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.IDEN_NUMBER: ID document number with its type and notes in one string, like a passport or company registration number. Mostly blank.
cols.IDEN_COUNTRY: Country that issued the ID document, as a three-letter code. Blank on some ID lines.
cols.CITI_LOGICAL_ID: ID of this citizenship entry. Filled only on citizenship lines.
cols.ENTITY_LOGICAL_ID_5: The person or company ID again, filled only on citizenship lines.
cols.CITI_LEBA_NUMTITLE: The EU regulation that added this citizenship. Filled only on citizenship lines.
cols.CITI_LEBA_PUBLICATION_DATE: Date the regulation that added this citizenship was published. Mostly blank.
cols.CITI_LEBA_URL: Link to the regulation that added this citizenship. Mostly blank.
cols.CITI_PROGRAMME: Sanctions program code for this citizenship line; codes need a lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.CITI_COUNTRY: Country of citizenship, as a three-letter code like RUS. Mostly blank.
cols.EU_REF_NUM: EU reference number for the listed person or company, like EU.4051.68.

JUSTICE__INTL_EU_SANCTIONS.summary: The European Union's consolidated list of people and companies under financial sanctions, from the file dated 05/06/2026: names and aliases, addresses, birth details, ID papers and citizenship, with the EU regulation behind each. cols.VETERAN_DEATHS_BY_SUICIDE_UNADJUSTED_AND: Year of the line, 2001 to 2023, mixed with header text.
cols.COL_1: Age group label, like All or 18-34, mixed with stray numbers and header text.
cols.COL_2: Suicide death counts, stored as text.
cols.COL_3: Veteran population counts, stored as text.
cols.COL_4: Suicide rate per 100,000, stored as text with long decimals.
cols.COL_5: Death counts for a second block of the table, stored as text.
cols.COL_6: Population counts for that second block, stored as text.
cols.COL_7: Rates per 100,000 for that second block, stored as text.
cols.COL_8: Female age group label, like All or 55+; . is a placeholder for blank.
cols.COL_9: Female suicide death counts, stored as text; . is a placeholder for blank.
cols.COL_10: Female veteran population counts, stored as text; . is a placeholder for blank.
cols.COL_11: Female suicide rate per 100,000, stored as text; . is a placeholder for blank.
cols.COL_12: Rates with long decimals, likely the age-adjusted rate. Filled on only 24 rows.

EDUCATION__FED_FRB_Z1_CSV.summary: The Federal Reserve's Financial Accounts of the United States, called Z.1: 423 columns of quarterly series on money flowing in and out of households, businesses, governments, banks and the rest of the world. 61 of those columns are repeat copies of another series, so there are about 362 distinct series. Every value is stored as text.
EDUCATION__FED_FRB_Z1_CSV.row: One quarter: the value of every series for one quarter, like 2026:Q1.

cols.RAW: The whole raw response as JSON, with device details like brand name inside.

HEALTH__FED_FDA_GUDID__STAGING.summary: 1,329 raw responses from FDA's medical device ID database, each kept as one block of JSON text.
HEALTH__FED_FDA_GUDID__STAGING.row: One raw response: a block of JSON with one or more device records.

cols.PRIVATE_AIRPORT_LIST_FOR_WHICH_INFORMATI: The airport's FAA location code, like WY11 or P16. The long column name is the file's title, not a real header.
cols.UNNAMED_1: The airport's name, often a ranch or farm, like Circle B.
cols.UNNAMED_2: The FAA site number for the airport, like 27779.73*A.
cols.UNNAMED_3: The city the airport is associated with.
cols.UNNAMED_4: The state, as two letters. Texas has the most.
cols.UNNAMED_5: The airport's status. Operational on every airport row; one row holds the header word Status.

TRANSPORT__FED_FAA_ADIP_PRIVATE_AIRPORTS.summary: The FAA's list of private airports whose information has not been updated in the last three years, with each airport's code, name, city and state; the columns came in unnamed, and one row holds the header text.
TRANSPORT__FED_FAA_ADIP_PRIVATE_AIRPORTS.row: One airport: one private airstrip or landing site the FAA has not heard from in three years.

cols.SEQNO: The data bank's number for this report. Each row has its own.
cols.REC_TYPE: A one-letter code for the kind of report: C, P, M or A. Codes need a lookup.
cols.REPORT_TYPE_CODE: A number code for the type of report, like 302 or 101. Codes need a lookup.
cols.ORIG_YEAR: The year the report was first filed.
cols.WORK_STATE: The state where the practitioner works, as two letters. Mostly blank.
cols.WORK_COUNTRY: The country where the practitioner works. Empty in this table.
cols.HOME_STATE: The state where the practitioner lives, as two letters.
cols.HOME_COUNTRY: The country where the practitioner lives. Empty in this table.
cols.LICENSE_STATE: The state that issued the practitioner's license, as two letters.
cols.LICENSE_FIELD_CODE: A number code for the practitioner's licensed field, like 10 or 100. Codes need a lookup.
cols.PRACTITIONER_AGE: The practitioner's age, rounded down to a ten-year band, like 40 or 50.
cols.GRAD_YEAR: The year the practitioner finished school, rounded down to the decade, like 1990.
cols.ALLEGATION_NATURE: A number code for the broad kind of malpractice claim, like 1 or 60. Codes need a lookup. Blank on non-malpractice reports.
cols.ALLEGATION_1: A number code for the main malpractice allegation, like 101 or 306. Codes need a lookup.
cols.ALLEGATION_2: A code for a second malpractice allegation. Mostly blank.
cols.OUTCOME_CODE: A number code for what happened to the patient. Codes need a lookup. Only on some malpractice reports.
cols.MALPRACTICE_YEAR_2: A second year of malpractice, when it spanned more than one. Mostly blank.
cols.PAYMENT_FLAG: The malpractice payment in dollars, stored as text with a dollar sign, like $97500. Values sit on a set list, so read them as rounded amounts, not exact ones.
cols.TOTAL_PAYMENT: The total paid across related payments. Empty in this table.
cols.PAYMENT_NUMBER: A letter code S, M or U for whether this was a single payment or one of several. Codes need a lookup.
cols.NUM_PERSONS: How many practitioners shared in this payment. 0 on most rows.
cols.PAY_TYPE: A letter code for how the payment was made, like S or U. Codes need a lookup.
cols.PAYER_RELATIONSHIP: A code for who paid, like 1 or P. Codes need a lookup.
cols.PATIENT_AGE: The patient's age in a ten-year band, like 50. Mostly blank.
cols.PATIENT_SEX: The patient's sex: F, M or U. Only on some malpractice reports.
cols.PATIENT_TYPE: A letter code for the kind of patient: O, I, B or U. Codes need a lookup.
cols.ADVERSE_ACTION_YEAR: The year the action against the practitioner was taken.
cols.AA_CLASS_1: A number code for the kind of action taken, like 1125 or 1280. Codes need a lookup.
cols.AA_CLASS_2: A code for a second kind of action taken. Mostly blank.
cols.AA_CLASS_3: A code for a third kind of action taken. Mostly blank.
cols.AA_CLASS_4: A code for a fourth kind of action taken. Almost always blank.
cols.AA_CLASS_5: A code for a fifth kind of action taken. Almost always blank.
cols.BASIS_CODE_1: A code for the reason behind the action, like 39 or A6. 0 is common. Codes need a lookup.
cols.BASIS_CODE_2: A code for a second reason. 0 fills most filled rows, so read it as none.
cols.BASIS_CODE_3: A code for a third reason. 0 fills most filled rows, so read it as none.
cols.BASIS_CODE_4: A code for a fourth reason. 0 fills most filled rows, so read it as none.
cols.BASIS_CODE_5: A code for a fifth reason. 0 fills most filled rows, so read it as none.
cols.AA_LENGTH_TYPE: A letter code I, S or P for how long the action lasts. Codes need a lookup.
cols.AA_LENGTH: How long the action lasts, in years, like 5 or 0.25. Mostly blank.
cols.AA_EFFECTIVE_YEAR: The year the action took effect.
cols.AA_SIGNED_YEAR: The year the action was signed.
cols.PRACTITIONER_TYPE_CODE: A number code for the kind of practitioner, like 300 or 500. Codes need a lookup.
cols.PRACTITIONER_REPORT_SEQ: A number that stays the same across one practitioner's reports. Use it to follow one unnamed person.
cols.PRIOR_MALPRACTICE_REPORTS: How many malpractice payment reports this practitioner already had.
cols.PRIOR_LICENSE_REPORTS: How many license actions this practitioner already had.
cols.PRIOR_CLINICAL_PRIVILEGE_REPORTS: How many hospital privilege actions this practitioner already had. Mostly 0.
cols.PRIOR_SOCIETY_MEMBERSHIP_REPORTS: How many professional society actions this practitioner already had. Almost always 0.
cols.PRIOR_DEA_REPORTS: How many DEA drug-license actions this practitioner already had. Mostly 0.
cols.PRIOR_EXCLUSION_REPORTS: How many exclusions from government health programs this practitioner already had. Mostly 0.
cols.PRIOR_GA_REPORTS: How many prior reports of a type coded GA this practitioner had. Mostly 0; the code needs a lookup.
cols.PRIOR_CTM_REPORTS: How many prior reports of a type coded CTM this practitioner had. Mostly 0; the code needs a lookup.
cols.FUND_PAYMENT_FLAG: A 0 or 1 flag on malpractice payments; 1 on a small share. What 1 means needs a lookup.

HEALTH__FED_HRSA_NPDB.summary: The public-use file of the National Practitioner Data Bank: malpractice payments and disciplinary actions against doctors, nurses and other health workers, with the people's identities removed.
HEALTH__FED_HRSA_NPDB.row: One report to the data bank: a malpractice payment or a license, privilege or other action against one unnamed practitioner.

IMMIGRATION__FED_EOIR_CASE_DATA.summary: Immigration court case records from the Justice Department's court office, EOIR. Broken: only one column loaded, so every judge, court, hearing, charge and outcome field is missing. Do not build on it until it is reloaded.
